We know how much privacy matters to you, and how careful many of you are about who you share personal information with. You trusted us with yours. We should have held ourselves to a higher standard in protecting it. We understand and we are deeply sorry.

On 5 October 2026, a security alert led us to discover the incident, and we contained the attack immediately. By then, some user data had already been accessed by the attacker. We fixed the vulnerability and tightened our access controls.

The attacker tried to reach deposited funds but was unable to. Funds on the Based Visa Card remain safe and cards remain operational. Funds in the Based App wallet and Trading Terminal are also safe and were not affected.

After the attack, we reviewed our other systems and found no sign that they were compromised.

As soon as we made sure that all systems were thoroughly audited and extra security precautions were put in place, then we proceeded to disclose this incident to affected users. Cardholders who are affected have the right to know.

If you were affected, please be extra careful. Sophisticated actors may use this information to try to trick you. 

For account queries, use the in-app support chat. It is the most secure way to reach us, and it lets us verify that you own the account. No one from the Based team will contact you on X or Telegram about your account.

We are committed to strengthening the security of our systems.

Once again, we are very sorry.

很多很多很多很多人在这个是什么工具
再次统一回答一下：

这是我自己把我自己平常看项目的指标以及交易逻辑写出来让技术给我做的，属于我自己的工具，没有对外，不过有几个交易员朋友在问也开放了一下，总结下功能：

二级的

1、自选币的观察判断：因为如果是系统自动推送，每天会有很多很多很多压根看不过来，所以就做了个自选功能，关注的币可以看到最近的oi、量、费率、链上持仓、借币利率、社媒热度、新闻等变化，然后结合一些固定指标做出判断，是偏多还是偏空

2、操作机会：会根据oi跟fdv关系、费率、借币率、oi持仓等等筛选出一些值得关注的币推送

3、项目备忘：会把一些币的操作手法和阶段记录下来，做之后的分析参考

目前还没做自动交易，还在调精度，而且这个东西是我主观的逻辑判断会比较多，所以跟其他平台的判断很不一样，目前我的准确率还是挺高的。

一级的

一级主要就是出新东西马上会做相应的工具监控，平常会收集一些庄的地址，还有一些地址持仓关联分析，监控这些地址的动作给信号。

text:
I feel mixed about the "all software is becoming open source" narrative.

While it's true that many apps and games can basically be reverse-engineered with AI now, there are still moats and trade-offs:

1. Distribution and network effects.

It's still hard to get a lot of people to join a game at the same time or connect with each other.

The flip side here is that if you have distribution, you can make alot of money in a short period of time even if your product is just an AI wrapper.

2. Enterprise compliance and trust.

Enterprises drive ~60% of software spend.

AI might make it easier for apps to pass security and compliance reviews, but big companies still want legal liability, support, and someone to blame when things break.

I don't think any Fortune 500 company is switching from Adobe to an open-source alternative anytime soon.

The counter-argument here is that enterprises might just build apps internally, which many are already doing.

I also think that many enterprise apps have become so bloated that most companies only need 20% of the features which makes vibe coding an internal replacement easier.

3. Proprietary data and memory.

This is the #1 moat if your app can generate proprietary data on users or usage.

The counter-argument here is that if your app actually generates valuable data, you can probably make more money just making it free and selling the data to AI labs instead of charging $25/month or whatever as a SaaS.

For example, Reddit is making $200M+ from its data licensing deals with OpenAI and Google, which far exceeds whatever it made from paid consumer subscriptions.

What do people think? Is it harder or easier now to make money from software?

Star Xu: Hyperliquid's Matching Engine Is More Market Maker Friendly  

OKX founder Star Xu @star_okx said on the New Era Finance Podcast @new_era_finance that Hyperliquid differs fundamentally from centralized order book exchanges in its technical design. While centralized exchanges process orders individually, Hyperliquid matches orders block by block and prioritizes cancellations within each block, allowing market makers to cancel orders ahead of takers. 

He believes this market maker friendly design explains why Hyperliquid's order book depth appears better than that of many centralized exchanges, while offering another approach for long-tail assets with limited liquidity.

text:
AI에 대한 대중들과 전문가들 인식 격차(안드레 카파시)

1/ 같은 AI를 두고 누군가는 “별로 쓸 일이 없다”고 하고, 누군가는 “몇 달 걸리던 일이 끝났다”고 함.

카파시는 이 인식 격차가 더 벌어지고 있다고 봄.

대다수는 검색과 글쓰기를 돕는 챗봇을 경험하고, 소수는 큰 프로젝트를 수행하는 에이전트를 경험한다. 서로 다른 사용 경험을 놓고 AI의 능력을 이야기하는 상황.

2/ 카파시가 그린 AI 사용자의 깔때기.

약 60억 명은 LLM을 거의 접하지 않음. 약 10억~20억 명은 무료 서비스를 가끔 사용. 약 2,000만 명은 최첨단 모델을 수학·코딩에 활용. 약 5,000명은 내부 최첨단 시스템에 접근.

숫자는 그의 거친 추정임. 핵심은 깊이 활용하는 집단으로 갈수록 사람이 급격히 줄어든다는 점.

3/ 수학·코딩 전문가들이 체감하는 변화는 작업 시간

카파시는 수주~수개월 걸리던 복잡한 프로젝트를 에이전트에 맡겨 완성하는 경험이 나오고 있다고 설명함.

내부 시스템에서는 수천 개 에이전트가 몇 주씩 협업하는 수준이라고 주장한다. 여기서는 사람이 결과를 검토하고 이해하는 속도까지 병목이 되기 시작했다는 것.

4/ AI의 체감 차이를 만드는 요인은 세 가지.

맡기는 문제의 크기, 사용하는 분야, 접근 가능한 시스템.

짧은 질문은 AI의 능력을 많이 시험하지 못함. 어렵고 긴 작업을 맡길수록 변화가 크게 느껴진다는 설명.

수학·코딩은 정답과 실행 결과를 검증하기 쉬워 학습에 유리하고, 무료·유료·내부 시스템 사이의 접근 차이도 여기에 더해짐.

5/ 카파시의 관찰에서 눈에 들어오는 건 서로 다른 현실이 동시에 존재한다는 점.

대중은 아직 AI를 거의 써보지 않았고, 많은 직장인은 조금 편리해졌다고 느끼며, 일부 전문가는 변화 속도에 어지러움을 느낀다.

AI에 대한 평가를 들을 때는 어떤 시스템으로, 어떤 일을, 어디까지 맡겨봤는지 함께 봐야 할 듯. 그 경험의 차이가 점점 커지고 있음.

✍️AI로 인해 AI를 잘쓰는 사람과 아닌 사람의 력의 격차가 더 벌어지는 것 같습니다.
많이 써봅시다!

quoted_text:
Dusting off this tweet from April because this gap in shared understanding of LLM capability is *widening*. It's now less "two groups of people speaking past each other" and more a sharp funnel.

- Napkin math somewhere around 6B people (~75% of the population) have barely come in contact with LLMs at all.
- Around 1-2B (~20%) are casual and infrequent users of free-tier ChatGPT-like products. This group sees derpy chatbots and treats them a bit like a better Google search, a writing aid, or etc. Maybe an agent tries to book you a flight. I have non-tech friends who (reasonably, imo) say they have not much use for it at all. Even many professionals outside of math&code are in this tier. For example, execs and many other functions spend a lot of their time talking to other people, so while they understand what is happening intellectually, it is still second-hand and a bit abstract.
- Now we get to professional use of frontier-grade LLMs in math&code. Somewhere around 20M people (0.2%) see first-hand that large, complex projects that used to take them weeks/months can now be completed by agents with a prompt. Building apps, copying apps, translating apps, decompiling apps from binaries... This has all happened very quickly and recently - less than 1 year ago, I was writing code manually by hand, typing memorized computer code commands into a code editor character by character, occasionally pressing Tab to autocomplete a little chunk of code.
- And finally we get to the ~5,000 people (~0.00006%) with access to frontier-grade systems internally. The external world has seen the preview. It looks like swarms of thousands of agents collaborating over weeks on software mega projects: minting zero days, running cyber attacks and defenses at machine speeds, discovering new science, advancing the frontier of mathematics. Things that would have taken top professionals in the industry years of work. Meanwhile, human review and comprehension are starting to fall behind. For example, people are still involved in the "archeology" of the OpenAI-HF incident from many months ago. Mathematicians may be poring over the 722 manuscripts on frontier mathematics for a while.

The funnel is driven by a combination of factors:
1. The impact scales with ambition, problem size, and horizon. A question with a paragraph answer barely stresses the system. You need a reservoir of big, difficult problems that you really care about. This aspect drives the consumer / professional dimension of the funnel.
2. The jaggedness of the system (which I have written about a lot separately). Capability peaks in domains that are digital, verifiable and economically valuable. This is because LLM capability emerges from reinforcement learning on verifiable rewards on a curated environment mixture driven by revenue potential. This aspect primarily drives the area (e.g. math&code) dimension of the funnel.
3. Access. Free-tier, paid-tier, internal.

So this is the weirdness of the moment. The general public has mostly not interacted with these systems. When they have, it looks like a derpy chatbot. The majority of professionals still see only a modest uplift. And a small sliver of professionals are experiencing the vertigo of the curve going vertical. And it is all happening at the same time.

text: Let's say a frontier model is a 10T MoE on GB300 NVL72. That's ~5 Joules/token or ~50 W at human thinking speed vs our brain at 20 W. The energy grid is $0.08/kWh and eating rice $0.50/kWh. So on an energy-per-thought standpoint rn we're surprisingly similar to frontier models!

text:
周末去香港参与了 Lighter 的私人饭局，迟到一年，终于见到了 Vlad @vnovakovski 还有几个网上认识的 team 成员。

一起参加的，有几个基金 fund，一些 big trader，还有做市商。其中基金的兴趣在于购入 ethereum:0x232ce3bd40fcd6f80f3d55a522d03f25df784ee2 。

饭局期间，我问了一些极其犀利的问题，拿到了很多一手信息，估计也是社区成员最想听的，来给大家转达一下。

1、美国合规牌照什么时候下来？

快了但不确定。首先大家要知道，CFTC 牌照其实不由 Lighter 团队所决定，而是政府部门什么时间能给批准。Lighter 的目标是 Q4 上了期权之后，同时拿到 CFTC 给的 Perps 和 Options 的牌照。

Lighter 已经与 CFTC 进行了长达 11 个月的合作与澄清，CFTC 已经“完全”认识并理解了 Lighter 的 ZK+Ethereum 技术架构、清算机制、ADL 策略以及 0 fee 的盈利模式等等。可以这样说 —— Lighter 是最最有可能拿到第一张美国的 Defi/DEX 合规牌照。

2、拿到牌照后，Lighter 会使用 Core/Robinhood 还是会重新开发一个实例？

获取到牌照后，Lighter 第一时间会上线 Lighter US，也就是另外一个实例，KYC/AML 均与传统交易公司对齐，同时 Lighter US 会引入 Citadel、Jump 等华尔街大型做市商为 Lighter 做市。（Vlad 之前被 Citadel CEO boss 直聘，工作多年）

资产类别逐一按照 CFTC 监管上线，保持 0 fee 的交易结构。

3、期权 Options 与 LighterEVM 什么时间上线？

目标都是 Q4 上线，但侧重在 Options ，因为技术原因，期权的上线会以二元期权，也就是预测市场为开始，随后升级为传统的欧式期权，同时期权考虑 0 fee 交易开始。

LighterEVM 也是预期 Q4，上线之后将会引入 BTC、HYPE、SOL 等非 EVM 资产现货，当然「股票现货 Spot」也在范围内，同时 LighterEVM 将会催生大量生态项目，例如我后面会发的 wick。

4、年底 12.30 的大额 unlock，团队怎么处理 investor 和 team 的巨量解锁？（这块我问的很直接）。

“investor 都不会卖！” Vlad 说这是他知道的信息。我再追问，你并不能控制他们手来让人家不卖吧， Vlad 意思是：他们说了不卖就是不卖，如果他们要卖的话，完全可以说出来，我们还能帮他们找 OTC 买家，甚至自己都可以买。二级市场直接砸的可能性不高，性价比低，同时也在消耗 VC 自己的信誉。

确实，桌上做的几个基金，都是想来谈 OTC 的。

5、Lighter 与 Robinhood 商业模式一样，要尽可能多获取散户流量，但团队在 Marketing 方面一直如此保守？

团队 Camila 告诉我，其实 Lighter 并不是没有做 MKT，而是一直在考虑 ROI 的问题，现在这个阶段，Lighter 牌照还没下来，而大规模、高质量的流量，只有在牌照之后才会出现。所以团队目前的 Marketing 投入不多，仅以欧美极个别 KOL、还有大的视频访谈为主。（我争取做一次）

Camila 还提到，Web3 贯以的 Agency 和 KOL 营销，她觉得性价比非常低，因此等牌照下来，会以 Web2 方式类似于 Kalshi/Polymarket/Robinhood 那样做营销。

加上 KOL 侧，主要集中在合约交易、PerpDEX的 KOL 为主，欧美、韩国、大中华等地区同时发力。

Marketing 是牌照下来之后，团队要侧重做的地方，因为他们也懂自己的盈利模式需要什么。

6、Vlad 你个人有投资 Cognition 吗？（Cognition 是 Vlad 上一个项目的合伙人 Scott wu 的企业 AI 项目，目前估值 500 亿美金）

Vlad 说，他是 Cognition 的第一个投资人，我说那很有钱了，恭喜。

饭局后，我和团队成员 Sebas 私下聊起，你觉得 Vlad 有没有当时后悔选择做了 Crypto 而没去做 AI，毕竟现在 LIT 代币总市值 40 亿不到，而 Cognition 还没上市就几百亿了。

Sebas 说绝不会，Vlad 同时喜欢 AI 和 Trade，从他之前在城堡证券工作过很多年、Robinhood 的第一个顾问就知道， Vlad 乐于构建交易系统，而 AI 那边，Vlad 个人投资了很多，这些 Vlad 自己也是很骄傲的。而现在好朋友的公司做的这么好，Vlad 更有动力将自己的公司做更好。

7、团队一直提倡的 100% 回购销毁代币，当然对持币者是好事，但公司会因此没有现金流，团队会怎么处理现金流问题？

Vlad 大方承认了这个问题，确实是，他的出发点一直都是 “Lighter 的所有收入权益归 LIT 代币持有者。”但也不得不考虑公司的长期经营问题，现在 team 花的钱都是之前 VC  给的。

长期来看，Lighter 可能会考虑从一些合作伙伴、渠道那里获得收益，Lighter 已经与新型合作伙伴达成协议，这些会在稍后公布。产品侧考虑后面的高级期权用户，同时回购销毁比例可能变为 99% or 98% 这种。（所有的都是设想，还未决定）

以上

就是我这次参加 Lighter 私局的记录，因个人英文水平没有那么 native，内容可能不那么精确，但大致意思趋同。
饭局上我感觉团队状态很好，他们对自己做的事非常有信心，Vlad 也经常自己开起玩笑，喝着茅台白酒，并没有屏幕上一直在正襟危坐很 nerd 的感觉。

稍后两天我会再着重撰写一篇 Lighter 和 Robinhood 相似商业模式的文章，大家敬请期待。

text:
AI Agent 最大的盲区之一，可能不是不会搜索，而是它查到的信息，未必还是现实世界的最新状态。

想象一下：一台机器人来到装卸区，发现现场布局已经变了，原来的地图和眼前的环境对不上。这时候，再多一条搜索结果，也没办法直接解决问题。

这也是 Vangrid (@vangrid_io) 让我感兴趣的地方。

1、AI 需要的不只是互联网数据，还有实时的空间信息。

网页和 API 能提供大量数字信息，但现实世界会持续变化。道路、建筑、装卸区和室内空间，都可能与过去记录的数据不一致。

Vangrid 的思路，是让真实世界中的参与者去采集特定地点的数据，再通过与具体位置绑定的 Bounty，把数据需求和能够完成采集的人连接起来。

简单说，不再只是等已有数据被发现，而是有人需要什么，就有机会针对那个地点去采集。

2、这个模式的关键，是把数据需求变成可执行的任务。

如果 AI Agent 或机器人需要某个位置的最新空间信息，就可以提出具体需求，由贡献者前往现场采集。

这让普通人的实地采集能力，有机会成为 AI 和机器人系统的数据来源。

团队背景也值得留意：CEO Robert Brighton 曾参与微软量子计算和 HoloLens 相关团队；CTO Khalid Benrafik 则拥有超过 14 年的分布式系统开发经验，曾在 https://t.co/rO0HsUnIGp、ING 和 Mollie 工作。Vangrid 也加入了 NVIDIA Inception 计划。

这些背景能提供一定参考，但真正决定产品价值的，还是技术能否落地。

3、从采集到机器人真正用上，中间还有不少关卡。

空间数据不是拍下来就能直接使用。

采集是否足够新、重建结果是否准确、不同来源的数据能否验证，以及最终能否接入机器人系统，都会影响实际效果。

如果这些环节能够打通，AI Agent 就有机会在需要时请求新的空间数据，而不是一直依赖可能已经过时的地图。

对我来说，Vangrid 最值得观察的，不只是它能不能收集现实世界的数据，而是能否建立一条可靠的数据供给链：从现场采集，到空间重建，再到 AI 和机器人真正使用。

AI Agent 可以理解数字世界，但要在物理世界里行动，就必须知道现场究竟发生了什么。

Vangrid 能不能成为两者之间可靠的桥梁，关键还得看真实场景中的数据质量和集成效果。

text:
Scale AI创始人，Meta首席AI官Alexandr Wang在聊马斯克、扎克伯格和拿破仑的共同点时，把一套顶级操盘手的心智模型说得极其透彻，
从两百年前的欧洲战场，到今天硅谷最激进的技术实验室，真正成大事的人竟然在用同一套心智模板，

真相非常反直觉，原来绝大多数人一辈子做不成大事，不是因为能力不够，而是被那种平均主义的避险思维生生拖垮了，

很多时候我们以为顶级统帅和今天的科技狂人靠的是某种神秘的天命。

但当Alex 把他们身上最坚硬的骨骼一层层剔出来的时候，你会发现他们几乎共享着同一套冷酷到极致的底层心智。

第一个被很多人轻视的常识，是马斯克用肉身证明过无数次的事实：
庞大的官僚层级除了制造沟通损耗，对突破边界没有任何帮助。

只要你手里有一支极小、技术密度极高、完全扁平且带着某种疯狂偏执的团队，执行的烈火就能在极短的时间里把一切所谓的行业壁垒烧穿。

更让我回味了很久的，是他讲到扎克伯格身上的那种风险观。

他在很早的时候就已经把对失败的恐惧彻底剥离掉了。

大部分人在日常里活得谨小慎微，生怕做错一步被惩罚，但他脑子里的算盘完全不一样：
失败是有物理上限的，亏完也就那么多；但赢的时候，回报是没有上限的。

所以最大的风险，从来不是冲出去犯了错，而是在一个每秒都在巨变的世界里，以为自己呆在原地就绝对安全。

原地不动，才是唯一注定沉船的宿命。

而拿破仑在两百年前留下的原则，给这套逻辑焊上了最后一颗铆钉：
犹豫永远是致命的。

做决定之前，要像学者一样极度冷静、从各个角度反复推敲推演，把棋盘的每一条生路和死路全部摸透；
可一旦确认自己踩在正确的路上，就要毫不犹豫地把弹夹全部打空。

慢慢想，快快干。

决定前把所有的退路算绝，决定后绝不在半山腰回头看一眼。

这种近乎暴烈的决断力，才是穿越漫长周期时，人身上最性感的品质！ https://t.co/5lblsTfFUb

text:
gmonad。从新加坡回来，把Open和这周几个@Monad真正值得看的update分享中文CT朋友们

Monad：一个足以承载全球资金的网络，主网一周年，Open上几个比较硬的更新：

1. 隐私结算功能（Private Settlement）：  
@category_xyz 在Open主舞台宣布的。Monad L1上直接做机密执行域，不用另起一条私有链。每个域通过L1上的标准EVM hub合约启用，不需要分叉也不需要协议升级。域内交易、状态、合约代码端到端加密，连L1本身都读不到；跨域转账也是加密的，地址和金额对外不可见。机构自己定验证者集合、信任模型、访问规则和管辖权，默认谁都看不到，审计或监管可以按需给权限。同时域还直接接到Monad的共享流动性，结算是原子的
现在还是设计方案，Category Labs在跟早期设计伙伴推进，还没上线。发布前有过“Privacy is coming”的预热。  
https://t.co/jDM67nqYDv  
https://t.co/wlb0R3sU7Y  

why matters：机构（银行、基金、交易台、企业财资）最怕的就是链上全透明。他们现在要么不上链，要么自己搞私有链把流动性切碎。这个设计如果跑通，等于让这些机构能直接用公开链的速度和流动性，同时业务还保密。对Monad来说，这是把大额资金和真实业务流程拉进来的关键入口，后面稳定币、RWA、支付的体量都有可能跟着放大

2. 股票上链，xStocks原生上Monad：
@valgui在台上宣布@xStocksFi 原生部署到Monad，覆盖1100+代币化美股和ETF。代币直接在Monad上铸造和结算，不是从别的链桥过来。1:1对应底层证券，ERC-20形态，可以往DEX、借贷、钱包里组合
这跟 @aave 之前提的V4代币化股票hub提案也能对上。链上后续也有合约部署和铸造的讨论  
https://t.co/dO3Bzok7O8  

why matters：股票类资产是全球最大的流动性池之一。原生上链意味着不用桥，可以直接在Monad做交易、抵押、组合。对交易者来说多了24/7的股票敞口，对DeFi协议来说多了新的抵押品和交易对，对持有美股的人来说多了链上使用场景。如果流动性慢慢起来，Monad的交易量和TVL都有机会从纯crypto资产往传统资产延伸，可以关心Monad上几个DEX的进展@perpltrade @hellotradeapp @KuruExchange 等还有几个还没宣发的

3. Cadence共识，提升性能并解决MEV： 
@_jhunsaker现场demo了Cadence。这是多并发提议者共识，多个验证者同时提议，配合极端流水线。现在Monad主网是300ms出块、600ms最终性，升级完成后目标100ms出块、300ms最终性，再配上BTX加密mempool，从协议层压MEV
https://t.co/GLULPvHZHe  

why matters：做市商和高频交易最在意的是延迟和被夹。100ms出块加上协议层压MEV，等于让链上交易体验更接近中心化交易所，同时减少被三明治的损失。对普通交易者和DeFi用户来说，滑点和被夹的成本会下降；对专业交易团队来说，更愿意把订单流放上来。后面如果真落地，交易量和做市深度有机会继续涨，CT里也会有更多人讨论“链上交易是不是开始能打CEX了”

4. StraitsX x Monad 新元稳定币：
XSGD和XUSD计划2027年初原生发行到Monad，XSGD会是链上第一条原生新加坡元稳定币，还受技术、监管和合规条件约束。双方也在看卡项目、支付和跨境结算这些场景。StraitsX是Open的title sponsor，持有新加坡大额支付机构牌照，累计稳定币交易量接近700亿。  
https://t.co/KTv4Q24Cly  

why matters：稳定币是链上真正的支付和结算入口。原生发行加上受监管牌照，意味着后面卡、跨境、商户结算这些场景可以更顺地接进来，而不是只停留在DeFi套利。对亚太用户和支付公司来说，多了一条合规的链上通道；对Monad来说，稳定币存量和使用量起来后，整条链的日常活跃和费用都会受益。后面如果卡和支付真落地，用户增长会从纯crypto圈子往更广的支付用户延伸

5. Open台上也拉了Visa、ETH Foundation、Dragonfly、Tether、Zero Hash等。主舞台之外还有DeltaV Demo Day，项目直接对VC路演。Metropolis黑客松也还在进行，奖金25万+，提交截止10/13  

链上数据目前DeFi TVL大概10亿，排名第十，钱包400多万，累计交易8亿多，DEX成交量累计330亿左右，应用170+
https://t.co/fS6gyQQkd5

why matters：这些数据说明主网已经有真实使用，不是纯叙事。机构方和头部协议持续进来，加上黑客松和Demo Day，开发者和项目方还会继续进场，这些都会直接反映在链上活跃和资产规模上

text:
All of this is so true, and honestly a sad reality of the Indian startup ecosystem.

I’ve supported and worked with so many founders coming out of India. A lot of them struggle to raise enough capital here and eventually end up moving to the US because the incentives are simply much stronger.

It’s similar on the job side too. Either you’re underpaid, or if you are paid well, the expectation is often that work becomes your entire life.

We have incredible talent in India. The incentives just haven’t caught up yet.
author: muskan_kalra24
quoted_text:
The smartest Indians continue to come to build in the US for the simple reason that the economic incentives are far far better.

Perplexity ($20B), Skild ($14B+), Baseten ($13B), Together ($8B), Glean ($8B), Modal ($5B), Rubrik ($25B), Harness ($5B), Blacksmith, Parallel, Greptile, CodeRabbit, Composio, Distyl ($2B), Resolve, Luma, Cartesia, Wispr, dMatrix, Arize and many more - all started by at least one Indian-born founder.

The US is a far easier to raise capital in with far less dilution. Most Indian companies are switching where they're domiciled to get access to the US capital markets. Every single Indian venture firm is trying very hard to invest in the US or risk not participating in the AI race (ironically, the management fees of venture firms are so high in India relatively that this is the one group that net of carry actually has incentive to be in India because they take home well north of a living wage whether or not funds perform do)

While Zomato ($35B now, $8B at IPO) might be the biggest outcome in Indian venture, Cursor ($60B), Reflection (potentially $20B+), World Labs ($8B), OpenRouter ($8B), HuggingFace ($12B) and of course the $1T+ big labs quickly make those outcomes seem small and happen on a much smaller time scale, with much higher IRR.

Engineers at these startups regularly get paid $1M/yr, and make $10M+ on exit. Even in BigTech, it is trivial to pull up levels fyi and see that if you're L6/L7+ with ~10 years of experience, you're making $1M/yr there too. And of course, we all know the slew of Indian CEOs of companies here, not to mention a huge bench of lesser known executives across the board in public and private companies.

I say all this because every time there is a slight immigration hiccup in the US, I hear the online pleas to "build in India", I struggle to understand why most engineers, academics or founders would do that net of desire to be close to family, failure to obtain visa and devout patriotism.

This is not a superiority thing or a US v India thing. The economic incentives at least for technologists to being in the US outweigh India by at least an order of magnitude.

We were able to fine tune an open weight model (Qwen3.5-9B) on proprietary internal data at @coinbase, and it out performed frontier models, at much lower cost and speed, for a specialized task (fraud prevention in this case).

I think we'll see more of this pattern inside companies. The frontier models are amazing generalists. But increasingly you'll see specialist models out perform on more narrow tasks, either working on teams, or by themselves.

We're making it easy to fine tune models internally for our employees. We even have a skill for it in our internal harness that makes it easy to spin these up and start training them:

I imagine we'll have some backend services that could be replaced entirely by this new architecture.

AI 狂欢要戛然而止了？十大见顶信号已触发四个：

1. 全靠讲故事，实利跟不上
股价涨全靠大家凭空给高估值，不看实打实的利润，涨得越高越怕加息高利率。

2. 赚钱跟不上花钱，大饼画到多年后
AI 收入全靠还没签合同的远期需求，买设备烧钱的速度远快于进账，以后折旧和还钱压力山大。

3. 业绩超预期，股价反而暴跌
财报明明挺好股价却跌了，说明好消息早就被吃干抹净，市场涨不动了。本周看ASML、台积电表现。

4. 只有几个巨头在撑场面
指数看着在涨，其实全靠一两个超级大块头拉动，大部分普通股票根本没怎么涨，甚至在悄悄走下坡路。

5. 大机构开始偷溜了，已现苗头 ⚠️：
德银把科技股降级，仓位开始向金融等落后板块转移，历史经验表明，这种急涨后极易出现倒V暴跌。

6. 边缘小弟市场先崩了，已现苗头 ⚠️：
韩国股市等AI小弟市场成交量暴跌70%，外资疯狂跑路；通常小弟先撑不住，大哥美股随后就见顶。

7. 公司和大股东急着高位套现，已现苗头 ⚠️：
各种AI公司抢着IPO、增发、大宗交易抽钱。公司高管最懂行情，他们疯狂卖，你千万别盲目接盘。

8. 借钱烧钱被警惕，大银行开始泼冷水，已现苗头 ⚠️：
星展银行警告AI基建借债风险太高。靠借钱维持的狂欢，最怕高利率夹击。

9. 剧烈上跳下窜，利好落地变成出货日
股价开始暴涨暴跌，出利好消息时大家不买账，反而成了大资金拉高出货的绝佳时机。

10. 全网只剩同一个信仰
整场行情全靠少数几家巨头承诺继续砸钱买设备撑着，只要有一家稍微下调下季度预期，整个板块就会闪崩。

绝对不加杠杆，留足现金，等趋势明确再右侧入场。

text:
Dusting off this tweet from April because this gap in shared understanding of LLM capability is *widening*. It's now less "two groups of people speaking past each other" and more a sharp funnel.

- Napkin math somewhere around 6B people (~75% of the population) have barely come in contact with LLMs at all.
- Around 1-2B (~20%) are casual and infrequent users of free-tier ChatGPT-like products. This group sees derpy chatbots and treats them a bit like a better Google search, a writing aid, or etc. Maybe an agent tries to book you a flight. I have non-tech friends who (reasonably, imo) say they have not much use for it at all. Even many professionals outside of math&code are in this tier. For example, execs and many other functions spend a lot of their time talking to other people, so while they understand what is happening intellectually, it is still second-hand and a bit abstract.
- Now we get to professional use of frontier-grade LLMs in math&code. Somewhere around 20M people (0.2%) see first-hand that large, complex projects that used to take them weeks/months can now be completed by agents with a prompt. Building apps, copying apps, translating apps, decompiling apps from binaries... This has all happened very quickly and recently - less than 1 year ago, I was writing code manually by hand, typing memorized computer code commands into a code editor character by character, occasionally pressing Tab to autocomplete a little chunk of code.
- And finally we get to the ~5,000 people (~0.00006%) with access to frontier-grade systems internally. The external world has seen the preview. It looks like swarms of thousands of agents collaborating over weeks on software mega projects: minting zero days, running cyber attacks and defenses at machine speeds, discovering new science, advancing the frontier of mathematics. Things that would have taken top professionals in the industry years of work. Meanwhile, human review and comprehension are starting to fall behind. For example, people are still involved in the "archeology" of the OpenAI-HF incident from many months ago. Mathematicians may be poring over the 722 manuscripts on frontier mathematics for a while.

The funnel is driven by a combination of factors:
1. The impact scales with ambition, problem size, and horizon. A question with a paragraph answer barely stresses the system. You need a reservoir of big, difficult problems that you really care about. This aspect drives the consumer / professional dimension of the funnel.
2. The jaggedness of the system (which I have written about a lot separately). Capability peaks in domains that are digital, verifiable and economically valuable. This is because LLM capability emerges from reinforcement learning on verifiable rewards on a curated environment mixture driven by revenue potential. This aspect primarily drives the area (e.g. math&code) dimension of the funnel.
3. Access. Free-tier, paid-tier, internal.

So this is the weirdness of the moment. The general public has mostly not interacted with these systems. When they have, it looks like a derpy chatbot. The majority of professionals still see only a modest uplift. And a small sliver of professionals are experiencing the vertigo of the curve going vertical. And it is all happening at the same time.
author: triketora
quoted_text:
Judging by my tl there is a growing gap in understanding of AI capability.

The first issue I think is around recency and tier of use. I think a lot of people tried the free tier of ChatGPT somewhere  last year and allowed it to inform their views on AI a little too much. This is a group of reactions laughing at various quirks of the models, hallucinations, etc. Yes I also saw the viral videos of OpenAI's Advanced Voice mode fumbling simple queries like "should I drive or walk to the carwash". The thing is that these free and old/deprecated models don't reflect the capability in the latest round of state of the art agentic models of this year, especially OpenAI Codex and Claude Code.

But that brings me to the second issue. Even if people paid $200/month to use the state of the art models, a lot of the capabilities are relatively "peaky" in highly technical areas. Typical queries around search, writing, advice, etc. are *not* the domain that has made the most noticeable and dramatic strides in capability. Partly,  this is due to the technical details of reinforcement learning and its use of verifiable rewards. But partly, it's also because these use cases are not sufficiently prioritized by the companies in their hillclimbing because they don't lead to as much $$$ value. The goldmines are elsewhere, and the focus comes along.

So that brings me to the second group of people, who *both* 1) pay for and use the state of the art frontier agentic models (OpenAI Codex / Claude Code) and 2) do so professionally in technical domains like programming, math and research. This group of people is subject to the highest amount of "AI Psychosis" because the recent improvements in these domains as of this year have been nothing short of staggering. When you hand a computer terminal to one of these models, you can now watch them melt programming problems that you'd normally expect to take days/weeks of work. It's this second group of people that assigns a much greater gravity to the capabilities, their slope, and various cyber-related repercussions.

TLDR the people in these two groups are speaking past each other. It really is simultaneously the case that OpenAI's free and I think slightly orphaned (?) "Advanced Voice Mode" will fumble the dumbest questions in your Instagram's reels and *at the same time*, OpenAI's highest-tier and paid Codex model will go off for 1 hour to coherently restructure an entire code base, or find and exploit vulnerabilities in computer systems. This part really works and has made dramatic strides because 2 properties: 1) these domains offer explicit reward functions that are verifiable meaning they are easily amenable to reinforcement learning training (e.g. unit tests passed yes or no, in contrast to writing, which is much harder to explicitly judge),  but also 2) they are a lot more valuable in b2b settings, meaning that the biggest fraction of the team is focused on improving them. So here we are.

text:
It's sad seeing @monad and @megaeth become background noise this fast

A year ago, these were two of the most hyped bets on the future of the EVM

- @megaeth’s public sale had $1.39B in demand for only ~$50M offered
- @monad raised $269M from more than 85K participants

Both were selling a similar dream: make the EVM insanely fast

And they actually delivered a lot of it
- @monad can handle up to 10K TPS with 300ms blocks
- @megaeth delivered ~10ms mini-blocks and reached tens of thousands of TPS in testing

But almost nobody is using anywhere close to that capacity

In August, @monad averaged only ~51 TPS & @megaeth was around 25 TPS

They spent years solving the speed problem, then launched into a market where speed wasn’t really the bottleneck
- @megaeth probably shows this best
TVL fell from a ~$245M peak in May to around $22M by the end of September
- @monad looks healthier with over $1B TVL, but nearly 90% of that sits in lending protocols, while @aave came with $15M of first-year incentives

So the real test is still simple:
What stays when the incentives stop?

They were debating which one would become the next big chain year ago. Now both barely get mentioned

Maybe the hard part is getting people to actually care was than just get the people

text:
My Thoughts on $CLAUDIA, $JEANPHIL, and AI-Native Virtual IP

I believe AI-native virtual IP is emerging as a new industry, although it has not yet become a clearly defined, mature industry with established business models. More accurately, it is an emerging sector at the intersection of AI technology, entertainment IP, virtual idols, digital humans, short-form video, and fan economics.

The key distinction is whether AI is simply a tool used to create IP, or the underlying production model through which that IP is created and operated from the very beginning.

Traditional virtual IP is nothing new. Virtual idols, anime characters, game characters, and virtual influencers have existed for years. The real change is that AI is significantly lowering the cost of character creation, music production, video generation, and ongoing operations, while giving characters new opportunities to interact continuously with their audiences. Deloitte, a media and entertainment industry research firm, has also identified the integration of generative AI into everyday creative workflows and the rise of AI musicians and virtual influencers as trends worth watching.

So why do I believe this is becoming a new sector?

There are three developments worth paying attention to.

1. Character production is shifting from project-based creation to continuous operation.

In the past, building a virtual character typically required teams specializing in modeling, animation, screenwriting, voice acting, and operations. AI is lowering the costs across these areas, giving individual creators the opportunity to continuously produce music, videos, stories, and social media content around the same character.

In 2026, Japan's Dentsu launched CHARAMO, an AI-driven IP growth platform covering character development, social media content, character chat, podcasts, and merchandise. This shows that the industry is beginning to explore how AI can be used to operate characters continuously, rather than simply generate individual pieces of content.

2. Characters have the potential to evolve from content people watch into interactive digital personalities.

The difference between traditional virtual IP and AI-native virtual IP is becoming increasingly clear.

Traditional virtual IP: Characters are designed by teams and reach fans through animation, comics, games, performances, and other forms of content. Interaction and content updates generally depend on the production team.

AI-native virtual IP: Characters can continuously generate different forms of content and maintain relationships with users through conversations, personalized responses, and community interactions. They have the potential to evolve from protagonists in individual pieces of content into digital personalities that can be operated over the long term.

There are already concrete commercial experiments in this direction. For example, in 2026, WEBTOON partnered with Genies, with plans to turn comic characters into interactive digital avatars, exploring new fan experiences and monetization opportunities for creators.

3. The barriers to producing and operating IP may both decline.

In the past, whether a character could become a commercially valuable IP depended heavily on the production resources behind it. AI gives more creators the opportunity to develop characters, but it also means that the supply of content will grow rapidly.

Ultimately, the competitive advantage may shift from who can produce content to who can create characters that people remember and continuously build their influence over time.

AI lowers the barrier to producing characters, not the barrier to building a successful IP.

Applying this idea to projects such as CLAUDIA and JEANPHIL, we can view them as early experiments in this emerging sector. Creators use AI to produce content continuously, build attention around a consistent character, and then attempt to develop that character into an independent entertainment IP.

However, two layers need to be distinguished:

At the IP level: Can the character develop a stable audience, a coherent body of content, and cultural influence?
At the token level: Can that influence generate sustained demand for the token and a clear mechanism for value capture?

Success at the first level does not guarantee success at the second. A character can become a popular virtual IP while its associated memecoin still lacks a sustainable economic mechanism.

My conclusion is that AI-native virtual IP is an emerging industry worth paying attention to. But the long-term opportunity is not about how many videos AI can generate. It is about whether AI enables more people to create virtual characters that attract sustained attention, independently expand their own content worlds, and eventually become commercially valuable IPs—and whether the associated tokens can capture some of that value.

Let's talk about $JEANPHIL and $CLAUDIA, and why I'm bullish on the AI Influencer + short-form video narrative.

GTBxUiw6wJdmmkCGZgRHLyYxqu1vG4KtRpeox6yDpump 
2j5SaS7xy776qCBpyPQbZjyQSAtKiFgrwjfErthnW2ZM 

First, the broader sector.

I believe AI Influencers combined with short-form video distribution could become one of the narratives worth watching in the next Meme market cycle.

The underlying logic is simple: AI is turning character creation from a high-cost, low-frequency process into a low-cost, scalable content business that can be operated continuously. In the past, building an influencer required appearance, performance, filming, editing, and long-term management. Now, creators can use AI to design characters, develop personalities, produce short videos, and even operate multiple virtual personas simultaneously.

But what really matters isn't how many characters AI can generate. It's whether those characters can consistently produce content that people want to watch, discuss, and follow.

Short-form video drives distribution, characters accumulate attention, and Memes can become a speculative vehicle for that attention in the crypto market. An AI character can build a distinctive persona through continuous video releases, participate in trending topics, create new memes, and interact with other characters, gradually evolving from a single viral clip into a recognizable IP.

Compared with traditional Memes that rely on an isolated event or a single image, these characters theoretically have the ability to continuously generate new material for distribution. If a character develops a stable audience and cultural recognition, it no longer has to rely entirely on a single viral moment to maintain attention.

If this model gains traction in the crypto market, speculation may shift beyond the next viral image toward AI characters that have already attracted genuine attention on platforms like TikTok and Instagram, can consistently produce content, and have the potential to channel that external attention on-chain.

This is why I've chosen to take a deeper look at JEANPHIL and CLAUDIA. They represent two different paths within this emerging narrative.

JEANPHIL: External traction that has already emerged.

Jean Phil is an AI-generated French male character. His blond bowl cut, curled mustache, brown houndstooth suit, and signature street-style boxing moves create a recognizable visual identity that is easy to imitate.

The character has attracted significant attention on TikTok and Instagram, generating imitations and derivative content. This demonstrates how an AI character with a distinctive persona and a simple, replicable video format can quickly capture attention on mainstream social platforms.

The logic is straightforward: the character attracts external traffic, the content inspires imitations and remixes, and that attention may eventually flow into its on-chain token.

Compared with Memes that rely solely on narratives originating within crypto, JEANPHIL already has an external source of attention. What it needs to prove next is whether that momentum can persist and whether the character's popularity can translate into sustained token demand.

CLAUDIA: From AI creation toward long-term IP development.

CLAUDIA is more focused on long-term IP development. Around Claudia, anabology has been building Claudia Gallery and proposed creating an open version of Hatsune Miku for the AI era. Related initiatives also include AI character creation tools, Agent Skills, and Claudia Local.

The Influencer mode brings this vision closer to the AI Influencer model: by continuously producing videos, maintaining a consistent character identity, and experimenting with high-frequency publishing, it aims to gradually build its own audience.

The logic is that AI lowers content production costs, continuous video output helps establish character recognition, and the character gradually accumulates an audience before attempting to convert that external attention into IP influence and on-chain interest.

Compared with JEANPHIL, CLAUDIA has greater potential in the direction of a long-term AI creator ecosystem. The goal isn't simply to make a character go viral in the short term, but to explore how an AI character can continuously produce content, build an audience, and develop into an expandable, open IP.

However, this path has a longer chain of validation. Being able to produce videos consistently doesn't mean the content will necessarily gain traction. Having creation tools doesn't guarantee the ability to build a successful character. And an open-IP vision doesn't automatically mean the token can capture the resulting value.

Although both projects fall under the broader AI Influencer narrative, their trading theses are different.

JEANPHIL is more focused on existing external traction. The key question is whether that attention can persist and translate into token demand. CLAUDIA is more focused on AI creation capabilities and long-term IP development. The key question is whether it can consistently produce compelling content and build a genuine audience.

What I'm bullish on is the shared potential behind both approaches: AI characters could evolve beyond static images into dynamic IPs that continuously produce content, participate in trending topics, build social relationships, and generate new Memes.

Of course, a compelling sector narrative doesn't mean every related token will appreciate.

We need to distinguish three separate outcomes: an AI character gaining attention, an IP building lasting influence, and a token capturing value from that influence. A character can become popular without benefiting its token. A project can have impressive creation tools without producing viral content. Even if an IP continues to grow, attention may remain entirely off-chain if the token has no meaningful connection to its development.

Therefore, what I'm really looking for isn't the first token to announce that it uses AI, but projects that have demonstrated their ability to attract external attention, consistently produce distributable content, and establish a clear connection between that attention and their tokens.

AI is the production tool, short-form video is the distribution channel, character IP is the vehicle for attention, and the token represents a separate speculative market.

When these four elements become genuinely connected, AI Influencers could evolve from a trending concept into a new Meme narrative with sustained distribution potential.

In my view, the projects most likely to break out will need a distinctive character identity, consistent content distribution, a genuine external audience, and a mechanism for translating attention into token demand. That's why I'm bullish on this direction and have chosen to take a deeper look at JEANPHIL and CLAUDIA.

text:
Your cloud agent can book a restaurant but can't touch your 3D printer.

The missing primitive in personal AI isn't a smarter model. It's a wire between machines.

Yobiru by @turingou is the cleanest attempt I've seen: agents messaging agents over Tailscale.

A short thread on why this pattern matters
author: howard_
quoted_text:
前几天写的那个让不同 agent 互相聊天的小脚本，现在整理成了一个开源项目：Yobiru（ヨビル，日语“叫醒”的意思）。

现在的 agent，包括各种 personal agent，基本都只有一台云端电脑。它能自动处理很多事，但碰不到你家里的家电，也连不上只有局域网才能访问的设备。比如我想让 Grokbot 控制家里的 3D 打印机，没有这个工具是做不到的。

Yobiru 做的事情很简单：只要机器都连在 Tailscale 上，Grokbot、我家里 Mac 上的 Codex、东京服务器上的 Claude Code 就可以直接互相发消息、传文件。家里的设备不用暴露到公网，安全上也更放心。

更重要的是，每台机器上的 agent 都有常驻进程。消息一到，就能把对方叫醒，给它指派任务，它再自己去派发新的子任务。也就是说，你可以用自己最习惯的、手机上常用的那个 agent，去指挥其他所有 agent，而且是真的让它们去干活，不只是聊天。

我现在的实际用法：
1. Grokbot 让家里的 Codex 去控制 3D 打印机
2. Grokbot 每天整理我的 X 书签，整理好交给东京的开发工作站，直接拿来做产品；同时也给家里的 Codex 发一份，万一要用到家里电脑上的 3D 设计软件
3. 微信没有开放接口，云端的 agent 碰不到。现在我让 Grokbot 订好餐厅、把菜单翻译成中文，再交给家里的 Codex，由它直接操作 Mac 上的微信发给朋友。发出去之前，Codex 会先等我确认
4. Grokbot 每天检查喂食器里还有没有猫粮，查询本身由家里的 Codex 在局域网里完成，如果缺货了，就告诉 Grokbot（我的杂货管家），在我的云端电脑里面自动下单

几个关键设计：没有中心服务器；消息只带文件的下载地址和 sha256，由收件方自己去拉；要不要被叫醒、能叫醒谁，由收件方决定，还可以 @ 到具体某一个 bot。

quoted_text:
这次 Ledger 通过授权经销商渠道被植入芯片的事件，其实和前段时间《区块链一百人》跟OneKey创始人王一石 @ohyishi 老板聊到的一些判断，有不少可以对照的地方

他当时其实就提到，如今的攻击趋势已经在发生转变。

以前更多是打合约漏洞、闪电贷、预言机这些技术点，但随着审计和形式化验证越来越成熟，单纯从代码层面找突破口的难度和成本都在上升，攻击者开始更多转向“人”以及上游的供应链和工具链。

正如这次马来西亚授权经销商 CryptoBilis 的情况，正是发生在供应链的经销商环节：设备本身的安全芯片没有被破解，正品检测也能通过，但在发出去之前被拆开植入了芯片，直接把助记词传出去。

问题不在产品核心的安全芯片，而在整条从工厂到用户的链路。

而且聊的时候他也把之前 Ledger 的一个技术型漏洞讲得很清楚

当时 OneKey 的 Anzen Labs 团队在实验室复现了旧版以太坊 App 的一个 TOCTOU（检查时到使用时）问题——用户在屏幕上看到的是一笔正常交易，实际签出去的却是被替换的交易。

同时他也提到 Ledger 至今不开源，一个产品让人“相信”它安全，和让人有能力去“验证”它是否安全，长期来看会有差别。

我感觉恰恰印证了行业里这种模块化、积木式的搭建方式带来的风险。

以 Bybit 那次 15 亿美金被盗为例，多签合约、冷钱包、Ledger 硬件本身单独看都没有明显问题，真正出事的是前端工程师被社工后植入的恶意代码，再叠加盲签。

每个环节看起来都还行，但拼在一起后，人的环节、第三方环节或供应链环节一旦出现问题，整个系统就会暴露。

硬件钱包也类似，安全芯片再强，从生产、运输、经销到芯片和屏幕之间那“最后一厘米”的数据传输，都可能成为被攻击的点。

所以当时采访的时候一石就说了：
“你的城堡是固若金汤的，然后你保安在外面溜达，身上带着钥匙。人家过来说「大哥来根烟」，你抽了跟烟，回头人家把你钥匙偷走了。就是这种感觉”

结合Ledger钱包出现这样严重的公关问题，完全是超级形象且准确的哈哈哈哈

text:
Arc @arc day 25 

目前 TVL 差不多稳在 $563m 左右，这几天大盘一直在窄幅横盘。链上其实没啥大变化，24h app fees 基本上在 $110k–$140k 晃悠，DEX 日成交量也就在 $30m 上下。

资金流向还是老样子，差不多 90% 的 USDC 都在 lending 里面，Morpho Blue 独大，#Aave V4 跟着喝汤。游资大部分时间还是在大户和头部几个协议之间倒腾，暂时没看到什么破圈的新资金进来。

Solon 算是有些创新 的pad，尤其是昨天的trade terminal 更新的效果不错，很流畅，团队审美在线

SolonPad（@Solonlabs1）算是第一个目前 Arc 上把 trading fees 跟真实股票（NVDA 1:1 reserve）绑得比较深的 launchpad 了，背后是靠 AI agent AXON 全天候跑。

最近更新几个点：

AXON panel 已经上线了，链上能直接审计 agent 幹了啥，timelock 和操作日志全公开，每一步都有迹可循。

SolonLend 出了：Arc 第一个股票抵押借贷（走 Morpho 的），拿 NVDA.sol 当抵押借 USDC，LLTV 卡在 62.5%。
V3.1 在跑，费用分成这块该给 staker 的股票奖励、buyback & burn 都在走。
Trading Terminal 跟 agent skill（已经到 v1.5）一直在迭代。

说实话，这算目前 Arc 上把「USDC + 真实资产 + agent」这套叙事跑得比较像样的了。

其他一些热点项目近况

$ARGUS（@Arguspad）：mc 稳在 $11m–$13m 左右。老牌 launchpad，流动性最厚，税跟回购逻辑也最清晰。龙头地位目前没人撼得动，但盘子大点，追高还是得防回调。

$ARCMAN：mc 差不多 $11m–$12m。天天跟 Argus 争第一，但低流通（low float）这事儿被群里吐槽好几次了，实际成交量跟社群活跃度经常对不上市值。

$ARCOON：mc 在 $9.5m 附近。也是 low float 盘子，价格挺黏糊的，就是平时成交量有点偏薄。

$PP（Peach People）：mc 约 $4.8m–$4.9m。纯情绪和社区盘，热度还可以，在同档期 meme 里算稳的。

$TOLLY（@TollyLabs）：mc 约 $2.1m–$2.4m。第二梯队的主力，跟 Argus 抢 launchpad 份额，后续主要看产品和收费能力。

$FAZE（@fazedotfun）：mc 约 $2.3m–$2.6m。v4-native launchpad + terminal 叙事，前阵子反弹过，但池子深度还是比不过头部。

$COOL（@usdciscool）：mc 约 $1.2m–$1.5m。USDC 主题的 meme，持有人挺分散的，波动大。

$AF（Arcflow）：mc 在 $1.1m–$1.6m 晃悠。多空博弈挺激烈的，偶尔单日放量能冲一下。

$ASTOCK（@TryArcStocks）：mc 大概 $570k。也是做美股叙事的，跟 Solon 重合度高，但体量和成熟度差了一截。

$FUCI（@fucidotfamily）：mc 只有 $70k–$80k，池子很薄。主打 agent 自己拿 USDC 钱包、x402 按次付费。这种看的是实际调用和分红，不是纯讲故事。

$UBI（@UBIdotFUN）：比较边缘的早期 pad，社区粘性高，目前交易量缩到最小，正在选择方向。

其实 Arc 的底层逻辑没变：gas 用 USDC、验证者基本是机构、大部分 TVL 全被借贷吃干抹净。launchpad 这块除了极少数，其他基本都是小打小闹。

有协议收入、回购机制硬挺的（比如 $Argus）适合拿得住一点；像 Solon 这种走 RWA + AI 的可以当成差异化标的盯着。

至于那些低流通大市值（$ARCMAN、$ARCOON 这类）或者浅池实验盘，懂的都懂，纯粹当波段玩玩就行。能跑出真实 USDC 收入或者有硬资产撑腰的，可以多点耐心。

传统美股每周只开市 32.5 个小时，但互联网和加密世界是 7×24 小时（168 小时）在运转。

长期以来，链上美股都只是纳斯达克的“影子”——看预言机脸色定价的 Price Taker。

但 @Natan_benish 聊到了一个真正的范式转移： 链上美股正在反向主导价格发现（Price Discovery），变成 Price Maker。

为什么这个判断不可忽视？

1. 时间真空的定价权：周末突发技术突破、地缘黑天鹅或财报前瞻，传统交易所大门紧闭，全球唯一能即时交易承接情绪的只有链上。

text:
One structural problem in DeFi is that access to financial tools has improved faster than the way risk and capital efficiency are managed.

Many protocols still focus on attracting liquidity and generating headline yields, while the harder question is whether those returns come from sustainable strategies and transparent risk management.

That is the perspective I find worth exploring with @zerufinance . The important shift is not simply chasing higher yields, but building structured financial products that make onchain capital more purposeful.

It is not just about maximizing returns, but understanding the strategy behind them. Not just putting assets to work, but considering how risk, execution, and capital allocation fit together.

For DeFi to mature, financial products need more than attractive numbers. They need clear mechanisms, disciplined risk frameworks, and incentives that reward sustainable participation.

The next phase of onchain finance will depend on whether protocols can turn these principles into systems that remain useful beyond short-term market cycles.

text:
you saw an AI-generated scene you couldn’t stop watching. 

what if you could buy the work, along with a verifiable record of how it was created?

the internet is filling up with AI-generated content.

and there is a reason for it.

AI unlocks dreamlike possibilities when you create characters and build scenes around them.

> a city floating inside a sleeping giant.
> a character walking through different versions of their childhood.
> an entire universe built around an emotion.
> things you could imagine but couldn’t easily produce before.
> now some of these generations are difficult to replicate.

sometimes you need the exact prompt.

sometimes even the exact prompt won’t give you the same output.

because the result can also depend on the model version, seed, settings, reference inputs, and the workflow behind it.

the prompt is only part of the creative process.

the artist still experiments, selects, rejects, edits, and connects the outputs into something people want to watch.

and when a generation attracts attention or becomes useful to someone else, there could be a market for it.

> a game developer might want the character.
> a musician might want the visual.
> a brand might want to license the scene.
> a collector might want a particular edition.

so artists should have ways to sell their work, license its use, or share the generation recipe under clearly defined terms.

this is where ERC-7007 gets interesting.
it is called the Verifiable AI-Generated Content Token standard.

it extends NFTs with a way to connect an AI-generated output to its input and verify that relationship against a specified model.

the NFT can reference the content and its generation metadata.

the verification system checks the computation behind it.

there are two approaches.

zkML uses a cryptographic proof to verify that the supported computation produced the output.

opML uses an optimistic process where a submitted result can be challenged before it becomes final.

both require actual verification infrastructure around the model. uploading an image and adding “AI-generated” to its metadata isn’t enough.

imagine an artist releasing a collection through a defined model.

each piece comes with its generation input, a reference to the output, and verification that connects them.

a buyer can inspect the provenance instead of relying only on the seller’s claim.

the artist could separately offer a commercial licence, a workflow package, or access to the model where they have the right to provide it.

those are different products.

buying the NFT doesn’t automatically give someone copyright, model weights, or permission to use the character in a movie.

the terms need to say what the buyer actually receives.

and verification has a boundary too.

if the artist edits the output afterward, a proof of the original generation doesn’t automatically verify every edit in the finished scene.

but that still leaves a useful foundation.

a marketplace where artists can sell distinctive AI works with clearer provenance, and buyers can understand what they are collecting or licensing.

the file can still be copied.

the collectible edition, documented generation history, and licence give people specific reasons to buy.

ERC-7007 doesn’t make every generation valuable.

it gives creators a way to support the provenance of the ones people already care about.

text:
I view $HOOKR current rally as a market reassessment of its ecosystem value.

0x18e674231a58c239dc7daedcffe15ec3a24cff5c 

That's because it is evolving from a token launch tool into composable trading infrastructure on Robinhood Chain, powered by Uniswap v4 Hooks.

Unlike memecoins that rely purely on hype, HOOKR has a usable product, on-chain liquidity pools, and a protocol fee mechanism. But that also raises the key question: has the growth in product capabilities translated into sufficient real usage and sustainable buying pressure for the token?

Let’s break down the catalysts.

The first catalyst is the expansion from a launch tool into infrastructure.

Hookr’s latest version is no longer just a launchpad where each token is tied to a single Hook. It is beginning to break Hooks into composable modules that different projects can select, customize, and integrate.

Available modules include dynamic fees, Anti-Snipe, automatic burns, LP rewards, and arbitrage value recapture. Creators can combine these rules to build pools for new or existing tokens, and the rules are fixed once a pool is created rather than being freely modifiable afterward. A single token can also have up to eight trading pools with different quote assets.

This means Hookr is trying to solve more than just token issuance. It wants to make trading pools programmable through customizable trading rules. For developers, this modular design can reduce duplicated development work. For the broader ecosystem, Hookr has the potential to become infrastructure that other projects can directly use to build trading products.

The second catalyst is the shift from conceptual integrations to concrete ecosystem collaborations.

Hookr’s latest version supports different quote assets, including ETH, stablecoins, HOOKR, and tokenized stocks. It also provides an SDK and a public module directory, allowing other applications to integrate trading, quoting, and pool creation functionality.

More importantly, Hookr pools can now be routed through Uniswap’s own interface and API. The project no longer has to rely entirely on users visiting hookrfun directly; it has an opportunity to attract activity through external trading interfaces. The team also claims that the new version reduces gas costs for trading by approximately 47%–70% and lowers token launch costs by around 40%. If these improvements hold up in real-world usage, Hookr could attract developers through a better product experience rather than relying solely on incentives.

Recent project updates have also mentioned several integrations. Saffron is integrating fixed-yield vaults; ZEALZ plans to launch zZEC pools with low base fees and LP rewards; rhook can replay real trading histories to compare different trading rules; hooddomains is bringing domains into the creator and trading pool experience; an OpenAI-related project plans to launch tokens with custom rules on Hookr; and Longbow Lend is exploring the use of Hookr pools for liquidations and collateral swaps.

These integrations serve different purposes. Some could increase the number of trading pools, others improve developer tooling, while some aim to connect Hookr with lending, yield, and trading applications. If they actually launch and generate sustained trading activity, HOOKR’s demand thesis could expand beyond token launches into broader ecosystem usage.

However, it is essential to distinguish between an announced integration, a live integration, and one generating meaningful trading volume. A list of partnerships alone does not prove that protocol revenue is growing.

The third catalyst is a clearer mechanism for token value capture.

HOOKR’s value proposition is not simply that all trading fees are used for buybacks. In the latest version, base LP fees go entirely to liquidity providers. The protocol primarily earns a share of revenue from additional mechanisms such as dynamic fees, Anti-Snipe, LP rewards, and automatic burns. The default protocol share is 20%, although the exact percentage is determined when each pool is created. Pools using arbitrage value recapture also contribute a portion of their proceeds to the protocol.

According to the project’s published token mechanism, protocol revenue is accumulated in a treasury and then used to buy back and burn HOOKR. If more pools adopt these additional mechanisms and trading volume continues to grow, the system could theoretically create a value capture loop: increased ecosystem usage leads to higher protocol revenue, which leads to more buybacks and burns.

However, this mechanism needs to be evaluated using actual data, not just its design. Public materials and different versions of the documentation do not describe the launch status of the new buyback engine consistently. I would therefore prioritize verifying actual buyback amounts, on-chain burn records, and protocol revenue rather than assuming every planned mechanism is already fully operational.

What is the market actually betting on?

I see three main bets.

First, trading activity on Robinhood Chain will continue to grow, more projects will need programmable trading rules, and Hookr will become an important infrastructure provider within the ecosystem.

Second, modular Hooks and the SDK will attract third-party developers. If other projects start using Hookr to build pools, launch tokens, or develop applications, the platform could establish network effects that extend beyond traffic to its own website.

Third, ecosystem usage will eventually translate into sustained HOOKR buybacks and burns. For token holders, this is the most important connection between product growth and token value.

Have the fundamentals strengthened or weakened?

From a product capability perspective, I believe they have strengthened. The modular architecture, multiple quote assets, SDK, external routing, and broader integration strategy give Hookr more room to expand than a standalone launchpad.

From an ecosystem adoption perspective, the direction is encouraging, but sustained trading volume, active developers, and actual usage of external integrations still need to validate the thesis.

From a token value capture perspective, the mechanism is becoming clearer, but actual buyback volumes, revenue stability, and the relationship between ecosystem activity and token demand still need to be demonstrated with on-chain data. Product upgrades alone do not mean the token’s fundamentals have improved across the board.

What are the potential upside catalysts from here?

The most important factor is whether new integrations can move beyond announcements and generate sustained trading activity. If more projects choose Hookr to create pools, trading volume, revenue from additional mechanisms, and protocol buybacks could all increase together.

Next, watch whether Hookr becomes infrastructure that other applications routinely adopt. If trading increasingly happens through Uniswap and third-party applications rather than primarily on hookrfun, growth in externally routed activity would be more meaningful than an increase in website traffic alone.

Finally, if Hookr continues releasing new Hook modules, developer tools, and trading mechanisms that are actually adopted by real projects, the market may increasingly value it as infrastructure rather than as a single-purpose launchpad.

The risks are equally clear.

First, if Robinhood Chain’s ecosystem grows more slowly than expected, Hookr may struggle to generate sufficient trading demand despite having a capable product. Second, modular Hooks are not impossible to replicate, and competitors can develop similar trading rules and tools. Third, additional fees may increase costs for users, while overly complex rules could discourage traders and developers from adopting the platform.

More importantly, protocol revenue does not automatically translate into token price appreciation. Even if trading volume grows, HOOKR may struggle to sustain an uptrend if the protocol’s revenue share is limited, buybacks remain small, or market selling pressure is too strong. The project’s website also states that the relevant contracts have not undergone a formal external audit, so smart contract security remains a risk that cannot be ignored.

My view is that HOOKR is worth watching because it is attempting to evolve from a token launch tool into composable trading infrastructure, and the market may already be pricing in this shift.

But what ultimately determines its valuation ceiling is not how many more Hook modules or partnership announcements it adds. It is how many real projects use it, how much sustainable revenue it generates, and whether that revenue can ultimately flow back to HOOKR through mechanisms such as buybacks and burns.

If product adoption, protocol revenue, and actual buybacks grow together, the infrastructure thesis will gain further validation. If the project delivers product updates and partnership announcements without sustained usage or meaningful value capture, a substantial portion of the current rally may still be driven by speculative expectations.

text:
港股调整，之后的机会会在哪里？还是要在具体行业里看。最近港股很萎靡，9月恒生指数累计下跌3.73%，恒生科技指数下跌7.92%。但把行业和公司拆开看表现差异很大：AI-bio就是一个例子，过去两个月恒生生物科技指数涨了30%多，港股这个板块里成份股票过去两个月走势都很强。强势也会伴随剧烈波动，上周7号恒生生物科技指数一度跌超 3%。

个人角度，看港股的投资价值，需要把视线从指数往下移。市场整体调整，并不会让公司的研发和商业化进程同时停下来。有些业务还在增长，有些新产品正在接受验证，也有新的公司进入公开市场。

先看 AI-bio 和创新药。
这条线吸引的地方是 AI 已经开始进入真实的药物研发流程，后续可以用临床数据和客户付款来检验价值。药明康德、金斯瑞、石药、翰森、再鼎等多次创新高。驱动跨国药企对中国管线的BD授权、部分公司中报由亏转盈或高增、国内医药工业规划强化创新定位，以及海外AI制药进展带来的情绪催化。摩根大通则表态对生物科技和CXO相对不那么担心利率冲击，当然短期过于拥挤还是会有调整的。

AI算力硬件链条（相对最清晰的产业趋势）
全球云厂商资本开支仍在上修，需求外溢到高层数PCB、覆铜板、电子布、光模块和部分接口芯片。港股这一块有不少可验证订单和涨价的公司。建滔积层板、建滔集团、胜宏科技、广合科技、长飞光纤等在9–10月反复走强，逻辑是AI服务器PCB层数和用量跳升、上游材料短缺带动提价、国内厂商满产并抢份额。高盛等对AI相关CCL需求到2028年给出较高复合增速。

可以把注意力放在订单能否持续、产品定价有没有改善，再看扩产后的折旧和现金流压力。港股里的半导体机会，需要落到具体公司的产品和客户结构上，单靠一个行业标签还不够。

高股息与现金流资产
银行、电信运营商、部分公用事业和能源股在高利率环境下提供股息缓冲。当然逻辑是估值和派息对冲波动，并不是高成长。成长股看未来业务能做多大，分红型公司则可以更多围绕现金回报来估值。不同类型的资产放在同一个市场里，给了投资者更大的选择空间。

还有一块值得留意，就是新股市场。
港交所数据显示，2026 年前八个月，香港市场 IPO 募资约 3,424 亿港元，同比增长 153%。新股发行持续活跃，也在不断补充二级市场里可以研究的公司。当然近期港股打新也没上半年收益率那么高了。

但对投资者来说，打新的价值，在于多了一个评估公司、参与定价的机会。
市场调整的时候，正好可以把这些方向重新梳理一遍。至于什么时候买，仍然要落到具体公司和价格上。研究范围扩展到港股，接下来就会碰到一个很现实的问题：账户和资金通道有没有准备好？

尤其对手里持有 USDT、USDC 的人，想参与港股，往往还得先解决钱怎么进证券账户。如果需要另办境外银行卡、安排跨境汇款，准备工作也会占用时间。

BIT证券这次上线港股，对这类用户就比较实用。
看公告10月12日， @BITstocks_CN 将正式开放港股交易，一个证券账户同时覆盖美股和港股。有几个点值得聊聊：
1）已经开通美股账户的用户无需重复开户，可以直接开通港股。支持稳定币USDT / USDC 7×24 小时出入金，秒级到账。**港币和美元可以在账户内直接互换。

2）这次一起接进来的还有港股IPO打新。稳定币入金后在账户内兑换成港币，就可以提交新股申购。 对本来就持有稳定币的人，这条路径省去了另行准备海外银行账户的步骤。
BIT还同时支持融资打新，融资倍数最高10倍，1个月内融资认购手续费及额度内的认购利息限时双免，每笔新股认购最高40万港币的免息融资额度。当然对于投资人来说也要注意风险控制。

3）也是真实股票，BIT港股交易由香港证监会持牌券商Atomic Vaults Asia提供，稳定币用于入金和资金兑换。用户按持仓及相关规则享有分红、投票等股东权益，美港股都支持股票转仓。

4）BIT支持内地身份注册和KYC，身份证就可以做地址证明，无需额外准备。而且BIT是不丹主体，不丹是不CRS的，这个对很多朋友来说都很友好了。

对本来就在研究港股、手里又持有一部分稳定币的人，BIT 这次更新提供了一个可以了解的交易入口。行业和公司可以持续跟踪，账户与入金路径也可以提前准备。等到出现自己看得懂、价格合适的机会，再决定如何参与。

quoted_text:
I demand a public explanation from @TechPowerUp and the author of the article, AleksandarK.

A publication specializing in computer hardware has a responsibility to accurately convey both the fundamentals of the technology it covers and the context of the reporting it cites. 

Yet this article quoted portions of my expert call report without my permission, omitted an important qualification explicitly stated in the original, and added market commentary without providing supporting evidence. 

As a result, my interview has been presented in a way that makes it appear to substantiate a company’s technological failure and weakening market competitiveness. 

Other websites have already cited the article and repeated the same narrative. As the author of the original report, I am setting the record straight.

First, Samsung’s shipment of HBM samples using hybrid bonding was already publicly disclosed.

During its earnings call on January 29, 2026, Samsung stated that it had delivered HBM4 samples using hybrid copper bonding to major customers in the fourth quarter of 2025 and had begun technical discussions with them. This was also covered by the press at the time. It was public information well before my interview.

Second, why did you omit the qualification explicitly stated in my report?

I do not understand why you exaggerated the wording in my article to portray SK hynix as being so far behind technologically. My original article explicitly states:

“This is a judgment about sample development progress. The discussion also included reservations about the performance of Samsung’s samples, so I would not extend that judgment directly to an advantage in production yield or customer qualification.”

Did you actually read my article properly before citing it? Or did you simply take a short snippet from Twitter and let your imagination run wild without bothering to investigate? Is this really what passes for professional reporting at a publication specializing in computer hardware?

Third, what evidence supports connecting a gap in hybrid bonding development to current HBM market share?

HBM products currently being mass produced and sold do not use hybrid bonding. What, then, does a gap in hybrid bonding technology have to do with current market share? Why introduce market share figures toward the end of the article in a way that misleadingly suggests these changes are occurring because of a gap in hybrid bonding technology?

Which customer has required hybrid bonding for which specific HBM product? Is there evidence that orders or supplier allocations changed because a supplier could not meet that requirement? If you are discussing a future risk, shouldn’t you first explain the relevant product generation, the timing of adoption, customer requirements, and the limitations of existing processes?

It is reasonable to discuss whether hybrid bonding could affect competitiveness over the long term. But that does not justify presenting current market share figures as if they were evidence supporting that outlook. I would like to know the intent behind publishing an article like this, using a sensational headline and plausible sounding language while framing the claims as things that “could happen.”

I put the following questions directly and firmly to the author and the editorial team.

How thoroughly did you review my original interview report and the information publicly disclosed before it? How did you distinguish between the interviewee’s statements, my interpretation, and your own speculation? What reporting did you actually conduct yourselves? Why did you connect information about a technology’s development status to current market conditions in this manner?

In my view, the way this article is constructed distorts the context of my reporting and risks misleading readers. Do not use my name to lend credibility to your questionable interpretations that lack adequate support.

I demand a clear response from the author and the editorial team explaining why my reporting was reframed in this way.

🎬 Check out our demo! We added brand-new AI functionality directly (and reliably!) to Apple's Preview app, without any source code!

Just Astra Max modifying the existing app in under 20 min, using less than 10% of the weekly token allowance on a $200 subscription!

We've released a proof-of-concept skill repository to help agents directly modify existing applications:

🔗 https://t.co/h7c9arppJY

And I think this points to something MUCH bigger.

I've never seen reverse engineering become such a hot topic in the past 10 years! 🔥 But with AI agents becoming incredibly capable at understanding binaries, I think it's time to ask a bigger question:

What is the future of reverse engineering?

Here's our answer: Omniform Software Engineering (OmniSE).

Over the past few months, following our SRE-Bench work, my research group has been exploring this new direction. 

SRE-Bench showed how capable AI agents have become at understanding and reverse-engineering binaries. 

But why should we stop at understanding software? Why not let agents directly develop on top of it?

That's the vision behind OmniSE: Software engineering should no longer have to start with source code. It should be possible to start with software in ANY form! Whether you have source code, compiled binaries, or an existing application, you should be able to directly customize and extend it.

Think about a simple scenario.

You love an app, but wish it had one additional feature.

Traditionally, you have to wait for the original developers to implement it.

Today, with increasingly powerful AI agents, you might instead reverse-engineer and rebuild the entire application. 

But think about how many tokens it would take to recreate something as mature as Apple Preview! Even worse, rebuilding everything can easily miss subtle but critical functionality. You don't want to spend your time repeatedly fixing an app that already worked perfectly well!

But why rebuild an entire application just to add ONE feature?

With OmniSE, you can bring your AI agent directly to the existing app. Let it understand the software, modify what is needed, and preserve the rest.

This is what excites me most:

Reverse engineering is no longer just a cybersecurity capability. It is becoming a fundamental software development capability that everyone can use and benefit from.

And I believe this is much more than a new task for AI agents. It could represent an entirely new paradigm of software engineering.

Imagine a future where you don't have to adapt yourself to the software you use. Instead, your AI agent adapts the software to YOU.

Every app could become your own customized app.

That's the future of software we want to build. 🚀 #rea #reverseengineeering #openai #codex #deepmind

text:
i often hear people talk about RL as if it’s just “an algorithm” which might or might not be the “right one” and speculate that we might “find a better one”

the issue with this is that all algorithms have some implicit goal of “solving a problem” or “improving an objective” and RL is just what pops out when you take the gradient for your objective

if you’re doing any algorithm other than RL, you are giving up on optimizing your on your ultimate objective directly and leaning on a proxy instead. this is often useful, because your objective might be imprecise, and you might have access to some teacher signal (a static dataset, a teacher model, process evaluation) which trades off unbiased optimization for robustness or reducing sampling costs. but if what you care about can be made explicit, there aren’t any shortcuts. policy gradients are minimum variance unbiased estimators for progress.

这几天，多位从 CryptoBilis 买过 Ledger 硬件钱包的用户报告资产被盗。Ledger 已确认，受影响用户的设备里被植入了未经授权的硬件。具体原因和影响范围还在调查。

CryptoBilis 也卖过 OneKey、Trezor、Tangem、SafePal、imKey 等品牌，所以很多人来问我：我的 OneKey 还安全吗？

截至发文，我们没有收到 OneKey 用户因这次事件遭遇资产被盗的报告。但没收到报告，不等于没有风险。用户的资产安全不能靠运气，我们不会去赌。

我们已经终止了 CryptoBilis 的授权，它不再是 OneKey 的授权经销商。

从今天起，我们做三件事。

第一，不再新增经销商。

即日起，OneKey 停止新增任何经销商。

第二，所有现有经销商重新审查。

以前通过认证的，也全部重新审核、重新排查。经营主体核实不了、最终受益人说不清楚的，一律取消授权，从官网下架。

经销商网络会大幅缩小。硬件钱包关系到用户的资产，渠道必须管严。

审查完成后，我们会在官网公布完整的授权经销商名单。到时，不在名单上的，就不是 OneKey 的授权经销商。

第三，在 CryptoBilis 买过 OneKey 的符合条件用户，免费换新。

2026 年 3 月 1 日至本声明发布之日，在 CryptoBilis 买过 OneKey 硬件钱包的用户，不限型号，不管有没有激活、有没有用过，都可以免费换新。

为什么从 3 月 1 日算？CryptoBilis 的原联合创始人公开表示，公司在今年早些时候被收购，3 月完成了经营管理职责的交接。我们从 3 月 1 日开始覆盖，把整个交接月份和之后的购买都算进去。这个范围已经超过 180 天，我们宁可多覆盖一点。

换新设备由 OneKey 官方商店直接发货。原来是什么型号，就换同一型号的全新设备；如果那个型号没货了，就免费升级成更新的型号。

旧设备不用寄回，我们直接寄新的，直接从 OneKey 官网发货。

Why I'm so bullish robinhood:0x18e674231a58c239dc7daedcffe15ec3a24cff5c and think it'll trade at 200M+ in the coming months:

First, why do V4 hooks matter?

A Uniswap V4 hook is a contract the pool calls inside every swap. That means a pool can run its own rules: fees that react to volatility, anti-snipe protection, auto burns, LP rewards, MEV protection, limit orders, vesting, and much more.

Every launchpad pool today looks the same. Same fee, same opening chaos, same snipers, same MEV bots eating the value. Hooks change that. The pool's behaviour becomes the product.

The problem: writing, auditing and getting a hook routed is hard. Most teams can't do it. That's the gap Hookr fills.

So, what is Hookr?

Hookr is modular infrastructure for surfacing, composing and integrating Uniswap V4 hooks. 

You don't write a hook from scratch. You pick Hook Blocks, tune them per pool, and launch. Or you remix them into a hook of your own.

They already offer 22 'Hook Blocks' and are integrating/building new ones on a weekly basis

(for the different hooks available go check their website, it's pretty fucking sick and game-changing)

And the part people are missing is that you don't have to launch on Hookr to use their tech.

In V4, a pool's hook is fixed when the pool is created. So a token that already trades is normally stuck without one.

Hookr solves it. One launch can open up to 8 hooked pools for a token that already exists, with no migration and no control over the token. Even Robinhood's tokenized stocks can sit in a hooked pool.

And the distribution part is also a big reason why people would want to launch or integrate into Hookr.

On Hookr you get:

> Distribution: every launcher can toggle your block on from the UI
> Revenue: the Hook Blocks Market lets builders publish blocks bonded in robinhood:0x18e674231a58c239dc7daedcffe15ec3a24cff5c, and every swap in a pool using one pays its usage fee
> Routing: Hookr's root hook is on Uniswap's allowlist, so the Uniswap app and API route through it out of the box
> Composability: your block stacks with anti-snipe, dynamic fees, burns and LP rewards on the same pool

That's why for example @whatthehookv4 built their arb recapture on Hookr instead of running it standalone.

It's literally becoming the backend for V4 markets.

More than 95% of trades on Hookr pools happen outside Hookr. 
Uniswap, Relay, 0x, KyberSwap, LI-FI, OKX DEX, Velora and PFOF all route robinhood:0x18e674231a58c239dc7daedcffe15ec3a24cff5c flow. 

And lastly, their ecosystem coin.

> Hookr never touches the base LP fee. It takes a share of the add-on streams (20% by default, capped at 50%, frozen per pool at creation) plus a cut of arb recapture profit.
> Every one of those protocol shares is swept to the treasury, used to buy back robinhood:0x18e674231a58c239dc7daedcffe15ec3a24cff5c, and burned. All visible onchain at the dead address.

Every new block, every new integrator, every new root profile adds another stream. 

More hooked pools means more fees. More fees means more burns.

So tldr of the thesis:

Every liquidity pool on every launchpad will eventually run a V4 hook. The question is where those hooks get built, discovered, composed and routed.

Hookr is setting itself up as that place. Not another launchpad with hooks bolted on, but the distribution layer for the whole V4 hooks meta.

Launch here or plug in later. Either way, the hooked pool ends up on Hookr. And that fuels buyback and burns of robinhood:0x18e674231a58c239dc7daedcffe15ec3a24cff5c.

Generational.

gmonad。从新加坡回来，把Open和这周几个@Monad真正值得看的update分享中文CT朋友们

Monad：一个足以承载全球资金的网络，主网一周年，Open上几个比较硬的更新：

1. 隐私结算功能（Private Settlement）：  
@category_xyz 在Open主舞台宣布的。Monad L1上直接做机密执行域，不用另起一条私有链。每个域通过L1上的标准EVM hub合约启用，不需要分叉也不需要协议升级。域内交易、状态、合约代码端到端加密，连L1本身都读不到；跨域转账也是加密的，地址和金额对外不可见。机构自己定验证者集合、信任模型、访问规则和管辖权，默认谁都看不到，审计或监管可以按需给权限。同时域还直接接到Monad的共享流动性，结算是原子的
现在还是设计方案，Category Labs在跟早期设计伙伴推进，还没上线。发布前有过“Privacy is coming”的预热。  
https://t.co/jDM67nqYDv  
https://t.co/wlb0R3sU7Y  

why matters：机构（银行、基金、交易台、企业财资）最怕的就是链上全透明。他们现在要么不上链，要么自己搞私有链把流动性切碎。这个设计如果跑通，等于让这些机构能直接用公开链的速度和流动性，同时业务还保密。对Monad来说，这是把大额资金和真实业务流程拉进来的关键入口，后面稳定币、RWA、支付的体量都有可能跟着放大

2. 股票上链，xStocks原生上Monad：
@valgui在台上宣布@xStocksFi 原生部署到Monad，覆盖1100+代币化美股和ETF。代币直接在Monad上铸造和结算，不是从别的链桥过来。1:1对应底层证券，ERC-20形态，可以往DEX、借贷、钱包里组合
这跟 @aave 之前提的V4代币化股票hub提案也能对上。链上后续也有合约部署和铸造的讨论  
https://t.co/dO3Bzok7O8  

why matters：股票类资产是全球最大的流动性池之一。原生上链意味着不用桥，可以直接在Monad做交易、抵押、组合。对交易者来说多了24/7的股票敞口，对DeFi协议来说多了新的抵押品和交易对，对持有美股的人来说多了链上使用场景。如果流动性慢慢起来，Monad的交易量和TVL都有机会从纯crypto资产往传统资产延伸，可以关心Monad上几个DEX的进展@perpltrade @hellotradeapp @KuruExchange 等还有几个还没宣发的

3. Cadence共识，提升性能并解决MEV： 
@_jhunsaker现场demo了Cadence。这是多并发提议者共识，多个验证者同时提议，配合极端流水线。现在Monad主网是300ms出块、600ms最终性，升级完成后目标100ms出块、300ms最终性，再配上BTX加密mempool，从协议层压MEV
https://t.co/GLULPvHZHe  

why matters：做市商和高频交易最在意的是延迟和被夹。100ms出块加上协议层压MEV，等于让链上交易体验更接近中心化交易所，同时减少被三明治的损失。对普通交易者和DeFi用户来说，滑点和被夹的成本会下降；对专业交易团队来说，更愿意把订单流放上来。后面如果真落地，交易量和做市深度有机会继续涨，CT里也会有更多人讨论“链上交易是不是开始能打CEX了”

4. StraitsX x Monad 新元稳定币：
XSGD和XUSD计划2027年初原生发行到Monad，XSGD会是链上第一条原生新加坡元稳定币，还受技术、监管和合规条件约束。双方也在看卡项目、支付和跨境结算这些场景。StraitsX是Open的title sponsor，持有新加坡大额支付机构牌照，累计稳定币交易量接近700亿。  
https://t.co/KTv4Q24Cly  

why matters：稳定币是链上真正的支付和结算入口。原生发行加上受监管牌照，意味着后面卡、跨境、商户结算这些场景可以更顺地接进来，而不是只停留在DeFi套利。对亚太用户和支付公司来说，多了一条合规的链上通道；对Monad来说，稳定币存量和使用量起来后，整条链的日常活跃和费用都会受益。后面如果卡和支付真落地，用户增长会从纯crypto圈子往更广的支付用户延伸

5. Open台上也拉了Visa、ETH Foundation、Dragonfly、Tether、Zero Hash等。主舞台之外还有DeltaV Demo Day，项目直接对VC路演。Metropolis黑客松也还在进行，奖金25万+，提交截止10/13  

链上数据目前DeFi TVL大概10亿，排名第十，钱包400多万，累计交易8亿多，DEX成交量累计330亿左右，应用170+
https://t.co/fS6gyQQkd5

why matters：这些数据说明主网已经有真实使用，不是纯叙事。机构方和头部协议持续进来，加上黑客松和Demo Day，开发者和项目方还会继续进场，这些都会直接反映在链上活跃和资产规模上

text:
未來的 App，可能越來越少被人打開，卻越來越常被 AI 使用。🤖

這就是最近在討論的 Headless App。

名字聽起來很技術，其實很好理解：把軟體的功能和操作畫面拆開，讓 AI 可以直接調用服務，不需要你親自進去按每一個按鈕。

🍽️ 舉個例子。

現在安排一場聚餐，你可能要查餐廳、找空位、填資料，再打開行事曆，最後另外叫車。

未來，你可能只需要交代：

「幫我找週五晚上七點、四個人的餐廳，每人預算兩千，我不吃牛肉。」

AI 在取得授權、接通相關服務後，就能查空位、比較選項，等你確認，再完成訂位和後續安排。

餐廳、訂位系統、叫車服務都還在，只是很多操作會移到背後。

🔌 這裡常會提到 MCP。

你可以把它理解成 AI 連接不同工具的「通用插座」。服務把功能開放出來，AI 就能用比較一致的方式讀取資料、執行任務。

Salesforce 已經在做這件事：透過 Headless 360，讓取得授權的 AI 直接使用平台裡的資料與工作流程。

📱 我覺得接下來有三個變化值得注意：

• 使用者會更在意「事情有沒有完成」，而不只是 App 裡有多少功能。

• 軟體公司除了吸引人，也要讓 AI 容易找到、理解並可靠地使用自己的服務。

• 掌握 AI 助理入口的平台，可能更有能力影響訂單最後流向誰。

這對商業模式的影響很大。

當使用者不再每次都進入你的 App，廣告曝光、加購推薦、會員經營，都可能需要重新設計。

但我不認為這代表所有 App 都會消失，更不認為軟體因此沒有價值。

看影片、玩遊戲、設計作品，介面本身就是體驗的一部分；付款、重要決策和異常處理，也仍然需要清楚的畫面與人的確認。

💡 我更在意的是：

以後做一個 App，除了問「使用者為什麼會打開我」，也要開始問：

「當使用者把事情交給 AI，它為什麼會選擇我的服務？」

📚 兩篇值得延伸閱讀的 X 原文：

🔹 Salesforce／Marc Benioff：開放平台能力，讓 AI 直接調用。
https://t.co/56DW33IwHO

🔹 Box／Aaron Levie：AI Agent 可能擴大軟體的使用量與應用場景。
https://t.co/vP0xRHcmli

Agents are going to use software 100X more than people will in the future. As a result, enterprise platforms will become headless and be able to work with any agent on or off platform. If you don’t do that you’re DOA.

What some have missed is that this creates vastly more use-cases for these platforms than even existed pre-AI. This isn’t zero sum. Software value props have traditionally been capped at the number of users you have in a company. Agents have no upper limit. 

We’re going to run agents to process data at a scale humans never could, they’re going to be running 24/7 in parallel doing work for us, and they can integrate workflows across systems to generate all new value propositions.

Once you embrace this approach, it becomes obvious how much more upside there is.

text:
PapertradeのPAPERは取引できません。送金も売買もスワップもブリッジもできず、ステーキングにしか使えないトークンです。

PAPERについて
・Papertradeで損失を出してクローズした時か、清算された時に、そのウォレットにミントされます
・ステーキングすると、PapertradeのUSDC収益の一部を受け取れます。アンステークはすぐにできます
・PAPER自体に価格はないので、APRも出せません
・他のチェーンで「PAPER」というティッカーのトークンが取引されていますが、PapertradeのPAPERとは別物です。ご注意ください

BankrでのPapertradeの使い方
・Papertradeは、HyperEVM上にあるBTCとETHの合成パーペチュアル（無期限先物）です。名前に「ペーパー」と入っていますが練習用ではなく、本物のUSDCで取引します
・Bankrに一文で頼めば取引できます。例：「long BTC 50x with $200 on papertrade」

这几天，多位从 CryptoBilis 买过 Ledger 硬件钱包的用户报告资产被盗。Ledger 已确认，受影响用户的设备里被植入了未经授权的硬件。具体原因和影响范围还在调查。

CryptoBilis 也卖过 OneKey、Trezor、Tangem、SafePal、imKey 等品牌，所以很多人来问我：我的 OneKey 还安全吗？

截至发文，我们没有收到 OneKey 用户因这次事件遭遇资产被盗的报告。但没收到报告，不等于没有风险。用户的资产安全不能靠运气，我们不会去赌。

我们已经终止了 CryptoBilis 的授权，它不再是 OneKey 的授权经销商。

从今天起，我们做三件事。

第一，不再新增经销商。

即日起，OneKey 停止新增任何经销商。

第二，所有现有经销商重新审查。

以前通过认证的，也全部重新审核、重新排查。经营主体核实不了、最终受益人说不清楚的，一律取消授权，从官网下架。

经销商网络会大幅缩小。硬件钱包关系到用户的资产，渠道必须管严。

审查完成后，我们会在官网公布完整的授权经销商名单。到时，不在名单上的，就不是 OneKey 的授权经销商。

第三，在 CryptoBilis 买过 OneKey 的符合条件用户，免费换新。

2026 年 3 月 1 日至本声明发布之日，在 CryptoBilis 买过 OneKey 硬件钱包的用户，不限型号，不管有没有激活、有没有用过，都可以免费换新。

为什么从 3 月 1 日算？CryptoBilis 的原联合创始人公开表示，公司在今年早些时候被收购，3 月完成了经营管理职责的交接。我们从 3 月 1 日开始覆盖，把整个交接月份和之后的购买都算进去。这个范围已经超过 180 天，我们宁可多覆盖一点。

换新设备由 OneKey 官方商店直接发货。原来是什么型号，就换同一型号的全新设备；如果那个型号没货了，就免费升级成更新的型号。

旧设备不用寄回，我们直接寄新的，直接从 OneKey 官网发货。

申请方法很简单：在 OneKey 官网点「客服」，或者打开 https://t.co/QG5Mu83nAr，提交工单。

标题写 CryptoBilis Replacement，附上：

- 购买凭证或小票，必须提供；
- 设备型号；
- 设备有没有激活、使用过。

申请截止：2026 年 12 月 31 日。

换新可以申请，资产安全不要等。

如果设备还没激活，先别激活，直接申请换新。

如果已经在用、里面还有资产，出于预防，请把旧助记词当作可能已经泄露来处理，尽快把资产转到使用全新助记词的钱包里，别为了等新设备而拖着。

手里有其他来源可信的硬件钱包，就在那台设备上生成全新的助记词，把资产转过去。暂时没有的话，可以在安全、可信的手机或电脑上，用 OneKey App 新建一个钱包，生成全新的助记词，先把资产转过去，作为临时过渡。

新设备到手后，在新设备上重新生成全新的助记词，再把资产转进去。不要把旧助记词导入新设备，也不要把临时 App 钱包的助记词导入新设备。资产转完后，旧设备和旧助记词就别再用了。

最后提醒一句：OneKey 客服永远不会问你要助记词或 PIN 码。任何以「换新」「验证」为由索要这些信息的人，都是骗子。

大家买 OneKey，是因为信任 OneKey。这份信任，我们得接住。

这件事我会跟到底，有新进展，我会第一时间更新。

text:
Copper is starting to hit its limits in advanced packaging.
Pure Cu is ~400 W/m·K, while at Semicon Taiwan there are debut of Cu/diamond composites reaching ~800 W/m·K, helping spread heat faster and reduce local hotspots. They can also reduce warpage: silicon is ~3 ppm/K CTE vs copper at ~17 ppm/K, while Cu/diamond can be tuned closer to ~6–10 ppm/K.

The challenge is the Cu/diamond interface. Copper does not naturally bond well with diamond, so Ti, Cr, Mo, or W are often added to form a carbide bonding layer. But too much carbide hurts thermal conductivity, making interface thickness critical. Compared with simply alloying Cu, the industry is working on pre-coating diamond particles using PVD or CVD giving much tighter control.

I want to clear a few things up, because two very different stories are getting blended together.

First, the card dashboard incident from Oct 5 is real. Someone accessed cardholder KYC data, and we take that seriously. It's right that people are talking about it. Funds were safe, and affected users have been notified. If you hold a Based card, please stay vigilant, as phishing attempts may use your real details. We will only contact you through in-app support. Any DM on X or Telegram claiming to be Based support is a scam.

The AI dashboard story being reshared alongside it is a separate incident from back in March.

That one was discovered by one of our die-hard users, who was always digging through our site to see what we were building next. It was an internal OpenClaw dashboard the team was experimenting with. It was never public-facing or launched. He flagged it, we shut it down, rotated the keys, and thanked him for catching it. The keys were for our internal AI gateway with usage caps. Card dashboard was kept separate.

We recognize that even internal experiments need to be handled with the right level of care. We appreciate the user who brought it to our attention, and we take these situations as opportunities to improve.

-
We've been through similar situations before, and each time, we've tried to clarify what happened. We understand that trust takes time to build, and people have every right to ask questions and expect clear answers from us.

What makes these situations difficult is that even after the facts are clarified, the original posts often continue to circulate while the follow-up receives much less attention. We hope to get the full context across this time, and we'll continue to be open and clear whenever concerns arise.

-
I also want to share a bit about how we've grown and where we're headed.

Based has been listed in Hyperliquid's docs since the early days, and we're proud to be featured on their site. But our growth hasn't come from the docs alone. Builder Codes were designed to help teams bring new users into Hyperliquid, and that's what we've focused on: introducing people to the ecosystem who might not otherwise have joined.

We're continuing to explore new ways to grow across Web2 and Web3, including community-led initiatives and UGC. Our goal is to keep bringing new users into the ecosystem while building products that give them more reasons to stay.

We know trust is earned through actions, not words. We'll keep listening, improving, and building.
