text:
I make this same post like every 2-3 years, because there's always new data further supporting it. 

Georges Harik (@gharik) is one of the most prescient people in AI, and definitely the least well known and underappreciated one. 

In 1999 he joined Google as one of the first employees (like #7 or something) because he thought he could use his AI knowledge to build a better ad system. He and Salar Kamangar built Adwords (Salar later bought YouTube and Georges later was the force behind Google wanting to buy Andy rubin's company to build Android)

Georges left Google so he could focus on AI research, which he self funded. He did so with someone he worked with closely at Google, our friend Noam Shazeer (they built the AdSense targeting engine). When Google finally decided to work hard on AI around the time of the deepmind acquisition, they tried to get Georges and Noam to come back. Georges wanted to stay independent, and our friend Noam went on to do great things obviously. This was my good fortune because it led to Georges and I hanging out a lot, because he basically needed a new lunch buddy. 

Georges at the time was working on language models and despite karpathy saying nobody saw LLMs being so big even in 2017, Georges was telling me they were on the cusp of changing everything in 2013. My wife and I literally changed some of our parenting priorities that year (less tigery) because georges convinced me the world was going to change so much. 

Later on he and I got involved in a company making CV photo filters called Lambda. They needed to make money to survive so they started building ML boxes which Georges bought a bunch of. But his significant other was mad there were so many loud and hot boxes in the house, she started worrying about fire risk, so Georges told the lambda guys they should build a cloud because in the future, the power density of the systems was going to be too big for even most enterprises to handle. This was like 2017.  That's how lambda cloud began, and the premise Georges had was that AI was going to change things so much, demand growth would outpace supply growth, and the value of compute was eventually going to rise and that lambda was effectively going to be a REIT... so we should own as many GPUs as possible. It took the world almost a decade to finally figure out what Georges saw then (see attached tweet). 

About 5 years ago when pretraining was still the only thing people cared about, Georges started telling me inference was going to be super impt. He was working on research investigating post training as a way to improve reasoning. He found some other guys working on the same idea that had a paper known as the STAR paper, and they worked together to prove it even further with another paper called quietstar. (They all later cofounded the neolab humans&). Georges got some friends to build https://t.co/HWFg5TUTv3 to be one of the first inference clouds because he saw it all early. He and the humans& team also smartly used all their money to buy compute knowing it would go up in price and also get harder to obtain. 

It's kind of amazing to me how he has gotten everything right so far ahead of time. It's also amazing to me how VCs don't really get or believe a lot of the things he says, they often tell me I am wrong whenever I parrot Georges' current thoughts... and then years later they all put out charts and papers reaffirming those same things as if they knew it all along. 

The founders of Google recognize Georges' brilliance and still talk to him a lot. (Besides being smart, he is a lot of fun to hang out with.) I'm just wondering when the rest of the world figures it out

3. A product you can feel: near(.)com, deposit and you are in a black box with 35 chains
4. Serious people saying it out loud: funds writing research, the big podcasts, and the same Twitter voices that called Zcash a year ago. Plus a regulated wrapper, the first US spot ETF, and a supply story, issuance cut to 1.6% on the table.

Same four ingredients, same two extras. The first three take years to build and near:native has them. The fourth is the match, and it was struck this month. On zcash:native, the match did 15x in two months.

text:
For this rally, I'm more inclined to view $HOOKR as Uniswap v4 Hook infrastructure on Rh Chain.

0x18e674231a58c239dc7daedcffe15ec3a24cff5c 

It is expanding from a token launch tool into composable trading infrastructure.

The market appears to be reassessing its ecosystem value.

Unlike a Meme token driven purely by hype, HOOKR has usable products, on-chain trading pools, and a protocol fee mechanism. But that also raises the key question: has the growth in product capabilities translated into sufficient real usage and sustainable buying pressure for the token?

Recent developments have also led me to update my analysis in an important way. HOOKR is not simply adding more Hook modules. It is beginning to connect capital flows, reward distribution, and revenue streams across different trading pools. This is more significant than simply adding token launch features, because it speaks to whether Hookr can evolve from a programmable liquidity pool platform into composable on-chain trading infrastructure.

Hookr’s website now positions the new version as modular infrastructure for Uniswap v4 Hooks. However, the relevant contracts have not yet completed a formal external audit. Product functionality going live and security being independently verified must therefore be evaluated separately.

The Latest Catalysts

1. Moving from individual trading pools to cross-pool connectivity

The most important update is Hookr’s announcement that three contracts connecting different trading pools are now live.

Pool Mesh allows a single vault to provide liquidity to up to four pools for different tokens. Capital can be allocated according to predefined weights or directed toward the pools with the thinnest liquidity. Once a project creates a Mesh, other pools can join it.

This means liquidity no longer has to remain entirely isolated within each pool. For projects operating multiple tokens or trading markets, this mechanism could make capital management more flexible.

Family Pinger allows a single call to automatically execute a group of related operations, including trading Zaps, periodic small fund distributions, and payments owed to a family of pools.

Fee Bridge allows a project to designate an address as a royalty recipient or tax recipient, then distribute the funds it receives in batches to liquidity providers in another pool, with a cap on the amount transferred in each distribution.

The common thread among these three features is that Hookr is beginning to coordinate capital across multiple pools rather than focusing solely on trading rules within individual pools.

If real projects adopt these mechanisms, Hookr’s infrastructure thesis will become much more compelling than a simple launchpad narrative. However, contracts going live only means the functionality is available. It does not mean large-scale adoption or substantial revenue has already materialized.

2. Modular tools and the developer ecosystem continue to expand

Hookr’s newly released HookBook documents 24 ways to combine Uniswap v4 pools with Hook Blocks, covering use cases ranging from fair launches to treasury management. Each combination comes with a full walkthrough, and users can open the Builder with the configuration prefilled in one click.

Hookr has also introduced or announced the following features:

Every live Hook Block can be configured directly in the app and has its own dedicated page.
Developers can submit requests directly through the search interface when they cannot find the module they need.
Swap Reward Mint allows users to create reward tokens within the app and distribute them to traders on every swap.
Multi-pool launches allow different pools to use separate Hook Blocks and different initial quote assets.
Existing tokens can also add Tax + Conversion mechanisms, with the pool page showing who pays each tax.
llms.txt allows AI agents and AI search tools to read Hook Blocks, documentation, and HookBook combinations.

In addition, Hookr has announced support for deploying custom Uniswap v4 Hooks in a single transaction and says the first such Hook is already on-chain. Developers can combine the Hook Blocks they need, deploy their own Hook, and then use Hookr’s launch, routing, and quote-asset tools to create trading pools. Existing tokens can also connect to new pools without modifying the tokens themselves.

These updates may seem scattered, but they point toward the same goal: lowering the barrier to building complex trading mechanisms.

If developers can select modules, combine parameters, deploy pools, and integrate them into their own applications through an SDK, Hookr has the potential to become a development tool for other projects rather than a product that serves only traffic on its own website.

3. Ecosystem integrations are expanding into more use cases

Hookr’s new version supports different quote assets, including ETH, stablecoins, HOOKR, and tokenized stocks. It also provides an SDK and a public module directory, allowing other applications to integrate trading, quoting, and pool creation functionality.

More importantly, Hookr pools can be routed through Uniswap’s own interface and APIs. This means projects do not have to rely entirely on users visiting https://t.co/rbi76Dkjxu directly; they may also attract usage through external trading interfaces.

The project also claims that the new version reduces gas costs for swaps by approximately 47%–70% and token launch costs by around 40%. If these advantages hold up in real transactions, Hookr could attract developers through a better product experience rather than relying purely on subsidies.

Recent project-related information also mentions several integrations:

Saffron is integrating fixed-yield vaults.
ZEALZ plans to launch a zZEC pool with low base fees and LP rewards.
rhook can replay historical trading activity to compare the effects of different trading rules.
hooddomains brings domains into the creator and trading pool experience.
An OpenAI-related project plans to launch tokens with custom rules on Hookr.
Longbow Lend is exploring the use of Hookr pools for liquidations and collateral swaps.

These integrations serve different purposes. Some could increase the number of trading pools, some improve developer tooling, and others attempt to connect Hookr with lending, yield, and trading applications.

If these projects actually launch and generate sustained trading activity, the demand thesis for HOOKR could expand beyond token launch activity into broader ecosystem usage.

However, it is essential to distinguish between an integration being announced, a feature being live, and an integration generating meaningful trading volume. A list of partnerships and a growing number of features do not, by themselves, prove that protocol revenue is increasing.

4. The token value-capture mechanism is becoming clearer

HOOKR’s value proposition is not simply to use all trading fees for buybacks.

In the new version, base LP fees go entirely to liquidity providers. The protocol primarily earns a share of revenue from additional mechanisms such as dynamic fees, Anti-Snipe, LP rewards, and automatic burns. The default revenue-sharing rate is 20%, with the actual rate determined when a pool is created. Pools using the arbitrage value-recapture mechanism also contribute part of their proceeds to the protocol.

The mechanism described by the project involves pooling protocol revenue in a treasury and using it to buy back and burn HOOKR.

If more pools adopt these additional mechanisms and trading volume continues to grow, this could theoretically create a value-capture loop: greater ecosystem usage leads to more protocol revenue, which in turn supports more buybacks and burns.

But this chain of causality still needs to be verified with real data. I will focus on actual protocol revenue, on-chain buyback records, and the amount of tokens burned rather than assuming that every mechanism is already operating at full scale.

What the Market May Be Betting On

I think the market may be betting on three layers of potential.

First, trading activity on Rh Chain will continue to grow, and more projects will need programmable trading rules, positioning Hookr as an important infrastructure entry point.

Second, modular Hooks, HookBook, and the SDK will attract third-party developers. If other projects begin using Hookr to build pools, launch tokens, or develop applications, it could create network effects that extend beyond traffic to Hookr’s own website.

Third, cross-pool capital management and broader ecosystem usage will eventually translate into sustained HOOKR buybacks and burns. For token holders, this is the most important connection between product growth and token value.

Where Things Stand Now

Product fundamentals are strengthening, ecosystem adoption remains unproven, and token value capture has yet to be fully realized.

From a product perspective, HOOKR is clearly more extensible than a single-purpose launch platform. Its modular architecture, pools with multiple quote assets, cross-pool connectors, SDK, custom Hook deployment, and external routing are expanding the range of problems it can solve.

From an adoption perspective, the direction is improving, but it still needs to be validated through sustained trading volume, active developers, and actual usage data from external integrations. The launch of connectors and partnership announcements do not necessarily mean they are already generating substantial trading activity.

From a token value-capture perspective, the mechanism is becoming clearer, but the actual scale of buybacks, the stability of revenue, and the relationship between revenue and token demand still need to be demonstrated with on-chain data. Product upgrades should not be equated with a fully realized improvement in token fundamentals.

Potential Upside Catalysts Ahead

First, real projects begin using the cross-pool connectors. If Pool Mesh helps multiple pools share and coordinate liquidity, Fee Bridge establishes consistent cross-pool revenue distribution, and Family Pinger handles recurring automated payments, that would be much more meaningful than simply adding a few more trading pools.

Second, third-party projects begin building their own products on Hookr. If launch platforms use custom Hooks, trading applications integrate pools through the SDK, and DeFi protocols use its mechanisms for liquidity and yield management, Hookr’s value would no longer depend entirely on how many tokens it launches itself.

Third, protocol revenue and buybacks and burns grow together. This is the key point at which the product narrative could translate into stronger token fundamentals. If real trading activity increases alongside sustained growth in protocol revenue, actual buybacks, and token burns, HOOKR’s long-term valuation thesis would gain much stronger support.

Fourth, additional features launch and attract real usage. Canonical Venue Token, Buy/Sell Block, Market Guard, Zap Relay, Entry Ratio Guarantee, Recovery Reserve, Pay Later, Tax + Conversion, Revenue Router, Vesting Milestone, Market-hours Fee, Limit Orders, Best Route, and Hook Blocks Market could all expand Hookr’s potential use cases.

However, not all these features are live yet. Zero-seed launches, auction-based launches, Floor Bid, Dev Drip, and Usage Fee are also still part of the development roadmap. Whether they become catalysts depends on their eventual launch and adoption, not merely their presence on a roadmap.

Key Risks

First, Hookr’s product capabilities may be ahead of market demand. If developer activity and trading on Rh Chain remain insufficient, even a comprehensive modular system may struggle to generate meaningful protocol revenue.

Second, complex trading rules and cross-pool capital flows increase system complexity. Pool Mesh, Fee Bridge, and similar features need to prove that their fund routing, transfer limits, and exception handling are reliable. More features do not automatically mean lower system risk.

Third, Hook modules are not impossible to replicate. Hookr’s long-term moat must ultimately come from developer adoption, tooling quality, its integration network, and sustained usage—not merely the number of modules it offers.

Fourth, security remains a critical risk. Hookr’s website has not confirmed that the relevant contracts have completed a formal external audit, while the project recently stated that the new version was being submitted for audit. Submitting contracts for an audit does not mean the audit is complete, nor does it guarantee that no vulnerabilities exist.

Finally, even if product usage grows, the token may not appreciate accordingly. If protocol revenue shares remain limited, buybacks are too small, or sustained selling pressure outweighs buying demand, the infrastructure narrative may still fail to translate into token price performance.

My Final Take

The latest batch of updates makes me more optimistic about HOOKR’s product direction.

Previously, its main story was modularizing Uniswap v4 Hooks so that projects could create pools with more flexible, customized trading rules. Now, Pool Mesh, Family Pinger, and Fee Bridge are beginning to connect capital and revenue across multiple pools, while HookBook, the SDK, and custom Hook deployment are lowering the barriers for developers to use these capabilities.

This pushes HOOKR’s potential positioning beyond “a more flexible token launch platform” toward “programmable and composable trading and capital-management infrastructure.”

But product upgrades do not mean token value has already been realized. The key things to track next are whether the connectors see real usage, whether third-party integrations continue to expand, whether protocol revenue grows, and whether buybacks and burns reach a meaningful scale.

If product adoption, protocol revenue, and actual buybacks grow together, HOOKR’s infrastructure narrative will gain much stronger fundamental support. If its features keep expanding but real usage and value capture remain elusive, the token could still be trading on a future that has been priced in too early.

text:
This is a good way to understand how early we actually are in AI diffusion right now. The vast majority of people are using AI as a chatbot for simple interactions that approximate next-generation search. This is super useful but dramatically underrepresents the full capability of AI.

On the complete other end of the spectrum, agent swarms represent possibly the ultimate form factor of what agents will do inside of our workflows. Math, cyber, bio, materials science, software engineering, finance, and any other field that has valuable tasks that can be executed in parallel where compute can be applied to accelerate work all have this characteristic.

Less than a fraction of a fraction of the population uses AI in this way right now, due to a mix of the capabilities of models relative to the user's domain, the cost of doing these types of workflows today, the harnesses available to do this style of AI work, and the availability (or lack thereof) of frontier models to the general public.

There will also be a huge amount of change management necessary to get most areas of work -beyond software and AI research- to benefit from this style of agents. Companies need to upgrade their workflows, data needs to integrated and migrated into modern platforms, and companies will need to work through compliance, governance, and security frameworks to pull it off. 

But this all represents opportunity right now. A lot of this is where the applied layer of AI will really shine in the enterprise because of the domain specificity of this type of work. You can get an early sense of where things are going and the opportunity ahead by seeing through the funnel that Andrej lays out.
author: levie
quoted_text:
Dusting off this tweet from April because this gap in shared understanding of LLM capability is *widening*. It's now less "two groups of people speaking past each other" and more a sharp funnel.

- Napkin math somewhere around 6B people (~75% of the population) have barely come in contact with LLMs at all.
- Around 1-2B (~20%) are casual and infrequent users of free-tier ChatGPT-like products. This group sees derpy chatbots and treats them a bit like a better Google search, a writing aid, or etc. Maybe an agent tries to book you a flight. I have non-tech friends who (reasonably, imo) say they have not much use for it at all. Even many professionals outside of math&code are in this tier. For example, execs and many other functions spend a lot of their time talking to other people, so while they understand what is happening intellectually, it is still second-hand and a bit abstract.
- Now we get to professional use of frontier-grade LLMs in math&code. Somewhere around 20M people (0.2%) see first-hand that large, complex projects that used to take them weeks/months can now be completed by agents with a prompt. Building apps, copying apps, translating apps, decompiling apps from binaries... This has all happened very quickly and recently - less than 1 year ago, I was writing code manually by hand, typing memorized computer code commands into a code editor character by character, occasionally pressing Tab to autocomplete a little chunk of code.
- And finally we get to the ~5,000 people (~0.00006%) with access to frontier-grade systems internally. The external world has seen the preview. It looks like swarms of thousands of agents collaborating over weeks on software mega projects: minting zero days, running cyber attacks and defenses at machine speeds, discovering new science, advancing the frontier of mathematics. Things that would have taken top professionals in the industry years of work. Meanwhile, human review and comprehension are starting to fall behind. For example, people are still involved in the "archeology" of the OpenAI-HF incident from many months ago. Mathematicians may be poring over the 722 manuscripts on frontier mathematics for a while.

The funnel is driven by a combination of factors:
1. The impact scales with ambition, problem size, and horizon. A question with a paragraph answer barely stresses the system. You need a reservoir of big, difficult problems that you really care about. This aspect drives the consumer / professional dimension of the funnel.
2. The jaggedness of the system (which I have written about a lot separately). Capability peaks in domains that are digital, verifiable and economically valuable. This is because LLM capability emerges from reinforcement learning on verifiable rewards on a curated environment mixture driven by revenue potential. This aspect primarily drives the area (e.g. math&code) dimension of the funnel.
3. Access. Free-tier, paid-tier, internal.

So this is the weirdness of the moment. The general public has mostly not interacted with these systems. When they have, it looks like a derpy chatbot. The majority of professionals still see only a modest uplift. And a small sliver of professionals are experiencing the vertigo of the curve going vertical. And it is all happening at the same time.

随手记一下这次 TOKEN2049 的一些 Takeaways：

1. Crypto 项目正在肉眼可见地变少。

至少从这次线下的体感来看，值得关注的新项目确实没有以前那么多了。

过去大家玩腻了 VC 币，逐渐转向玩Alpha壳。铁打的流水线组局工厂在未来listing的难度会越来越大，上币的难度在大大提高。

换个角度看，一些本身具备资源和渠道的壳子，未来可能也会水涨船高。听说现在已经有专门炒壳的市场了。

2. 非常 Bullish RWA，特别是美股相关的基础设施。
这次 Connect 了很多来自北美的团队，大家对 RWA 的预期都非常高。

这个叙事在过去可能存在于美债上链，但在美股Perp上线后，但随着美股 Perp 的发展，尤其是 @HyperliquidX 的 HIP-3，大家开始意识到 24/7 交易和非传统交易时段价格发现的价值。

未来会有更多传统金融资产、发行平台和交易基础设施逐渐进入 Crypto。比如 @RobinhoodApp 现在正在做的事情，将传统金融用户带来Crypto。

3. 传统 Agency 靠信息差赚钱的时代，正在慢慢结束。

在过去的几年时间内，很多Agency通过信息差的方式就能赚得盆满钵满。

但 AI 正在快速压低 Research、内容生产和信息获取的成本。以前需要一个团队做的事情，现在可能几个人配合 AI 就能完成。

单纯卖人力、卖资源的 Agency，未来会越来越难。

反而比较看好新型 GTM 模式：以 Advisor/CMO 的角色深度加入团队，不只是帮项目宣发，而是一起做增长、做市场，拿到更长期的收益和杠杆。

另外也可以关注一些新的宣发渠道，比如众包内容分发、UGC 和短视频矩阵。对mkt感兴趣的可以研究一下@higgsfield 这个产品的官推运营/内容增长打法。（Insights from @otzgary )

4. 多关注那些在饭桌上不怎么说话的人。

他们可能才是真正的 Alpha。见到了太多低调的隐藏大佬。有些人完全不会主动介绍自己在做什么，但聊起来才发现非常有东西。
如果有一个人咋咋唬唬和你讲他做过什么，大概率只是一个BD。

这几天，多位从 CryptoBilis 买过 Ledger 硬件钱包的用户报告资产被盗。Ledger 已确认，受影响用户的设备里被植入了未经授权的硬件。具体原因和影响范围还在调查。

CryptoBilis 也卖过 OneKey、Trezor、Tangem、SafePal、imKey 等品牌，所以很多人来问我：我的 OneKey 还安全吗？

截至发文，我们没有收到 OneKey 用户因这次事件遭遇资产被盗的报告。但没收到报告，不等于没有风险。用户的资产安全不能靠运气，我们不会去赌。

我们已经终止了 CryptoBilis 的授权，它不再是 OneKey 的授权经销商。

从今天起，我们做三件事。

第一，不再新增经销商。

即日起，OneKey 停止新增任何经销商。

第二，所有现有经销商重新审查。

以前通过认证的，也全部重新审核、重新排查。经营主体核实不了、最终受益人说不清楚的，一律取消授权，从官网下架。

经销商网络会大幅缩小。硬件钱包关系到用户的资产，渠道必须管严。

审查完成后，我们会在官网公布完整的授权经销商名单。到时，不在名单上的，就不是 OneKey 的授权经销商。

第三，在 CryptoBilis 买过 OneKey 的符合条件用户，免费换新。

2026 年 3 月 1 日至本声明发布之日，在 CryptoBilis 买过 OneKey 硬件钱包的用户，不限型号，不管有没有激活、有没有用过，都可以免费换新。

为什么从 3 月 1 日算？CryptoBilis 的原联合创始人公开表示，公司在今年早些时候被收购，3 月完成了经营管理职责的交接。我们从 3 月 1 日开始覆盖，把整个交接月份和之后的购买都算进去。这个范围已经超过 180 天，我们宁可多覆盖一点。

换新设备由 OneKey 官方商店直接发货。原来是什么型号，就换同一型号的全新设备；如果那个型号没货了，就免费升级成更新的型号。

旧设备不用寄回，我们直接寄新的，直接从 OneKey 官网发货。

申请方法很简单：在 OneKey 官网点「客服」，或者打开 https://t.co/QG5Mu83nAr，提交工单。

标题写 CryptoBilis Replacement，附上：

- 购买凭证或小票，必须提供；
- 设备型号；
- 设备有没有激活、使用过。

申请截止：2026 年 12 月 31 日。

换新可以申请，资产安全不要等。

如果设备还没激活，先别激活，直接申请换新。

如果已经在用、里面还有资产，出于预防，请把旧助记词当作可能已经泄露来处理，尽快把资产转到使用全新助记词的钱包里，别为了等新设备而拖着。

手里有其他来源可信的硬件钱包，就在那台设备上生成全新的助记词，把资产转过去。暂时没有的话，可以在安全、可信的手机或电脑上，用 OneKey App 新建一个钱包，生成全新的助记词，先把资产转过去，作为临时过渡。

text:
Dusting off this tweet from April because this gap in shared understanding of LLM capability is *widening*. It's now less "two groups of people speaking past each other" and more a sharp funnel.

- Napkin math somewhere around 6B people (~75% of the population) have barely come in contact with LLMs at all.
- Around 1-2B (~20%) are casual and infrequent users of free-tier ChatGPT-like products. This group sees derpy chatbots and treats them a bit like a better Google search, a writing aid, or etc. Maybe an agent tries to book you a flight. I have non-tech friends who (reasonably, imo) say they have not much use for it at all. Even many professionals outside of math&code are in this tier. For example, execs and many other functions spend a lot of their time talking to other people, so while they understand what is happening intellectually, it is still second-hand and a bit abstract.
- Now we get to professional use of frontier-grade LLMs in math&code. Somewhere around 20M people (0.2%) see first-hand that large, complex projects that used to take them weeks/months can now be completed by agents with a prompt. Building apps, copying apps, translating apps, decompiling apps from binaries... This has all happened very quickly and recently - less than 1 year ago, I was writing code manually by hand, typing memorized computer code commands into a code editor character by character, occasionally pressing Tab to autocomplete a little chunk of code.
- And finally we get to the ~5,000 people (~0.00006%) with access to frontier-grade systems internally. The external world has seen the preview. It looks like swarms of thousands of agents collaborating over weeks on software mega projects: minting zero days, running cyber attacks and defenses at machine speeds, discovering new science, advancing the frontier of mathematics. Things that would have taken top professionals in the industry years of work. Meanwhile, human review and comprehension are starting to fall behind. For example, people are still involved in the "archeology" of the OpenAI-HF incident from many months ago. Mathematicians may be poring over the 722 manuscripts on frontier mathematics for a while.

The funnel is driven by a combination of factors:
1. The impact scales with ambition, problem size, and horizon. A question with a paragraph answer barely stresses the system. You need a reservoir of big, difficult problems that you really care about. This aspect drives the consumer / professional dimension of the funnel.
2. The jaggedness of the system (which I have written about a lot separately). Capability peaks in domains that are digital, verifiable and economically valuable. This is because LLM capability emerges from reinforcement learning on verifiable rewards on a curated environment mixture driven by revenue potential. This aspect primarily drives the area (e.g. math&code) dimension of the funnel.
3. Access. Free-tier, paid-tier, internal.

So this is the weirdness of the moment. The general public has mostly not interacted with these systems. When they have, it looks like a derpy chatbot. The majority of professionals still see only a modest uplift. And a small sliver of professionals are experiencing the vertigo of the curve going vertical. And it is all happening at the same time.
author: bitfalls
quoted_text:
Judging by my tl there is a growing gap in understanding of AI capability.

The first issue I think is around recency and tier of use. I think a lot of people tried the free tier of ChatGPT somewhere  last year and allowed it to inform their views on AI a little too much. This is a group of reactions laughing at various quirks of the models, hallucinations, etc. Yes I also saw the viral videos of OpenAI's Advanced Voice mode fumbling simple queries like "should I drive or walk to the carwash". The thing is that these free and old/deprecated models don't reflect the capability in the latest round of state of the art agentic models of this year, especially OpenAI Codex and Claude Code.

But that brings me to the second issue. Even if people paid $200/month to use the state of the art models, a lot of the capabilities are relatively "peaky" in highly technical areas. Typical queries around search, writing, advice, etc. are *not* the domain that has made the most noticeable and dramatic strides in capability. Partly,  this is due to the technical details of reinforcement learning and its use of verifiable rewards. But partly, it's also because these use cases are not sufficiently prioritized by the companies in their hillclimbing because they don't lead to as much $$$ value. The goldmines are elsewhere, and the focus comes along.

So that brings me to the second group of people, who *both* 1) pay for and use the state of the art frontier agentic models (OpenAI Codex / Claude Code) and 2) do so professionally in technical domains like programming, math and research. This group of people is subject to the highest amount of "AI Psychosis" because the recent improvements in these domains as of this year have been nothing short of staggering. When you hand a computer terminal to one of these models, you can now watch them melt programming problems that you'd normally expect to take days/weeks of work. It's this second group of people that assigns a much greater gravity to the capabilities, their slope, and various cyber-related repercussions.

TLDR the people in these two groups are speaking past each other. It really is simultaneously the case that OpenAI's free and I think slightly orphaned (?) "Advanced Voice Mode" will fumble the dumbest questions in your Instagram's reels and *at the same time*, OpenAI's highest-tier and paid Codex model will go off for 1 hour to coherently restructure an entire code base, or find and exploit vulnerabilities in computer systems. This part really works and has made dramatic strides because 2 properties: 1) these domains offer explicit reward functions that are verifiable meaning they are easily amenable to reinforcement learning training (e.g. unit tests passed yes or no, in contrast to writing, which is much harder to explicitly judge),  but also 2) they are a lot more valuable in b2b settings, meaning that the biggest fraction of the team is focused on improving them. So here we are.

Monad：一个足以承载全球资金的网络，主网一周年，Open上几个比较硬的更新：

1. 隐私结算功能（Private Settlement）：  
@category_xyz 在Open主舞台宣布的。Monad L1上直接做机密执行域，不用另起一条私有链。每个域通过L1上的标准EVM hub合约启用，不需要分叉也不需要协议升级。域内交易、状态、合约代码端到端加密，连L1本身都读不到；跨域转账也是加密的，地址和金额对外不可见。机构自己定验证者集合、信任模型、访问规则和管辖权，默认谁都看不到，审计或监管可以按需给权限。同时域还直接接到Monad的共享流动性，结算是原子的
现在还是设计方案，Category Labs在跟早期设计伙伴推进，还没上线。发布前有过“Privacy is coming”的预热。  
https://t.co/jDM67nqYDv  
https://t.co/wlb0R3sU7Y  

why matters：机构（银行、基金、交易台、企业财资）最怕的就是链上全透明。他们现在要么不上链，要么自己搞私有链把流动性切碎。这个设计如果跑通，等于让这些机构能直接用公开链的速度和流动性，同时业务还保密。对Monad来说，这是把大额资金和真实业务流程拉进来的关键入口，后面稳定币、RWA、支付的体量都有可能跟着放大

2. 股票上链，xStocks原生上Monad：
@valgui在台上宣布@xStocksFi 原生部署到Monad，覆盖1100+代币化美股和ETF。代币直接在Monad上铸造和结算，不是从别的链桥过来。1:1对应底层证券，ERC-20形态，可以往DEX、借贷、钱包里组合
这跟 @aave 之前提的V4代币化股票hub提案也能对上。链上后续也有合约部署和铸造的讨论  
https://t.co/dO3Bzok7O8  

why matters：股票类资产是全球最大的流动性池之一。原生上链意味着不用桥，可以直接在Monad做交易、抵押、组合。对交易者来说多了24/7的股票敞口，对DeFi协议来说多了新的抵押品和交易对，对持有美股的人来说多了链上使用场景。如果流动性慢慢起来，Monad的交易量和TVL都有机会从纯crypto资产往传统资产延伸，可以关心Monad上几个DEX的进展@perpltrade @hellotradeapp @KuruExchange 等还有几个还没宣发的

Meta's chief AI officer Alexandr Wang says @ElonMusk taught him something that helped shape Meta's AI strategy

You don't necessarily need thousands of engineers to move fast.

You need a small group of exceptionally talented people, very little hierarchy, and the freedom to get things done.

Wang says he brought that idea to Mark Zuckerberg, who embraced it as a central part of their approach to AI.

Meta, a company with enormous resources, is now deliberately borrowing from the way Elon builds small, highly technical teams.

At some point, adding more people stops making you faster.

And in AI, where the technology can change dramatically in a matter of months, the speed of a decision can matter as much as the resources behind it.

text:
最近重新翻了 Dario Amodei 的几次访谈，我觉得我们可能一直低估了 Anthropic 当年的战略判断。

2024 年，OpenAI 正忙着做语音、搜索、视频，想把 ChatGPT 变成所有人的 AI 入口。

Anthropic 却开始在编程能力上建立优势。那年 6 月，Claude 3.5 Sonnet 在内部 Agent 编程测试中的成功率达到 64%，上一代 Opus 只有 38%。

当时我觉得这很容易理解。ChatGPT 的消费者市场已经有了巨大的先发优势，Anthropic 先抓住程序员，找到一群真正愿意为模型能力持续付费的用户。

但 Dario 后来在一次访谈里提到了一个更重要的理由，模型越擅长编程，就越能帮助 Anthropic 开发下一代模型。

编程是少数几种能够直接反过来推动 AI 自身发展的能力。

模型可以写代码、运行测试、发现错误、反复修改，很多结果都有明确的验证标准。更重要的是，开发前沿模型本身就需要大量工程工作，从训练基础设施到实验脚本，再到性能优化和调试。

当 Claude 开始接管这些工作，Anthropic 的研发团队就可以用上一代模型，加速下一代模型的开发。

Anthropic 今年披露，截至 2026 年 5 月，内部合入代码库的代码已有超过 80% 由 Claude 编写。2026 年第二季度，工程师人均每天合入的代码行数约为 2024 年的 8 倍。

与此同时，Claude Code 还成为了一个成功的商业产品。Anthropic 在今年 2 月披露，其年化收入运行率已经超过 25 亿美元。

Anthropic 找到了一个既能从外部客户那里赚钱，又能直接提高自己研发效率的市场。模型每进步一次，产品就更有价值，内部的研究员也能获得更强的工具。

Anthropic 最厉害的地方，是很早意识到了编程能力的特殊性，并且愿意持续投入。

当然，今天距离真正意义上的递归自我改进还有距离。AI 已经很擅长执行实验，但决定研究什么、判断什么方向值得投入，依然高度依赖人类。

可一旦这部分能力也逐渐被自动化，前沿模型公司的竞争逻辑就会发生很大的变化。

我觉得可以设定一个新的指标，一家 AI 公司发布新模型后，需要多长时间才能让它实质性地参与下一代模型的研发。

未来决定竞争差距的，可能就是这个指标。

Today we are releasing the new Injective Whitepaper.

It is the first full rewrite since our original paper in December 2018, which described a front-running-resistant exchange protocol on Ethereum.

Eight years later, Injective has evolved greatly into becoming a layer-1 blockchain for institutional-grade finance and tokenization. Every layer of the protocol exists to issue real-world assets and give them real utility across markets, applications, and AI agents.

Inside the paper

→ Asset issuance. Native RWA tokenization with role-based permissions over mint, send, receive, and burn, plus programmable receive hooks and sealable namespaces

→ RWA exposure. iAssets, stablecoin-margined, oracle-priced derivatives that track external assets with no wrapping or pre-funding

→ Trading. Tokenized assets trade on a fully onchain CLOB where each block runs a sealed frequent batch auction at a uniform clearing price, resisting front-running and ordering MEV

→ Settlement. BFT consensus with a greater-than-two-thirds commit threshold delivers deterministic finality with ~600ms blocks

→ Composability. Native EVM and WASM in one canonical state, with the MultiVM Token Standard keeping a single bank-module balance per asset, exposed to Solidity through precompiles

→ Derivatives. Perpetuals with time-weighted premium funding, initial and maintenance margin checks, reduce-only liquidations, and insurance funds

→ Agentic finance. AI agents operate on tokenized assets through MCP servers, policy-bounded signing, and x402 machine payments in USDC

→ Value accrual. Onchain protocol revenue flows to the recurring Community BuyBack for $INJ

The paper formalizes each mechanism, from the consensus threshold and block lifecycle to the batch clearing rule, oracle accounting, derivative risk checks, permission model, and dynamic issuance controller.

From issuance to settlement, one chain built for the full lifecycle of tokenized finance.

text:
AI × DePIN  重新利用已经存在的硬件是一个值得关注的方向

全球有大量智能手机每天处于闲置状态，如果这些设备也能参与 AI 计算，能释放多大的潜力？

@Acurast 已经在尝试这个方向, 值得重点关注！

目前 Acurast 的网络规模：目前网络已接入约 30 万至 32 万多个计算单元，覆盖 175 多个国家。

核心优势在哪里？

第一，算力来自现有设备。
用户通过 Processor 应用接入网络，不需要自己购买专业 GPU，也不必建设数据中心。对于大量中小规模的计算任务，这种模式提供了另一种选择。

第二，计算过程可以验证。
Acurast 利用 TEE 可信执行环境与硬件远程证明，让任务能够在受保护的环境中运行，并验证设备和执行代码的真实性。

这对隐私敏感的 AI 推理、自动化任务和 AI Agent 都有实际意义。

第三，已经开始尝试真实 AI 工作负载。
今年 9 月，Acurast 将 Laya 决策模型部署到全球手机节点。它面向分类、评分、内容审核、提示注入检测等结构化决策任务，可以在手机 CPU 上执行。

这类任务未必需要昂贵的 GPU 集群，却需要稳定、可靠且能够保护数据的执行环境。

我个人更看重 Acurast 的应用边界

手机算力不可能全面取代大型数据中心，但 AI 计算也不一定全部需要集中在云端。

越来越多 AI Agent 需要处理用户数据、执行自动化工作流，或者完成轻量级实时决策时，分布式、可验证的边缘算力就有了发挥空间。

所以，AI × DePIN 的长期机会，取决于这些设备究竟能完成多少有价值的工作。

如果这条路径跑通，全球分散的手机就有机会成为去中心化 AI 基础设施的一部分。

接下来，重点关注三个指标：真实计算需求、网络激励的可持续性，以及 $ACU 能否捕获网络增长带来的价值。

@EchoHunt_ai #Acurast #ACU #DePIN

text:
WANTED: how it was made

The song
- It started as a piano piece: the Allegretto from Beethoven's 7th Symphony, using piano. Took the notes from the public-domain score and re-performed the theme voiced over the accompaniment, phrase rubato, legato, and a custom pedal engine. Then transposed the piece to F minor.
- The lyrics were written as a duet between a bounty hunter and the AI he's hunting. They went from "Bounty On Your Head" to WANTED over three drafts.
- I took the piano into Suno with a style prompt and the duet lyrics and turned it into the song, a 4:13 duet at 149 BPM. The style: future house, detuned chord stabs, his voice through a vocoder, hers clean, lo-fi tape wobble.
- I developed the story with Grok Bot.

Mapping the song
- The track was split into vocal and instrumental stems, transcribed word by word, and beat-tracked.
- Pitch analysis of the vocal stem showed who sings every line: his vocoder baritone or her voice.
- The edit is 128 shots, each cut on the beat grid. Cuts in the drum sections land on the kick drum, and every big section change gets a cut.

The stills
- Every line was storyboarded, first as late-90s cel animation with Grok Imagine, then switched to photoreal.
- 128 photoreal stills, with both leads locked to cast photos.
- Two full review passes at full size redid 26 stills and fixed continuity, like what shows through the cockpit canopy and her costume in the lab.
- Upscaled locally to 8K on my GPU:
  - a FLUX detail pass in tiles
  - a second pass that redraws only the eyes and locks their colour
  - a colour match back to the original still, overall and region by region
  - an automatic check of every upscale

The video
- We looked at Grok Imagine for the singing first, but its API can't lip-sync to an existing vocal, so the sung shots went to MiniMax H3.
- Every shot starts on its own still.
- Shots without singing: ByteDance Seedance 2.5. API Drafts at 480p came first, then 1080p. Start and end frames were set for shots that needed exact action, like the bullet sliding into the chamber.
- Sung shots: MiniMax H3 at 2K, driven by the real vocal, so the mouths lock to the song. sync. so was tested and dropped.
- Every take was checked: faces against the cast photos, lip sync against the vocal, and timing slips fixed to the frame.
- Two rounds of fixes:
  - frames edited with Google's Nano Banana Pro: her cuffs, the gun, the rail yard, the ship diving into the wormhole
  - re-takes
  - one re-timed cut
- The last 65 shots were remade in MiniMax H3 at 2K.

Post-processing
- Shot matching, so clips from different models look like one film.
- A film grade: rich blacks, teal shadows and warm highlights. Her red and the bounty-screen green stay strong.
- A separate colour for each world: Ganymede cold and wet, Europa icy, Io hot, space inky, the dawn golden.
- Temporal clean-up removes the AI shimmer, then one even layer of 35mm grain goes on top.
- Film optics: halation, bloom, a light vignette, chromatic aberration, and anamorphic lens streaks on the brightest moments.
- Text fixes in post: misspelled text baked into the footage was re-lettered and tracked to its surface: SLOW BURN on the hull, PROPERTY on her arm.
- Graphics drawn in code:
  - location titles
  - the bounty and hunter counters
  - DEAD OR ALIVE on every hook: dead in green, alive in red, and DEAD struck out at the end of each chorus
  - flash frames on the gunshot and the gate
  - the voice log typed out on the spoken words
- The ending: the AgenC Studios ident on an amber CRT, built from the official logo, then the Tetsuo SI card.

Sound
- The song remastered.
- Spotting: five Opus sub-agents spotted every shot frame by frame for sound effects.
- 106 effects generated with ElevenLabs. An AudioSet classifier checked each one for stray music or voices, and the bad ones were regenerated.
- Placement:
  - each effect lands on its exact frame (the gunshot hits on the muzzle flash)
  - each is panned to where its source is on screen
  - each sits in the room of its scene: a tight cockpit, a wooden noodle stall, a huge hangar
- Ambience runs under every scene, and the clips' own sound is used where it was clean.
- The CRT ident has its own sound design: power-on, hum, power-off.

How Opus 5.5 ran it
- Opus 5.5 built and ran the pipeline, and did the review, the edit, the finish.
- It reviewed by looking: frame by frame, every take, every cut, and every graphic checked against the faces.
- Sub-agent teams took the big parallel jobs.
- Local models worked alongside the APIs: FLUX for upscaling, WhisperX for transcription, demucs for stems, ArcFace and YOLO face detection for identity checks, and an AudioSet model for the audio. The grade, the graphics and the mix are all code.

Tried and dropped
- SeedVR2 local video upscaling
- optical-flow detail transfer
- sync. so lip sync
- a 2.39 widescreen letterbox
- a full 8K pass on every still (stopped at 81 of 128) the rest were done in 4k. My GPUs were melting.

STRC 从入坑到盈利：套利自救之三

在前面两篇的回本路径中，有两种套利方式：

1/ apxUSD 与 apyUSD 的脱锚套利；

2/ apxUSD、apyUSD、sUSDat 与合约开空 STRC 的价差套利；

让我们回到公式，既然 apxUSD 和 sUSDat 都与 STRC 相关，那么公式可以转换：

sUSDat ≈ apxUSD × y ≈ STRC × 0.01 × y

也就是说，sUSDat 与 apxUSD 之间也可以做脱锚套利。

操作上说白话，就是当 apxUSD 相比 sUSDat 的系数关系跌超时，抄底相对便宜的一方，等待价格收敛。

通常是 apxUSD 下跌，而 sUSDat 稳定。

不过在连续吃了一个多星期的 apxUSD 和 sUSDat 的锚定互换后，机会突然变少了。

发现居然有人组了 apxUSD 与 sUSDat 的 LP，导致它们之间的汇率越来越稳定。

接着我也转向去做 LP，并且只在极度波动的情况下才进行互换，每天赚个 $300-500 是很简单的。

不过随着组建 LP 的仓位越来越大，割肉 apxUSD 的人越来越少，机会也越来越少。

到这时，时间已经来到 6 月底，STRC 的价格也回归到 80 左右，我已接近回本，记得回本价是 82。

接下来，便是盈利之路！

接着看，apxUSD 与 sUSDat 可以理解为同一标的的汇率差导致的脱锚套利，以及通过提供 apxUSD 与 sUSDat 的 LP，可实现自平衡与抽税。

核心还是同一件事：系数关系一旦错位，就会出现可操作的窗口。

但窗口往往很短，深度和抽水会快速吃掉利润。

不过在步入 7 月后，之前三种套利方式的利润，在不上杠杆的情况下，利润很难超过 1%，而上杠杆，深度又不够。

主要原因还是 6 月太多人割肉离场，剩下的大多数人要么沉默等待 STRC 回锚，要么已经麻木了，当时链上和群里都能看到，大规模资金流出之后，价差出现的频率明显下降。

但我一直到 9 月中旬还持有 apyUSD 和 sUSDat，直到最近才清空 apyUSD。

当然不是因为产生了感情，是因为还有套利空间与利润。

在 apxUSD 与 sUSDat 汇率差机会越来越少后，我就在找另外一条路，但路其实早就有了，依旧公式先行。

继续推导与演变公式。

不难发现，sUSDat 与 apyUSD 也存在系数关系：

sUSDat × x ≈ STRC × y

在这个公式的逻辑下，操作上其实与 apxUSD 和 sUSDat 的汇率差操作基本一致，依旧是互换，依旧是LP。

最疯狂的一天，某个大户单日抛了 200 万的 apyUSD，导致我其中一个 $20K 的 LP 钱包，单日收入超过 $3000。

这种单日大额抛售带来的窗口，之后很少出现。。

不过整体收入依旧是递减的，从 7 月到 9 月，虽然日结收入偶有爆发，但每天的利润也从日常的 $1-2000，到后来不足 $100。

这个递减也很容易理解：即使 STRC 跌幅很大，大家很恐慌，Apyx 项目方的做法也非常可恶，但存量资金是有限的，割肉的肯定是慢慢减少的。

而最相信的人，往往受伤最深。

所以最开始的大规模资金流出是来自 apxUSD。

毕竟它从稳定币变成不是稳定，也没办法赎回（后来可以赎回了，但官方抽税严重），而且价格还一直追不上 STRC。

帖子写到这里，通过分享的这些路径，我早早就回本并实现了持续两个月的盈利。

在配图的左边为 sUSDat 与 apyUSD 的汇率走势，右边为 sUSDat 与 apyUSD 的汇率走势，这其中每一个波动都是机会。

系列的套利复盘到此也告一段落～

下一篇，我想结合最近的阅读计划，聊聊这波经历后，我接下来怎么看、怎么做。

以上仅为信息分享，不构成任何投资建议。

持续进化中的 BitHappy

继上一篇的 apxUSD 与 apyUSD 脱锚套利后，我已经看到了解套的希望。

核心观察是：只要系数关系存在，只要出现价差就有机会赚一笔，虽然时间窗口往往很短。

apyUSD ≈ apxUSD × x ≈ STRC × 0.01 × x。

apxUSD ≈ STRC × 0.01

apyUSD ≈ STRC × 0.01 × x

sUSDat ≈ STRC × 0.01 × y

恰好整个 6 月，STRC 相关代币的持有者都惶恐不安，中间有数不清的人割肉跑路，而每次割肉都会产生价差。

当时群里和链上都能看到，有人选择直接离场，也有人按系数关系在找机会。

只是由于 apxUSD 和 apyUSD 的链上抽水太高，价差如果不高于 0.5% 的话，基本没有利润空间。

而 sUSDat 又太稳定，很少给机会。

我手里还是只有 sUSDat 和 apyUSD，应该如何继续辗转腾挪呢？

且等下篇更新套利新的姿势！

Claude Code 跑长任务，先把模型和任务分工排清楚。

开源 Skill phase-plan，会读取仓库里的计划、Issue 和 TODO，把剩余工作拆成阶段：改哪些文件、怎样验收、建议用什么模型和思考强度，一张表列明。

执行时有个实用的取舍：

• 短任务留在单个会话里，减少子 Agent 重读上下文的开销
• 长任务中修改文件互不重叠的阶段，可交给子 Agent 并行处理

作者公布的一项 Swift 长任务测试中，Sonnet 加 Skill 并行执行后，平均费用从 $4.09 降到 $1.97，耗时从约 17 分钟降到约 6 分钟，两种配置都通过了 29 项隐藏测试。

text:
I analyzed the Ohio telephone conversation about Talarico at Lindner. It appears likely to be an authentic, i.e., not AI-generated. Here is the analysis. It is lengthy. You can point @grok
at it for a summary or to ask questions.

# Is the Lindner call audio AI-generated? Feature report and assessment

Checked 2026-10-11 by the interactive session. The material is the three released recordings (Current Revolt 6:40, Amacher 0:55, Sortor 0:47) and Amacher's call-log screenshot.

Method:
- **Measurements on the audio:** `forensics/forensics_signal.txt`, `forensics_align.txt`, `forensics_noisefloor.txt`, `forensics_speaker_band.txt`.
- **Two model listening passes:** `forensics/gemini_forensic__*.json`.
- **Four open deepfake-speech classifiers with positive and negative controls:** see "Classifier results" below.

Claude cannot hear audio. Everything below comes from measurements, transcripts and model outputs.

## Three separate questions

1. **Is it AI-generated?** Synthetic text-to-speech or voice cloning, as opposed to real people on a real phone call.

2. **Did the call really reach Lindner, and is the speaker a Lindner employee?** A real call to an impostor or a staged human call would pass every AI test.

3. **Is what she said accurate?** No audio test can answer this.

This report answers 1 and part of 2.

## Features that point to a real recorded phone call
| Feature | What was measured or heard | Weight |
|---|---|---|
| Two channel signatures | The staffer and the IVR are cut hard at about 3.8–4.2 kHz (−37 to −44 dB at 3.8–4.2 kHz, about −55 to −65 dB above 4 kHz): a narrowband phone network. The caller's voice carries energy to 8–10 kHz (about −20 to −33 dB): a wideband local phone mic. The difference holds for every turn of both speakers. A fake would have to synthesize two voices and then model two different channels consistently, including in overlaps | strong |

| Speaker attribution by channel works | Per 100-ms frame, the staffer is always telephone-band and the caller always wideband, so turns can be told apart mechanically. This includes brief interjections ("Oh", "Okay") and the overlap at 6:18–6:22 | moderate |

| Continuous line noise under the key line | The telephone-band noise floor sits at −25 to −31 dB through the 6-s pause at 5:58–6:04 and the key sentence at 6:04–6:14, with no steps or resets. A spliced-in sentence usually leaves a noise-floor discontinuity at its edges | moderate (1-s resolution) |

| The three releases are one recording | Amacher's and Sortor's clips are re-encodings of the last 55.1 s and 47.0 s of the 6:40 file: sample correlation 0.986 and 0.998, with residuals −16 and −24 dB (codec loss). There are no internal splices in either clip | moderate (consistency, not authenticity) |

| Matches the call log | The screenshot shows calls to 513-536-4673, Lindner's published number: 8:53 (2 min), 8:56 (2 min), 8:59 (6 min). The recording is 6:40 and opens with that number's IVR menu prompt. The caller says "did I just talk to you like two minutes ago?", which fits the 8:56 call | moderate (the screenshot itself could be faked) |

| Spontaneous conversational behavior | Dense false starts and self-repairs from both speakers; an improvised spelling alphabet ("Todd, Apple, Larry…"); turn-taking overlaps and an immediate repair ("Mm, I'm sorry"); variable response latency; a 3-minute hold and a "let me go to a computer" errand | moderate. Current voice AI can imitate disfluency, but rarely live two-party overlap over a phone channel |

| Background activity | Other voices and (per both Gemini passes) typing behind the staffer, continuous under her speech. The publisher muted two stretches as background staff talk about "lab work, medications, and what may be other patients" (Current Revolt) | weak to moderate (background can be mixed in, and the muted parts cannot be checked) |

| Gemini listening passes | Gemini 3.1 Pro and 3.7 Flash both judged both voices real (99/100) and heard breaths, natural sibilants and no vocoder artifacts | weak. LLM listening is not a validated detector, and both models wrongly said the caller was also phone-band-limited, which the measurements contradict |

## Features that point away from authenticity, or limit what can be said

| Feature | What was found | Weight |

|---|---|---|

| The file is edited | Two publisher mutes are exact digital zeros: 1:03.1–1:06.2 and 1:13.1–1:16.3, labeled on screen. The 3-min hold, 2:38–5:45, is 186.8 s of exact digital zero. Mutes cannot hide AI, but anything said in those 3–4 s and during the hold cannot be checked | limits the record; not evidence of AI |

| Telephone band limits the forensics | Narrowband audio removes the high frequencies where many cloning artifacts show, and lowers classifier reliability (see the controls below) | limits confidence |

| The caller's channel is "clean" | The caller's side has little background noise, which suits a phone with noise suppression. Weak either way | neutral |

## Assessment

**AI generation.** Every feature that can be measured fits a genuine recording of a two-party phone call: a narrowband far end (staffer and IVR), a wideband near end (caller), continuous line noise through the key sentence, and natural overlap. I found nothing pointing to text-to-speech or voice cloning, apart from the disclosed edits. **My judgment: very unlikely to be AI-generated (roughly 90–95%).** It is not higher because:

- the band-limited far end hides some artifact classes;

- a sophisticated forger could, in principle, synthesize the staffer and pass her through a real phone path;

- the classifiers have limited validity on phone audio (below).

## Classifier results: they failed their controls, so they are uninformative

I ran four open wav2vec2 deepfake-speech classifiers from Hugging Face on 4-s windows of the call and on controls:

- MelodyMachine/Deepfake-audio-detection-V2;
- mo-thecreator/Deepfake-audio-detection;
- Gustking/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-deepfake-audio-classification;
- garystafford/wav2vec2-deepfake-voice-detector.
The controls:
- known AI speech: three Gemini-TTS lines written to mimic the call;
- known human speech: three Wikimedia "Spoken Wikipedia" readings, two uploaded in 2014 and one recorded in 2023.

Each control was run both as recorded (wideband) and through a simulated 8 kHz μ-law phone line. Full table: `forensics/classifier_table.txt` and `forensics/detect_results.json`.

Mean P(fake) by speaker or control (window counts in the table):

| Model | Call: staffer | Call: caller | Known AI (TTS), wideband / phone | Known human 2014 (two readers), wideband / phone | Known human 2023 |

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| MelodyMachine | 1.00 | 0.96 | 0.00 / 0.00 | 0.83–1.00 / 1.00 | 0.00 |
| mo-thecreator | 0.96 | 0.89 | 0.00–0.67 / 0.50–0.67 | 0.83–1.00 / 1.00 | 0.00–0.33 |
| Gustking | 0.69 | 0.34 | 0.16–0.53 / 0.13–0.37 | 0.62–0.79 / 0.66–0.88 | 0.10–0.14 |
| garystafford | 0.82 | 0.52 | 0.49–0.97 / 0.42–0.86 | Earth 0.96–0.99; Universe 0.01–0.12 | 0.27–0.39 |
**Reading.** Read naively, three of four classifiers would call the staffer's voice "fake". But the same classifiers:
- call real human speech recorded in 2014 "fake" with the same confidence (1.00 / 1.00 / 0.66–0.88 / 0.99);
- mostly call the Gemini AI voice "real": MelodyMachine scored it 0.00, and Gustking scored it 0.13–0.53.

Only garystafford leaned the right way on the AI controls, and it still flagged one of the human readers at 0.99. No model separates the known-AI from the known-human controls. Their high scores on the call's narrowband staffer channel are what domain shift looks like: these models are trained on clean wideband datasets, and both telephone audio and older encodings look "out of distribution" to them. **The classifier scores therefore carry no weight either way.** Do not cite them as evidence of AI generation or of authenticity. A calibrated telephone-domain detector would be needed: a commercial service, or an ASVspoof-style model validated on phone audio. Sending the audio to an outside service needs Kevin's yes.

**Net assessment unchanged.** The judgment of "very unlikely to be AI-generated (roughly 90–95%)" rests on the channel and continuity measurements and the conversational structure above, not on the classifiers.

---

## Corrections after audit A-S6 (2026-10-12T05:42:00Z)

- **A-S6-AI-06:** the "90–95%" figure above is a subjective, uncalibrated estimate. No validated telephone-domain model or likelihood ratio supports a number, and the classifier controls failed. It is withdrawn as a probability. What stands: the measured properties (two consistent channel signatures, located publisher mutes, no detected hard cut at the key lines). Endpoint identity and the accuracy of what was said remain unresolved.

- **A-S6-AI-04:** the "−25 to −31 dB through the key sentence" range does not hold for every second in forensics_noisefloor.txt. The FFT normalization is uncalibrated (it also produces positive dB values). The supportable statement is "no detected hard cut or noise-floor step at the key lines", not proof of no splice.

- **A-S6-AI-07:** forensics_signal.txt is a preliminary log with invalid correlation values above 1, and it is superseded. Only forensics_align.txt (r = 0.986 and 0.998, independently reproduced by the auditor as 0.988 and 0.998) is used for numbers.
author: kevinnbass

text: The analysis finds the Lindner call audio consistent with a genuine two-party phone recording, not AI-generated. Key evidence: distinct channel signatures (narrowband phone for the staffer/IVR, wideband for the caller) holding across turns and overlaps; continuous noise floor with no hard cuts at key lines; matching shorter clips as re-encodings of the full file; natural disfluencies, overlaps, and background activity. Deepfake classifiers failed controls and are uninformative. Probability estimate withdrawn as subjective. This addresses only synthetic generation, not whether the staffer was authentic or the statements accurate.

text:
A $30M investment in a project that's moving away from its own L1.

You don't see that every day in crypto.

That's exactly what's happening with @datafdn as it prepares to move from its own chain to Sui.

I actually find the decision more interesting than the headline number.

For years, launching your own L1 was a big deal.
Your own chain, validators, ecosystem, the whole thing.
And then you have to keep all of it running while trying to get people to use your product.

Running a chain and building a product are two very different jobs. You can spend years improving infrastructure and still have no clear reason for anyone to show up.

@datafdn used to be Story Protocol. In June, it narrowed its focus to AI training data and Trace, a product recording receipts for rights-cleared data.

Trace has passed 250M receipts since then.

That's a lot of activity. I'd still want to see how much of it turns into lasting demand. Receipts alone don't tell you that.

The team is now choosing to build Trace on Sui rather than keep maintaining a standalone L1.
Walrus can handle storage, while DATA puts more attention into the product and getting it used.

Sui gets something out of it too.
Trace brings rights-cleared AI training data into an ecosystem with tools for storing and working with that data.

And Sui Foundation is putting $30M behind that direction, becoming DATA's largest institutional holder.

It's easy to keep adding things to a roadmap. Cutting something you've already spent years building is a much harder decision.

It doesn't guarantee anything.
The migration is still ahead, with more details and timelines to come. $DATA remains the protocol token, and nothing changes for holders immediately.

But I'd rather watch a team make one product work than keep adding things to a roadmap just because they can.

text:
To the Hyperliquid community,

I'm not sure the algorithm will put this in front of you. If it did, hello. I'm ZK, and we're building OpenETF.

OpenETF is an open, composable ETF layer on Hyperliquid. Anyone can create a fund without asking us: a basket of spot assets, a perps strategy, a market-neutral book. Investors hold its shares in their own wallets, as a token they can transfer. The manager trades the fund under public rules, but cannot withdraw its assets.

That part is fairly simple to describe. What took us longer were the questions that come once someone else's money is inside.

Building on HyperCore and HyperEVM changed how we answered them. Every order, fill and liquidation on HyperCore is public. Contracts on HyperEVM can hold assets and trade on that same order book. Anyone can build on it without asking. We have not worked on infrastructure this transparent and this composable before, and it has been more fun than we expected. It also sets a standard: if the venue is this open, a fund built on it should be too. Thank you to the team and the community who made it that way.

A few things follow from that, and I think they are where we differ most from funds as they have worked so far.

The share is a token in your own wallet, not a line in someone else's books. Ownership should not depend on whoever keeps the ledger, and you should be able to move what you own without asking anyone.

A manager can trade the fund but cannot withdraw its assets. Many of the worst moments for investors have not come from bad trades. They have come from money going where it should not. So we separate the power to trade from the power to move money, and every trade through our execution service is checked before it is signed.

We do not pick which funds get seen. Whoever decides what people see ends up steering where the money goes. We want a fund be found for what it has done, not because we chose it.

The rest is in the piece below. We feel pretty settled on the principles. The details will keep changing as we learn. If something here would keep you from using it, now is the most useful time to tell me.

Hyperliquid feels like open water. This is us calling out across it to anyone who might want to build, manage or invest here. If you run a vault, trade for a living, or build on HyperEVM, my DMs are open.

If you'd rather ask a machine first, there is a prompt in the reply below.

Thanks for reading.

text:
用 AirDrop 传专业设备拍的超大照片和视频（动辄 20GB）一直很痛苦。

更难受的是 iPhone 的“文件”和“相册”之间几乎不互通：在“文件”里解压一个大包，想全部存进相册，没有进度，还经常闪退，存一半都不知道存到哪了。

这两天啵啵自己把它解决了。她完全没写过代码，让 Dots 操控云端电脑写了个 App，拿到她的 Mac 上，用数据线直接装到了自己手机上。没有 Apple 开发者账号，整个 App 只有 66KB。

功能很简单：把超大的 ZIP 解压之后一张一张存进相册，能看到进度，中断了还能接着存，已经存过的会自动跳过。

刚才实测 953 个文件、15.32GB，4 分钟左右全部存完。

以前遇到这种事儿只能忍或者不断自己再试试，现在不会写代码的人也能花两天给自己做个工具了，今年 vibe coding 的发展可以说是真的震撼。

text:
为了平衡能以个人套餐限制下的最优经济性与最佳智力，兼顾并行速率，并且能扛下 5-hour 的 usage cap 不断片（不损失 session 缓存），当前比较均衡的方式是：
1. 以 fable 5.1 ultracode 的执行外壳主导工程
2. 但 harness/hook 标注必须要求 ultracode 的 subagent 调度必须是 opus 5.5，不允许 subagent 也调用 fable，否则几乎一定会打到 5-hour cap。
3. fable 的价值在于精确统筹调度，opus 的价值在于高性价比执行。
4. 主 context 容量设到 600-700k 之间，越接近 1M token 越贵，质量也越差；调太低显然也不行，短任务的 compact 损失的质量和时间严重。

text:
ZEROBASE WEEKLY 10.5–10.11

ZBT traded a wider, softer range this week, mostly between $0.076 and $0.090. It opened October 5 near $0.086, pushed toward $0.090 early in the week, then sold off with the broader market to a low around $0.076 on October 8 before a modest recovery to close near $0.082, down roughly 5%. Spot volume expanded on the decline days (into the $5–12 million range) and liquidity stayed orderly, with the bid holding and spreads not blowing out on the dip.

Crypto spent the week digesting elevated yields, oil volatility, and a midweek equity scare. Total market capitalization finished near $2.80 trillion, down about 3.6% from the October 4 wrap. Bitcoin dominance edged up to 59.5% from 58.9%; Ether’s share slipped to 10.9%. Only 9 of the top 50 coins finished higher, and the median move was about −5.3%.

Bitcoin opened the period near $86,600–$86,700 on October 5 (the week’s high), faded through midweek, printed a low around $80,650 on October 8, then stabilized and closed the wrap near $83,000, down about 2.6% on the week. That still left it roughly 34% below its all-time high and up about 6.9% over 30 days. 

Ether tracked lower with more damage, touching about $2,414 before finishing near $2,502, down about 7.3% on the week and essentially flat over 30 days. Solana lost closer to 9–10% and traded near $110 by the weekend.

The 10-year Treasury yield opened the week at 5.311% (its highest since 2002) and stayed elevated in the low-to-mid 5.2–5.3% area, touching higher midweek after the September FOMC minutes showed most participants still expecting another hike by year-end. 

Brent crude rose about 2.4% to near $104.70 on residual Iran-related energy and shipping concerns plus weather effects; WTI held near $91–92. U.S. equities absorbed the crosscurrents better than crypto: the S&P 500 gained 1.15% to close at 7,811.54 (setting a record close on Tuesday at 7,818.93), the Nasdaq added 0.64% to about 27,366, and the Dow rose 0.93% to 51,655. 

A Thursday Financial Times report that OpenAI’s annualized revenue ran roughly $20 billion below earlier figures briefly pressured chip and AI-related names before a Friday recovery.

U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded roughly $680 million in net outflows over the five sessions to October 9 (with the bulk on October 7–8), reversing the prior week’s modest inflows; Ether products also saw large withdrawals in a similar range. 

Liquidations spiked midweek—more than $1 billion in leveraged positions were cleared in a 24-hour window on October 8, the large majority longs—as Bitcoin briefly tested the low $80,000s. Funding rates on major pairs stayed near neutral to mildly positive, and Bitcoin futures open interest declined roughly 7% on Binance over the week.

Crypto Fear & Greed Index cooled from the low 70s (greed) early in the week toward the mid-50s to low 60s (neutral/greed) by the weekend.

On-chain signals stayed relatively constructive through the price action. A large share of supply remains in longer-term hands, futures leverage was reduced rather than expanded into the dip, and quieter sessions showed net coins moving off exchanges. Stablecoin supply edged lower by roughly $900 million on the week.

In summary, October 5–11 was a digestion and deleveraging week after the early-October probe above $86,000–$87,000. High yields, residual geopolitical oil risk, and the midweek AI-revenue scare weighed more heavily on crypto than on equities. 

Bitcoin’s relative outperformance and rising dominance, together with cleared leverage and stable longer-term holder structure, left the market consolidating lower but not broken, with the $80,000–$82,000 zone as the nearer reference.

quoted_text:
这几天，多位从 CryptoBilis 买过 Ledger 硬件钱包的用户报告资产被盗。Ledger 已确认，受影响用户的设备里被植入了未经授权的硬件。具体原因和影响范围还在调查。

CryptoBilis 也卖过 OneKey、Trezor、Tangem、SafePal、imKey 等品牌，所以很多人来问我：我的 OneKey 还安全吗？

截至发文，我们没有收到 OneKey 用户因这次事件遭遇资产被盗的报告。但没收到报告，不等于没有风险。用户的资产安全不能靠运气，我们不会去赌。

我们已经终止了 CryptoBilis 的授权，它不再是 OneKey 的授权经销商。

从今天起，我们做三件事。

第一，不再新增经销商。

即日起，OneKey 停止新增任何经销商。

第二，所有现有经销商重新审查。

以前通过认证的，也全部重新审核、重新排查。经营主体核实不了、最终受益人说不清楚的，一律取消授权，从官网下架。

经销商网络会大幅缩小。硬件钱包关系到用户的资产，渠道必须管严。

审查完成后，我们会在官网公布完整的授权经销商名单。到时，不在名单上的，就不是 OneKey 的授权经销商。

第三，在 CryptoBilis 买过 OneKey 的符合条件用户，免费换新。

2026 年 3 月 1 日至本声明发布之日，在 CryptoBilis 买过 OneKey 硬件钱包的用户，不限型号，不管有没有激活、有没有用过，都可以免费换新。

为什么从 3 月 1 日算？CryptoBilis 的原联合创始人公开表示，公司在今年早些时候被收购，3 月完成了经营管理职责的交接。我们从 3 月 1 日开始覆盖，把整个交接月份和之后的购买都算进去。这个范围已经超过 180 天，我们宁可多覆盖一点。

换新设备由 OneKey 官方商店直接发货。原来是什么型号，就换同一型号的全新设备；如果那个型号没货了，就免费升级成更新的型号。

旧设备不用寄回，我们直接寄新的，直接从 OneKey 官网发货。

申请方法很简单：在 OneKey 官网点「客服」，或者打开 https://t.co/QG5Mu83nAr，提交工单。

标题写 CryptoBilis Replacement，附上：

- 购买凭证或小票，必须提供；
- 设备型号；
- 设备有没有激活、使用过。

申请截止：2026 年 12 月 31 日。

换新可以申请，资产安全不要等。

如果设备还没激活，先别激活，直接申请换新。

如果已经在用、里面还有资产，出于预防，请把旧助记词当作可能已经泄露来处理，尽快把资产转到使用全新助记词的钱包里，别为了等新设备而拖着。

手里有其他来源可信的硬件钱包，就在那台设备上生成全新的助记词，把资产转过去。暂时没有的话，可以在安全、可信的手机或电脑上，用 OneKey App 新建一个钱包，生成全新的助记词，先把资产转过去，作为临时过渡。

新设备到手后，在新设备上重新生成全新的助记词，再把资产转进去。不要把旧助记词导入新设备，也不要把临时 App 钱包的助记词导入新设备。资产转完后，旧设备和旧助记词就别再用了。

最后提醒一句：OneKey 客服永远不会问你要助记词或 PIN 码。任何以「换新」「验证」为由索要这些信息的人，都是骗子。

大家买 OneKey，是因为信任 OneKey。这份信任，我们得接住。

这件事我会跟到底，有新进展，我会第一时间更新。

理解機制, 才能夠抓住下次類似的機會, 單指注意力的部分, 光是一個 Papertrade 其實已經勝過各種 token2049 的文了

@papertrade_xyz 數據有多誇張？

1. 第一天合約交易量 650B , 整個 defillama 收錄的 perpdex 加起來收錄也就 10B 左右

2. 當前 Open Interest 為 1.4B

3. 第一個小時收入破 5M , 單日破 20M 

4. pre deposit 超過 140M , 不乏許多 $HYPE 巨鯨參與, 連 @machibigbrother 也出現了

＝＝＝＝＝＝
當前屬於第一個階段：純虧損搶跑

若市場出現「loss rush」（大家搶著虧錢鑄幣），早期虧的人反而可能更划算，因為幾乎每 1 美元虧損都流向質押者。

在 $5M 之前虧的人，到累計虧損 $13.5M 時已回本。

＝＝＝＝＝＝
$PAPER 核心機制

1. LP 從 $0 開始，只能靠交易虧損成長，用戶無法直接存入 LP , 最高緩衝為 5M , 超過部分全分給質押者

2. mint $PAPER 速率隨時間遞減 , 初始 100 PAPER / $1 虧損（LP < $2M 時維持最高），隨累計利潤上升遞減至約 30，但一旦 LP 跌破 $2M 會重新回到 100 , 當前已經跌至 36 

3. 質押 $PAPER 可獲得：1% 的已實現 PnL , + LP 超過 $5M 後的全部溢出

⚠️這邊要注意的是，隊列清空且 LP 足夠時才會給到以上的 1% 

早期 farming 有正期望，但必須策略性操作。單純 1000x 賭博或純虧損效率低且風險高

💀 風險

1️⃣ LP 緩衝上限只有 $5M（超過全部分給質押者）。若支付隊列累積過大，嚇退新交易者，平台可能出現無法支付的壞帳

2️⃣ 如玩家們過於理性，選擇對沖交易，對協議貢獻有限，將會開始出現 $PAPER 價值大幅稀釋的現象，降低 Papertrade 本身的存活率

即使 Papertrade 本身壽命可能不長, 但完全代表市場上仍有資金有意願衝進交易者認為有利可圖的平台

只要機制創新, 總有玩家買單, 繼續努力吧

text:
Nikita Bier 今天发了个挺有意思的判断：

技术护城河基本已经消失了。未来真正能长期守住的东西只剩三种，专有数据、网络效应，以及某种物理世界的组成部分。

我很认同这个方向，但他自己的创业经历其实也揭示了一个更残酷的问题。

Nikita 先后做出了 tbh 和 Gas 两款爆红的社交产品，分别卖给了 Facebook 和 Discord。这两款产品都非常擅长利用真实的人际关系传播，但最终也都在收购后不到一年被关闭。

所以就连网络效应，也可能只是一阵短暂的流行。

最近看各种 AI Agent，我对这件事的感受越来越强烈。今天一个团队花几个月打磨出来的功能，可能下一次模型更新就成了标配。代码、界面、工作流，甚至原本需要大量工程投入的复杂能力，都在迅速贬值。

但有些东西依然很难复制。

比如微信的关系链、苹果的系统入口、一家企业十几年建立的客户信任。再比如 Personal Agent，谁都可以做一个帮你整理邮件的助手，但要让用户真正把邮箱、日历、工作关系乃至支付权限长期交给你，就没那么容易了。

我觉得 Nikita 的清单里还应该加上分发能力和信任关系。而且所谓专有数据，也得看它是否能持续产生独特价值。

AI 让技术越来越廉价，但也让时间、关系和信任这些无法被快速生成的东西变得越来越贵。

这可能才是这一轮 AI 创业最大的变化。

鉴于到现在了还有很多道德卫士来不停指责我，指责我骂人在先，素质低下，以及我也想满足一些人的吃瓜需求，所以我在这里梳理一下今天凌晨发生的事情以及我的心路历程，大家也不用去吃二手瓜了。因为其中有些当事人已经删推了，我会放上我手机推特中的缓存推文截图。

本次事件的主人公有「我」、「芒果刀」、「清凤」以及其他参与者，时间是今天凌晨。

事情是这样的，今天凌晨我提前洗漱完躺在床上玩着手机并迎接困意准备美美入睡的时候，突然刷到了推特上的「芒果刀」的推文（见图一），推文内容是在质疑 Magpie 软件质量，虽然文中所述他自己都没有用过，只是用「听说」来直接表达否定性质疑，不过我看到这条推文并没有任何不快，我反倒是想等我有时间了跟大家分享一下我的工作流是什么样子的，但是当我打开这条推文看到了一条来自「Seefs」的评论后，让我感到深深的冒犯，他在评论中（见图二）上来就直接扣帽子说我是「快餐式服务」、「有对应的受众」、「这种作者」、「成什么样子都无所谓」，用这些词汇来直接侮辱我和我的产品以及我产品的用户，我随后引用了他的这条评论并表达了我的不快，这是我对这次事件的第一次回应，完全没有骂人只是在陈述事实和表达我的不快，其实事情到这里「Seefs」给我一个道歉一切就结束了，但是偏偏这个时候「芒果刀」专门跑过来评论了我这条引用推文，也是在这条评论里完全暴露了他自己真实的面目，就是想通过通过有罪推论不分青红皂白直接批评我的软件，紧接着在我同样的这条引用推文下「清凤」下场评论（他现在已隐藏推文），他在评论里直接贴了一个我这条推文内容的截图，说我不像人类，「清凤」后面还说我在引用推文里在扣帽子并说我表达我用订阅最贵的模型来给产品迭代是在卖惨，后面感到冒犯的用户以及我的一些支持者在他们推文下面开始反击，然后「清凤」发了个新推说「警惕推特饭圈化」开始抹黑我的产品用户，紧接着「芒果刀」引用了「清凤」的这条推文也发了一个「警惕推特饭圈化」，关键是「芒果刀」和「清凤」的名字后面都挂了相同的 memoh 的官方认证 logo（现在他们都已经撤下这些认证 logo） ，很难不让人认为这是一个小团体一起抱团跑过来恶意抹黑，这也就让我的愤怒值到达了顶峰，关键是他们一个个道貌岸然美美隐藏在中性词汇后面甚至时不时站在道德制高点偷偷摸摸来表达自己眼红嫉妒抹黑的伪君子的样子实在令人作呕，对于这种因为眼红心理扭曲只会阴阳怪气诋毁的伪君子我认为对他们最大的尊重就是献出民族魁宝「国骂」应对之。

text:
最近看到一个回测。有人从 2012 年开始，每年只做一件事，买入上一年度标普 500 涨幅最高的股票，持有一年，然后换成下一只冠军股。

据说这么做，100 美元最终变成了 17.6 万美元，整整 1760 倍。

2023 年的冠军是英伟达，2024 年又涨了约 180%；2024 年的冠军是 Palantir，全年涨了 341%，结果 2025 年又涨了 135%；2025 年冠军换成 Sandisk，全年涨了 559%，2026 年到 10 月初又翻了好几倍。

这让我想到一个问题，为什么我们总觉得一只股票涨了三五倍，就应该差不多到头了？

我感觉很多人，包括我自己，都容易低估一个产业的利润最终会向少数几家公司集中到什么程度。

英伟达如此，Palantir 也是如此。Sandisk 的上涨还叠加了存储周期和供需变化，商业逻辑各不相同，但它们都有一个共同点：当基本面不断超出预期时，市场需要反复修改对它们的定价。

很多人热衷于寻找下一个英伟达，觉得现在的英伟达已经太贵了。但过去几年，美股似乎一直在提醒我们，一家已经被所有人发现的公司，依然可能被严重低估。

当然，满仓追逐上一年的冠军股，风险也非常极端。尤其是这种漂亮得不像话的回测，必须仔细检查选股口径、成分股变动和最大回撤。

不过我感兴趣的也不是这套策略能不能复制。

我觉得它揭示了一个很有意思的市场错觉，我们太习惯用过去的涨幅来衡量一只股票未来的空间，却很少认真想过，市场究竟需要多长时间，才能真正理解一家公司的盈利上限。

我是真不理解，为什么有人会 @yetone  用AI负责Magpie的开发，就开始喷他，甚至对这种项目感到担忧。

哥们，对于yetone这种本来就有很强工程能力的佬来说，AI只会加速他们做出更多、更高质量的项目。

真正值得担忧的，其实是那些完全没有开发经验，也不懂软件工程的人，拿着AI生成的代码就直接上线了。因为他们可能连哪里有问题、哪里存在风险、什么东西需要验证都不知道。

但对于有经验的开发者来说，这完全是另一回事。
他们很清楚应该让Agent做什么、不该做什么，哪些地方需要设置边界，哪些地方必须测试和验收。

而且说实话，现在的模型能力，配合一套成熟的Harness，已经完全可以承担从开发、提交PR、Review、测试到验收的绝大部分流程了（也可以说全部）。
只要你有足够的工程经验，提前设置好规则、约束和验证机制，很多问题完全可以在流程里被发现和解决。

更何况，我特别想问一句：
怎么搞得好像AI写代码就一定会出问题，人写代码就从来不会出Bug一样？

Cloudflare、AWS哪个没挂过？国内的支付宝、滴滴，难道你们就没经历过它们崩溃的时候吗？

软件工程本来就是一个不断发现问题、修复问题、控制风险的过程。人会犯错，Agent当然也会犯错，所以才需要测试、Review和各种工程约束。

我觉得批评一个项目的工程质量、代码质量，甚至质疑它的安全性，都很正常。

但现在有些人，连项目具体是怎么开发的、有什么工程保障都不了解，一听说是AI负责开发的，就觉得这东西不靠谱。

怎么连用AI开发软件都能变成一个喷点了😅.....

text:
After recording 250M+ Trace receipts, DATA’s next big challenge is turning all that activity into a stronger AI data business.

That’s why @datafdn’s planned move to Sui makes sense.

It could free the team to focus on what AI labs actually pay for: useful training data with clear rights and verifiable origins.

DATA began as Story Protocol, pursuing a broad vision for programmable intellectual property. In June, it narrowed its focus to AI training data, with Trace as its flagship audit product.

Now its infrastructure strategy is following that sharper focus.

Running an independent Layer 1 means maintaining blockchain software, coordinating upgrades, and supporting validator infrastructure. Those responsibilities draw on the same resources needed to improve products and win customers.

One team. Two demanding jobs.

For DATA, the strongest source of value is connecting data supply, permissions, and verification into something buyers can use with confidence.

Trace helps buyers inspect records of data origins, consent, licensing terms, and payment status, while keeping the underlying content confidential.

As I said before, DATA reports 250M+ receipts recorded by Trace.

The planned division of work is straightforward:

- Sui → shared blockchain infrastructure for DATA’s protocol

- Walrus → the planned default storage layer for DATA Foundation apps, suited to large files like images and video

- Trace → the audit and provenance product DATA can keep evolving around its specific market

The wider Sui stack also offers Seal for access control and Nautilus for verifiable offchain compute, giving DATA additional building blocks as implementation progresses.

The efficiency thesis is simple: Better resource allocation.

If shared infrastructure reduces the burden of maintaining a standalone chain, more engineering effort can go toward better verification tools, smoother integrations, and broader adoption.

Sui Foundation’s announced $30M investment adds institutional commitment to that direction. The partnership also gives Sui’s infrastructure a substantial data supply to support.

Execution still matters. Migration takes work, shared infrastructure comes with tradeoffs, and DATA will depend on another ecosystem. The efficiency gains need to become tangible.

The transition is still ahead. $DATA remains the protocol token, nothing changes immediately for holders, and more migration details will follow.

I think this is a credible comeback strategy both for DATA and SUI where both can apply the lessons from the broader experiment and concentrate resources where the product has the clearest purpose.

NFA. DYOR.

text:
I think crypto founders’ lack of long-term ambition did more to erode this industry’s talent density than we admit.

Crypto is fundamentally trust infrastructure. Building something that meaningfully improves the financial system is a (long) compounding game. It takes a decade of focus.

But when prices go crazy every year, there are endless ways to make stupid money: speculation, advisory gigs, scattered investments, farming. It’s been very easy to get distracted.

The good news: it’s gotten SO MUCH better. Many short-sighted founders and projects have moved on.
Tangible impact attracts the best people. And we’re finally seeing concrete improvements in payments, financing, and trading from bringing them onchain.

As an industry, we should do more to make those improvements visible. Our “ChatGPT moment” will come when people open their financial app and feel a step change in what they can do and at what price, without needing to know that stablecoins, DeFi, or tokenized stocks made it possible.

I think we’re close. That’s what will drive the next wave of adoption, and make the most ambitious people want to build here.

text:
OK $kas

So I was emailed by some Wikipedia moderators asking me to justify the existence of an article about Sompolinsky (which is now up for deletion). I read the article, and it reads like promotional AI slop that gets a lot of details wrong, including wrong publication dates, wrong descriptions of technical terms, etc.. But I think the most embarrassing part was trying to pass him winning a glorified X poll by binance as "professional recognition and awards".

But the bottom line, I think, is that Sompolinsky is simply not significant enough to have a Wikipedia article.

I believe whoever tried this stunt honestly believes Sompolinsky is a historical figure. But they are wrong, and that's a huge part of the gap between how Kaspa (and cryptocurrencies in general, tbh) is viewed internally vs. externally.

Yeah, it has its merits, and there are reasons you love it. But at the end of the day, Kaspa is just another crypto project, founded by just another crypto founder, that has hardly made a dent in reality, or even in the cryptocurrency space outside the PoW mini-bubble. Despite its technical superiority, it failed to become revolutionary.

When you try to pass it off as something revolutionary, just because you think it should be, you come off as delusional. And if you truly think there is any "revolution" to Kaspa's name, outside a very narrow theoretical discussion, then you are delusional.

Promoting your project is fine, but Kaspa used to be about integrity (until Sompolinsky let his ego ruin everything, and most people with a modicum of integrity were driven away), and promoting it as you would any ye olde shitcoin just makes its few unique benefits drown in the brownish-gray, depressing sea of  ramnants of what was once an industry.

text:
周鸿祎摔碎膝盖，傅盛发了八个字

10月10日，56岁的周鸿祎在抱石攀岩时从3米高处坠落，左膝粉碎性骨折。第二天深夜，傅盛在朋友圈发了八个字：“苍天有眼，鸿膝当碎。”截图流出后，疑似删除。

1｜事故经过
10月10日，周鸿祎进行抱石攀岩时，从约3米高处失手坠落。落地瞬间未能做出正确缓冲动作，左腿单独承受全部冲击力，当场听见膝盖发出异响，左腿随即失去活动能力。
影像报告显示：左侧胫骨、腓肠豆粉碎性骨折，左侧腓骨骨折，伴膝关节腔积液和周围软组织肿胀。未来两三个月内，所有出差和外出活动全部取消，近期一个月需佩戴固定器在家静养。
周鸿祎在视频中说，刚过完56岁生日，感慨极限攀岩类运动对年长人群存在不小风险。

2｜傅盛的反应
10月12日，网传傅盛深夜在朋友圈发文：“苍天有眼，鸿膝当碎。”八个字，意思很直白——人在做，天在看。
截图流出后，据多家媒体查看，该朋友圈疑似已被删除。

3｜二十年的恩怨
2005年，傅盛加入周鸿祎创办的奇虎，从一线员工成长为360安全卫士项目负责人。这款产品成为360崛起的关键。
2008年，因业务理念分歧，傅盛离职。此后双方陷入长达十余年的诉讼与口水战，周鸿祎公开称傅盛为“叛徒”。2011年，360在香港高等法院起诉傅盛，指控窃取商业机密、挖角员工，官司拉锯十余年。

4｜短暂的“世纪和解”
2024年1月，在猎户星空大模型发布会上，两人决裂16年后首次公开同台。
周鸿祎说：“过去的事都不算事，要往前看。”傅盛也表达了对周鸿祎的感恩。
外界一度以为这段恩怨画上了句号。

5｜三个月前刚撕过一次
和解没维持多久。2026年3月20日凌晨，傅盛在多个微信群内公开指责周鸿祎“欠钱不还、拉黑好友”，称涉及金额上亿元。
他称对方曾承诺归还至少1亿元以换取他中止香港的诉讼，但360完成A股上市后再无回应，并将他拉黑。
360回应称“属于谣言，没有证据”。数日后，傅盛发道歉信，称当晚系酒后冲动。
然后是10月，周鸿祎摔伤，傅盛发了那八个字。

身体可以愈合，恩怨没有期限。

text:
这几天，多位从 CryptoBilis 买过 Ledger 硬件钱包的用户报告资产被盗。Ledger 已确认，受影响用户的设备里被植入了未经授权的硬件。具体原因和影响范围还在调查。

CryptoBilis 也卖过 OneKey、Trezor、Tangem、SafePal、imKey 等品牌，所以很多人来问我：我的 OneKey 还安全吗？

截至发文，我们没有收到 OneKey 用户因这次事件遭遇资产被盗的报告。但没收到报告，不等于没有风险。用户的资产安全不能靠运气，我们不会去赌。

我们已经终止了 CryptoBilis 的授权，它不再是 OneKey 的授权经销商。

从今天起，我们做三件事。

第一，不再新增经销商。

即日起，OneKey 停止新增任何经销商。

第二，所有现有经销商重新审查。

以前通过认证的，也全部重新审核、重新排查。经营主体核实不了、最终受益人说不清楚的，一律取消授权，从官网下架。

经销商网络会大幅缩小。硬件钱包关系到用户的资产，渠道必须管严。

审查完成后，我们会在官网公布完整的授权经销商名单。到时，不在名单上的，就不是 OneKey 的授权经销商。

第三，在 CryptoBilis 买过 OneKey 的符合条件用户，免费换新。

2026 年 3 月 1 日至本声明发布之日，在 CryptoBilis 买过 OneKey 硬件钱包的用户，不限型号，不管有没有激活、有没有用过，都可以免费换新。

为什么从 3 月 1 日算？CryptoBilis 的原联合创始人公开表示，公司在今年早些时候被收购，3 月完成了经营管理职责的交接。我们从 3 月 1 日开始覆盖，把整个交接月份和之后的购买都算进去。这个范围已经超过 180 天，我们宁可多覆盖一点。

换新设备由 OneKey 官方商店直接发货。原来是什么型号，就换同一型号的全新设备；如果那个型号没货了，就免费升级成更新的型号。

旧设备不用寄回，我们直接寄新的，直接从 OneKey 官网发货。

申请方法很简单：在 OneKey 官网点「客服」，或者打开 https://t.co/QG5Mu83nAr，提交工单。

标题写 CryptoBilis Replacement，附上：

- 购买凭证或小票，必须提供；
- 设备型号；
- 设备有没有激活、使用过。

申请截止：2026 年 12 月 31 日。

换新可以申请，资产安全不要等。

如果设备还没激活，先别激活，直接申请换新。

如果已经在用、里面还有资产，出于预防，请把旧助记词当作可能已经泄露来处理，尽快把资产转到使用全新助记词的钱包里，别为了等新设备而拖着。

手里有其他来源可信的硬件钱包，就在那台设备上生成全新的助记词，把资产转过去。暂时没有的话，可以在安全、可信的手机或电脑上，用 OneKey App 新建一个钱包，生成全新的助记词，先把资产转过去，作为临时过渡。

新设备到手后，在新设备上重新生成全新的助记词，再把资产转进去。不要把旧助记词导入新设备，也不要把临时 App 钱包的助记词导入新设备。资产转完后，旧设备和旧助记词就别再用了。

最后提醒一句：OneKey 客服永远不会问你要助记词或 PIN 码。任何以「换新」「验证」为由索要这些信息的人，都是骗子。

大家买 OneKey，是因为信任 OneKey。这份信任，我们得接住。

这件事我会跟到底，有新进展，我会第一时间更新。

Five days since mainnet, here's what's been built on Covenants so far:

@realchriswilder was first in and has two out already. A sealed-bid auction on testnet, reveal and settle working end to end. Then a time vault. Seal a letter or a link, it stays shut until a date you pick, then it's published on Ethereum. No keeper

@nikshepsvn shipped an app called Sealed on launch day. Price calls nobody can read, and stop-losses nobody can see that sell on Uniswap in the same tx

@ChooseKCorp has Zilch live on mainnet, Covenants plus Zama confidential transfers. The instruction stays encrypted until it fires, and the amount never gets revealed at all

@DefiPreacherr built Nilayer. Review, approve and schedule USDC payments from a Safe treasury, privately. Grants, prizes, payroll, vendors, and more

You don't even need the docs. Copy the agent brief off the SDK page into your project and tell your agent to read it. Conditions, hooks, the traps, it's all in there

Things I'd love to see built:

OTC where neither side shows a price until the window closes

Depeg cover that pays out on its own if USDT prints under 0.98. No claims desk, no oracle vote, and the policy stays sealed

Buy ETH if BTC breaks 90k. An order no venue offers, resting where nobody can read it

If BTC drops 30%, buy YES on "MicroStrategy sells any Bitcoin by Dec 31" on Polymarket. Written now, sealed, fires without you watching

Borrowers on Aave or Morpho set a repay level nobody can see, and it pays down the loan before the public liquidation price ever gets hit

A DAO treasury hedge that sells on its own if ETH breaks a level. The DAO votes it through, the level stays sealed

A curator vault whose next rebalance is sealed until it fires. Steakhouse, Sentora and Veda move billions against rules that sit in the open today

A trading agent that seals every entry, exit and stop it intends to place, then walks away. Nothing resting on a venue, nothing in a mempool, and the orders fire even if the agent is dead

If you're building one, my DMs are open
