The funnel is the story.

Same model. Some people ask it trivia. Others hand it a budget and a deadline.

Prediction: the gap compounds faster than the models improve.

https://t.co/d6pdajctH7
author: questflow
quoted_text:
Dusting off this tweet from April because this gap in shared understanding of LLM capability is *widening*. It's now less "two groups of people speaking past each other" and more a sharp funnel.

- Napkin math somewhere around 6B people (~75% of the population) have barely come in contact with LLMs at all.
- Around 1-2B (~20%) are casual and infrequent users of free-tier ChatGPT-like products. This group sees derpy chatbots and treats them a bit like a better Google search, a writing aid, or etc. Maybe an agent tries to book you a flight. I have non-tech friends who (reasonably, imo) say they have not much use for it at all. Even many professionals outside of math&code are in this tier. For example, execs and many other functions spend a lot of their time talking to other people, so while they understand what is happening intellectually, it is still second-hand and a bit abstract.
- Now we get to professional use of frontier-grade LLMs in math&code. Somewhere around 20M people (0.2%) see first-hand that large, complex projects that used to take them weeks/months can now be completed by agents with a prompt. Building apps, copying apps, translating apps, decompiling apps from binaries... This has all happened very quickly and recently - less than 1 year ago, I was writing code manually by hand, typing memorized computer code commands into a code editor character by character, occasionally pressing Tab to autocomplete a little chunk of code.
- And finally we get to the ~5,000 people (~0.00006%) with access to frontier-grade systems internally. The external world has seen the preview. It looks like swarms of thousands of agents collaborating over weeks on software mega projects: minting zero days, running cyber attacks and defenses at machine speeds, discovering new science, advancing the frontier of mathematics. Things that would have taken top professionals in the industry years of work. Meanwhile, human review and comprehension are starting to fall behind. For example, people are still involved in the "archeology" of the OpenAI-HF incident from many months ago. Mathematicians may be poring over the 722 manuscripts on frontier mathematics for a while.

The funnel is driven by a combination of factors:
1. The impact scales with ambition, problem size, and horizon. A question with a paragraph answer barely stresses the system. You need a reservoir of big, difficult problems that you really care about. This aspect drives the consumer / professional dimension of the funnel.
2. The jaggedness of the system (which I have written about a lot separately). Capability peaks in domains that are digital, verifiable and economically valuable. This is because LLM capability emerges from reinforcement learning on verifiable rewards on a curated environment mixture driven by revenue potential. This aspect primarily drives the area (e.g. math&code) dimension of the funnel.
3. Access. Free-tier, paid-tier, internal.

So this is the weirdness of the moment. The general public has mostly not interacted with these systems. When they have, it looks like a derpy chatbot. The majority of professionals still see only a modest uplift. And a small sliver of professionals are experiencing the vertigo of the curve going vertical. And it is all happening at the same time.

text:
红果在国内杀疯了，字节正在海外再复制一个

红果日活近1.7亿，人均每天125分钟。按时长算，已经是中国第四大App。
在海外，字节正在复制同一套打法——免费模式+流量协同+本土内容，用PineDrama再造一个红果。

1｜双产品试错：Melolo的教训
Melolo是字节在2024年底打出的第一张牌，主攻东南亚，内容以译制为主。用户反馈很直接：“没吸引力，配音怪。”优先级很快被下调。
2025年底的PineDrama吸取了教训：免费+本地制片网络。上线约9个月，累计下载破1亿，日活约700万。这是今年海外下载破亿的7款短剧App中，唯一的新面孔。

2｜获客有效，但变现错位
免费短剧App的用户时长占比，在六个季度内从约15%飙升至约83%。免费模式在抢时间这件事上，已经赢了。
但收入还留在付费平台手里。2026年中国以外短剧收入约36亿美元，仍高度集中在ReelShort、DramaBox等付费平台，两家合计约占一半。
PineDrama下载的82%来自印尼和巴西，广告ARPU低，北美等高价值市场占比有限。红果在国内能跑通，靠的是1.68亿日活加人均125分钟形成的广告库存。PineDrama目前的用户规模和市场分布，还不足以证明具备同样的商业化条件。

3｜本土化：从翻译到共创
PineDrama没有走简单译制的老路，而是本地搭制片网络，本土演员+本土故事。
《10亿奈拉新娘》一周播放破4000万，累计超6000万；《印尼豪门风云》《里约救赎》均破2亿播放。把国内豪门恩怨、家庭反转的工业化叙事，嫁接到本地文化土壤里。这一步比单纯翻译难得多，也更有壁垒。

4｜AI降本 vs 获客变贵
一分钟AI真人短剧成本从四五千元降到约一千元，降幅超90%。小团队可以快速出片，供给持续增加。
但流量投放成本同比涨超100%，收益端承压。成本降了，获客更贵，免费的差异化优势正在被稀释。

5｜TikTok生态协同是结构性优势
PineDrama支持TikTok账号一键登录，产品交互接近短视频。2026年Q1，TikTok短剧分账超2400万美元，上半年累计8200万美元。广告管理平台为PineDrama单开效果竞价广告位。
“短视频种草、独立App留存”的闭环，独立平台很难复制。
author: roger9949
quoted_text:
红果日活接近1.7亿，人均每天刷125分钟。
按使用时长算，它已经是中国第四大App，排在抖音、微信、抖音极速版之后，超过了快手和小红书。

这不是一个“短剧增长很快”的故事。时长是内容平台最核心的指标。谁拿走更多时间，谁就更有机会拿走广告、内容和商业化空间。

被挤压的不只是短剧同行。游戏、长视频、小说、社交，都在被它重新切蛋糕。

腾讯已经让微信亲自下场做“绿泡泡短剧”，并动用微信生态的分发能力。聊天群转发、朋友推荐、视频号承接、小程序跳转——这些能力一旦打通，短剧的传播路径就完全不同了。

text:
Muse 的最新留存数据出来了，表现确实很强。D7 超过 30%，甚至高于 ChatGPT，D14 则是 22%，只比 ChatGPT 略低。

Meta 自己手里就有一个 D14 留存 67% 的 WhatsApp，还有 54% 的 Instagram。YouTube 是 59%，TikTok 和 Snapchat 也有 37%。

这组数据放在一起看，其实能看出目前 AI 产品一个很大的问题。

ChatGPT 和 Muse 已经能让用户反复回来使用，但距离让用户的生活围绕它们运转，还有很长一段距离。

我最近一直在关注 Personal Agent，也越来越觉得，行业可能高估了模型能力在消费级产品竞争中的权重。

一个 Agent 能帮我订机票、整理邮件，我当然觉得厉害。但这些事情并不是每天都有。今天我可能觉得 Muse 很神奇，明天打开三次，后天突然没什么事情需要它做了。

WhatsApp和微信这种就不一样。我的朋友、家人、工作关系都在那里。哪怕产品十年不更新，我还是得每天打开。

Meta 有现成的社交关系和通讯入口，Muse 也已经可以通过 WhatsApp 使用。如果能让 Agent 真正参与到用户已有的关系和日常事务中，它就有机会解决独立 AI App 很难解决的使用频率问题。

AI 公司现在都在争谁能把事情做得更好，但最终可能是那个最自然地进入用户生活、让用户懒得迁移的产品赢。

Meta 在这件事上，可能比任何一家纯 AI 公司都更有经验。

text:
It is my last "Drama" post.

I was wrong about a lot of things. 
I made mistakes, hurt people, and handled situations and criticism badly. 
I can't undo what happened, and I won't pretend otherwise.

It took courage to finally face my detractors, confront their arguments, and address the accusations made against me. 
But the most difficult part was to be actually open to the critics and also to accept the mistakes I made, without of course accepting all the labels and humiliation given.

I wanted to show my genuine self :
my intentions, my perspective, but also my mistakes and the things I got wrong.

I know that explaining myself doesn't erase the harm I've caused, but I felt it was important to face these criticisms rather than keep hiding from them.

I know I hurt people, and also Dark Prince as a character, and Dark Bandit as a ship.
Yet I don't want to erase the few things I did good too.

All I can do now is move forward, learn from my mistakes, and try to do better.
But right now I just want to cry, and I just feel the need to reflect on myself and a lot of things again.

I'm not asking to forgive me or forget what happened. I know that rebuilding trust takes time, and that words alone aren't enough. Also, I don't ask for forgiveness.

Finally, thank you to the kind people who have continued to support me throughout this difficult time, for months. Your kindness means more to me than I can express.

For now, I need to take a step back, reflect, and focus on becoming a better person.

The backdoored Ledger story keeps getting crazier. Attackers used the backdoor to grab $90+ million in crypto from users who bought hardware wallets precisely because hackers steal crypto keys from normal computers.
1) Someone built an implant into Ledgers to steal keys, with an “LTE module, Antenna, e-SIM, a MCU connected to the Ledger’s SPI bus.” (c/o @MagicalTux)
2) It looks like the attackers acquired CryptoBilis, a Ledger authorized retailer, and tampered with their inventory.
3) @MagicalTux found the implant by accident. He was tearing down Ledgers for unrelated reasons and bought them from the cheapest place possible, which was, unsurprisingly, the malicious CryptoBilis.
4) Once the implant was detected, the attackers quickly used the keys they’d stolen to drain the wallets.
5) There appear to be multiple generations of implants.

quoted_text:
The recent XRP Ledger security fix raised a lot of questions and some misconceptions. Let's clear them up.

1. Was any XRP created?

No. XRP's supply was fixed at 100 billion when the XRP Ledger launched, and no transaction is allowed to create more. This bug was a way around that rule, and 3.4.1 fixed it 2 weeks ago.

You don't need to trust us on this. All ledger data is public, and explorers and data sites read it every day. New XRP would show up in account balances for everyone to see. There is no hidden place for XRP on the XRP Ledger, every balance is public.

We monitor the XRP Ledger 24/7 and have verified the supply throughout the history of the ledger. Others in the community verified this too, and anyone can do the same.

Transaction fees are destroyed, so the supply is deflationary. About 99.986 billion XRP exist today.

2. How did this go unnoticed, and what's next?

No normal payment comes anywhere near triggering it. It took hundreds of deliberately constructed operations.

AI makes bugs like this faster to find, for the bad guys and the good guys. 

Together with RippleX and the community, we will ensure the XRP Ledger is protected against such vulnerabilities. This means radically applying Formal Verification and AI adversarial testing, collaborating closely with security researchers, and strengthening the bug bounty program.

You'll hear a lot more about this as we progress.

3. XRP Ledger decentralization at the core of this.

A public fix shows attackers where the bug is, and AI makes that fast. With a normal amendment vote, the fix would have been public for weeks before it took effect, risking network security.

As a reaction to this, the XRPL community came together, and among them the XRP Ledger Foundation, RippleX, core devs and validators formed a social consensus and agreed on a path forward that involves shipping the fix directly. Patching a live network is never trivial, so the plan was also designed to minimize disruption for everyone running on it.

We shared the build with the default UNL validators, using the contact details each one publishes in its xrp-ledger.toml file. Public binaries followed the same day, September 25.

No single party could make that call alone. Every validator and node operator chooses what software to run, and 3.4.1 only became required through a normal amendment vote with more than 80% validator support for two weeks. Protocol changes still go through amendments.

Big thanks to Cayden Liao and Veria AI for finding and reporting this responsibly, to the XRPL core developers for building and testing the fix, and to every node operator who upgraded so quickly, especially the validators.

Full report: https://t.co/aWxdvthYPt

text:
Let me teach you what an AI harness is in 90 seconds, because once you get this, every AI product on the market starts making sense.

The model is the part everyone talks about. GPT, Claude, Gemini. Those are just brains in a jar.

They produce text and nothing else.

The harness is the invisible software wrapped around the brain that turns its text into real action.

Here's the loop that runs every single time.

> Step one.

The harness loads your goal, the rules, the history, and any previous results into one big pile of context.

> Step two.

It hands all of that to the model and asks "what's the next move?"

> Step three.

The model either answers you directly or asks for a tool. Read a file. Run a test. Search the web.

> Step four.

The harness checks the permission, runs the tool, and feeds the result back as the next input.

Then it loops. Over and over. Until the job is done or it hits a time, cost, or step limit you set.

That's it. That's the whole magic.

Every autonomous AI agent you've ever used is just this loop with a bigger brain and better tools strapped on.

Now you know what's actually under the hood.

text:
I am the United States Ambassador to a warm, strategically vital ally on the Aegean. 

I will not say which one. We have a sea, a debt we cannot discuss, and a residence the State Department calls, in its own documents, a “representational asset.” I am the asset’s current occupant. There’s a pool. I’m told the last occupant wanted a basketball court by it. I admire the ambition. He was thinking like a citizen diplomat.

It’s nearly ten. Here they dine at ten, which took adjusting. Twenty guests, the long table, the government’s own sterling laid out, because the silver is federal property, ours for the formal dining room table only, it says so in the Foreign Affairs Manual, the one document I read to the end. On the sideboard sits a silver-and-enamel icon the Archbishop gave me last month. It’s worth more than the gift limit, five hundred and twenty-five dollars now, they adjust it for inflation, so by law it isn’t mine. It belongs to the United States government and will end its days in a GSA warehouse in Virginia, in a bin, beside twelve hundred other dead men’s gratitude. I took a photo of it first. Remember the icon. It comes back.

Down the table, against the wall, stands my Deputy Chief of Mission. Career man. Thirty years. He is, by regulation, 2 FAM 113.2, my “alter ego,” which means he is me when I am not here, and he is me rather a lot. He speaks the language. He took the 44 weeks of it at the Foreign Service Institute, a thousand classroom hours, before he landed, the way the law says: “a useful knowledge of the principal language.” I did two weeks in Washington, and the career officers got to leave the afternoon sessions early. I asked why. Someone said, kindly, that the afternoon sessions weren’t for me.

I’ll call him Stephanos, which isn’t his name, because he deserves the privacy I don’t.

Let me tell you about the people who built this profession, because I did not come to it ignorant. I studied. I have heroes. I have a whole pantheon, and I can recite them the way a girl raised in the faith can recite the saints.

Saint Cynthia Stroum, of Luxembourg. A bundler, half a million for the campaign, handed a tiny rich country and a residence. She put three thousand four hundred dollars of wine and liquor on the embassy account. She made the staff screen two hundred houses for her temporary lodging, tour thirty or forty in person, and she rejected every single one. She got herself reimbursed, improperly, for a mattress she didn’t like. Her people requested transfers to Iraq and Afghanistan, active war zones, rather than spend another month with her. She told them her letter from the President gave her the right to read their email. She resigned two weeks before the Inspector General’s report hit. I have read that report the way other women read the Psalms. And her only sin, her single, fatal flaw, was that she was sloppy. She bought the wine on the government card. She left prints on the mattress. Amateur. I buy my own wine. That’s her lesson, handed down: the master’s one visible mistake is the whole curriculum.

Saint Jeffrey Ross Gunter, dermatologist, of Iceland. Never been. Sat in his confirmation hearing and said, out loud, under oath, that he had never set foot in the country he was about to represent, and they confirmed him anyway, because the hearing is theater and everyone in the room knows it. Then, in the single safest nation on the face of the earth, a country whose president does his errands on a bicycle, he demanded a firearm, a stab-proof vest, and door-to-door armored-car service. And here is the relic I keep closest, the bone in the gold box: in under two years, he went through seven deputy chiefs of mission. Seven. One of them had studied Icelandic for an entire year to prepare for the post, and Gunter blocked him because he “didn’t like the look of him.”

Seven.

I look at Stephanos, against the wall.

I’ve replaced two. In this company, I’m a moderate.

Saint Colleen Bell, producer of a daytime soap opera, of Hungary. A United States senator asked her, twice, to name one American strategic interest in Hungary, and she could not produce a single one, and the White House said she had “the president’s confidence,” which is the only qualification that has ever mattered and the only one anyone was ever honest enough to say out loud.

Saint Noah Mamet, of Argentina, asked by a senator, simply, “Have you been to Argentina?” and answering, to his eternal credit, honestly: “I haven’t had the opportunity yet.” Confirmed regardless. That’s faith.

And the patron saint of this particular sea, Saint George Tsunis, who in his hearing to be ambassador to Norway called its governing party a fringe element and its monarchy a republic, who could not, in front of the cameras, locate the apparatus of the Kingdom of Norway, who withdrew in disgrace, and was then, a few quiet years later, handed this very post as a consolation prize. Sit with that. The chair I occupy was the runner-up ribbon for a man who lost a fight with a Scandinavian king.

Do you understand what that tells you? It tells you the job was never, not for one hour in a hundred years, about competence. These are not the failures of the system. These are the system’s trophies, lined up on the shelf, catching the light. I didn’t betray the institution. I’m its honor student.

So understand my position when I arrived, by the pool, in the gold light, with a drink I hadn’t paid for. I had been handed an asset worth a fortune in a currency no one would let me name: proximity. And I was expected to give it away for free, out of something called honor, to whoever Stephanos decided was important that week.

I asked the only question a serious person asks.

Why is it free?

Because the ambassadorship was already sold. That’s what the donation bought, mine and every cushy post before me. There’s a study, real economists, that prices the embassies like a wine list: London runs somewhere between six hundred thousand and two million, and, here’s the connoisseur’s tip, bundling is cheaper than giving it yourself. Half a million in personal checks buys a 90 percent shot at a sea and a palazzo. The dangerous posts, the poor ones, the ones that actually matter to the Republic, go to people like Stephanos, who earns in a year roughly what the man on my right would pay to make a single phone call happen. We send our professionals to the war and our donors to the beach, and nobody calls it corruption, they call it the tradition of citizen diplomats, and it is, I checked, explicitly against the law.

This is my favorite thing in the world, and I want to be exact. The Foreign Service Act of 1980, Section 304, paragraph 3: “Contributions to political campaigns should not be a factor in the appointment of an individual as a chief of mission.” Should not. There’s a law. And the same Act, a few lines down, required me to file a report of every political contribution my family and I made in the four years before my name went up. So I was legally obligated to submit an itemized receipt for the job the law says cannot be bought. I complied. I filed my violation in triplicate. Nobody read it. Nobody ever reads the part that matters, which is the entire secret of this profession and most others.

Now, tonight. The guest of honor owns the port. Not all of it, a Chinese state company owns 67 percent, bought during the bailout when my hosts had to sell their own harbor to make a loan payment. My guest owns the rest, and the men who own the rest.

Over the second glass of the dry white from the volcanic island, I raise it, and I say the warm thing, the gracious thing. I congratulate him on the magnificent Chinese investment in his harbor. What a vote of confidence. What a partnership.

There is a small silence.

Stephanos is there before it lands. From the wall, in fluent Greek, smooth as oil on the water, he says the thing I should have said, folds my blunder into a joke about the weather and the shipping season, and the table laughs, and the port man laughs, and the moment closes over like it never was. I beam. I have no idea I’ve just thanked a man for letting Beijing park a navy ten kilometers from my pool, in the one country whose only real value to Washington is the deep-water quay on the big island, the only berth in this entire sea where an American carrier can tie up. Stephanos knows that. Stephanos thinks about that quay the way I think about the seating chart. I will find out tomorrow, reading his cable, that I said something wrong tonight. The cable will not say which part. He is too kind for that, and I am not worth the paragraph.

Then the port man leans in with his real business. A tedious matter, back home, a tax thing, the kind that keeps a serious man awake. He’d be so grateful for a conversation. Not with me. With someone three rungs above me, whose direct line I have because of the laminated badge.

And I give him a quote. Allegedly.

Because that is the entire charge against me, stripped of the gasping. Not that I did it. Every saint in my pantheon did a version of it, leveraged the residence, traded the number, took the private jet to the island. They did it over gentlemanly years with good lawyers and the strict understanding that it would never appear in a message with a figure attached. My one sin, the thing that has the whole clubhouse shrieking into their tsipouro, is that I wrote the number down. I said the quiet part with a decimal point. The quiet part was always the business. I just failed to keep it quiet, which in this town is the only crime that has ever existed.

The dinner ends. The cars come at the hour Stephanos ordered them. The port man kisses my hand and calls me a wonderful hostess, which is the Greek word philoxenia, the sacred welcome to the stranger, the thing this whole marble house was built to perform, and I have turned it into a payment terminal, and he means it as the highest compliment, and I take it as one.

One regret. Not the price. The price was fair, I’d argue low. The regret is that I quoted retail. Stroum went down over wine and a mattress; the dermatologist over a bulletproof vest in the safest country on earth. Small. Undignified. If I’m going to end up in the report, and we all end up in the report, I intend to be in it for a sum. Go big. It’s the one lesson the saints left unlearned, and I’ll be the one to teach it.

I remain, with deep and abiding values, committed to representing the American people with dedication and integrity.

By the pool. Which is a representational asset.

The last guest goes. Stephanos straightens a place card no one will ever see, says kalinychta to the staff by name, and goes home to write the cable that will quietly repair, in three careful paragraphs, whatever I agreed to tonight without understanding it. He will fix the harbor sentence too. He will not be thanked. It goes out under my name.

The icon on the sideboard, the Archbishop’s icon, goes in a crate Monday, to a warehouse in Virginia, to sit in the dark with twelve hundred other tokens of a gratitude the law won’t let us keep.

I kept the photo, though.

That’s the job. You keep the photo. The government keeps the gift. Stephanos keeps the country running.

And I keep the pool.

text:
回国后在智驾行业干了这么多年，见证了这个行业的起高楼，现在感觉楼真的要塌了

连智驾行业头部都过得如此艰难，被主机厂压账期，降价，各种白盒交付

盘点了下国内智驾公司发展的三条路径：破产倒闭，苟延残喘和上市股价腰斩

一、倒闭/实质性停摆的公司
这类公司大多在资本退潮后资金链断裂，进入破产清算、司法重整或被母公司回收解散。共同特点是：依赖单一客户、技术路线难商业化、持续烧钱却缺乏规模收入。
•中智行：王劲创办的L4车路协同公司。2025年因连1.5万元欠薪都付不起被法院裁定破产清算，资不抵债。
•毫末智行：长城汽车孵化的独角兽。2025年11月全员停工放假，实际基本解散，账户冻结、欠薪、高管离职，高度依赖单一客户。
•纵目科技：曾估值超90亿的ADAS/自动泊车公司。2025年进入司法重整，总部曾断电封楼、欠薪断保，多次IPO失败。
•禾多科技：广汽主要合作伙伴，累计融资超10亿。2024年核心研发部门解散，后进入破产清算。
•大卓智能：奇瑞控股，前特斯拉Autopilot核心团队。2025年5月解散，业务并回奇瑞集团。
•清研微视：清华苏州汽车研究院孵化的传感器公司。2025年破产清算，申报债权超1.38亿元。
•其他：图森未来2024年主动从纳斯达克退市；极越（百度+吉利）停摆后启动预重整。
簡要分析：主機廠獨立孵化的智駕團隊幾乎全軍覆沒。缺乏真實規模訂單的中間層最先出局。

二、还在苟活（未上市）的公司
已排除已上市标的。这些公司能活下来，主要是因为绑定了真实车企项目或封闭场景订单。
•华为乾崑：全栈自研，高端市场领先。主要合作问界（赛力斯）、阿维塔、智界（奇瑞）、极狐（北汽）等，城市NOA和整体智驾搭载量持续领先。估计也是唯一一家赚钱的
•元戎启行：城市NOA方案商中的强势选手，近期装机量多次冲进前列。主要合作长城（魏牌等）、吉利等，在主流价位段放量明显。
•轻舟智航：辅助驾驶搭载量已破百万。核心项目来自理想汽车、奇瑞等，同时布局Robobus和无人物流。
•卓驭科技（大疆车载）：主打性价比与工程落地。已与一汽、上汽通用五菱、奇瑞、东风、长城、福田等多家车企合作，并加速向商用重卡扩展。
•千里科技：吉利系，主要依托吉利集团车型落地，方案装机量进入前列。
•百度Apollo / 萝卜快跑：Robotaxi运营规模领先，同时对外输出技术平台。

纯智驾标的大多在港股上市，整体表现偏弱。高估值+持续亏损导致多数大幅回撤。

•小马智行（https://t.co/iJj5a6lRuN）：2025年11月港股上市，发行价139港元。目前约45港元，较发行价跌约67%，创上市新低。Robotaxi持续大额亏损。
•文远知行（https://t.co/7gMBoI47Fm）：同日上市，发行价27.1港元。目前约12港元，较发行价跌超55%，同样创上市新低。
简要分析：上市后股价普遍承压，尤其是纯L4/Robotaxi方向回撤最猛。有规模化量产的公司基本面更好，但仍需消化高估值。市场已从“市梦率”转向更看重交付和造血能力。

Ok guys, I’ve been looking into Malala Yousafzai’s charity, the Malala Fund and I have some questions. 

According to its 2024–2025 financial reports:

Revenue: $16.48 MILLION
Expenses: $23.34 MILLION
Net assets: $42.97 MILLION

That means the charity spent approximately $6.86 MILLION MORE than it brought in‼️

CEO: Approximately $372,000
Chief Adviser: Approximately $320,000
COO: Approximately $241,000

The charity’s tax filings also disclose FIRST CLASS or PRIVATE travel for officers or key employees. ✈️ WTF?! 

But here’s what I’d like to know:

How much of that $18.94 MILLION in program spending actually reaches girls and local educational organizations?

How much goes toward salaries, consultants, advocacy campaigns, and travel?

What measurable educational results can donors independently verify?

And why did a charity with $16.48 million in annual revenue spend over $23 million that year?!? 🤯

When you’re raising millions in the name of educating vulnerable girls, I don’t think asking where the money goes is unreasonable.

Charity should be about the cause, not the celebrity attached to it.

It now makes sense why Malala looked so comfortable dining at Claridge’s. Malala lives a life like a rockstar.

quoted_text:
The Most Underestimated Barrier to Institutional Crypto Is Not Regulation

Panelists Samar Sen (@talostrading), Benjamin Stani (@FalconXGlobal), Jean-David Péquignot (@JDP_VS, @DeribitOfficial) and CJ Hetherington (@cjhtech, @lmtls_research) discussed "The Institutional Trading Stack: Liquidity, Execution, and Prime Brokerage."

What actually keeps institutional money out?

Sen of Talos named liquidity, and called it the most underestimated factor in the whole conversation. Not regulation, not custody. Institutions have to connect liquidity scattered across venues to execute size reliably, and the trading systems traditional firms already own are not sufficient for this market's structure. What the job requires is algorithmic execution routing across centralized exchanges, OTC and DEXs while slicing orders to market conditions.

What product is missing entirely?

This was the most interesting unbuilt thing on the stage. Hetherington of Limitless pointed out that traditional finance manages portfolio risk with instruments like interest rate swaps and credit default swaps, while large parts of this market have no appropriate hedge at all. His specific target was private credit: default risk on lending to private companies is rising, and there are far too few products that let that risk be transferred or dispersed to other investors.

Digital asset contracts as a hedging venue for risks traditional products never handled well. That is a very different pitch from faster settlement.

Who wins as the two markets converge?

Possibly the incumbents. More financial firms are investing in digital asset companies or building their own trading and custody infrastructure, and as the markets merge, licenses, client bases and accumulated regulator trust turn into an advantage rather than a legacy cost.

What is the risk in that?

Geography. US regulatory change is accelerating the convergence, and the panel's warning was that if other jurisdictions do not build frameworks at a comparable pace, the entire institutional stack simply concentrates in the United States.

Moderated by Daniel Kim (@TIGER_NODE), Founder and CEO of Tiger Research (@tiger_research_).

最近两天，带着“1000倍杠杆”和“亏钱即挖矿”设定的链上DEX  @papertrade_xyz 引起很多讨论。

Taiki Maeda 最新的一期的播客节目请到了这个项目的联合构建者 jez @izebel_eth。很多人不知道的是，他是个拥有 TradFi 量化背景的资深交易员。

而他在节目中透露，要做 Papertrade 的原因很简单：

Perps 赛道整体还有 10 倍的上涨空间。既然投机潮不可逆，不如满仓最好的生意：与其自己赌，不如自己开赌场。

此外，他还分享了一些自己的交易经验和在加密市场里摸爬滚打的心得，对普通交易者来说也有一些启示，一些核心观点如下：

1.与其在赌场里下注，不如拥有赌场 

Jez 认为，投机是 Crypto 最真实的产品市场契合点（PMF），而且这股趋势不会轻易逆转。 在他看来，整个 Perps 市场未来还有 10 倍增长空间。

与其反复参与高风险交易，不如拥有能够持续从交易活动中获益的生意。 

2.不要把钱押在第二好的机会，集中持仓才能把小账户做大 

Jez 认为，分散投资是保护财富的手段，而不是创造财富的最佳方式。 真正值得重仓的机会，必须建立在远超市场的认知优势之上。

他建议交易者问自己一个问题： 「如果今年只能做这一笔交易，你会选它吗？」 如果答案是否定的，就不应该轻易浪费子弹。 

3.自己做衍生品，却劝普通人远离杠杆 

「如果所有人都只做现货，世界会好很多。」 这是 Jez 在访谈中给出的一个颇为反直觉的观点。 

他认为，即使看对了方向，高杠杆也可能因为短期波动让交易者提前出局。真正摧毁账户的，往往不是缺乏判断力，而是过大的仓位和失控的情绪。 

4.从爆仓到满仓 $PEPE 翻盘，传奇交易经历背后是复利的代价 

Jez 曾卖掉全部亚马逊股票买入山寨币，也曾因高杠杆做空 ETH 爆仓，随后在 2023 年靠满仓 PEPE 实现翻盘。 

这些经历听起来像传奇，但他如今反而认为，反复爆仓再翻身，牺牲的是最宝贵的长期复利。 「如果当年我稳稳复利，而不是来回爆仓、来回翻身，现在的位置会高得多。」 

5.不要急着辞职，先找到自己的信息优势 

对于想把 10 万美元做到 100 万美元的普通人，Jez 的建议不是全职交易，而是保留工作，把工资当作稳定的资金来源。 

与此同时，找到一群真正敏锐、能够互相纠错的交易伙伴，比每天刷推特、追逐热门代币更重要。

昨天英文区都在刷屏讨论一个建立在 Hyperliquid 的 HyperEVM 上的新 Perp DEX 项目 @papertrade_xyz。

而之所以受关注，是因为项目启动时预存阶段吸引了 1.38 亿美元资金，开盘后几分钟内名义交易量就突破了百亿。

以及，一个带着浓厚资金盘设定的规则：亏钱即挖矿。

这个 DEX 开局自带1000倍杠杆，且0资金费率。
但开局时项目的 LP 是空的，也就是说你每一次开高杠杆爆仓亏掉的钱，会直接变成了庄家 LP 池的本金；

而作为补偿，协议会发给你代币$PAPER，让你变成它的“早期股东”，去分未来别人亏的钱。

在目前的极早期，每亏损 1 美元大约能换取 100 个 PAPER。质押这些 PAPER，就能分享协议对赢家抽成所产生的真实利润。

这就催生了一个荒诞的现象：

很多人故意开高杠杆去送钱爆仓，本质上是用确定的亏损，去“买”这个链上赌场的早期分红权。

这时你可能会问如果大家都赚钱，那 LP 池是空的，协议拿什么给大家钱呢？

根据其机制，赢家的本金可以直接退还，但利润需要进入一个排队系统（FIFO 队列）。

你赚了钱拿不走，必须等后面进场的新玩家爆仓亏钱了，资金池有了进账，才能按排队顺序把利润发给你。🤡

所以，目前冲进去“亏钱挖矿”的玩家，赌的是早期极高的代币红利，但项目飞轮很依赖后续源源不断的交易者进来亏钱输血。

那么你在这个 DEX 上亏多少钱就值得玩味了。亏少了，拿到的 PAPER 代币不够，质押分成可能也不多；

亏多了，考虑项目中长期风险，分给你的收入可能还抵不上你亏损的本金。

text:
After reading millie's tweet i was fascinated enough to clear up last weekend to fully read all 32 chapters of snowmoon end to end

I remember vitalik's point from a talk earlier that too many crypto bros fantasize about having their own country but not enough think about what would actually be different in it

snowmoon is his answer to that question

The geopolitical setting of the novel is three primary groups: the arctic empire (a mix of russian expansionism with american exceptionalism), veridia (european equality with a cryptographic bureaucracy) and dzego (ukrainian resistance with asian ingenuity).

i see a large impact of his novel as hyperstitioning the world we should create with the tech we've developed, so the rest of the post (spoilers ahead) summarizes the technology, institutions and ideology strands in his narrative

A. Technology

1. Warfare has shifted almost entirely to drones.

We get introduced to our Dzego protagonist zei when he is competing at a game that secretly doubles up as military recruitment strategy

After all, war is just computer screens with human handlers like zei working with AI to wipe out enemy dots (drones) on the screen using their own dots

2. Zk, zk everywhere: A stranger walks up to Seila, the wife of Veridian protagonist Gladias, and says he works with her husband. Naturally suspicious, she asks for evidence and he gives a zk proof showing that he spends a lot of time in proximity to him. 

The book is rife with zk proliferation, for example entering some buildings simply requires a zk proof of a certain reputation score

the best one was the freetown economics institute, where you are charged the square root of every minute you are in the building, but the price per minute is cheaper if your academic reputation score is high

3. Voice AI and personal agents feature prominently in the book. Any character can access LLMs at any time by simply moving throat muscles in a barely audible whisper. 

AIs are also linked to people, so when the Veridian protagonists wife calls him in an agitated state, the call shows up in red to indicate her emotional mood at the time of calling

4. Defi gets a mention as the protagonist forgets to transfer funds into his wallet, so he simply takes out a loan against his reputation score to pay the vendor

To secure a meeting with senators, characters sometimes burn zipcoin to show that they wont waste the persons time

5. There are 2 social media platforms in snowmoon, bluewhale which is proprietary and silverchat which is fully cryptographic. 

Civic technology is much more advanced in his world, so towards the end they run a cryptographic poll on silverchat asking what the citizens of Veridia desire as a response to the arctic empires encroachment of their territory, with results used to establish legitimacy for declaring a military emergency. 

The AI bots on silverchat access confidential military information and provide forecasts on likelihood of success for each option to inform voters on likely consequences of their vote

The technology theme in the book is a useful guide for us, as we now just need to work backwards from snowmoon to work at their integration in daily life

B. Institutions

This segment is really interesting in how Vitalik sees cryptographic institutions (called the steering) operating in the world. 

far from replacing parliament and other democratic structures, they instead work in parallel. 

The Steering has primarily 5 bureaucratic roles;

1.  keepers design rubrics that incentivize certain behaviors or actions. for example, if a music concert has violent themes, they fit into a category that pays a greater tax

almost nothing is banned in veridia, it is simply taxed more or less depending on how good it is for society

2. sentinels enforce these rubrics, performing spot checks by going to the concert and assigning a tax category to it

One of the other great examples was on how land tax is assessed, where citizens walking down the road may be randomly polled to give their rating on the aesthetics of a building, which determines its band

hilariously, citizens in veridia end up choosing the highest tax slab on plum harbor for reasons other than aesthetics as they dont like its ideology

3. Next up are acolytes who train to be sentinels or keepers. their exam is performing the same spot checks as sentinels and getting judged on how closely their own assessments match with the sentinels

All 3 of the organs above are anons, with a bounty paid to any citizen who uncovers the identity of steering members & the job they are working on

Becoming part of the steering from an acolyte requires confirmation by parliament

4. Heralds are members of the steering that have relinquished all their responsibility so that they can be a public face of the steering

its interesting that a public presence is perceived as incompatible with impartially carrying out duties

5. finally, the funding organs are quadratic funding and graph funding. 

QF is attacked in the book by closed social media giant bluewhale (and later the arctic empire) by paying out extra money to donors for giving money to a bad project. their goal is simply ensuring the matching funds do not go to genuine good projects that threaten their dominance. 

Graph funding is the more interesting organ, where some money may be allocated to a category like "airborne disease resistance". 

the category then divides into nodes such as air quality, detection, prevention, treatment, etc 

each category has a cryptographic committee that sets a % split and removes or adds nodes. however, committees can easily separate the good from the bad but not the great from the good, so the top 10% all having equal chance of selection

Another interesting tradeoff discussed is between randomized spot checkers who have less knowledge about an issue vs expert committee members who have abiliy to assess but special interests can end up capturing

the other interesting point was how lower down talent needs accountability to perform well while the top ones should have freedom from optimizing for the game

Overall this segment read like a blueprint for how bureaucracy should be reformed today, without having to overthrow existing institutions.

Maybe the main idea was the tradeoff between accountability and transparency, as the steering turns out to be less corruptible by the arctic empire than democratic structures since their identities are secret and it is difficult to threaten or cajole them (although an attempt is made). 

after all, accountability also means accountability to powerful interest groups who push on the weakest link, so some privacy in public affairs is required for its effective functioning

C. Ideology

This was maybe my favorite part of the book, what i loved was how the strongest version of arguments were presented instead of a strawman

1. the arctic empire argues for maximization of economic growth over all other objectives. the reason?

other goals keep changing according to the winds of preferences, but compounding economic growth is a base that helps in pursuit of anything else which  becomes the fashion of the day. 

so stop accelerating things that go in circles and focus on increasing economic output

in my view none of the counters offered in the book invalidate the argument;

a. health and education make people more productive and are also compounding across generations, so focusing on that is equally important

b. in reality, people do not want to maximize economic output so much as increase their relative growth. in the novel, the arctic empire suppresses other countries science and technology, which goes against the ideology of increasing economic growth

c. technological dominance can close off entire paths to humanity, so maximization of economic growth can lock us in to a certain path for decades. 

for eg becoming richer while reducing freedom thru lock into global imperial rule via mass surveillance  and robots is negative

2. the other big strand was veridia's belief in equality of all and love unconditional on achievement

the arctic empire argues against this belief by showing that it goes against the very idea of self improvement

for example, if you are a better version today than you were yesterday, then surely equality is impossible?

the counters here are;

a. rewarding excellence usually ends up protecting  hierarchy of supposedly superior people 

In the novel, a character defects to the arctic empire. however she soon loses her enthusiasm for their meritocratic ideals after being thrown in detention for challenging the instructor

b. excellence can come from curiosity more than it does from greed for appreciation or resentment at others. the winner of the national game zei is motivated by curiousity, compared to the runner up that cared about the achievement

c. affection when someone is struggling helps them thrive more than condemnation upon failure and adulation upon success

so being countercyclical in our encouragements brings out the best, in one instance a hug to Gladias made the difference in giving him the motivation to continue

at the same time, there is a concession that Veridia needs more ambition and recognition of achievement in their society

my favorite moment in the book was when the dzegoban protagonist zei has a game against a girl he has grown up with, bai

she asks whether they should spend the day at the mall instead of practicing drills. He goes on a long thought around game theory and how if they both dont practice neither has an advantage over the other, so its a good idea, while she simply replies that she'd like the economic surplus of spending time with him

overall definitely worth the weekend read, hope we see printed copies of it soon! 

Maybe the biggest underexplored theme in the book which i'd have liked to see more of was around how the future of work changes in a world of LLMs

Last Sunday, Vitalik released the full version of Snowmoon.

An underpinning concept to many of the ideas in the story is something V calls “Coordination Quotient.”

Coordination Quotient is his invention, there’s no pre-existing literature on that exact idea!

In simple terms, CQ is a cure for the prisoner’s dilemma or tragedy of the commons.

A community with high CQ is capable of defying its respective social or economic nash equilibrium.

High CQ basically says that even if we are individually incentivized to act selfishly, we are effective at *choosing* to act in the collective interest without external forces pressuring us to.

My personal analogy is that a society with a perfect Coordination Quotient wouldn’t need formal laws or a governing body to function at scale because it would be so good at acting in good faith and achieving sophisticated positive-sum goals.

Today is the day. 

Two whole years. 

I have learned so much in that time span. 

And while there are far more lessons to be grasped, I'll say that the one thing that has been the most valuable in that time span is the value of community. 

When I came into this, I didn't have any expectations. Truth be told, I was just thrilled I was finally making a living off of my camera. 

A dream 10 years in the making finally coming to fruition.

I had no idea that people I never knew existed a short while ago would leave such an indelible impression on my life. 

I found a second home in cities I never thought I would visit. 

I found a love for a game I didn't play.

I discovered the most vibrant community I've ever been a part of.

For all the good, and for all the not-so-good, the journey has led me to this point. 

I know I have bridges to repair.

The good news is I can finally look myself in the mirror and admit that maybe I'm the problem sometimes, and for that, I genuinely apologize. 

The better news, and perhaps the most goodest, is that the future not only looks - but for the first time in a long time - FEELS bright. 

More on this journey to come, but for now, I know I'm blessed to be here, and I'm thankful for the opportunity to have met so many wonderful humans along the way. 

Cheers to 2 years y'all 🥳

text:
Lee Robinson 这节斯坦福课，把 Grok Bot 这类常驻 Agent 的底层讲得很透：Agent 循环跑在服务器上，云电脑按需唤醒、用完就睡，状态全存在服务器，客户端和服务器之间只有一个工具 send_to_user。

我自己跑 agent 自动化，有三条做法和这套架构正好对上：

1. 结果从对话里收，别指望云电脑一直醒着。我用 Grok Bot 跑长期项目跟踪，最早让 Mac 定时去它的云电脑取文件，它一睡就取不到。后来改成让 Bot 每次在对话里回一段固定格式的结果块，Mac 从对话里收。对话本来就是它设计好的出口。

2. 别把沉默当成功。它被设计成没必要就不吭声，所以每轮都要求附结果块，没收到就记「待补」，不记成功。

3. 结果不明的动作不重跑。课里讲 durable workflow：崩了从第三步接着走，不重放前两步。我在发帖这类动作上手工做同一件事：结果不明先回读确认，不重发。

想把常驻 Agent 接进自己工作流的，10:06 和 18:07 这两段值得反复看。

text:
我是真不理解，为什么有人会 @yetone  用AI负责Magpie的开发，就开始喷他，甚至对这种项目感到担忧。

哥们，对于yetone这种本来就有很强工程能力的佬来说，AI只会加速他们做出更多、更高质量的项目。

真正值得担忧的，其实是那些完全没有开发经验，也不懂软件工程的人，拿着AI生成的代码就直接上线了。因为他们可能连哪里有问题、哪里存在风险、什么东西需要验证都不知道。

但对于有经验的开发者来说，这完全是另一回事。
他们很清楚应该让Agent做什么、不该做什么，哪些地方需要设置边界，哪些地方必须测试和验收。

而且说实话，现在的模型能力，配合一套成熟的Harness，已经完全可以承担从开发、提交PR、Review、测试到验收的绝大部分流程了（也可以说全部）。
只要你有足够的工程经验，提前设置好规则、约束和验证机制，很多问题完全可以在流程里被发现和解决。

更何况，我特别想问一句：
怎么搞得好像AI写代码就一定会出问题，人写代码就从来不会出Bug一样？

Cloudflare、AWS哪个没挂过？国内的支付宝、滴滴，难道你们就没经历过它们崩溃的时候吗？

软件工程本来就是一个不断发现问题、修复问题、控制风险的过程。人会犯错，Agent当然也会犯错，所以才需要测试、Review和各种工程约束。

我觉得批评一个项目的工程质量、代码质量，甚至质疑它的安全性，都很正常。

但现在有些人，连项目具体是怎么开发的、有什么工程保障都不了解，一听说是AI负责开发的，就觉得这东西不靠谱。

怎么连用AI开发软件都能变成一个喷点了😅.....

quoted_text:
🤨一个最高 1000 倍杠杆的链上赌场，连赔付也得排队？

由于流动性池从零启动、完全依赖后续亏损填充，当用户平仓盈利时，协议会立即退回其初始保证金，但如果池子当前资金不足以覆盖全部利润，超额部分就会进入队列，按先进先出（FIFO）顺序等待后续交易者的亏损补入后再兑付。

文档明确写明：池子允许在特定情形下出现负余额，未兑付的利润成为公开债权，而不是即时可提取的余额。

这一机制在上线初期被放大。平台预期会有大量用户同时交易，因此采用了排队优先级安排——官方承认，在技术约束下，小额名义价值订单无法与大额订单获得完全相同的优先级，否则前端可能面临大量垃圾请求导致拥堵。

团队称现有排队机制已在限制条件下尽量提高公平性，但社区反馈显示，部分用户在上线首日经历了明显的确认延迟和优先级差异。

有人吐槽「赢家提款还得排 FIFO 等下一个输家爆仓」，认为这更像是用账面浮盈打白条，而不是即时结算的交易所。

排队问题与价格操纵争议存在交集。官方在回应中提到，上线初期因预期拥堵而将持仓上限设得较为宽松，队列本身因交易确认时间不确定，也对操纵构成一定自然防护。随着流量下降，团队已开始在链上与中继层面收紧持仓限制。

但从用户视角看，排队不确定性带来了两重影响：一是盈利无法及时提取，影响资金周转；二是在对抗性环境下，如果定向提取持续发生，队列可能拉长，进一步降低新用户进入和持续交易的意愿。

从机制设计看，排队是「池子从零自举」的必然结果：没有外部做市商或预注入资金，盈利兑付就只能依赖后续亏损的流入节奏。这在理论上可以自我维持，但在实际运行中，确认延迟、优先级差异和潜在的队列积压，都会增加用户摩擦。

目前 @papertrade_xyz  公开数据尚未提供完整的排队债务时间序列，不过相对于中心化交易所与其他 DEX，仍是一大槽点。对于以高杠杆、零滑点为卖点的平台而言，结算的不确定性可能削弱其相对于传统永续交易所的体验优势。如果队列长期存在或在波动中反复拉长，可能会影响平台的交易留存和流动性池的填充效率。

如果池子资金不足，赢家就要排队等待；排队时间拉长后，部分用户可能选择离开，新的亏损流入减少，池子更难恢复，形成恶性循环。

如果某天，第一笔让赔付队列排起来的大行情到来时，这条「输家供养赢家」的流水线，讲面临终极考验。

quoted_text:
72 hour update on reseller CryptoBilis incident  🔽

As the investigation continues, we are working with relevant authorities. The volume of impacted devices is limited. We know this is concerning, especially for those directly affected, and we are reaching out to impacted users.

To date, all confirmed cases related to the disclosed draining incident of Oct 9th, 2026, involve devices sold through the Southeast Asia reseller CryptoBilis. Our systems and direct sales channels remain unaffected. 
We take the CryptoBilis situation seriously and are actively investigating.

We encourage impacted users to reach out to Ledger Support through official channels and file complaints with their local law enforcement authorities. As a reminder, CryptoBilis has confirmed having ceased all sales of hardware wallets.

We are reminding our authorized resellers and distributors to source products only through authorized channels and never to restock returned products.

Also, we strongly advise users not to purchase from unauthorized resellers, where the risk of buying suspicious, counterfeit or modified devices is important as nothing operates under ledger security guidelines.

Security isn’t static and this incident underscores why we continuously review and strengthen our distribution and anti-tamper processes. 

We are continuously improving that work now and events like this strengthen our resolution: reviewing authorized reseller controls, advancing hardware protections, and cooperating with authorities. Thanks to @SEAL_911 for their collaborative support and all their efforts.

This is an ongoing threat that doesn’t just impact Ledger, but the whole ecosystem, and we are calling others in the space to work with us on making improvements for users.

We believe in jointly working with researchers, other vendors and partners on improving industry chain-of-custody practices and anti-tamper techniques. Raising the bar on physical supply-chain integrity benefits the entire ecosystem. If you have relevant information, contact security@ledger.com.

For CryptoBilis buyers: do not initialize unused devices. If already set up, move to a new seed on a device from Ledger. If you have concerns that your device was impacted by the CryptoBilis incident, please contact Ledger Support through the official site: https://t.co/JUcWwJO9iF. 

Ledger Support is available 24/7 to answer your questions and concerns.

Scammers often try to take advantage of incidents like this. Rely only on official Ledger channels. Ledger will never call you, DM you, or ask for your 24-word recovery phrase.

🤨一个最高 1000 倍杠杆的链上赌场，连赔付也得排队？

由于流动性池从零启动、完全依赖后续亏损填充，当用户平仓盈利时，协议会立即退回其初始保证金，但如果池子当前资金不足以覆盖全部利润，超额部分就会进入队列，按先进先出（FIFO）顺序等待后续交易者的亏损补入后再兑付。

文档明确写明：池子允许在特定情形下出现负余额，未兑付的利润成为公开债权，而不是即时可提取的余额。

这一机制在上线初期被放大。平台预期会有大量用户同时交易，因此采用了排队优先级安排——官方承认，在技术约束下，小额名义价值订单无法与大额订单获得完全相同的优先级，否则前端可能面临大量垃圾请求导致拥堵。

团队称现有排队机制已在限制条件下尽量提高公平性，但社区反馈显示，部分用户在上线首日经历了明显的确认延迟和优先级差异。

有人吐槽「赢家提款还得排 FIFO 等下一个输家爆仓」，认为这更像是用账面浮盈打白条，而不是即时结算的交易所。

排队问题与价格操纵争议存在交集。官方在回应中提到，上线初期因预期拥堵而将持仓上限设得较为宽松，队列本身因交易确认时间不确定，也对操纵构成一定自然防护。随着流量下降，团队已开始在链上与中继层面收紧持仓限制。

但从用户视角看，排队不确定性带来了两重影响：一是盈利无法及时提取，影响资金周转；二是在对抗性环境下，如果定向提取持续发生，队列可能拉长，进一步降低新用户进入和持续交易的意愿。

从机制设计看，排队是「池子从零自举」的必然结果：没有外部做市商或预注入资金，盈利兑付就只能依赖后续亏损的流入节奏。这在理论上可以自我维持，但在实际运行中，确认延迟、优先级差异和潜在的队列积压，都会增加用户摩擦。

目前 @papertrade_xyz  公开数据尚未提供完整的排队债务时间序列，不过相对于中心化交易所与其他 DEX，仍是一大槽点。对于以高杠杆、零滑点为卖点的平台而言，结算的不确定性可能削弱其相对于传统永续交易所的体验优势。如果队列长期存在或在波动中反复拉长，可能会影响平台的交易留存和流动性池的填充效率。

如果池子资金不足，赢家就要排队等待；排队时间拉长后，部分用户可能选择离开，新的亏损流入减少，池子更难恢复，形成恶性循环。

如果某天，第一笔让赔付队列排起来的大行情到来时，这条「输家供养赢家」的流水线，讲面临终极考验。

text:
There's different ways to go about pitching your startup.

From 4 smart people you might hear 4 different pieces of advice:
i) put the team slide first
ii) put the problem slide first
iii) put the strongest slide first
iv) put the context slide first

Sometimes one advice is objectively better than the other, sometimes it depends on the situation, and sometimes  it's just a subjective preference of whomever is giving you the advice.

But between all the approaches that work, you can't go wrong by just blindly following a proven path from a person who's already succeeded (raised multiple times, made exits, got into accelerators etc.)

If you're a founder with a couple of mentors, a common mistake you can do is try to please everyone.

You pick up advice from mentor A, iterate on his feedback and then go to mentor B to get another round of validation. You can make more corrections and go to mentor C.

At this point, you're just butchering your pitch deck.

Pick one mentor to be your primary reviewer / spiritual leader and follow their advice almost naively. Even if they sometimes give suboptimal advice, it's still good enough to succeed (after all, your mentor has used this approach to secure investments, get into accelerators, make exits).

In this particular case, you can't go wrong by following Vibhu's advice 👇

quoted_text:
The pitch itself is a joke but the deck construction is worth noting for last minute @colosseum submitters. Bookmark this.

I have used these general principles to raise $100 million+:

1. Start with the most impressive thing about your company (your accolades, your traction) to form instant credibility 

2. Start wide to paint a picture of the state of your industry

3. What’s changing that makes this urgent to solve right now

4. Lay out the TAM (reviewer needs to know this can be big if solved)

5. Your unique insight or moat

6. BRIEFLY touch on the solution and product

7. Prove your thesis is correct with your traction (how fast are you growing?)

8. Touch on what’s next that unlocks distribution 

9. Finish with your big vision (how does the world change if you win?)

text:
A thief gets seven tries at an Ethereum account, and one of them works.

That's not a hack report.
It's the demo inside a new https://t.co/ydxw7xbfR2 post from Sunday morning, by Nethermind Ethereum core dev  Ankushin Daniil, about his draft ERC-8403.

Let me set the scene first.
Native account abstraction lets one account hold many keys, but it never says what add a key or revoke a key actually means.
Every wallet invents its own answer, and every other wallet has to learn it.
ERC-8403 tries to give that one shared shape.
The account doesn't store a list of keys.
It stores one 32-byte root.

Each authority is a leaf, keccak256(authority_id || predicate), where the predicate is usually a public key but could also be a spend limit or an unlock time.

To send a transaction, you bring two things.
One is a Merkle proof that your leaf sits under the root, and the other is a signature showing that leaf's holder approved this exact transaction.
Adding, rotating or revoking a key is the same move every time: write a new root.
The address never changes. 

Now back to the thief.
He has a key that was revoked, plus an old proof that it used to be in the tree.
The draft offers two tiers, and this is where they split.
A tier 1 account reads a recent root named by the transaction, which keeps validation cheap for the public mempool.
So it accepts the old root until that root falls out of the window, and in the demo the thief walks off with 2 ETH.
A tier 2 account reads its current root from storage, and refuses the revoked key from the very next block.
His other attempts, like a copied signature or a forged home block, get nothing.

You will like that the author kept that loss in the demo instead of hiding it.
There's more - on a second chain, the account carries no keys at all, just a storage proof that its root sits on a home chain.
Honest limits - the demo used secp256k1  keys, a single home-chain signer, and a minimal account where any key can set a new root.

72 hour update on reseller CryptoBilis incident  🔽

As the investigation continues, we are working with relevant authorities. The volume of impacted devices is limited. We know this is concerning, especially for those directly affected, and we are reaching out to impacted users.

To date, all confirmed cases related to the disclosed draining incident of Oct 9th, 2026, involve devices sold through the Southeast Asia reseller CryptoBilis. Our systems and direct sales channels remain unaffected. 
We take the CryptoBilis situation seriously and are actively investigating.

We encourage impacted users to reach out to Ledger Support through official channels and file complaints with their local law enforcement authorities. As a reminder, CryptoBilis has confirmed having ceased all sales of hardware wallets.

We are reminding our authorized resellers and distributors to source products only through authorized channels and never to restock returned products.

Also, we strongly advise users not to purchase from unauthorized resellers, where the risk of buying suspicious, counterfeit or modified devices is important as nothing operates under ledger security guidelines.

Security isn’t static and this incident underscores why we continuously review and strengthen our distribution and anti-tamper processes. 

We are continuously improving that work now and events like this strengthen our resolution: reviewing authorized reseller controls, advancing hardware protections, and cooperating with authorities. Thanks to @SEAL_911 for their collaborative support and all their efforts.

This is an ongoing threat that doesn’t just impact Ledger, but the whole ecosystem, and we are calling others in the space to work with us on making improvements for users.

We believe in jointly working with researchers, other vendors and partners on improving industry chain-of-custody practices and anti-tamper techniques. Raising the bar on physical supply-chain integrity benefits the entire ecosystem. If you have relevant information, contact security@ledger.com.

For CryptoBilis buyers: do not initialize unused devices. If already set up, move to a new seed on a device from Ledger. If you have concerns that your device was impacted by the CryptoBilis incident, please contact Ledger Support through the official site: https://t.co/JUcWwJO9iF. 

Ledger Support is available 24/7 to answer your questions and concerns.

Scammers often try to take advantage of incidents like this. Rely only on official Ledger channels. Ledger will never call you, DM you, or ask for your 24-word recovery phrase.

quoted_text:
AI × DePIN  重新利用已经存在的硬件是一个值得关注的方向

全球有大量智能手机每天处于闲置状态，如果这些设备也能参与 AI 计算，能释放多大的潜力？

@Acurast 已经在尝试这个方向, 值得重点关注！

目前 Acurast 的网络规模：目前网络已接入约 30 万至 32 万多个计算单元，覆盖 175 多个国家。

核心优势在哪里？

第一，算力来自现有设备。
用户通过 Processor 应用接入网络，不需要自己购买专业 GPU，也不必建设数据中心。对于大量中小规模的计算任务，这种模式提供了另一种选择。

第二，计算过程可以验证。
Acurast 利用 TEE 可信执行环境与硬件远程证明，让任务能够在受保护的环境中运行，并验证设备和执行代码的真实性。

这对隐私敏感的 AI 推理、自动化任务和 AI Agent 都有实际意义。

第三，已经开始尝试真实 AI 工作负载。
今年 9 月，Acurast 将 Laya 决策模型部署到全球手机节点。它面向分类、评分、内容审核、提示注入检测等结构化决策任务，可以在手机 CPU 上执行。

这类任务未必需要昂贵的 GPU 集群，却需要稳定、可靠且能够保护数据的执行环境。

我个人更看重 Acurast 的应用边界

手机算力不可能全面取代大型数据中心，但 AI 计算也不一定全部需要集中在云端。

越来越多 AI Agent 需要处理用户数据、执行自动化工作流，或者完成轻量级实时决策时，分布式、可验证的边缘算力就有了发挥空间。

所以，AI × DePIN 的长期机会，取决于这些设备究竟能完成多少有价值的工作。

如果这条路径跑通，全球分散的手机就有机会成为去中心化 AI 基础设施的一部分。

接下来，重点关注三个指标：真实计算需求、网络激励的可持续性，以及 $ACU 能否捕获网络增长带来的价值。

@category_xyz 在Open主舞台宣布的。Monad L1上直接做机密执行域，不用另起一条私有链。每个域通过L1上的标准EVM hub合约启用，不需要分叉也不需要协议升级。域内交易、状态、合约代码端到端加密，连L1本身都读不到；跨域转账也是加密的，地址和金额对外不可见。机构自己定验证者集合、信任模型、访问规则和管辖权，默认谁都看不到，审计或监管可以按需给权限。同时域还直接接到Monad的共享流动性，结算是原子的
现在还是设计方案，Category Labs在跟早期设计伙伴推进，还没上线。发布前有过“Privacy is coming”的预热。  
https://t.co/jDM67nqYDv  
https://t.co/wlb0R3sU7Y  

why matters：机构（银行、基金、交易台、企业财资）最怕的就是链上全透明。他们现在要么不上链，要么自己搞私有链把流动性切碎。这个设计如果跑通，等于让这些机构能直接用公开链的速度和流动性，同时业务还保密。对Monad来说，这是把大额资金和真实业务流程拉进来的关键入口，后面稳定币、RWA、支付的体量都有可能跟着放大

2. 股票上链，xStocks原生上Monad：
@valgui在台上宣布@xStocksFi 原生部署到Monad，覆盖1100+代币化美股和ETF。代币直接在Monad上铸造和结算，不是从别的链桥过来。1:1对应底层证券，ERC-20形态，可以往DEX、借贷、钱包里组合
这跟 @aave 之前提的V4代币化股票hub提案也能对上。链上后续也有合约部署和铸造的讨论  
https://t.co/dO3Bzok7O8  

why matters：股票类资产是全球最大的流动性池之一。原生上链意味着不用桥，可以直接在Monad做交易、抵押、组合。对交易者来说多了24/7的股票敞口，对DeFi协议来说多了新的抵押品和交易对，对持有美股的人来说多了链上使用场景。如果流动性慢慢起来，Monad的交易量和TVL都有机会从纯crypto资产往传统资产延伸，可以关心Monad上几个DEX的进展@perpltrade @hellotradeapp @KuruExchange 等还有几个还没宣发的

3. Cadence共识，提升性能并解决MEV： 
@_jhunsaker现场demo了Cadence。这是多并发提议者共识，多个验证者同时提议，配合极端流水线。现在Monad主网是300ms出块、600ms最终性，升级完成后目标100ms出块、300ms最终性，再配上BTX加密mempool，从协议层压MEV
https://t.co/GLULPvHZHe  

why matters：做市商和高频交易最在意的是延迟和被夹。100ms出块加上协议层压MEV，等于让链上交易体验更接近中心化交易所，同时减少被三明治的损失。对普通交易者和DeFi用户来说，滑点和被夹的成本会下降；对专业交易团队来说，更愿意把订单流放上来。后面如果真落地，交易量和做市深度有机会继续涨，CT里也会有更多人讨论“链上交易是不是开始能打CEX了”

4. StraitsX x Monad 新元稳定币：
XSGD和XUSD计划2027年初原生发行到Monad，XSGD会是链上第一条原生新加坡元稳定币，还受技术、监管和合规条件约束。双方也在看卡项目、支付和跨境结算这些场景。StraitsX是Open的title sponsor，持有新加坡大额支付机构牌照，累计稳定币交易量接近700亿。  
https://t.co/KTv4Q24Cly  

why matters：稳定币是链上真正的支付和结算入口。原生发行加上受监管牌照，意味着后面卡、跨境、商户结算这些场景可以更顺地接进来，而不是只停留在DeFi套利。对亚太用户和支付公司来说，多了一条合规的链上通道；对Monad来说，稳定币存量和使用量起来后，整条链的日常活跃和费用都会受益。后面如果卡和支付真落地，用户增长会从纯crypto圈子往更广的支付用户延伸

5. Open台上也拉了Visa、ETH Foundation、Dragonfly、Tether、Zero Hash等。主舞台之外还有DeltaV Demo Day，项目直接对VC路演。Metropolis黑客松也还在进行，奖金25万+，提交截止10/13

why matters：这些数据说明主网已经有真实使用，不是纯叙事。机构方和头部协议持续进来，加上黑客松和Demo Day，开发者和项目方还会继续进场，这些都会直接反映在链上活跃和资产规模上

author: trylimitless
quoted_text:
The Most Underestimated Barrier to Institutional Crypto Is Not Regulation

Panelists Samar Sen (@talostrading), Benjamin Stani (@FalconXGlobal), Jean-David Péquignot (@JDP_VS, @DeribitOfficial) and CJ Hetherington (@cjhtech, @lmtls_research) discussed "The Institutional Trading Stack: Liquidity, Execution, and Prime Brokerage."

What actually keeps institutional money out?

Sen of Talos named liquidity, and called it the most underestimated factor in the whole conversation. Not regulation, not custody. Institutions have to connect liquidity scattered across venues to execute size reliably, and the trading systems traditional firms already own are not sufficient for this market's structure. What the job requires is algorithmic execution routing across centralized exchanges, OTC and DEXs while slicing orders to market conditions.

What product is missing entirely?

This was the most interesting unbuilt thing on the stage. Hetherington of Limitless pointed out that traditional finance manages portfolio risk with instruments like interest rate swaps and credit default swaps, while large parts of this market have no appropriate hedge at all. His specific target was private credit: default risk on lending to private companies is rising, and there are far too few products that let that risk be transferred or dispersed to other investors.

Digital asset contracts as a hedging venue for risks traditional products never handled well. That is a very different pitch from faster settlement.

Who wins as the two markets converge?

Possibly the incumbents. More financial firms are investing in digital asset companies or building their own trading and custody infrastructure, and as the markets merge, licenses, client bases and accumulated regulator trust turn into an advantage rather than a legacy cost.

What is the risk in that?

Geography. US regulatory change is accelerating the convergence, and the panel's warning was that if other jurisdictions do not build frameworks at a comparable pace, the entire institutional stack simply concentrates in the United States.

Moderated by Daniel Kim (@TIGER_NODE), Founder and CEO of Tiger Research (@tiger_research_).

🎉 REA 太牛了，一周冲到了 12 万星，这里扒一扒 REA 实操

REA 本质：是一个夹在 Agent 和分析器中间的工具。Agent 用自然语言问，REA 通过 MCP 调工具，把结果汇总为证据：伪代码、汇编、字符串、符号、调用关系，和缺失情况。

写伪代码的是 Ghidra，这是是美国国家安全局开源的逆向套件，负责把机器码拆成汇编，再翻成近似 C 的伪代码。

这次我们只给了编译好的镜像，看看 REA 是怎么像素级还原应用的：

一、跑通链路

克隆 REA，配置 JDK 21 和 Ghidra 12.1.4。配好之后，REA 的 Ghidra provider 可以按函数粒度生成伪代码，最终变成 JSON。这一步给出一个函数，就能拿回可读的近似 C 代码。

二、基于证据还原代码

只还原几个函数，并不足够覆盖整个应用，于是用同一套 Ghidra 的 headless，加上自写的 https://t.co/7wQ6HlDyWr，一次导出 2567 个函数。

同时用额外的四个工具补足 Ghidra 盖不住的部分：

1. nm 和 swift-demangle，还原方法签名和协议遵循
2. https://t.co/5qKLtwMBwC，解析 Swift 反射元数据，拿出每个属性的名字、类型和枚举 case
3. otool -tV，伪代码丢了浮点或看错分支时，按 arm64 指令把数字还原出来
4. plutil 导出 11 种语言的文案、图标和 Info.plist 从安装包直接复制

最后一步再按模块构建出来 Swift 项目。

中国古代有个叫“子贡赎人，子路受牛”的故事

子贡花钱赎回在外国沦为奴隶的鲁国人，却拒绝领取国家补偿，孔子批评他：这样会让拿补偿的人显得不够高尚，承担不起费用的人，以后可能就不再救人了。子路救起落水者，收下对方送来的一头牛，孔子却很赞许，因为这会鼓励更多人救人。

ZachXBT 今天对 XRP Ledger 的漏洞赏金提出了类似质疑。安全团队 Veria Labs 发现并报告了一个可突破 XRP 供应上限的严重漏洞，获得 25 万美元奖励，他在回复 XRP Ledger 基金会时质疑，金库拥有数十亿美元，却只给发现如此严重漏洞的白帽 25 万美元。

他担心，这样的奖励会削弱善意报告漏洞的动力，让下一位发现漏洞的人更倾向于利用它获取上亿美元。

目前该漏洞已被修复，但奖励是否与白帽避免的潜在损失相称，仍值得讨论。

text:
Chess蔡司的毒舌日记 #3 🏦

不要再无脑相信中心化了，尤其是很多地方银行，理财结构，无论是传统金融还是币圈。

兜兜转转，宜信还是暴雷了。

这件事儿让蔡司想起来2016年还是2017年，当年很多互联网人都很信赖「懒投资」，就是那个微信公众号上叫「大玩家张磊」的懒投资，我自己也放了快70W RMB进去，那时候还没进入区块链，但是懒投资的很多收益年化大概7-12%之间。

我那个时候对金融没啥认识，然后就是单纯的觉得张磊这个人很不错，从公众号里包括很多Web2互联网大V都在给他背书，我听说他们自己员工也很多把家底都存进去了。

后来不出意外的暴雷了，张磊这哥们现在是完全不知道干啥了，反正是资不抵债，然后财新还报道过。

最后成立了一个追债小组，期初还有一些回音，给我们的一些资产回来都是什么广东某饭店粮票，某超市米面这些乱七八糟的兑换券，那时候后看感觉简直离谱的要死，全是垃圾资产懒投资可以这么不负责的放贷出去，最后全是坏账。

我家人因为这个事儿还emo了好久，也正是因为这个原因，让我2018年开始定投BTC，从那个时候开始减少法币资产，并且大多数时候都是自己掌管自己的BTC，ETH之类，赢钱钱包开始体验各种，并且只从官网购买，从来不在淘宝或者其他渠道购买。

所以啊，即使某些人说的非常好，但真的不要轻易相信。「Trust」相信这个东西，太重了。不是商K里喝多了推杯换盏就可以信任，也不是每次搞活动一起玩就可以信任，更不是谈过恋爱就可以信任。

信任真的需要谨慎，无论对某个产品，某个服务，还是某个人。

希望所有的朋友们都不要在遭受信任的无妄之灾，而这也恰恰是我们 @bagel_win 为什么第一天就坚持onchain，自托管的原则，我们基于Polymarket，也在接入Hyperliquid，但原则都是只接入龙头onchain的产品，不碰任何中心化服务和产品，这很重要。

本集，完。

just because regulated markets are easier to access for consumers in the us today, a lot of excitement is dwindling. but the opportunity for onchain is exporting unified financial services to the world

中国古代有个叫“子贡赎人，子路受牛”的故事

子贡花钱赎回在外国沦为奴隶的鲁国人，却拒绝领取国家补偿，孔子批评他：这样会让拿补偿的人显得不够高尚，承担不起费用的人，以后可能就不再救人了。子路救起落水者，收下对方送来的一头牛，孔子却很赞许，因为这会鼓励更多人救人。

text:
$HOTBOT has recently rolled out several updates, and my take on this latest round of developments is that its product fundamentals are strengthening

8nnaeWCw8mUypcGAgbmSuzAT85uWx4UN12adDrMhXrGF 

But whether it can evolve from an ecosystem token with a working product into an AI Trading project backed by sustained demand still depends on real users, trading performance, and token value capture.

The most noteworthy part of this update is not the addition of a few more AI bots. It is that Hot Bot is starting to connect strategy creation, execution, review, and optimization into a more integrated workflow. Previously, the main thesis behind HOTBOT was its position in ClawPump’s Agentic Finance ecosystem, embedding AI trading agents into existing trading workflows and gaining attention through ClawPump and AnsemHack. Now, the product is demonstrating more concrete strategy configuration and self-optimization capabilities, suggesting that the team is moving beyond the ecosystem narrative and making tangible progress on the product itself.

However, three things must be distinguished: product improvements do not mean trading performance has been validated; ecosystem attention does not equal genuine user demand; and product growth does not mean HOTBOT has established sustainable token value capture.

The Latest Catalyst: Hot Bot Is Moving from Trade Execution Toward Strategy Optimization

The update I find most interesting is RSISS, or Recursive Self Improving Strategy Suggestions.

According to the team, RSISS draws on Hot Bot’s proprietary trading data, while each user’s individual trading team learns and continuously improves from every token researched, entry taken, and exit executed. The system can recommend strategy parameter adjustments in real time, which users can apply with one click or dismiss.

Examples include:

Reducing the trailing stop from 30% to 25%.
Raising the minimum market cap threshold from $40K to $60K.
Adjusting the Entry Score threshold.
Using ShieldBot checks to filter out trades that do not meet the required conditions.

This means Hot Bot is no longer simply executing rules defined by users. It is attempting to use historical data and the outcomes of individual trades to improve subsequent strategies.

If this mechanism works, it could create a feedback loop: more trading generates more data, better data improves strategy recommendations, and better strategies potentially improve user retention.

However, the team explicitly describes these recommendations as suggestions, not guarantees of returns. What we can confirm from the current materials is that the strategy recommendation feature is being presented. We cannot conclude that the suggested adjustments have actually improved win rates, risk-adjusted returns, or long-term profitability.

The meaningful evidence will be verifiable performance comparisons before and after optimization, including actual results after fees, slippage, and losing trades.

Easy Mode vs. Advanced Mode: Lowering the Barrier to Entry

Hot Bot is also refining two different user experiences.

Easy Mode is closer to a “coding agent experience for trading.” Users can start with preset strategies instead of building or configuring complex rules from scratch.

The posts showcase several strategy options, including Oracle, Clips, Balanced, Degen, and Custom. These presets target different trading scenarios, such as newly launched tokens, small and fast trades, tokens already showing momentum, or more aggressive trading in either direction.

Users can also configure take-profit levels, stop losses, trailing stops, budgets, and the number of tokens traded simultaneously. Degen mode offers different market-cap ranges and risk profiles.

Advanced Mode is better suited to users who want more granular control over their trading logic.

These two modes address different needs: some users want AI to handle much of the strategy configuration, while others prefer to retain greater control.

If Hot Bot can help beginners get started quickly while giving experienced users room to refine their strategies, it could expand its user base beyond people already familiar with trading bots and automated strategies.

But preset strategies alone are not a moat. The real question is whether they remain effective across different market conditions and whether users continue using them over time.

Trading Agents as a Service: Integrating the Full Trading Workflow

The latest Daily Update places Trading Agents as a Service, RSISS, Easy Mode, Advanced Mode, and UX/UI improvements within the same product direction.

Based on the product interfaces shown previously, Hot Bot aims to let different agents handle different responsibilities:

ResearchBot: Researches tokens and identifies potential trading opportunities.
SniperBot: Monitors new tokens and specific entry opportunities.
TraderBot: Tracks the market and executes trading strategies.

Users can configure budgets, permissions, and strategies, allowing different agents to operate within their assigned roles.

The potential value is that users no longer need to find separate tools for research, market monitoring, and trade execution. They can organize the entire trading workflow within one product.

The team has also emphasized reducing reliance on third-party APIs so that new-token data reaches trading bots faster. A project update claimed that faster data delivery could allow new tokens to reach bots approximately 60 seconds earlier. If this improvement holds up in real-world conditions, it could matter for new-token trading, but data coverage, latency consistency, and actual execution quality still need to be verified.

Integrating multiple agents into one product can improve the user experience. Proving that those agents deliver a genuine trading edge requires stronger evidence.

What Is the Market Betting On?

I think the market is betting on three things.

First, AI agents could become a new entry point for trading.

Hot Bot is not trying to build just another buy-and-sell bot. It aims to integrate research, screening, entry decisions, execution, and strategy adjustments. If users become accustomed to delegating parts of their trading workflow to agents, the product could generate recurring demand.

Second, RSISS could make strategies continuously adaptive rather than leaving them as static rules.

Traditional trading bots generally execute conditions specified by users. Hot Bot aims to go a step further by using its own trading data and individual users’ trading histories to recommend ongoing adjustments. If this approach improves results across different market conditions, it could create a more meaningful product advantage than UI improvements or preset strategies alone.

Third, HOTBOT could evolve beyond the attention generated by ClawPump and AnsemHack into a product-driven token with real users and sustained trading demand.

Ecosystem support and hackathon exposure have been important sources of attention. But the market ultimately needs to see whether that attention converts into actual usage, whether users stick around, and whether the product generates sustainable economic activity.

The market can price in the future of AI trading early, but a long-term valuation cannot rely on that narrative indefinitely.

My Assessment: Product Fundamentals Are Improving, but Commercial Validation and Token Value Capture Remain Unproven

At the product level, this is meaningful progress. Preset strategies, parameter recommendations, user-controlled approvals, different levels of complexity, and a design centered on continuous learning from trading data make the product’s intended user journey more concrete. Earlier analysis focused more on its agent architecture and ecosystem positioning; now, we can see more of the actual strategy configuration and optimization experience.

At the commercial level, Trading Agents as a Service offers a potential path forward. If users are willing to pay for automated trading capabilities, Hot Bot could establish a business model that does not depend entirely on token speculation. However, the current materials do not provide paid user numbers, subscription revenue, retention metrics, or unit economics. It is therefore too early to conclude that commercialization has been proven.

At the token level, the situation needs to be assessed separately. A previous snapshot of the ClawPump page showed approximately 627.485 SOL in cumulative creator fees, 252.403 SOL in buybacks, and roughly 79,950.5 ANSEM distributed to holders, valued at around $11,025 at the time. These figures reflect economic activity within the ClawPump ecosystem. They cannot be treated directly as Hot Bot product revenue or attributed entirely to value capture for the HOTBOT token.

Frequent product updates alone are therefore not enough to conclude that HOTBOT’s buyback demand, cash flow, or token demand has strengthened. The connection between product growth and token value still needs to be demonstrated.

Four Developments I Will Continue Watching

First, verifiable results from RSISS.

If the team begins publishing verifiable strategy performance, including win rates before and after optimization, average win/loss ratios, maximum drawdowns, returns after trading costs, and performance across different market conditions, RSISS could become a measurable product advantage rather than just a feature.

Second, genuine demand for Trading Agents as a Service.

Growth in active users, paid conversions, retention, and sustained trading activity would give Hot Bot a valuation basis that extends beyond ecosystem attention. If users only try the product once, or primarily show up to speculate on the token, the narrative will be less durable.

Third, continued ecosystem support and user growth after AnsemHack.

Ecosystem backing and hackathon exposure have helped attract attention. The real catalyst is not being mentioned again; it is whether that exposure leads to integrations, users, partnerships, and sustained usage. If the team continues making product progress after the event-driven attention fades, the market may begin to reassess the project more favorably.

Fourth, a clearer economic connection between product usage and HOTBOT.

This is the most important issue for token holders. We need to establish which product features, if any, require HOTBOT, what role the token plays in access or other mechanisms, and whether product growth generates verifiable token demand or a sustainable buyback mechanism.

If the product becomes increasingly useful but users never need to hold or buy HOTBOT, product success and token appreciation remain two separate things.

Key Risks

Competition. AI trading agents, automated strategies, and trading bots are not unique to Hot Bot. It needs to establish an advantage through data quality, execution speed, strategy performance, and user experience rather than relying on the AI label alone.

Retention and commercialization. Automated trading tools can attract users during active market conditions, but usage frequency and willingness to pay may decline when volatility falls or strategies underperform. The speed of feature releases cannot substitute for retention data.

Token value capture. Growing product usage does not necessarily translate into greater demand for HOTBOT. The token’s actual utility, the relevant economic mechanisms, and the flow of funds need to be established. ClawPump’s fees, buybacks, and rewards cannot simply be treated as direct support for HOTBOT’s value.

Fading ecosystem attention. ClawPump and AnsemHack have provided entry points for attention, but if subsequent growth is not supported by new users, product progress, or verifiable trading performance, the market may once again classify HOTBOT as a token primarily driven by ecosystem hype.

Final Take

The three things I will prioritize are whether RSISS actually improves trading performance, whether Hot Bot develops a sustained base of real users and commercial revenue, and whether that growth translates into actual demand for HOTBOT.

If all three begin to receive meaningful validation, HOTBOT could evolve from a token benefiting from ecosystem attention into an AI Trading project supported by real product usage and economic mechanisms.

If feature releases and ecosystem exposure continue without verifiable trading advantages, user retention, and token value capture, it may remain a speculative position trading the AI agent narrative ahead of its fundamentals.

text:
Getting GPUs, paying for them, and keeping them busy are three different problems.

Many providers make you solve the second one before you’ve ever spun up your first GPU.

You’re asked for upfront advances and a guarantor, then locked into contracts that outlast your product roadmap.

Flexible demand shouldn’t need a locked-in supply.
author: ionet
quoted_text:
I have had a front row seat to this market at @ionet since 2024.

One thing a GPU price index cannot tell you is whether a funded startup, cash in hand, will get told no. Or asked for 30-40% upfront and a guarantor (preferably the lead VC or top client).

Compute increasingly behaves like a landlord business. Parts of AI landscape still behave like a VC growth bet. They do not want the same things.

The compute supplier has financed hardware and needs a tenant who keeps paying. A fresh funding round of the customer helps, but it does not guarantee that the customer will survive the contract period.

The AI players want adoption measured typically by subs and LTV on retained users. A new model or agent workflow brings traffic. Their customers experiment, change direction and switch providers. A feature that attracts users this month can become a basic expectation next month.

The capacity commitment is much harder to change.

That leaves the AI solution provider in the middle committing cash upfront while selling to their customers the freedom to leave.

Token volume can easily grow with more compute while more cash gets locked into supplier advances. Engineering improves efficiency, competition pushes prices down, and the customer gets much of the saving. The AI solution provider still carries the risk of empty GPU hours.

Two teams can run the same hardware and serving stack yet have very different economics because one gets better payment terms and has customers who commit.

That is where I expect the market to move: committed enterprise demand alongside flexible API traffic, more minimum spend agreements and a premium for guaranteed capacity.

Turning recurring usage into contracts that suppliers can finance could become a meaningful cost advantage.

It also adds another dimension to the @Silicon_Data charts. The hourly rate needs to be read alongside the advance, guarantees and buyer approval requirements. A higher rate paid monthly can be easier to fund than a lower rate that ties up the cash needed to grow.

Getting the GPUs, paying for them and keeping them busy are three different problems. An inference business has to solve all three.

We were able to fine tune an open weight model (Qwen3.5-9B) on proprietary internal data at @coinbase, and it out performed frontier models, at much lower cost and speed, for a specialized task (fraud prevention in this case).

I think we'll see more of this pattern inside companies. The frontier models are amazing generalists. But increasingly you'll see specialist models out perform on more narrow tasks, either working on teams, or by themselves.

We're making it easy to fine tune models internally for our employees. We even have a skill for it in our internal harness that makes it easy to spin these up and start training them:

"/fine-tune-and-serve-llm I want to fine-tune Qwen for payments risk review. help me get started"

I imagine we'll have some backend services that could be replaced entirely by this new architecture.

author: ViewsOfChris
quoted_text:
这是一个高度集中、激进的AI主题2千万美金的投资组合（0杠，分配大概率维持到2028年底），围绕当前AI基础设施与变现链条构建，向“马斯克生态倾斜”和带“镐与铲”偏向，对SpaceX进行了刻意的大幅超配 。

1. SpaceX主导仓位（31%）
将SpaceX视为核心高上行仓位，而非卫星仓。它结合了发射基础设施、Starlink连接能力，以及AI相关敞口（通过xAI/Grok整合及更广泛的马斯克生态）。该仓位规模反映了对SpaceX具备超越纯AI硬件的多年增长期权的强烈看法。

2. 硬件为主的核心（约44%）
最大板块集中在半导体与光模块：
存储（美光 + SK海力士）——定位于HBM持续紧张及AI加速器需求。

定制硅与网络（博通、迈威尔、英特尔）——暴露于超大规模厂商定制ASIC及数据中心互联。

光模块（Coherent、Lumentum）——AI集群规模扩张推动高速光互联需求。

英伟达与AMD保持较小但存在的仓位，提供直接加速器敞口而不主导组合。

3. 选择性云/平台敞口（约20%）
Meta与谷歌为最大云端持仓，同时反映AI基础设施支出与应用层变现。亚马逊与微软经过前期减仓后仓位较小。其如加上SpaceX等，其实51% 都是云。

4. 特斯拉作为战术性AI/机器人袖套（5%）
特斯拉仓位有意义但非主导，捕捉自动驾驶、Optimus及Dojo相关AI敞口，而不使组合过度依赖。

5. 5% 现金 / 国债
永久性流动性缓冲，用于波动管理、机会性再平衡或新想法。这是有意设置，而非剩余现金。

整体方法
激进且集中：头部持仓按设计较大；组合接受较高的特异风险（尤其是SpaceX）以换取上行空间。

“镐与铲”偏向：硬件、存储与光模块获得的资本多于纯软件/应用名称。
马斯克生态倾斜：SpaceX（31%）+ 特斯拉（5%）= 合计36%敞口。

迭代优化：当前权重反映了多轮调整（移除台积电、降低英伟达、提升博通与美光、加入光模块名称、锁定现金）。

该结构适合优先考虑基础设施瓶颈与高信念个股的激进AI主题委托，而非广泛多元化。它具有较高波动性与单名风险，需根据AI资本开支趋势、存储定价及SpaceX特定发展进行主动监控。

$SPCX $MU $META

text:
伊朗的战争压力，正在变成越来越直接的民生压力

伊朗多地的工人和退休人员抗议还在持续。10月初，德黑兰、阿瓦士、克尔曼沙阿等地都有相关报道，到了10月11日，伊斯法罕、舒什和拉什特又出现了退休人员集会。他们要求提高养老金、补发拖欠款项、改善医疗保障，说到底，就是收入已经越来越难覆盖正常生活。

伊朗统计中心最近公布的数据中，物价同比上涨89.8%。也就是说，同样一篮子商品和服务，现在平均要比一年前多花接近九成的钱。食品价格涨得更快，而退休人员的大部分收入恰恰要用来吃饭、买药和支付日常开销。养老金即使有所增加，只要追不上物价，实际能买到的东西还是越来越少，遇上补发款项拖延，生活就更难安排。

这也解释了为什么民生抗议中会出现反战声音。按照反对派组织公布的记录，克尔曼沙阿的部分抗议者喊出了不要战争和杀戮、要求生活保障的口号。至少对这些参与者来说，战争已经和自己的饭钱、药钱、养老金联系在了一起。他们要求政府回答的，是眼前的生活困难什么时候才能解决。

伊朗承受的压力也在相互叠加。制裁和海上封锁限制石油出口和外汇收入，本币贬值又让进口商品、原材料和设备变贵。企业经营更困难，工人的工作和收入承压，政府用于维持补贴、工资和养老金的财力也受到挤压。原本就存在的欠款、医保和管理问题，在这种环境下会更加突出。

现在连伊朗内部的一些强硬派议员，也开始公开批评央行和政府的经济政策。这说明围绕经济困难的争论，已经延伸到了体制内部：外部压力当然存在，但国内政策是否加重了普通人的负担，同样有人追问。对政府来说，外部冲突持续多久，和国内还能承受多久，是必须同时面对的问题。

这些抗议会增加伊朗缓和冲突、争取放松制裁和恢复贸易的现实动力，可以看到的是，继续对峙的成本正在落到更多家庭身上。如果工资和养老金的购买力继续下降，医疗和基本生活问题迟迟得不到解决，政府承受的国内压力就会继续增加。

一个 @Gate ，交易更多市场
author: PhyrexNi
quoted_text:
美国财政部长贝森特表示，美国本周可能扣押约10亿美元与伊朗有关的加密货币，进一步切断伊朗获取和转移资金的渠道。

从此前披露的案件看，这些加密资产有一部分来自石油收入。伊朗受到金融制裁，卖出石油之后，收款和跨境转账都受到限制，于是通过中间商把货款换成加密货币，再转给相关机构，用于资金调拨和对外付款。

美国司法部9月公布的一起案件就涉及这种操作。检方指控，相关网络通过交易所账户和多个钱包，转移了超过15亿美元的伊朗石油销售收入，并申请没收其中约 6,100万 美元的加密资产。这些目前仍属于检方指控。

另一部分是直接用外币买来的。链上分析公司 Elliptic 发现，伊朗央行相关钱包累计购入至少 5.07亿 美元USDT，其中两笔采购使用阿联酋迪拉姆付款。按照该公司的分析，这些 USDT 可能被用于跨境贸易结算，也可能在本地市场换成里亚尔，帮助支撑伊朗的汇率。

但 USDT 有发行方冻结机制。钱即使放在自己的钱包里，被列入黑名单后也可能无法转出。Tether在 9月 表示，今年已经协助冻结约 5.5亿 美元与伊朗有关的 USDT 。
