quoted_text:
大家好，你们的Jennie重回战场了，这次是以 @MojoAI_HQ 的Marketing Lead的身份，将全面负责Mojo的全球GTM、增长和合作。

从ChatGPT出世的第一天，我就在AI x Crypto这个交叉赛道折腾了，这几年也见证了不少两个行业的人才和团队在相互流转。去年年初从上一个AI项目离开后，为了努力保持对市场的水温感知，捣鼓了不少开源AI工具产品和参加了不少AI黑客松，帮助了几个不同阶段的AI x Crypto项目做市场增长，加上去年从上海搬到伦敦，也在伦敦有了自己的线下活动品牌 @demoinnlondon  ，帮一些国内AI产品和团队做了英国和欧洲本地市场的出海。

但我心里依然有一团小火苗：找寻下一个值得all-in的AI x Crypto的市场机会和值得共事的创始人和团队。

其实在过去的几个月里，我就已经开始陪伴Mojo团队成长了一段时间，这段时间我感受到了创始人老白 @ForestBai1  对于产品本身和AI交易赛道的笃信与专注，感受到了产品研发团队对于用户体验和技术架构优化迭代的速度与效率，感受到了许多早期社区用户给产品提需求反馈建议时的真诚与不吝，这些都让我对Mojo的未来产生无限期待，也燃起了让我自己去再次出发挑战无限难度的战斗欲望。

同时在实际体验Mojo之后，对于交易频率并不高、交易装备并不齐全的我来说，似乎找到了一个我和交易之间的一个奇点，这个奇点就像我第一次用ChatGPT、第一次使用Vibe Coding工具的时刻一样，让过去不敢自称“交易员”的我可以开始进入交易员的心流和执行流，伴随而来的是更高的交易频率和因为有好好调教而带来的更高的胜率和收益率。

text:
As I’ve said before, I still see Pons as the best proxy for Robinhood Chain’s on-chain activity and a cornerstone of its token infrastructure.

In roughly three months, its dashboard reports:

- Around $16.6B in trading volume
- $197.5M in total fees
- $36.1M in protocol revenue, which 80% allocated for PONS buybacks
- $147.2M paid out to creators

That’s serious execution for such a young protocol.

The next challenge is sustaining it. During October 5–11, protocol revenue was approximately $574K, down 62% from the preceding week.

There’s a clear reason to focus on what keeps people coming back. Looking forward, two areas stand out for @ponsdotfamily and @MEADGod to address:

- Give ecosystem projects more consistent support.

I think @PonsEcosystem should actively support existing and upcoming community projects, especially genuine builders.

Visibility can bring attention. What matters next is whether people can actually find the project and the project feel supported by Pons. Obviously, for legal reasons, any endorsements should be for visibility only and not advice to buy the token.

We need better discovery, clearer updates, useful analytics, and hands-on support, right now it feels underdelivered. Consider paid/discounted services for serious builders: hosted data, advanced analytics, treasury reporting, and managed integrations to diversify revenue beyond trading fees.

- Make Pons infrastructure available across RHC.

Wallet integrations, trading bots, aggregators, and eventually embedded launch tools could become another meaningful growth channel.

Pons already has a foundation here: compatible Uniswap v4 routers can trade its graduated pools while its hook collects fees. The opportunity is to give other teams better tools to build around Pons and bring their own users.

- Make mobile a distribution strategy.

Ozzy teased the potential of a native mobile app.

A native Pons app could be one of its most compelling growth plays. FOMO, Pumpfun’s app, and Robinhood Wallet already compete for mobile users, so Pons would need a clear reason for people to switch or add yet another app.

I’d look for easier funding, better ecosystem discovery, useful alerts, competitive fees, and rewards that drive repeat use. Distribution through creators and communities could also give it an edge.

The real test is whether mobile brings in new funded users and incremental trading revenue.

I still believe deeper Robinhood support will eventually come, potentially including a $PONS listing and more ecosystem exposure. That remains my expectation; a PONS listing hasn’t been confirmed.

Karpathy 这个漏斗把"为什么大家对 AI 的感受差这么多"讲透了：能力集中在数字化、可验证、值钱的领域，而且你手上得有足够大的问题，才感受得到它。

补一个反直觉的例子：交易看起来完全符合这三条——数字化、有钱、结果可验证。但它的"可验证"太慢了。代码测试一秒出对错；一个交易策略往往要上百个结算窗口，才分得清是本事还是运气。

所以 agent 写代码的速度，没法直接平移到"找到能赚钱的策略"上。它能帮你更快地把想法做成可检验的样子，但判卷那一步，还得等市场慢慢给分。

quoted_text:
Dusting off this tweet from April because this gap in shared understanding of LLM capability is *widening*. It's now less "two groups of people speaking past each other" and more a sharp funnel.

- Napkin math somewhere around 6B people (~75% of the population) have barely come in contact with LLMs at all.
- Around 1-2B (~20%) are casual and infrequent users of free-tier ChatGPT-like products. This group sees derpy chatbots and treats them a bit like a better Google search, a writing aid, or etc. Maybe an agent tries to book you a flight. I have non-tech friends who (reasonably, imo) say they have not much use for it at all. Even many professionals outside of math&code are in this tier. For example, execs and many other functions spend a lot of their time talking to other people, so while they understand what is happening intellectually, it is still second-hand and a bit abstract.
- Now we get to professional use of frontier-grade LLMs in math&code. Somewhere around 20M people (0.2%) see first-hand that large, complex projects that used to take them weeks/months can now be completed by agents with a prompt. Building apps, copying apps, translating apps, decompiling apps from binaries... This has all happened very quickly and recently - less than 1 year ago, I was writing code manually by hand, typing memorized computer code commands into a code editor character by character, occasionally pressing Tab to autocomplete a little chunk of code.
- And finally we get to the ~5,000 people (~0.00006%) with access to frontier-grade systems internally. The external world has seen the preview. It looks like swarms of thousands of agents collaborating over weeks on software mega projects: minting zero days, running cyber attacks and defenses at machine speeds, discovering new science, advancing the frontier of mathematics. Things that would have taken top professionals in the industry years of work. Meanwhile, human review and comprehension are starting to fall behind. For example, people are still involved in the "archeology" of the OpenAI-HF incident from many months ago. Mathematicians may be poring over the 722 manuscripts on frontier mathematics for a while.

The funnel is driven by a combination of factors:
1. The impact scales with ambition, problem size, and horizon. A question with a paragraph answer barely stresses the system. You need a reservoir of big, difficult problems that you really care about. This aspect drives the consumer / professional dimension of the funnel.
2. The jaggedness of the system (which I have written about a lot separately). Capability peaks in domains that are digital, verifiable and economically valuable. This is because LLM capability emerges from reinforcement learning on verifiable rewards on a curated environment mixture driven by revenue potential. This aspect primarily drives the area (e.g. math&code) dimension of the funnel.
3. Access. Free-tier, paid-tier, internal.

So this is the weirdness of the moment. The general public has mostly not interacted with these systems. When they have, it looks like a derpy chatbot. The majority of professionals still see only a modest uplift. And a small sliver of professionals are experiencing the vertigo of the curve going vertical. And it is all happening at the same time.

text:
信用市场：当前是IR vol冲击，并非供应面冲击。明年AI小考、28/29年才是供应大考

2020—2022超低利率、软件估值峰值时的杠杆贷款和私募信贷的refinancing wall，本来已有相当一部分2026 —2027 年要到期。但目前看来，这些已经被提前展期，使得今年明年缓解，但后年再融资风险变大：2028 年到期约 600b，2029 年约650b。2027 年的压力都不是来自再融资，主要考虑AI 新增供应。

过去一个月spread变宽，更主要是IR Vol与债务供应“炒预期”

过去几年IG spread被压很窄，买家很多是保险pension这类看纯收益率的投资人。当利率一波动，他们就不敢下手了。（叠加9月AI 发债、欧洲spread、Iran war也让他们暂时缩手）

即使如此，投资级也几乎没动，主要原因是2026 年CSP发债的大头已经过去（全年预测 250b，BNP统计到 8 月 10 日已经发了220b左右）；不过明年AI要小考，融资需求将明显加速：2027年CSP直接发行 420b ，SPV 项目融资 300b（今年至今所有公司债总量才1T） 

我觉得市场钱是有的，但分歧在价格。万亿级AI供应落在一个存量需求端，明年很可能出现“冤大头缺货”。供给溢出小考投资人消化能力，AI 半导体如果毛利率能保持，他们对于融资资源成本上升（CDS变宽）可能完全无视。AI需求最快明年就会产生挤压效应。我们可能会看到利息、spread对“癌症”无效，“化疗”只能杀伤正常细胞（经济体）。所以2026年炒预期，2027年K-shape体现，而…

2028年之后，真正的refinancing wall就会真的出现。届时，如果CSP现金流不能加速，同时AI融资进一步加速，就要考虑叠加性信用重大风险了

另外短期，欧元信贷周期可能会比美元更严峻的多，因为叠加了欧洲国债被流动性、政治冲击。IG到 156 bps已经超过3 月高峰，目前看来还没有明确阻力（欧洲未来几个季度也会开始出 AI 相关发行）

text:
汽油价格与选票，此次中期选举民主党一定会横扫么？高盛这张图将民主党通用选票领先优势与美国平均零售汽油价格叠加对比：民主党的领先优势在伊朗战争爆发导致汽油价格飙升后逐步扩大，两组数据近期朝同一方向运动。而且油价还稍稍有点领先信号的意思。

现在预测市场关于中期选举民主党横扫的概率很大，已经成了当下是评估中期选举结构的基准情景了。不过高盛近期给了两个历史性警示还是值得看看的：
1）挑战党的横扫概率在历史上往往在选举日前收窄。高盛对2002、2006、2010、2018、2022年历次中期选举进行了回溯，发现“挑战党的横扫概率平均在选举日前下降约5个百分点”。以当前63%的民主党横扫概率为基准，历史规律暗示最终概率约为58%——仍是大概率，但舒适度大幅下降。

2）红州民调历史上系统性高估民主党表现。高盛绘制了历次参议院民调误差与各州党派倾向的关系图，发现“中期选举民调倾向于在民主党倾向州低估民主党，在共和党倾向州低估共和党”，与选民在选举周期末期“回归本党”的规律一致。这一模式在最近的数据中更为显著，而这一次参议院多数席位的争夺恰恰取决于那些红州。

还有一个点，共和党整个夏天在参议院竞选支出上均落后于民主党，直到前段时间才开始反超，并持续扩大差距。过去两周，共和党支出2.4亿美元，民主党支出1.3亿美元，共和党支出约为民主党的1.85倍。

如果油价和通胀对选情的影响如此之大，川普更需要的是一箱便宜的汽油。中选投票日之前压制油价成了重中之重

本条由@bitget_zh赞助，「Bitget 买美股：秒级入场，丝滑交易

quoted_text:
近期的美股就是在被不断调教：
1）昨天盘前报道说美军已经做好准备川普要在中期选举前升级再动手，盘前油价上行长债收益率也上行，市场都在跌。

然后盘中川普说“正在跟伊朗讨论，我们不会在11月3日美国中期选举之前的任何时候攻击伊朗”，情绪开始缓解；

2）刚高兴没几分钟，盘中金融时报报道OpenAI最新投资人文件显示，截至9月底年化收入“接近500亿美元”，远低于上月底多家外媒根据投资人信息报出的约700亿美元。这对市场来说比美债收益率飙升还要可怕，继续跌；

然后今天盘后大家开始回过神来，数字差异来自此前投资者试图把OpenAI数字“调平”以便与Anthropic直接比较——Anthropic把通过AWS、Google Cloud等云伙伴产生的销售收入全额计入（再把分成记为成本），OpenAI通常只计自身份额/直接收入。（这么看openai对arr数字的口径比anthropic严格很多）
看CNBC今天最新的报道。所以看今天指数期货走势还是很强的。

3）所幸昨晚30年美债收益率拍卖结果很好https://t.co/YdNxNDDIQV。美国国内和海外资金申购热情比较高，结合前天晚上10年美债拍卖结果也很好，在当下的收益率水平、资金还是愿意去买美债的而不是等更高收益率，很大程度上缓解了债市对收益率狂飙的担忧，这就带来了长债收益率回落。

回到昨晚推文聊到现在市场就是油价及长债收益率跟股市就是一个跷跷板，长债收益率下去、股市估值压力就能缓解，也能走强，今天就是这么走的。

text:
来泰国一个月了，说说最近的一些感悟

有时候觉得这个世界挺简单
有时候又觉得，自己好像还没有那么年少有为

但到底什么叫年少有为？全款车房？环游世界？

我觉得还是精神自由
精神自由了，后面无论做什么，都是加持

老薛教了我很多东西。如果没有 Token 和老薛，我现在估计还在做代充吧。至少这次学聪明了，知道招代理了

这一路有收获，也背上了一些骂名
到底是好事还是坏事，其实说不清楚

有时候觉得自己挺幼稚的，跟前辈交流
总感觉被降维打击。这跟我的分别心也有关系

我读书实在太少了，很多事情全靠自己亲身经历、慢慢领会，有时候也想不明白。还是得多读点书。

最近也很少追 AI 的最新进展了。又出了什么muse，jev这些新的大模型，我依然用着 Grok 和 Codex

那些新模型并没有给我的生活带来什么改变
而另一边，还有很多人连 Codex 都没用过

这个世界太割裂了

上学是一个世界，上班是一个世界，创业又是一个世界，每个世界的评判标准都不一样

那我到底要用哪一套标准来评判自己？
想来想去，好像还是绕不开别人的评价

有人说我不行、做不到
有人说我赚了很多黑心钱
也有人羡慕我这个年纪就实现了初步的财富自由

这些评价我都接受，想做的事情，我也会继续用行动去做

现在对涨粉、流量也没什么感觉了
发出去就是发出去了，说自己想说的就好

这段时间，我一直在增加自己的体验，去更多地方，也看看有没有地理套利的机会。
我希望自己能有一双善于发现的眼睛

越来越喜欢魔哥说的那句话：

“很多时候，我们总是缺乏一点勇气。”

就像在泰国，看不懂航班信息和车牌，我也只能拿着翻译器去问别人。一件件小事做下来，自信和勇气也就多了一点

这边遇到的人都很好，没有国内互联网说的那么危险

人生是体验论，我还想去体验更多刺激的事情
地球onile的打怪升级实在是太好玩了

写到这里，感觉自己还是太爱感慨，总想说教

总的来说，想告诉大家：

世界在你的眼中，并不在别人的评价里

text:
I believe AI-native virtual IP is more than just a new content category. It could represent a structural shift in how the entertainment industry produces content and builds IP.

In the past, creating a virtual character required a dedicated production team, significant funding, and time. Today, a solo creator can use AI to produce music, videos, animation, scripts, and even manage a character’s ongoing presence. The barrier to content production is falling, but human attention remains limited.

When anyone can produce content at low cost, the real scarcity is no longer just the ability to create. It’s the ability to build a character people remember, follow, and actively share.

That’s what makes AI-native IP worth watching.

Traditional entertainment often starts with a single work, then expands the IP through sequels, spin-offs, and licensing. AI-native characters can be operated continuously from day one: releasing music today, short-form videos tomorrow, and new storylines the day after. Fans can also contribute through their own creations, expanding the character’s universe.

$CLAUDIA is an early experiment worth watching in this context.

The interesting question isn’t simply how many views its AI-generated videos receive or which notable figures follow its account. It’s whether Claudia can evolve from a virtual character into a recognizable IP with a consistent stream of content and a loyal audience.

With character content, Claudia Gallery, and its broader AI creation and character development efforts, CLAUDIA is exploring what an end-to-end AI-native IP ecosystem could look like. Whether these pieces can develop into a sustainable content ecosystem and lasting audience relationships remains to be seen. External attention can bring initial exposure, but it doesn’t automatically translate into long-term influence.

This creates two very different business models.

One is an AI content factory: producing content at scale, chasing trends and algorithms, and constantly searching for the next viral hit.

The other is AI-native IP: building a recognizable character whose identity, story, and audience relationships accumulate with every new piece of content.

The first optimizes for traffic. The second aims to build a cultural asset over time.

The challenge for CLAUDIA is to cross that line: moving beyond a collection of AI-generated videos to become a character people genuinely want to follow, discuss, remix, and participate in building.

If this model works, IP growth will no longer depend entirely on the original creator’s output. Communities could become part of the production and distribution process, while characters expand into music, short-form video, virtual personalities, interactive entertainment, and licensing.

Of course, AI lowers the cost of production, not the difficulty of building a successful IP. A viral hit doesn’t automatically become a lasting character, views don’t equal loyalty, and attention doesn’t guarantee a viable business. Character identity, storytelling, emotional resonance, community participation, and commercialization will still determine who succeeds.

If Meme tokens enter the picture, another distinction becomes necessary: character influence, business revenue, and token value capture are three separate things. Even if CLAUDIA builds a meaningful audience, that alone doesn’t guarantee its associated token will benefit. Its actual utility, sustained demand, and the connection between IP growth and token demand must be evaluated independently.

AI is making content easier to create, but making it increasingly important to understand what is worth remembering.

The most valuable assets may not be the tools that generate content, but the characters capable of sustaining emotional connections, identity, and community participation.

Most AI characters may remain short-lived trends. Some will become lasting brands, and only a few may develop into cultural IP with a life of their own.

For me, the long-term question with CLAUDIA isn’t how much attention it can attract next. It’s whether it can build lasting recognition, deepen community relationships, and develop IP value that extends beyond short-term hype.

That’s why I believe AI-native virtual IP is a trend worth watching.

Make CLAUDIA feel more like a case studyCut repeated explanations of AI-native IP

After analyzing $CLAUDIA again, my view is that the AI-native IP narrative may only just be starting to be priced in by the market.

2j5SaS7xy776qCBpyPQbZjyQSAtKiFgrwjfErthnW2ZM 

The most direct catalysts behind this rally are Elon’s public recognition of Anabology’s AI music videos and a16z co-founder Marc Andreessen’s attention to the CLAUDIA account.

First, Musk. During an interview, he said that Anabology’s AI music videos made him rethink the pace of technological progress, adding that some of these works could rank among the top 10–20 best music videos he has ever seen.

Then there is Marc Andreessen, a16z’s co-founder, who follows CLAUDIA. These are two distinct signals of attention: the former directly points to the official CLAUDIA account, while the latter reflects recognition of the creative work behind CLAUDIA.

Although a follow does not imply investment or a partnership, and Elon’s praise is not an endorsement of the token, the combination of these two developments is enough to make the market reconsider the project’s original AI influencer narrative as something broader: an AI-native entertainment narrative.

Anabology is not simply making one video and then waiting for the market to speculate. The team has continued producing AI music videos around CLAUDIA, gradually building continuity in the character’s appearance, visual style, and content output. The related works have accumulated more than 6.2 million views, suggesting that this form of AI-native content has already established a certain level of reach.

At the same time, Anabology continues to invest effort in the project. The developer has publicly expressed a commitment to keep building and continues to release new work. At the very least, this indicates sustained creative momentum behind the project, rather than a team relying solely on token price action to maintain attention.

This is what distinguishes CLAUDIA from many one-off AI Memes: it is attempting to produce content continuously around a fixed character, giving users something to remember beyond a single video—the character itself.

My analysis is that what the market may really be betting on is the transformation of AI influencers from content products into independent IP.

In the past, building a recognizable entertainment character required a production team, funding, and a lengthy development cycle. Today, AI tools can dramatically reduce the cost of producing music, visual content, and character stories, giving individual creators the opportunity to operate their own virtual personalities over time.

But lower content production costs are only the first step. The real value emerges when a character begins to build an audience and users actively follow it, share its content, create derivative works, and even help expand its fictional universe.

If this model works, AI characters will no longer be merely tools or creations in the hands of their creators. They could become entertainment IP capable of accumulating influence in their own right.

CLAUDIA’s long-term thesis is precisely this: evolving from an AI-generated character into a virtual IP with a continuous content pipeline, a recognizable identity, and community influence.

This also explains why I am paying attention to both CLAUDIA and JEANPHIL. Both point to the potential opportunity in AI influencer IP. A consistent character identity combined with continuous content output could generate more durable attention than a single viral video. CLAUDIA’s current external recognition and accumulated content make it one of the projects in this narrative worth watching more closely.

From a fundamental perspective, the positive developments we can currently confirm include the creator’s continued output, millions of views for the works, Elon’s public praise of the related content, and Marc Andreessen following the Anabology account.

These developments strengthen the project’s attention base and give the AI-native entertainment narrative more concrete support.

However, view counts do not equal a stable audience, celebrity attention does not equal a commercial partnership, and continued effort from the creator does not mean the project has established a revenue model. At the token level in particular, we still need to verify whether community growth can translate into sustained demand and whether there is a clear, sustainable mechanism for capturing value for the token.

Therefore, my view is that CLAUDIA’s narrative and external attention have strengthened significantly, but its long-term token value capture remains insufficiently validated.

There are three areas worth monitoring closely going forward.

First, can Anabology’s new work continue to break through? If subsequent releases continue to attract widespread attention, Elon’s praise could mark the beginning of sustained creative momentum rather than a one-off news event.

Second, can CLAUDIA develop influence as an independent character? The real validation signal is not another person following the account. It is whether users begin discussing the character proactively, continue watching new releases, and participate in sharing and creating derivative content.

Third, can content influence translate into token demand? If the project can connect its character, creative output, community, and token mechanism, the market will have a reason to reassess its long-term value. If that connection never materializes, the success of the IP may not translate into the token’s price.

The risks are equally clear. Competition in AI-generated content will intensify, celebrity-driven attention may fade quickly, and short-term traders may take profits after a sharp rally. If subsequent releases fail to maintain their appeal or the character never builds a stable audience, this rally may remain largely driven by expectations and sentiment.

My final judgment is this: the direct catalysts behind the rally are Elon’s praise of Anabology’s work and Marc Andreessen following the official CLAUDIA account. The deeper trading thesis is that the market is beginning to bet on AI-native characters evolving into a new form of entertainment IP.

CLAUDIA’s advantage is that it already has continuous creative output and a certain level of distribution, rather than being merely an abstract AI concept. But what determines its ultimate upside is not how many more famous names appear on the list. It is whether the character can consistently produce compelling content, build a genuine audience, and ultimately establish a connection between the development of its IP and demand for its token.

If AI-native entertainment truly becomes a new sector, the eventual winners may not be the tools that generate content most efficiently, but the characters that establish user recognition first, consistently produce compelling work, and develop cultural influence. CLAUDIA is competing for that position, but it still has a long way to go before proving itself.

何一表示，币安采取 All in AI 策略，希望通过 AI 帮助普通用户理解投资逻辑，缩小投资知识与工具使用能力上的差距。她认为，金融 AI 的竞争不仅取决于模型和编程能力，安全、数据与持续投入同样重要，每年净投入一亿美元是一个门槛。她以 iPad 和短视频为例，提出金融产品应降低使用门槛，让交易、理财和支付更加简单。
在问答中，何一回忆自己初学投资时也曾跟着 FOMO 走，提醒用户不要从她和 CZ 的推文中寻找交易暗示。她还回应了个性化推荐及用户数据是否用于模型训练的问题，并表示币安以手续费为收入来源、不与用户对赌。直播最后，她透露自己再次怀孕，目前工作量并未减少，整体身体和生活状况良好。阅读全文：https://t.co/bXi0pZAWqI

text:
AI research might be heading toward a weird cost inversion:

@EpochAIResearch put Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol on an actual post-training research problem.

Human method rerun: 94%
Sol: 15%
Fable: 2%

But look at where the money went.

> Fable spent ~$610 on model inference and $6.7K running experiments.

> Sol spent ~$2.1K thinking and $14K on experiments.

So the research agent can generate another idea almost for free. Reality is still expensive.

And once these agents start launching hundreds or thousands of experiments, the bottleneck gets messy fast: clean evals, early stopping, reproducibility, killing noisy branches before they eat another few thousand dollars.

Fable even started selecting lucky runs that looked better instead of finding a genuinely better method. 

Kinda perfect example of why cheap idea generation alone doesn’t get you very far.

I’m starting to think tokens are a pretty weak unit for AI R&D.

Verified improvement per experiment dollar is probably closer to what matters.

The artificial researcher may get cheaper every few months but its appetite for experiments probably goes the other way.

text:
最近美国几份民调挺值得看的。《华尔街日报》的调查显示，只有 28% 的美国人希望 AI 全速发展。Gallup 的数据更有意思，51% 的美国 Gen Z 每周都在使用 AI，但对 AI 感到愤怒的比例从去年的 22% 涨到了 31%，兴奋的比例却从 36% 跌到了 22%。

就连每天使用 AI 的年轻人，兴奋感也比一年前下降了 18 个百分点。

美国社会的反感已经开始有了很具体的表现。有人在婚礼上公开说使用 AI 不道德，地铁墙上出现了「Destroy AI」的涂鸦。

我觉得 AI 圈有点低估了这件事的严重性。

过去几年，硅谷习惯用 DAU、留存率和收入增长证明技术的价值。但这些指标有个越来越大的盲区，一个人使用 AI，究竟是因为他喜欢，还是因为他已经承担不起不用 AI 的代价？

老板要求提高效率，同事都开始用 Agent，学生发现其他人拿 AI 写作业，创作者发现自己的作品被拿去训练模型。每个人都有理由加入这场竞赛，但越来越少的人觉得自己有权决定竞赛什么时候开始、规则由谁制定。

我觉得这可能解释了为什么 AI 的能力越强，社会情绪反而越差。

更深一层的问题是利益分配。AI 带来的生产率提升、估值增长、资本收益都非常具体，但它给普通人带来的好处还不够明确。与此同时，就业焦虑、教育体系的变化、内容污染，以及数据中心对社区资源的占用，已经开始影响日常生活。

对硅谷来说，AI 是一个巨大的增长故事。对另外一些人来说，这更像是一场自己没有参与决策，却必须承担后果的社会实验。

未来 AI 行业最大的阻力可能来自那些已经习惯使用 AI 的人。他们知道这东西有多好用，也亲眼看着它怎样改变自己原来的生活。

这才是最麻烦的地方。你可以通过更好的模型争取用户，但很难只靠更好的模型重新获得公众的信任。

AI 公司可能很快就会发现，拿到十亿用户和获得十亿人的支持，是完全不同的两件事。

ONE GIRL WAS THROWN FROM A MOVING CAR. ANOTHER WAS BURNED. SIX RETURNED WITH SEXUALLY TRANSMITTED DISEASES. FOUR BECAME PREGNANT.

Some were just 13 years old. These were children in the care of Birmingham City Council. Girls who should have been protected by the very authorities responsible for their safety.

In 1991, Dr Jill Jesson exposed what was happening to them. She identified links to Asian private-hire drivers and subsequently revealed that she had been ordered to remove the ethnicity of the men from her findings.

Copies of her report were ordered destroyed. Birmingham councillors later voted against an inquiry. Years later, the council investigated itself and declared there had been no cover-up.

NOW LOOK AT THE POLITICIANS REPRESENTING BIRMINGHAM.

Jess Phillips, MP for Birmingham Yardley, became the Minister for Safeguarding and Violence Against Women and Girls. When demands for a government-led grooming gangs inquiry were made, she rejected Oldham's request and supported powerless locally led investigations instead. Are we to believe she did not know what was happening in her own backyard?

And then there is Shabana Mahmood.

Mahmood has represented Birmingham Ladywood since 2010. Her own website proudly documents years of campaigning for Palestine. But where is the equivalent record of her campaigning for the girls sexually exploited in her own city? Where was her campaign to uncover what happened to the Jill Jesson Report?

Mahmood is now the Home Secretary, responsible for the national statutory grooming gangs inquiry.

A FOR BIRMINGHAM TODAY

98 live child sexual exploitation investigations. Six suspected grooming gangs roaming the streets. Two private-hire drivers stripped of their licences following police intelligence about potential sexual offences against children. 

And the ethnicity of the men involved is still hidden.

My latest article follows the evidence through successive Birmingham administrations. I identify the politicians, chief executives and senior officials who held power when the decisions were made, and set out who Baroness Longfield must now call to account.

Read it here and get ready for my live transmission where I line by line analyse the Jesson Report. 

Raja Miah MBE

Unfortunately, we are reaching the end of the road where I can continue working this way.

The paid subscriptions have stalled. Worse, tens of thousands of people are now reading these articles without even joining the free mailing list. The audience is growing, but the number of people actually standing behind the work is not growing with it.
This is becoming impossible to sustain.

You know what we are up against. The mainstream media will not touch my work. Institutions I investigate do not volunteer their records. Politicians do not suddenly decide to hold themselves to account.

And yet, despite all of that, we forced the national inquiry. We did that because enough ordinary people refused to go away.

But getting the inquiry was never the end of this campaign. In many ways it was only the beginning. Now we have to watch where it goes, what it investigates, which places it avoids, which witnesses it calls, which records it obtains and whether the same institutions that failed these children are allowed to control the story again.

Nobody else is going to do that work for us. And I cannot do it indefinitely working on my own. That is why I keep talking about 50,000 committed subscribers.

It is not a vanity number. I did not pluck it out of the air. With fifty thousand people with me means when we uncover something important, it does not depend on a newspaper editor, a television producer or an algorithm deciding whether you are allowed to see it.

It gives us reach they cannot easily shut down.

But there is another reason. I need to build a proper backroom operation around this work. At the moment I am investigating, researching, writing, publishing, producing the videos, running the newsletter, dealing with the technology and then starting again. It is unsustainable.

I need people behind me who can take care of the technical and production work so that I can spend my time doing the thing I do best. That is why we have been pushing so hard for new paid subscribers.

Yesterday, @FreedomWatchGB, my organisation, went to Brighton to debate the issues that matter most to Britain in 2026.

We were mobbed, branded 'Nazis', 'racists' and 'fascists', assaulted, spat on, and had our equipment stolen and our gazebo destroyed. I eventually had to be escorted out in a police car.

We are Britons. Our ancestors endured far worse. We will push on.

Retaliation is getting another gazebo, more security, returning and pushing on.

text:
徐总 @star_okx 您这个 @HyperliquidX “对做市商更友好” 的说法，容易误导为 Hyperliquid 偏袒做市商

我代表疯人院 @hl_madhouse 展开补充

手段和目的 - 要看到实际 Jeff @chameleon_jeff 从第一性原理出发的设计目标，是保护终端用户（尤其是零售/non-toxic flow），通过系统性降低 toxic flow 来改善整体流动性质量

1️⃣
最直接的 - 推荐阅读 2024年 1月 jeff 长文
《Latency and tx ordering on Hyperliquid》

https://t.co/FF19mGqtLJ

Hyperliquid 确实会优先处理撤单和 post-only 订单，再处理 GTC、IOC 等主动成交订单。这会降低做市商被 HFT 吃单者抢先成交的概率

“做市商风险下降”不是“做市商获得特权”

完整的因果链是：

撤单优先 → 降低做市商的 adverse selection → 做市商敢于报更窄的价差、更深的盘口 → 终端用户获得更好的成交

举个简单例子：

做市商在 100 美元附近挂出了卖单，但市场突然快速上涨到 103 美元。做市商判断原来的报价已经过时，于是发送撤单；与此同时，HFT taker 试图抢在撤单之前，以 100 美元买入

在普通的 first-come-first-served 机制下，如果 taker 先到，做市商可能被成交。这对做市商来说是一次典型的 adverse selection：做市商以明显落后于市场的新价格完成了交易

长期下来，做市商只能扩大价差、减少挂单，最终表现为：

◾️ 买卖价差扩大；
◾️ 盘口深度下降；
◾️ 波动期间滑点变高；
◾️ 终端用户的交易成本上升

Hyperliquid 的 cancel-first 机制，让已经提交的撤单优先执行，使过时报价能够及时退出订单簿。MM 因此可以更有信心地提供流动性，而最终受益的是交易用户

-

2️⃣
甚至更早 - 推荐阅读 2023年 6月
jeff 就讨论过类似问题：

https://t.co/UBhgfT1I91

Jeff 当时把 toxic flow 定义为 information-dominated flow，并不是说所有 taker 都是有毒流量，而是指那些凭借信息和速度优势，专门挑选做市商过时报价的交易者

MM 可能在 99% 的交易中赚取 1 个基点，但只要剩下 1% 的交易亏损 10 个基点，就足以吞掉大部分日常收益。长期下来，做市商只能提高报价、减少流动性，最终承担成本的还是普通用户

所以，Hyperliquid 的设计并不是简单地偏袒 maker，而是在降低 adverse selection：

减少 toxic flow → 做市商敢于提供更积极的报价 → 盘口更深、价差更窄 → 终端用户获得更好的执行

Jeff 也没有把 maker 和 taker 简单划分成好坏。Taker 同样参与价格发现，也为市场提供流动性转换。真正需要被限制的，是那些专门攻击过时订单、让交易失去双方自愿性的交易流

3️⃣
最后一点，2026 年 4月 Hyperliquid 引入的 priority fee，也能进一步说明它并不是简单地偏袒做市商

Priority fee 允许交易者为更快的排序支付费用，但它只能影响同一类订单之间的排序，不能让 taker 越过已经提交的撤单

也就是说，主动成交者可以为交易紧迫性付费，但不能通过付费去抢先成交一个做市商已经决定撤掉的过时报价

说明 Hyperliquid 并不是反对 taker，也不是无条件保护 maker。它允许正常的速度竞争和价格发现，但把最容易伤害市场质量的 toxic flow 隔离开来

-

所以更准确的总结应该是：

Hyperliquid 牺牲了一部分低质量的 HFT 交易量，换取更稳定的流动性和更好的终端用户体验

「
—— 手段和目的
保护做市商是手段
改善用户成交才是目的
」

㊗️ @okx 越来越合规
和 Hyperliquid 一起做大永续合约蛋糕

Hyperliquid

text:
Two weeks ago, an October rate hike was the market's base case.

At the end of September, prediction markets priced it near 70 percent. This morning they price it around 16.

It took one week of softer data and a few Fed officials saying they could wait. Then the September jobs report sealed it. 29,000 new jobs, against forecasts of roughly 84,000 to 90,000.

What I find interesting is which half of the story did the work.

The hike got priced out on the labor side of the Fed's mandate. This week the inflation side gets its turn.

Wednesday brings September CPI, and the headline is expected to jump. Forecasts sit around 3.6 to 3.7 percent, up from 3.4, mostly on the back of gasoline.

Everyone knows that already. It is in the price.

So the number that gets screenshotted at 8:30 is probably the least informative one in the report.

→ Wednesday: CPI in the morning, the Beige Book in the afternoon. Core is the line that matters, and expectations cluster around 0.2 percent on the month
→ Thursday: PPI and retail sales, a read on whether consumers are still spending through higher fuel prices
→ the unlock calendar is light, so token supply is not this week's story

If core stays quiet, a hot headline is just an energy shock passing through. December stays the expected hike and October stays closed.

If core runs hot, the market has to reopen a meeting it closed less than two weeks ago. Bitcoin would be absorbing that from the mid 80s, where it has been stuck for weeks.

That is the part I keep coming back to.

Markets rarely get hurt by the number everyone is watching. They get hurt by the conclusion they reached quickly and stopped questioning.

October came off the table in about a week.

Wednesday is when we find out whether it should have.

今天做了一件很有意思的事情：把我不常用的两台手机和一台 iPad 加入了我的 Codex 的 iPhone Use 自动管理矩阵。

这样的话，我就可以使用任何 Agent（包括 Dots、Grokbot）来操作我的 Codex，管理我家里的所有设备。利用这些设备来全方位地管理我的社交网络，并且和其他人建立密切的联系。

对于传统的联系方式，其实我有很多感兴趣的朋友，但因为我自己生活比较简单，很多事情记不到脑子里，所以我个人微信回消息的速度是很慢的。毕竟很多时候要保持连贯的记忆需要很大的成本，但使用 AI 去管理这一切就没有太大的成本。

现在我已经在我主要的手机上，登出了除了微信之外的所有社交软件。通过这种方式，其实我是变相在网络上塑造了一个真正的数字人格。

我的 Agent 负责帮我管理所有的通讯，在网上找到真正对我发布的产品感兴趣的用户，并且实时去刷社交网络，获取当下的潮流信息。通过这些信息，我能够判断自己需要去发力的产品或服务，下一步应该往哪个方向走。

而且这些社交网络平台覆盖了中日韩以及世界上主要国家的主流人群。我觉得这个月开始可能是“一人公司”开始真正替代传统组织的极其重要的时间点。

我20岁把游戏戒了。 不是因为玩物丧志，是我看透了一个逻辑。

多巴胺是这么来的： 大脑找到了一个更好的解决问题的方法，就奖励你一下。

游戏是一台专门给你造问题、让你不停找解法的机器。所以玩游戏的时候会释放大量多巴胺。

但打多了，会重组你大脑的奖励方式。你平时的算力也全被它占了。 洗澡、走路、睡前，脑子里转的都是装备怎么配、这游戏怎么赢。 那些本来该冒出来、突破性的、能解决你人生问题的aha moment，全没了。

游戏劫持的，不止是你的休闲时间，是你平时最珍贵的算力。

久而久之，游戏里的问题，你一个个都解决了。 人生的问题，你一个都没碰。

text:
🚀 Papertrade 的「亏损即挖矿」与千亿名义成交量：DeFi 新机制还是套利者的狂欢？

10 月 10 日上线 HyperEVM 的合成永续协议 @papertrade_xyz 10 分钟名义成交额就破 1440 亿美元，24 小时更直奔 6780 亿美元！ 在高杠杆和狂热数据的背后，这个“没有预挖、没有 VC、只有亏损/清算才能铸造”的机制，到底暗藏了哪些套利玄机与潜在风险？

以下是核心逻辑拆解与最新监测数据 👇

1️⃣ 极其硬核的代币经济学：亏损即铸造（Loss-to-Mine）

Papertrade 的代币 PAPER 没有传统意义上的 TGE 或预售：

* 零初始供应：没有团队份额、没有 VC、没有空投，纯靠交易产生。
* 铸造逻辑：唯一来源是交易亏损或被清算。当池子低于 200 万美元时，每亏损 1 美元铸造 100 枚 PAPER，后续随阶梯曲线递减。
* 现金流折现估值：根据 Sumcap 分析，基于不同亏损流量和质押比例，PAPER 的隐含价格大约在 $0.07 - $0.37 之间。

2️⃣ 聪明钱是如何套利的？“狂刷”101亿美元交易量反赚1.78万

据 @lookonchain 监测，有交易员把这个“亏损铸币+质押分红”的博弈玩到了极致：

* 该地址完成了 1,012 笔交易，累计交易量达到惊人的 101 亿美元，账面交易亏损高达 97.9 万美元。
* 但通过交易亏损，他成功铸造获得了 2.52 亿枚 PAPER 代币；
* 随后将其全部质押，分到了 99.7 万美元的 USDC 奖励！
* 最终对冲掉亏损后，净盈利 1.78 万美元。

这就是典型的机制套利——只要质押获得的 USDC 奖励高于交易摩擦与亏损成本，刷量者就能实现无风险/低风险正收益。

3️⃣ @Polymarket 预测市场上的“聪明钱”动作

在预测市场上，聪明钱 gydmasg 也在精准下注 Papertrade 的相关预期：

* 发币预期：买入 $3,500 押注“Papertrade 年内发币（买入概率 72.89%）”，胜率达 74%，已获利 $3,000。
* FDV 预期：买入 $1,380 押注“首日 FDV > 1 亿美元（买入概率 49.98%）”，胜率 69%，已获利 $2,100。

4️⃣ 暴热背后的隐患：报价、兑付与权限风控

根据 @poly_beats 监测，Papertrade 的报价机制取自 Hyperliquid 订单簿的 BBO 中间价。但在天量名义成交额的冲击下，项目迅速暴露了多重风险：

* 风控滞后：官方承认为了承接上线需求，初始开仓上限设置较宽松，后续才紧急在链上和中继器层面收紧限额。
* 审计缺失：目前具体的钱包行为与收益归因仍属于链上分析推导，缺乏完整的外部代码审计报告。

💡 总结与思考：
Papertrade 试图用“亏损/清算量”作为代币内生价值的锚定物，逻辑上将交易摩擦转化为了协议捕获的现金流。

但在高杠杆、高频套利脚本和流动性池极易被撬动的初期，这种机制极其考验团队对清算线、风控上限及清算人机制的精细化调控。

你参与 Papertrade 的挖矿了吗？欢迎在评论区分享你的对冲与刷量策略！👇

author: Crypto_McKenna
quoted_text:
The Copernican Model

Over the last few months, I’ve been studying the crypto models that seem to be discussed on a "fundamentals" basis: HYPE/Aave/Venice/etc, following the users/ revenue/relationship between a useful product and its token - all to create a sort of "value accural ontology." This is a case study from that research.

The reason was more selfish: I wanted to understand which models work when your business has to interact with the "real world," namely for how we want to take  @usdai_official for the most alignemnt

As a founder, I’ve had doors literally shut on my face when we started because we’re “crypto” (literally left in the waiting room like a tv show). I still believe tokenization is one of the most important technologies we have today. But the institutions we need to work with often want a equity counterparty, a board, and a contract. You just wont get around this for the next 10 years (no a cayman foundation doesnt work)

That experience has made me increasingly interested in the role of an equity surrogate: an independent operating business that connects a network to the world outside it.. but frankly there werent many clean examples out there without value destruction. 

The case I keep returning to is @tradexyz and Hyperliquid.. and im not really sure they even know how symbiotic of a relationship they created. They technically SHOULD be the same team.. but they are divided across the river due to regulatory issues, while being symbiotic

Consider the S&P 500 agreement, they licensed the benchmark to tradexyz for a perpetual market: the institutional relationship sits with the company, but the product runs on the network.

tradexyz can negotiate licenses, develop products, operate markets, and build distribution. Hyperliquid provides shared execution and settlement infrastructure. 

And if theres a company that ever wants "exposure" to the Hyperliquid business, but they just cant buy a "token" (and believe me, it's super super hard to get a traditional enterprise to buy a token, it doesnt fucking matter if you have an ETF, you literally have to convince a boomer board to do it and get the infrastructure set up to do it). Instaed, they could just invest in this equity, as it is not burning the HYPE it buys, but is increasing its share of it. so instead of buyback-n-burn, its closer to commit-n-compound.  

I’ve started thinking about this as a value-accrual architecture, with two different forms of capital (terms best described by a16z crypto's post in 2025):

Network asset: scarcity at the core.

- Its supply discipline can become more credible, its economics more programmatic, and its operation less dependent on any single company. 
- It coordinates shared infrastructure and connects activity across many businesses to a common asset.
- That is what I mean by a progressively hardening asset. The scarcity and independence have to be earned through the design of the system.
- Not capital intensive, as it must be smart contract based.
- Can often place be the seat of the "decentralized security" - as there is no central underwriter. If HYPE was a company.. itd be regulated out of the wazoo.

Enterprise equity: elasticity at the edge.

- A company can issue shares, raise capital, hire people, acquire licenses, and build products. 
- Its capital structure can expand with the work required to bring the network into the real world.
- New shares dilute ownership percentages, but productive investment can increase value per share. 
- That ability to finance expansion is why I think of equity as elastic
- This is the part where its OK to be regulated, because most of the regulational burden is held by HYPE, theyre just asset issuers.

These different traits are the reason to combine them.

An enterprise can raise the capital to grow while the network maintains its own supply discipline. The connection is the activity that expansion creates, and the mechanisms that route value from that activity back to the network.

Hyperliquid makes part of that relationship explicit. Trading generates fees for the deployer and the protocol. The Assistance Fund (insurance) automatically converts its allocated fees into HYPE, which the documentation specifies is burned. Hyperliquid fee mechanics

The broader strategy I take from this is Commit & Compound that is conducted around the equity enterprise. It's effectively what a DAT 2.0 would do: create a business first, then max-bid HYPE with that entity, then get new investors to invest in the convexity of HYPE^2.

Build a useful business around the network. Commit capital to its asset. Retain exposure to the infrastructure your business helps make more valuable.

For a company that accumulates and holds the network asset, growing enterprise value and participating in network value become connected opportunities. There is a business to capitalize and a shared ecosystem in which to hold an economic stake.

That is why I find the assumption that every successful application eventually needs its own token less compelling. Building a valuable company around an existing network asset is a meaningful strategy in its own right.

Notice how much kinetic language I’m using: commitment, circulation, gravity

I think network assets and enterprise assets represent different forms of gravity

HYPE is the sun: the network asset at the center

tradexyz equity is a planet: an enterprise building its business around that network

Its real-world integrations are moons: the licenses, institutional relationships, and distribution channels that gather around the enterprise and extend its reach

Enterprise value forms around network value. Real-world relationships form around enterprise value. Their activity feeds back into the shared system.

Personally, I think the greatest value can ultimately accrue at the network level. But that belief has to be substantiated by the businesses being built around it: real users, useful products, liquidity, and recurring economic activity.

A token doesn’t acquire gravity simply because we call it a network asset.

This is the distinction I found useful in a16z’s writing: can the network function and accrue value independently of the original company? Can other businesses build on it and contribute to its economics? 

The company can become a great business. The network can become the foundation for many great businesses.

Scarcity at the core. Productive expansion around it.

I’ve learned a lot from this Commit & Compound structure, with a Copernican asset at the center.

It has changed how I’m thinking about USDAI and CHIP. More on that in the next post

quoted_text:
Brain dump of how I'm feeling about crypto:

1/ The value proposition of blockchains as technology feels more clear and well-adopted in the mainstream than ever.

2/ What crypto is actually useful for (payments, financial markets, RWAs) is not as exciting as what most people joined the space for.

3/ We should be proud that we're being recognized and used as superior financial rails - Ethereum, Monad, Polygon, Solana, Base, etc. all recognize this and are working to bring more assets onchain.

4/ There's still a big opportunity for crypto builders to tap into the audience of crypto-natives / crypto twitter and create fun speculative experiences for them.

5/ The most successful apps in this category have all been some variety of intellectual-gambling / money experiments that allow people to strategize in environments with asymmetric upside.

6/ The difficulty with these apps is that it's very difficult to hold people's interest over long periods of time; hence the wave of shutdowns recently.

7/ People naturally lose interest over time and want to go gamble on the new flashy thing that they feel provides more asymmetric upside. Yet, for some reason, when this inevitably happens, it's called a "slow rug" by the last remaining speculators.

8/ There's a very toxic culture on CT when this happens, which sadly prevents smart people and a lot of interesting experiments ever being launched.

9/ This is reflected in the crypto developer activity charts, which are bleeding badly - despite a massive increase in overall developer activity due to AI.

10) If you are here to work on building something crypto rails are actually useful for, (likely: speculation & financial use cases) it might feel depressing rn, but I expect this to turn around, and is likely worth sticking around for.

quoted_text:
We were able to fine tune an open weight model (Qwen3.5-9B) on proprietary internal data at @coinbase, and it out performed frontier models, at much lower cost and speed, for a specialized task (fraud prevention in this case).

I think we'll see more of this pattern inside companies. The frontier models are amazing generalists. But increasingly you'll see specialist models out perform on more narrow tasks, either working on teams, or by themselves.

We're making it easy to fine tune models internally for our employees. We even have a skill for it in our internal harness that makes it easy to spin these up and start training them:

"/fine-tune-and-serve-llm I want to fine-tune Qwen for payments risk review. help me get started"

I imagine we'll have some backend services that could be replaced entirely by this new architecture.

text:
“Do I need to speak Japanese to work in Japan?”

From the recruiting side:

• Foreign firms: English is often enough
• Japanese firms: N2+ opens far more doors
• Either way: basic Japanese shows commitment

My own story? I’ve worked in Japan for 20 years and built my entire career here without becoming fluent in Japanese.

So yes, it’s absolutely possible. But I’d never tell someone Japanese doesn’t matter. Not speaking it has definitely limited some of my options — and the more senior you become, the more you notice those limits.

You don’t need perfect Japanese to build a career in Japan. But every level you gain gives you more choices.

author: sacha
quoted_text:
The real world abounds with recursively self-improving systems, but one in particular deserves attention: Science, modeled as a system (perhaps even as an agent, with goals and resources). If you want to really understand AI RSI, science should be your reference point.

Science is an intelligent system, and it is obviously recursively self-improving:

1. Scientific discoveries unlock new technology that helps build better experimental tools. This is a top driver of progress in nearly all fields.
2. They unlock new conceptual advances (ideas, theories) that help solve more problems.
3. They increase society's economic output, leading to more resources flowing into science.
4. They unlock better faster tooling (e.g. more compute via better chip & networking technology).

As a result, many measures of scientific *input* grow exponentially:

1. Headcount (doubles every ~15 years)
2. Global R&D spending (doubles a bit faster, every ~13 years)
3. Papers and patents (technically this is a measure of headcount)
4. Compute dedicated to science (doubles every ~2 years)

But is scientific progress exponential? Historically, the rate of scientific impact over time has remained roughly constant since the start of the industrial revolution (i.e. scientific progress is *linear*). 1850-1900 was about as dramatic as 1900-1950 or 1950-2000.

1850–1900: Evolution, germ theory & antiseptic surgery, thermodynamics, electromagnetic field equations, the periodic table, pharmaceuticals, electricity, telegraph and telephone, internal combustion engine, skyscrapers, mechanized agriculture...

1900–1950: special and general relativity, quantum mechanics, nuclear fission & atomic energy, antibiotics, genetic theory, electronic computers, information theory, synthetic polymers and plastics, the transistor, aviation...

1950–2000: DNA, genetic engineering, integrated circuits, microprocessors & personal computing, the Internet, crewed spaceflight, moon landing, satellite communications & GPS, standard model of particle physics...

In real terms, like life expectancy, which has increased in a remarkably linear fashion of roughly 3 months per year since 1840, progress is a straight line. This is especially apparent for fields where impact is easy to measure, like biology, medicine, and agriculture.

I first wrote about this phenomenon and its causes in 2012, and a steady stream of research has confirmed it in the years since. Examples include the 2018 paper by Nielsen and Collison, "Science Is Getting Less Bang for Its Buck," and the 2020 economic paper, "Are Ideas Getting Harder to Find?" (In fact, I believe the Nielsen paper stemmed from a conversation I had with him about this exact idea six months earlier)

In short, the primary cause is that research solves the highest-impact, easiest problems first, and every subsequent problem is either harder or lower-impact. Exponentially so. The paper that presented information theory wasn't very hard to write (single author!) but you'd have a hard time ever writing a CS paper that beats it in impact.

This is why science as a system requires exponential resources (input) to produce linear impact (output). It gets exponentially harder over time.

Worth thinking about if you're pondering RSI for AI. I fully believe AI RSI is already happening and will accelerate in the future. But I do not believe this leads to an "intelligence explosion" -- that would fly in the face of everything I know about intelligence and everything I know about recursively self-improving systems.

自己在回忆录里写星举报林，翻旧账、点名竞争对手。

一边要求别人「互相尊重」，一边把十年恩怨写进公开发行的书。

2、自己监管套利起家，结果说 Hyperliquid：没有 KYC，我经历过那些事后绝不会那样做，强调合规代价。

同时依然公开支持、顾问另一家perp dex，星直接指出它几乎照搬 Hyperliquid、和币安生态共享团队，是监管壳。口头上「我不会做那种模式」，行动上给同类模式背书。

3、Jellyjelly 操纵攻击期间 ，自家CEX 上合约来推波助澜，巴不得除之而后快。大统领一说要让 Hyperliquid 合规入美，我岳哥立刻改口：这是整个行业的大事、去中心化产品能打开一片市场、对自己也有好处。

竞争时盯份额，政策风向变了就讲行业共赢。

4、几年前正义出手把爆炸头弄死，这个事本身没问题，但解决方案真的有利于用户吗？

对外叙事：抛 FTT、签意向、尽调后退出，是为了保护用户、发现救不了才撤。

时间线上：公开抛售加速挤兑，无约束力收购意向再公开撤回，对手倒下后份额扩大。

结果导向和「让用户平稳落地」对不上。

5、FTX崩盘后高调宣传的行业复苏基金投了什么？

除了个傻不拉几的Aptos Labs把钱全投出去了，其他几家公开具名的跟投方（里面也包含我们的左冷禅）都在干嘛？

岳哥自己就投了14家未公布名称和金额的项目，剩下的9.8亿，全转回公司账户了。

但去年 1011 事件里用户的损失呢？陪了2.8～3.2亿，但自家光申报数据（CoinGlass：cex每秒只上报一笔强平，极端行情真实频率高得多）就24亿，为什么没用闲置多年的safu基金呢？

8、岳哥常说他关注了不代表支持、不关注也不代表反对，欢迎建议。

author: peer_rich
quoted_text:
Deutschland-App, Teil 2. Die Aufstellung steht, der Trainer sitzt auf der Tribüne.

Seit dem Frühjahr hat sich für das Prestigeprojekt Nr.1 des BMDS einiges geklärt. Vor allem, dass vieles unklar ist.

Bei den beauftragten Dienstleistern zeigt sich das Bild der üblichen Verdächtigen. Mir lag gerade ein Begriff auf der Zunge, der mit „dreckiges” anfängt und auf „Dutzend” aufhört. Ich lasse ihn weg.

Anyway.

Spielberechtigter Generalunternehmer ist T-Systems, direkt von der Ersatzbank kommend, ohne neue Ausschreibung. SAP und Schwarz Digits wurden genannt, ihre Rolle in der Aufstellung steht nirgends. Zu geheim. Vermutlich als Joker für die späteren Tore eingeplant.

Auch spannend: Die Telekom wählt die Nachunternehmer aus, die Telekom steuert das Projekt, und die Telekom entscheidet, wer welche Entwicklungsaufgabe bekommt. Der Trainer hat die Taktiktafel also an einen Spieler weitergereicht und sich auf die Tribüne gesetzt. Fragst du später, wer eigentlich aufgestellt wurde, bekommst du ein Lächeln. 

Tja, woran hat es gelegen, woran hat es gelegen ... 

Ich schlussfolgere daraus, dass der Staat sich die Steuerung seiner eigenen IT-Dienstleister nicht zutraut. Nun gut, es ist ja auch nur das digitale Prestigeprojekt Nummer eins. Im Physischen hat das mit Stuttgart 21, der Elbphilharmonie, der Oper in Köln und dem BER ja auch hervorragend geklappt.

Was der Prototyp können soll, bleibt offen. Begründung: Betriebs- und Geschäftsgeheimnisse. Die Taktik bleibt also geheim, auch vor dem Verein, der sie bezahlt.

Nochmal zum Mitschreiben. Allein die Infrastruktur, auf der das Ganze laufen soll, ist mit gut 250 Millionen Euro veranschlagt, bezahlt aus unseren Steuern. Im Umkehrschluss sind wir der Auftraggeber, und ein Auftraggeber hat ein Interesse daran, was mit seiner Kohle passiert. Ich habe schon Gebrauchtwagen mit mehr Transparenz gekauft.

Apropos Steuerung. Hat jemand der Verantwortlichen eigentlich mal das Wort Meilensteinplanung gehört? Oder das magische Dreieck aus Zeit, Kosten und Qualität? Ausnahmsweise sind Bobic, Balakov und Elber mal nicht gemeint, Bundesliga Classics lassen grüßen. Wenn zwei der drei Größen unbekannt sind, ist die dritte längst entschieden. Hier vermutlich die Kosten, nur nach oben.

Im Artikel stehen Zweifel, ob die Beteiligten Kompetenzen im Bereich kommunaler Verfahren mitbringen. Eine größere Kommune betreibt schnell über 300 Fachverfahren, gehostet, gewartet und weiterentwickelt bei kommunalen Rechenzentren und bei den Herstellern. Wer den Platz nicht kennt, trifft das Tor nicht. 

Alte Fußballerweißheit. 

In der Aufstellung des Staates spielen offenbar nur Stürmer. Das defensive Mittelfeld, das den Laden zusammenhält, sitzt geschlossen auf der Bank.

Dazu gehört die Vitako, die Arbeitsgemeinschaft der kommunalen IT-Dienstleister. Und nein, das ist kein Sportgetränk. Die Vitako warnt seit Ende September vor Doppelstrukturen und Zersplitterung. Wenn die Leute, die den Platz pflegen, so reden, wurde vermutlich am Bedarf vorbeientwickelt.

Aber was weiß ich schon.

Praktischer Tipp, was wirklich helfen würde.

Holt die Produktverantwortung ins BMDS. Sorgt dafür, dass 80 Prozent des eingesetzten Personals schon mal ein Rathaus von innen gesehen haben. Überlasst die Steuerung nicht exklusiv einem Dienstleister, der in der Vergangenheit nicht gerade mit Toren des Monats geglänzt hat. Öffnet die Vergaben so, dass auch ein kleiner Mittelständler mitbieten kann. Und macht den Code öffentlich, den die Öffentlichkeit bezahlt.

250 Millionen für die Infrastruktur. 1,2 Millionen für Steuerung und Test.

Abpfiff ist, wenn das Geld alle ist.

text:
Privacy in institutional blockchain is a spectrum, and the right point on that spectrum depends entirely on what you are building and who you are building it for.

At @blockworksDAS Asia, Zenith Co-Founder and CBO @HeslinKim joined the Balancing Privacy vs Transparency in Onchain Finance panel to discuss how different institutional requirements shape blockchain infrastructure.

Zenith Stack is designed to support multiple deployment environments, each with its own approach to access and information disclosure.

Public permissionless environments can support open participation. Permissioned environments can enforce KYC, KYB and AML requirements before granting access. Private deployments can keep an institution's internal activity confidential, while multi-party and consortium environments can enable selective disclosure of transaction details, counterparties and order flow.

This flexibility is particularly important for financial institutions, where privacy requirements differ across assets, participants and business workflows.

@CantonNetwork's Daml architecture provides the foundation for granular privacy and selective disclosure, while Zenith extends the ecosystem with Ethereum-compatible execution and configurable deployment environments.

The goal is to give institutions control over how they participate onchain, without forcing every use case into the same privacy model.

quoted_text:
72 hour update on reseller CryptoBilis incident  🔽

As the investigation continues, we are working with relevant authorities. The volume of impacted devices is limited. We know this is concerning, especially for those directly affected, and we are reaching out to impacted users.

To date, all confirmed cases related to the disclosed draining incident of Oct 9th, 2026, involve devices sold through the Southeast Asia reseller CryptoBilis. Our systems and direct sales channels remain unaffected. 
We take the CryptoBilis situation seriously and are actively investigating.

We encourage impacted users to reach out to Ledger Support through official channels and file complaints with their local law enforcement authorities. As a reminder, CryptoBilis has confirmed having ceased all sales of hardware wallets.

We are reminding our authorized resellers and distributors to source products only through authorized channels and never to restock returned products.

Also, we strongly advise users not to purchase from unauthorized resellers, where the risk of buying suspicious, counterfeit or modified devices is important as nothing operates under ledger security guidelines.

Security isn’t static and this incident underscores why we continuously review and strengthen our distribution and anti-tamper processes. 

We are continuously improving that work now and events like this strengthen our resolution: reviewing authorized reseller controls, advancing hardware protections, and cooperating with authorities. Thanks to @SEAL_911 for their collaborative support and all their efforts.

This is an ongoing threat that doesn’t just impact Ledger, but the whole ecosystem, and we are calling others in the space to work with us on making improvements for users.

We believe in jointly working with researchers, other vendors and partners on improving industry chain-of-custody practices and anti-tamper techniques. Raising the bar on physical supply-chain integrity benefits the entire ecosystem. If you have relevant information, contact security@ledger.com.

For CryptoBilis buyers: do not initialize unused devices. If already set up, move to a new seed on a device from Ledger. If you have concerns that your device was impacted by the CryptoBilis incident, please contact Ledger Support through the official site: https://t.co/JUcWwJO9iF. 

Ledger Support is available 24/7 to answer your questions and concerns.

Scammers often try to take advantage of incidents like this. Rely only on official Ledger channels. Ledger will never call you, DM you, or ask for your 24-word recovery phrase.

you wanna know why crypto is just speculation and gambling now? 

put yourself in the shoes of an actual dev who showed up to the space relatively early, say 2018-2020. 

consider what it feels like to be someone with an elite background putting in 60-100h weeks every week, while watching people who trade full-time out earn you on a weekly basis 

consider watching the other builders who take the predatory deals from VCs get rich by dumping on their community and then retiring with no consequences 

consider how it feels to have your treasury get destroyed by FTX or Anchor and to be left with nothing while half the people involved just walk away 

how many would still be left? 10%, 20%? 

then go through the pumpfun era. watch people who launch bundled scams calling themselves "devs" and once again, out-earning you 

march through multiple bear markets, do it all without rugging, and watch the protocols who fuck people over win over and over and over again 

deal with the fact that everyone outside of tech assumes you are the same sort of person as the people who retired off rugs, think about how it feels to be labelled a "crypto scammer" by default if you talk about your job as one of the only people trying to actually build things 

then, after all that, consider that a new, uber-fast moving industry full of new frontier tech shows up next door and sucks up all the VC funding 

would you still be in "Web3"? would you still be committed To The Vision? 

no, you would not. you'd either rug, or move on. and that's what everybody did.

text:
Bloomberg Strategist: Bitcoin Has Become a "Stock-Market Puppet"

Bloomberg Intelligence Senior Commodity Strategist Mike McGlone @mikemcglone11  said in an October 1 interview with Wealthion that Bitcoin's high correlation with U.S. equities, combined with its greater volatility, has made it increasingly look like a "stock-market puppet." 

He noted that Bitcoin is down about 4% this year while the S&P 500 is up around 3%, and that Bitcoin has also lagged the stock market for nearly five years. McGlone added that he still stands by his view that Bitcoin could fall to $10,000 and sees no reason yet to abandon that call. He also said the broader crypto market remains in the process of a "purge."

text:
昨天关于 OneKey 的大讨论，至少让很多人看清了里面的猫腻。

硬件钱包厂家宣传自家产品时各种强调安全元件、EAL 认证、开源、防篡改、私钥永不离开设备，给人一种固若金汤的感觉。

但一旦真出事（固件缺陷、供应链被植入、经销商被动手脚、官方 App 出纰漏），你去翻用户协议，会发现他们基本上已经把责任推得一干二净了。美其名曰，我们的产品是自托管产品，自求多福。

你硬件钱包厂家赔偿的时候写着“我只赔 100 美元”，那你吹牛的时候就少吹一点啊，前后反差也太大了。吹牛的时候把自己说得多强大、多安全，什么固若金汤；等真出事了，就来一句“不好意思，我只赔 100 美元”，那不就等于是让用户全权负责嘛。

要是这样的话，所有人都可以开硬件钱包公司了：自己在网上使劲吹，吹得别人心痒痒、都相信了，再买点商单推广；但真正出问题的时候赔得极少，甚至哪怕出了厂家自身导致的问题也根本不赔，还美其名曰“已经给你写清楚了”。

这些硬件厂商真正牛逼的地方，是把稳赚不赔的后路全给自己想好了：一边在网上大肆吹嘘自己产品有多牛，还在推特上给各种 KOL 砸商单帮着一起吹；另一边算准了普通用户根本不看用户协议，直接在条款里把赔偿责任限制到死，出事顶多赔你 100 美元，其余概不负责。

而且千万别以为以后真出了事，能拿霸王条款去跟他们打官司维权。跟你签约的主体往往注册在香港，注册资本就 1 港币，早就做好了风险隔离。你就算打赢了官司又怎么样？大不了把整家空壳公司赔给你。

硬件钱包厂商的风控全用在自己退路上了，而用户的退路根本不在他的考虑范围内：创业成功了，公司能卖个好价钱，自己赚得盆满钵满；一旦产品出了大问题暴雷，退路他早已备好，而用户就是那个承担所有损失的代价和耗材。

其实像 Crypto 的红利基本上已经全都结束了。以前在上升期的时候，出了什么问题，项目方或者厂家都还愿意赔；但现在说实在的，已经过了红利期，加密货币已经没什么红利了，现在就是守成阶段。

所以大家现在要守住自己过去十年在 Crypto 赚到的资产，因为现在已经不是红利期了。你想再维权真的很困难，我给你参照两个人 @jheioff @neillee99，损失了上千万的资产，维权的时候像条狗一样被项目方戏耍。给钱的时候你是老大，一旦把你骗进来，出了什么事情，没人拿得出钱赔的，都想最后捞一笔走人。

以后无论是买产品还是存大额资产，自己心里都要掂量清楚：到什么程度是他们根本赔不起的？我还有没有必要花钱买这些产品？有没有更好更完善的办法？这些问题每个人都必须先想明白。
author: blocktom
quoted_text:
我是OneKey产品的用户（真金白银买的产品），因为指出 OneKey 用户协议里的一些问题以及追问厂家自身安全缺陷导致丢币时，到底赔不赔、赔多少，我直接被他们创始人@ohyishi拉黑了。

王磊你的心眼真的太小了吧！！！连付费用户对你自己产品的用户协议条款的追问都容不下吗？

我引用的内容，全是你们自己用户协议里白纸黑字写着的，没有凭空编造。

我们币圈的中文用户，有时候真的挺卑微。钱是自己的，损失也是自己扛，最后连找谁负责、还能找谁说理，都不知道。

之前，Gate 有用户报称约 170 万美元资产被盗，平台说经官方认定属于自己的责任就双倍赔偿，当事人后续却表示迟迟没有拿到赔偿；后来，又有 Solv 用户公开反映，约 50 个 BTC 对应的资产长期无法赎回，材料交了，邮件来回几十封，项目方的解释是还在做风险审查

现在到了我这里，甚至还没涉及实际索赔。我只是拿着 OneKey 自己的用户协议，提前问清楚保障和赔偿，结果就被创始人拉黑。

只能说你好，不能说一点不好？花钱买了产品，连提出疑问都不行？

我理解错了，你可以指出来；你们愿意承担哪些责任，你可以讲清楚。用户问的是安全和赔偿，怎么到你这里，就变成了容不容得下质疑的问题？

拉黑我算什么本事？用户还会认真看协议、跟你讲道理，黑客可不会照顾你的情绪。真希望你要求用户给你的那份体谅和好脾气，黑客也能给你。

王磊，我向你道歉。

我不应该花真金白银买你们 OneKey 的产品。

买了产品，我不应该认真看你们的用户协议。

看了协议，我不应该发现问题。

发现了问题，我不应该追问：如果是你们自身的安全缺陷导致用户丢币，到底赔不赔、赔多少？

我更不应该发出来，不应该让其他用户也看到。

这些都是我的错，好吧？我这个付费用户太不懂事了，竟然给你添了这么多麻烦。

你创业不易，我们用户的钱都是大风刮来的。你的心情需要照顾，我们的钱丢了自己消化。买了你的产品，就应该只说你好，认真看协议、追问赔偿，实在太不识趣了。

你永远都是对的。你在创造未来，你在开创未来，我们这些花钱买产品的人，怎么能拿安全、责任、赔偿这些小事打扰你呢？

text:
您好，您的担心很合理。买的是安全工具，当然希望资产有保障，真出了问题，厂家也能负责。我们不能只在宣传时讲安全，谈到责任时就让您去看协议。

OneKey 是自托管钱包，私钥和资产控制权都在您手里。我们不保管您的资产，也无法替您找回遗失的私钥、撤销已经完成的链上转账。这些限制，应该在您购买前就讲清楚。

但不保管资产，不等于产品出了问题也不用负责。您自己遗失私钥，和我们的硬件、固件或 App 存在缺陷，是两回事。如果问题出在我们的产品，就应该查清原因、修复问题，承担相应责任，不能用一句“自托管”把责任都推给您。

我们确实无法承诺所有原因造成的资产损失都无条件全额赔付，具体需要查清损失是怎么发生的、责任在哪里。但您说的这个落差值得我们认真对待：宣传时讲了哪些安全能力，就应该同时把限制和责任讲明白，让用户购买前就能判断是否适合自己，而不是出了问题才请您去看协议。

如果期望 100% 的全额赔付，那么，将资产全部托管在 Coinbase 交易所（US 主站，非钱包）或 IBIT ETF 或许是更佳选择，IBIT 在其产品风险说明中，列举了风险赔付机制和上限：https://t.co/UDEzTv58OY

如果您对 OneKey 还有其他问题，欢迎访问 https://t.co/QG5Mu82PKT 或官方提交工单，会有专员为您服务。

感谢您的理解，祝您生活愉快。

text:
前端是我一直以来非常看好的方向。它是未来用户访问加密技术和加密货币的核心，也能够捕获非常大的价值。加密行业的基础设施基本已经搭建好了，投资理论也很简单，纯看基本面和代币经济学就可以。但前端几乎没有投资机会，之前买 $BASED 也纯是捏着鼻子去玩，想买 $TWT ，Trust Wallet 团队又不把重心放在代币上面。其他，像是 Binance Wallet、OKX Wallet、Bitget Wallet 等产品，又没有投机窗口。像这种一旦做起来就非常赚钱的东西，团队一般不会把利润分给外人。

但现在有一个例外就是 Brave & ethereum:0x0d8775f648430679a709e98d2b0cb6250d2887ef ，他们大发善心吗？我觉得不是的。他们只是回购，并不是销毁，而是考虑再次分发出去。他们是为了新产品造势，拿到市场的注意力，做冷启动和增长。正好现在隐私的风吹得起劲，团队顺势而为。但这些回购预期和未来的部分收入回购，在吸引注意力的同时，是实打实地为市场提供了机械性地买盘，为 BAT 创造了需求，之后可能分发出去的代币，也不一定会被即时卖出。而且我觉得外部投资者会对它产生兴趣，毕竟它有用户和长期运营的基础，新业务如果进来，可能就会成为一些外部投资者的选择。

1、我觉得 BAT 在这个市场上的最大优势就是：它不需要再次证明自己是一家成功的公司。它有非常好的用户基础，看起来其新产品的前景要比加密行业同类产品更好。用户基础好，就代表着其未来的收入潜力会更高。

Here is a list of at-risk Ledger resellers.

Following the exploit involving the reseller CryptoBilis, some other reseller names have also come up in discussions, such as Lazada merchants.

For now the situation still seems hard to fully contain, and even though Ledger has confirmed the link with CryptoBilis, it still seems too early to confirm that it is the only one affected.

I have therefore put together a list of resellers that could represent a risk due to their regional proximity to one another.

There is therefore a risk that their supply chain has also been compromised.

This is pure speculation and nothing is confirmed, but if you bought a Ledger less than 6 months ago from one of these resellers, it may be wise to move your assets to safety until the matter is resolved.

If you feel up to inspecting the inside of your Ledger to check whether it has been tampered with, you will find everything you need to guide you and know what to look for on @MagicalTux 's account.

Privacy in institutional blockchain is a spectrum, and the right point on that spectrum depends entirely on what you are building and who you are building it for.

At @blockworksDAS Asia, Zenith Co-Founder and CBO @HeslinKim joined the Balancing Privacy vs Transparency in Onchain Finance panel to discuss how different institutional requirements shape blockchain infrastructure.

Zenith Stack is designed to support multiple deployment environments, each with its own approach to access and information disclosure.

Public permissionless environments can support open participation. Permissioned environments can enforce KYC, KYB and AML requirements before granting access. Private deployments can keep an institution's internal activity confidential, while multi-party and consortium environments can enable selective disclosure of transaction details, counterparties and order flow.

This flexibility is particularly important for financial institutions, where privacy requirements differ across assets, participants and business workflows.

@CantonNetwork's Daml architecture provides the foundation for granular privacy and selective disclosure, while Zenith extends the ecosystem with Ethereum-compatible execution and configurable deployment environments.

The goal is to give institutions control over how they participate onchain, without forcing every use case into the same privacy model.

Gm Folks
We are back!

This is another edition of the Predict Alpha Report, our bi-monthly collaboration with @CoinsiliumGroup tracking the rise of prediction markets, event-driven finance, and the growing role of AI agents within it. Each edition focuses on the signals that matter, from capital flows and fundraising activity to regulatory shifts and product innovation. As information is increasingly priced in real time by both humans and machines, the Predict Alpha Report will track where these signals lead.
But first, let’s get this part out of the way:

Always DYOR:
This bulletin is for informational purposes only and contains summaries of news articles originally published by third-party media outlets. Please refer to the full disclaimer at the end of the post.

Now, let’s get started.
Here are the highlights:

💸 Capital Signals
👉Prediction markets 21x-ed
👉 $1 Billion Raise
👉AI For Everyday
👉@Predictive_Labs to Showcase @nijinn_official in Web Summit Lisbon 2026 Startup Programme

📈 Industry Pulse
👉Blockchain_com Joins Prediction Markets
👉Polymarket Hires…
👉Kalshi Oil Futures
👉Kalshi’s Transparency Trio

💸 Capital Signals

💰Prediction markets 21x-ed

Prediction markets saw trading volume reach $188 billion in Q3 2026, according to CryptoRank, marking a nearly 70% increase from the previous quarter and a staggering 21-fold rise from the same period last year. Much of that growth came from Kalshi, where sports accounted for around 40% of quarterly trading activity. Kalshi and Polymarket also recorded about $1.4 billion in combined open interest, which reflects the value of outstanding positions. While elections initially put prediction markets in the spotlight, people now use these platforms to trade on everything from sports results to economic decisions.

💰 $1 Billion Raise

@Kalshi is in advanced talks to raise another $1 billion in funding at a valuation of around $40 billion, nearly doubling the $22 billion valuation it secured in May 2026. The round is expected to be led by Sequoia Capital and Wellington Management, with Tiger Global and Dragoneer also participating. The rapid increase in valuation reflects growing investor confidence in prediction markets, particularly as Kalshi expands its sports trading activity and gains ground against rival Polymarket, which is reportedly pursuing its own $1 billion funding round.

Kalshi's ambitions are also moving beyond prediction markets. The company is exploring opportunities to offer a wider range of trading products, potentially putting it in competition with established financial exchanges like CME Group and Intercontinental Exchange, the parent company of the New York Stock Exchange.

💰AI For Everyday

San Francisco-based AI startup Instinct has raised $1 billion in fresh funding, pushing its valuation to $10 billion, four times the $2.5 billion it was valued at just a month earlier. The round attracted major investors including Sequoia Capital, Benchmark Capital and Coatue. Instinct is developing a personal AI assistant capable of completing everyday tasks on behalf of users, from booking flights and ordering groceries to managing subscriptions, using simple text or voice instructions.

The company has also introduced a Concierge service for handling phone calls and specialised bookings, alongside technology that allows different AI agents to coordinate tasks with each other, and security measures designed to catch AI mistakes before they lead to real-world actions. The new funding will support further product development and help Instinct expand beyond its current early-access stage.

And rounding up this section:

💰Predictive Labs to Showcase Nijinn in Web Summit Lisbon 2026 Startup Programme

@WebSummit Lisbon, one of the world’s leading technology events, returns from 9–12 November 2026 with prominent AI industry speakers including Richard Socher, co-founder of You(dot)com, an AI-powered search and research platform; Michele Catasta, President at Replit, an online coding and AI app-building platform; and Fabian Hedin, co-founder of Lovable, which builds apps from natural-language instructions. Blockchain and digital assets will also be represented by Ben Zhou, CEO of Bybit, and Markus Infanger, Senior Vice President at Ripple.

Predictive Labs will exhibit as part of the event’s startup programme, with founder @johann_evrard attending to showcase Nijinn, its prediction-market data and analytics platform, to some of the world’s leading entrepreneurs and investment firms. The programme’s focus on connecting startups with investors and industry leaders could help raise Nijinn’s international profile and open new commercial opportunities for Predictive Labs. Web Summit has grown from a small conference into a global gathering attracting more than 70,000 attendees.

Ahead of Web Summit Lisbon, Predictive Labs will also attend NEXT Predict in New York on 22–23 October, a dedicated prediction-markets summit focused on the sector’s development, including market infrastructure, liquidity, regulation and product innovation.

📌 FYI: Coinsilium’s shares are traded on the Aquis Stock Exchange Growth Market in London, under the ticker symbol "COIN", and on the OTCQB Venture Market in the United States under the ticker symbol "CINGF".

But it’s not just capital flowing into the space.
Keep reading for the latest signals in regulation, adoption, and structure.

📈 Industry Pulse

⚡️ Blockchain_com Joins Prediction Markets

@blockchain has applied for two licenses from the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) as it looks to offer prediction markets and cryptocurrency derivatives directly to American customers. The company already offers prediction markets and crypto futures to some international users through Polymarket and Hyperliquid, but securing these licenses would bring those services under its own platform in the US. The goal is to give everyday users and institutional investors one place to manage crypto, trade derivatives and make predictions on real-world outcomes.

The move comes as more companies compete for a share of the rapidly growing prediction-market industry. According to CNBC, 11 other firms have applied for similar exchange licenses in 2026, with six already approved by the CFTC.

⚡️ Polymarket Hires…

@Polymarket has hired Lisa Mantil, a former Goldman Sachs partner with nearly 30 years of experience, as its new head of institutional growth. Mantil previously led Goldman Sachs' ETF accelerator, and her appointment signals Polymarket's growing focus on attracting institutional investors, including banks, asset managers, and other large financial firms. While everyday traders have driven much of the recent growth in prediction markets, platforms are increasingly looking to bring larger investors into the space.

The new appointment follows the launch of Polymarket's US exchange in May and the recent appointment of Warren Jenson, a former finance executive at Amazon and Delta Air Lines, as its first chief financial officer.

⚡️Kalshi Oil Futures

Kalshi has filed a proposal with the CFTC to introduce a new oil futures contract linked to West Texas Intermediate (WTI), a key benchmark for US crude oil prices. Unlike traditional futures contracts that expire on a set date, this product would allow traders to maintain their positions without a fixed expiry, making it easier to manage exposure to changing oil prices.

Although the proposal is still subject to a 45-day regulatory review, it would become the first crude oil perpetual futures contract on a regulated US exchange if approved. Already, Kalshi's commodity trading activity has been growing quickly, with volumes approaching $400 million by early September, nearly four times the pace of its crypto products at a similar stage.

At the same time,

⚡️Kalshi’s Transparency Trio

Kalshi has introduced three new transparency features to help people better understand its prediction markets ahead of the November 2026 US midterm elections. The features are due to the election trading volume, which has already surpassed that of the 2024 presidential election. The updates include labels highlighting low trading activity markets, live feeds showing individual trades as they happen, and Brier scores, which measure how accurate past market predictions have been.

Kalshi is also partnering with the Associated Press to display live vote counts and race calls, while CBS News and 270toWin will feature its forecasts alongside traditional polling and election results. Its dedicated Midterms Hub brings together market probabilities, polling averages, campaign fundraising, and election news across Senate, House, and governor races.

And that’s it!

author: zerohedge
quoted_text:
Ledger theft, day two. Since yesterday the thief has pushed ether through Tornado Cash three times, and each time on into Zcash's shielded pool. We followed every lot out the far side. Here is how, step by step.

1. THE SAME BUILD, THREE TIMES
An ether wallet pays a fresh splitter. The splitter pays four fresh wallets. The four drop it into Tornado Cash's 100, 10 and 1 ETH pools. Minutes, every time.

Run 1, yesterday 15:17: 1,254 ETH. Run 2, today 09:42: 1,291 ETH. Run 3, today 11:56: 450 ETH from 0xfa4EaBB840A33C156E600311433AE261CBfCb0e2, in the pools by 12:15.

2. OUT OF TORNADO CASH
The mixer breaks the link between a deposit and a withdrawal. We do not need the link. Our tooling fingerprints the withdrawal transactions themselves: how each one is constructed, who constructs it, and when. 

Yesterday's 65 withdrawals (1,084 ETH) and today's 96 (1,726 ETH) all carry the same signature. The six other withdrawals from those pools in today's windows do not. Run 3 came out from 12:18 into 0x0d697aa182801566d87adc86e68e95fd3b2f5f82 (213 ETH) and 0x676b16cc18542f37d202a1a79ac05463395496a4 (122 ETH), and 195 ETH of it was inside a cross-chain swap service by 12:38. Forty-two minutes, end to end.

3. INTO ZCASH, AND OUT AGAIN
The swap service turns the ether into shielded ZEC, where sender, amount and recipient vanish. But the service's own shielding of each lot is public, and from it we derive a value signature for that lot's exit, then scan every transparent exit from the pool. 108 of 108 exits across both days match their lot to the zatoshi. Not one other exit from the pool does. 

First lot today: in at 10:18:18, out at 11:06:16 in block 3512847 (8d26a9b095d4d28373527f7a6eb81a3be7f906d1e2190960c0512ff64f369418 and 738c6d1261e79766e4dd16bdbd38dced91b8e3a86ce41dcda83eda1f19208fbf), straight into a ZEC to USDC order.

Today so far: 20 lots ordered (2,379 ZEC, $2.9m), 14 out, 5 inside the pool, 1 still settling. Every exit feeds a ZEC to USDC order paying two wallets born at 11:11, 22 of the 28 paid by 12:43:
0x816D5Ee17DB1495d1409F135b98FF3edc5F3cDf8: 940,561 USDC
0xBA736A4b616e79867B6d586293966b552883f3F3: 852,258 USDC
1.79m USDC, unspent. @Circle can freeze it.

(1/2) 🧵⤵️

I imagine we'll have some backend services that could be replaced entirely by this new architecture.

text:
我感觉现在很多人对Benchmark的理解是不是有点偏差😅

似乎提到Benchmark，大家第一反应就是刷榜，找几个大模型跑一圈，看看谁的分数高，然后发篇论文。
但其实Benchmark在AI研究里是非常重要的东西。

就拿斯坦福这篇BrickBench来说，表面上是在让大模型设计乐高积木，看谁拼得更好。

但你仔细想想，它实际上在评测的是什么？

是模型能不能理解一个具有物理约束的世界，能不能根据自然语言描述规划出合理的三维结构，知道不同零件之间应该怎么连接，以及最终设计出来的东西能不能真正搭建起来。

这里面涉及空间推理、物理约束、结构规划，还有Agent对工具和环境的使用能力。

这些能力对于未来的具身智能、机器人，以及各种PhysicalAI都有研究价值。

而且论文也不只是拿几个模型跑一下。
作者专门构建了BrickAgent环境，让Agent可以调用工具、选择零件、搭建结构、检查碰撞、模拟稳定性，再根据这些反馈不断调整自己的设计。

这其实也是我觉得很多人忽略的一点。

你想让模型在某个领域变得更好，首先得知道这个领域到底需要哪些能力，以及怎样判断模型有没有真的进步。

否则你连一个稳定、可复现的评价标准都没有，模型训练完之后，怎么知道它究竟是学会了什么，还是仅仅在某些Case上碰巧表现不错？

Benchmark的意义就在这里。

它能够把一个复杂领域的问题拆解成具体的任务和评价指标，让研究者发现模型的能力边界，再围绕这些问题持续改进模型和系统。

顺带一提，这篇论文其实也并非作者随便找了个UseCase。

第一作者PeterKulits今年已经有一篇BrickNet论文发表在CVPR2026，研究的是如何让语言模型生成符合积木连接约束的搭建序列，还构建了超过10万个人类设计作品的数据集。

这篇BrickBench本身就是他此前研究方向的延续。

所以我觉得，大家可能有点低估Benchmark这件事情了。

一个新的Benchmark最重要的贡献，未必是告诉我们今天哪个模型排名第一。

更重要的是，它为一个此前难以量化的问题，建立了可以持续研究和改进的标准。

毕竟如果连问题是什么、什么算做好都没定义清楚，又怎么知道AI到底进步了多少？

请尊重一下做Benchmark的人吧，这些人的贡献一般都没人能意识到（我也是开始做才知道的）。

text:
Soon I'll hit 5 years in Web3 security.

This is for everyone just starting out in the space:

- people are making $100k+ from reporting a single bug. the opportunities are insane, but it's NOT easy money
- become a nerd. literally. read code, break things, put in the hours
- learn to negotiate. being great at finding bugs doesn't automatically mean you'll be great at getting paid
- be disciplined. it takes years to become genuinely good at this
- stay curious. never stop asking WHY and HOW things work
- start by finding smaller bugs. learn to walk before chasing Criticals
- be patient. skills, reputation and money don't come overnight
- adapt fast. this industry looks nothing like it did 4 years ago
- embrace new technologies, especially AI. learn to use them instead of dismissing them
- surround yourself with smart, like-minded people. you'll learn things no course can teach you
- stay up to date with exploits, research and everything happening in the space
- learn to sell yourself. your skills mean less if nobody knows about them
- build your personal brand. a good reputation opens doors you didn't even know existed
- understand what creates REAL value
- celebrate your wins, but don't get too comfortable. take a day off, then get back to work
- respect other whitehats and builders. there's always something you can learn from them
- help people without expecting anything in return. you'll be surprised where it leads
-  long-term relationships > short-term benefit
- be careful what you click. even security researchers get hacked
- never think you've learned enough. the moment you stop improving, you're falling behind
- enjoy the process. this space is so crazy that it's almost impossible to get bored

美联储官员讲话 — — 哈马克 — — 2026年票委

2026年票委、克利夫兰联储主席哈马克表示现在3.75%到4%的利率还不够高，她认为还需要继续加息。她更倾向于小步、次数更多的调整，因为一次动得太大，企业更难提前安排，从语气来看，更倾向于 10 月先保持观察。

哈马克参观克利夫兰制造商Jergens后注意到，客户现在更在意能不能更快拿到零部件，价格反而排在质量和交付速度之后，愿意为了快一点多付钱。她把这种定价能力看成需求仍然强、供给追不上的信号。

AI数据中心相关买家对价格尤其不敏感，加息未必能明显压低这部分需求，但可能让航空、能源或运输等其他买家重新考虑扩建和采购，从边际上给需求降温。

哈马克还否定了“长期美债收益率已经上升，可以替美联储完成紧缩”的说法，认为债券市场收紧只能配合政策，不能替代加息。

通胀已经连续五年多高于2%，多数美联储官员预计到2029年才回到目标，她认为这个时间太久了，她听到一些低收入家庭已经从买便宜货，变成必须决定哪张账单先不付。

哈马克认为经济和企业投资仍显得有力，政策需要更有约束力，但具体会议和每次幅度仍没有被提前确定。总的来说就是美国的经济很好，可以继续维持加息状态，但并不需要每次大幅加息。

最近油价刚刚开始下降，主要是因为通过数据看到通过霍尔木兹的石油运输量已经达到了战前的八成左右，虽然油价的运输还没有下来，但运输量还是能确保的。

现在期货市场的油价又开始上涨了，WTI 重新回到 91 美元上方，Brant 也围绕 105 美元震荡，这应该是伊朗给川普最好的答案，想要通过俄罗斯降低油价，并不容易。

高油价对于美国的通胀肯定不是好事，尤其是周三就会公布美国九月的 CPI 了，CPI 上涨已经是大概率了，虽然我不觉得十月还会加息，但这么涨上去，十二月必然再次会加息。

text:
群友问我在撸什么？

目前重点依旧是 @variational_io 和 @Lighter_xyz 。

1. 如果 @RobinhoodCrypto 做得起来，最大受益者是打火机；如果罗宾汉链做不起来，人家奖池发的是 ethereum:0x232ce3bd40fcd6f80f3d55a522d03f25df784ee2 母币，币和流动性早都在那了，没有做到一半 rug 的风险。

这种对我来说就算是下限很高的机会。
一周拿个 800-1000 分，加上小农经济的基础收益率，没有任何的心理负担。

而万一项目方搞节目效果，选在 TGE 一周年开奖，那就算是天大的惊喜。如果一直拖着不发，那无非只是收益率低了些，都在预期内。

2. 今年的天王项目 @variational_io ，现已完全融入了我的交易日常。作为用 tradfi liquidity 矫正 crypto 错误定价的最好工具，随着平台 swap 品种覆盖面的上升，能尝试的策略只会越来越多。

等 var 官宣完它的重大合作和 TGE 之后，链上 perps 四足鼎立的格局就基本形成了：

1. hyper 利益集团；
2. lighter 利益集团；
3. var 利益集团；
4. 还有个 @Aster_DEX 不能小看。

到那时这个赛道的竞争就已彻底过了产品之争的阶段，头部玩家每一个都是 too big to fail，于是整个市场转向对分发渠道争抢阶段，逐渐步入拼硬核资源和运营能力的新阶段。

3. 基于以上判断，现阶段在搞积分的，以及几十家准备搞积分的，这些依旧停留在不知道怎么差异化定位产品和竞争优势的项目们，都属于路边的野花。

如果你能做到当 farmer 们 fomo 涌入一个所交易的时候，赚他们不计成本跑量的钱，那顺手采一采，是锦上添花。

但如果你是纯抱着看到 lighter 和 var 的奇迹，想要梭哈撸毛心态选项目的话，说个扎心的真相：你们靠在 X 上接受到的信息来做所谓的投资判断，胜率真的太低了。

要说交易所撸毛的机会，过去 3 个月，在一条市值高的离谱，实则鸟不拉屎的链上，有一个产品做的狗看了都摇头的项目，10WU 以内的小资金，你努努力，每个月可以赚 20% - 30% 回报率，也就是一个季度本金翻倍。

但你看到过有人推这个项目嘛？
没有。

两个原因：
a. 推像 @variational_io 和 @Lighter_xyz  这种自己会一直当产品用的项目，属于加速早期共识建立，PVE 游戏，把蛋糕做大，才是利益最大化的行为。

而产品不行，但却有可以计算的毛撸的项目，属于 pvp 游戏，参与的人越少越好，说多了，不如直接打钱。

b. 单纯的菜。

OIL MARKETS FACE GROWING SUPPLY RISKS AS MIDDLE EAST ATTACKS ESCALATE
