author: imsongshu
quoted_text:
Quite a few people have been asking me to take a closer look at solana:6Mix12LiHrQFojaQEnfPUC65Qkwd6X4Y5Qg93oFbordr after its recent move into the $4–5M MC range

I've spent some time researching Bordrless, from its new token standard and DEX to its launchpad, revenue model, and what the team has actually delivered over the past few days

Personally, I think the technology behind this project is pretty interesting. This isn't just another memecoin trying to ride a narrative

However, there's still a pretty big gap between what the team is building and the actual adoption we're seeing so far

Here are a few things that caught my attention

1. What exactly is Bordrless building?

The most interesting part of Bordrless is its new token standard on Solana, called Bordrless Token Standard (BTS) 

With Token-2022, transfer hooks are mainly used to check conditions and approve or reject transactions

Bordrless wants to take this further by allowing hooks to directly modify the amount of tokens being transferred, enabling things like automatic fees, burns, holder rewards, and custom token rules

For example, a token could be programmed so that the receiver gets 90% of a transfer, 6% goes toward fees, and the remaining 4% gets burned, all handled on-chain

This reminds me somewhat of Uniswap v4 hooks, except Bordrless is bringing that programmability directly to the token level rather than focusing only on liquidity pools

If executed properly, I think this could open up some interesting possibilities for tokenomics on Solana

2. They're building an entire ecosystem, not just a token standard

Bordrless is developing several components around BTS, including its own DEX, Launchpad, Bridge, and SDK for creating custom hooks

The launchpad allows creators to define token rules at launch, including creator fees, holder rewards, burns, max wallet limits, and more advanced mechanisms

According to the documentation, 75% of the supply is distributed through a bonding curve, while the remaining 25% is reserved for liquidity after graduation

The rules are fixed at launch, and post-graduation liquidity is designed to be permanently locked

What I like here is that the team isn't simply introducing a new token standard and waiting for other developers to adopt it

They're building the infrastructure needed for BTS tokens to launch, trade, and generate revenue

That said, having a complete ecosystem doesn't automatically mean people will use it

And that's still the biggest challenge for Bordrless

3. Companions are one of the features I find most interesting

This is probably the part that caught my attention the most after BTS itself

Instead of sending creator fees directly to a personal wallet, Bordrless allows creators to use a program called a Companion to manage those funds automatically

Companions can handle buybacks, burns, holder rewards, vesting, and even mechanisms like Lottery, Jackpot, and Streak

These processes are designed to operate on-chain without relying on a trusted centralized bot or keeper

Another interesting example is the Half-Life hook

A token could start with a 20% sell or transfer fee, which gets cut in half every six hours until reaching zero after 48 hours

Features like these create far more flexibility than what we normally see on traditional launchpads

But there's another side to this

More complicated tokenomics don't necessarily create stronger demand. A mechanism can look impressive technically without attracting sustainable trading activity

4. solana:6Mix12LiHrQFojaQEnfPUC65Qkwd6X4Y5Qg93oFbordr has a relatively clear value capture mechanism

Unlike many infrastructure tokens that rely almost entirely on future expectations, solana:6Mix12LiHrQFojaQEnfPUC65Qkwd6X4Y5Qg93oFbordr is designed to benefit from protocol revenue

According to the project's documentation, Bordrless charges protocol fees on launch pools and ordinary pools, alongside revenue sharing from certain hook and creator fees

The documentation currently lists a 0.3% protocol fee for launch pools and 1% for ordinary pools

50% of protocol revenue is allocated toward buying back solana:6Mix12LiHrQFojaQEnfPUC65Qkwd6X4Y5Qg93oFbordr from the market

At the time of my research, the dashboard showed approximately $9.2K in cumulative buybacks, up from around $8.44K earlier

The buybacks are executed periodically through an off-chain keeper, and the purchased tokens are held in the protocol treasury rather than automatically burned

I see this as a positive because there's already a measurable mechanism to track, rather than just promises about future buybacks

However, we also need to look at the scale

Around $9K in buybacks is still relatively small compared to a token trading at a multimillion-dollar market cap

And buybacks don't guarantee price appreciation

What matters is whether protocol revenue can keep growing and whether that buying pressure becomes meaningful relative to liquidity and market selling pressure

5. Early traction looks decent, but I'm not fully convinced yet

According to the figures displayed on the website, Bordrless has recorded around 85 token launches and approximately $346.5K in 24-hour trading volume

The ecosystem has also recorded roughly 19.8 SOL distributed to holders, 65.3 SOL in creator fees, and 12.3 SOL burned across launched tokens

For a platform that only launched around October 8, I think these are decent early numbers

But what matters more to me is the quality of those launches

Among the tokens I checked, Borderless Cat ($BCAT) was one of the more notable examples, but its MC was only around $75K

Others like $GENNY, $CHM, and $HLIFE were still trading at market caps of just a few tens of thousands of dollars

In other words, Bordrless has people experimenting with its product, but it still hasn't produced a meaningful runner capable of attracting broader attention from Solana CT

There's a huge difference between a launchpad generating activity and one actually creating a trend

6. Axiom integration is the biggest catalyst right now

One positive development is the team's announcement on October 12 that Bordrless Token Standard and its DEX are now integrated with Axiom

I think this is an important step because accessibility has been one of the biggest limitations for BTS tokens

If tokens can only be traded through the project's own website, attracting significant liquidity and producing major runners becomes much harder

The team is also working toward integrations with platforms like Jupiter, GMGN, and Fomo

However, I wouldn't treat those as completed catalysts until the integrations are actually live

If Bordrless becomes accessible through several major trading terminals, that's when I'd seriously reassess the ecosystem's growth potential

7. What I don't particularly like about solana:6Mix12LiHrQFojaQEnfPUC65Qkwd6X4Y5Qg93oFbordr

Even though I like the concept, there are several concerns worth mentioning

First, the platform is extremely new. A few days of activity aren't enough to evaluate the technology's long-term stability or sustainable demand

Second, 85 launches sound decent on paper, but there's still no meaningful runner. This is probably the biggest weakness in the current thesis

Third, visibility across the broader community remains limited. I haven't seen many major KOLs seriously focusing on tokens launched through Bordrless

Fourth, based on the information I've reviewed, the program still retains upgrade authority while awaiting an audit

That's an important technical risk, especially for a protocol handling complex token mechanics

And finally, Solana's launchpad market is already extremely competitive

Having better technology doesn't necessarily mean you'll capture market share

8. My thoughts on the chart and MC levels

solana:6Mix12LiHrQFojaQEnfPUC65Qkwd6X4Y5Qg93oFbordr recently made a strong move from around $1.5–2M to approximately $4.65M MC, briefly pushing above $5M on the chart I reviewed

This suggests that market attention is starting to build around the narrative

However, after such an aggressive move, I don't find the risk/reward of chasing the price particularly attractive

If we get a pullback, the first area I'd watch is around $2.5–3M MC

A deeper retracement toward $1.5–2.2M MC would be more interesting to me from an R/R perspective, assuming volume doesn't completely disappear and the project's fundamentals remain intact

These are observation zones, not guaranteed support levels, and there's no certainty price will revisit them

At the current valuation, I'd rather wait for a healthier market structure than chase a vertical candle

9. What catalysts could take solana:6Mix12LiHrQFojaQEnfPUC65Qkwd6X4Y5Qg93oFbordr further?

I think three things will largely determine where solana:6Mix12LiHrQFojaQEnfPUC65Qkwd6X4Y5Qg93oFbordr goes next

First is integration

Axiom has already been announced, but I want to see more major terminals supporting BTS and, more importantly, actual trading volume flowing through those integrations

Second is runners

If Bordrless can produce even one or two tokens reaching $300–500K MC or higher through unique hook mechanics, the attention surrounding the launchpad could change significantly

Third is revenue

I want to see buybacks grow consistently alongside trading volume rather than relying on a short burst of activity immediately after launch

If all three improve together, the solana:6Mix12LiHrQFojaQEnfPUC65Qkwd6X4Y5Qg93oFbordr thesis becomes much more convincing

10. Final thoughts

Personally, I like the direction Bordrless is taking

This isn't just a project that puts together a website, attaches a technology narrative, and launches a token

The team has built its own token standard, DEX, Launchpad, programmable hooks, and a revenue-linked buyback model

But I also don't want to confuse interesting technology with guaranteed token success

Right now, solana:6Mix12LiHrQFojaQEnfPUC65Qkwd6X4Y5Qg93oFbordr has the technology and the narrative, but it still lacks the level of adoption needed to fully validate the thesis

I'll continue watching the project, particularly its integration progress, buyback revenue, and whether the launchpad can produce its first meaningful runner

If the team manages to deliver on those three fronts, I think Bordrless has a real chance to become an interesting player in Solana's programmable token infrastructure

If not, it could easily end up being another technically interesting project that struggles to retain speculative capital

For now, I see solana:6Mix12LiHrQFojaQEnfPUC65Qkwd6X4Y5Qg93oFbordr as a high-risk, high-potential play that's worth researching and monitoring rather than blindly chasing the chart

Now back to the interesting question.

Which other old tokens could experience something similar?

I’ve been looking at a few.

1. $APT (main candidate??)

$774M market cap

It’s a recognizable L1, listed on major exchanges, with actual infrastructure behind it.

But let’s be serious, when was the last time you saw CT genuinely excited about Aptos?

Of course, it still needs a stronger catalyst.

2. $STX (the Bitcoin alternative???)

$717M market cap

A narrative that people already understand.

Bitcoin DeFi.

And considering that Bitcoin-related developments are part of the excitement around Starknet, I wouldn’t completely ignore a project that has been working on Bitcoin smart contracts for years.

Its daily momentum is currently weaker, and the volume isn’t particularly impressive.

3. $DOT (the forgotten giant)

$2.15B market cap

Remember when Polkadot was supposed to be one of the biggest ecosystems in crypto?

Me neither.

I also struggle to find a genuinely new catalyst that would make people suddenly rush back into it.

4. $TAO (probably the most obvious narrative)

$3.36B market cap

I like the fact that Bittensor already has a recognizable identity around decentralized AI and subnets.

5. $ENA (the one with the strongest momentum)

$3.15B market cap

Ethena has a real product narrative around synthetic dollars, but also carries risks around funding conditions, token supply and crowded positioning.

6. $QNT
This one is particularly interesting.

$QNT is up 273% in 30 days.

The move has been associated with its selection for a tokenized-money initiative involving The Clearing House.

A token being 90% below its ATH doesn’t automatically make it cheap.

I spent years watching CT jump from one new narrative to another.

Now we’re apparently reaching a point where some of the best-performing tokens are projects people had already buried.

Imagine spending months researching the next revolutionary blockchain only to get outperformed by a token you stopped following two years ago.

Crypto never stops being ridiculous.

NFA, DYOR here but we will see how Dino coins perform this cycle.

谁是币圈“岳不群”？

友商10·11事件席卷全球加密市场，波及全球用户数百亿美元的资产，让无数加密行业参与者蒙受巨大损失，承受难以言说的痛苦。整个 Crypto 市场也由此陷入漫长的寒冬，无数人的财富、信心与希望在这场风暴中遭受重创。

然而，面对这样一场给整个行业留下深刻伤痕的灾难，首富在接受采访时，竟然睁眼说瞎话，如此轻描淡写地说道：

“实际上，币安拿出了大约8亿美元，用于赔偿那些在币安平台上遭受损失的用户，尽管币安本来并没有义务这样做，对吧？也就是说，币安没有任何必须进行赔偿的义务，但币安完全出于自愿，主动进行了这些赔偿。”

数百亿美元的市场损失、无数用户的痛苦，在他口中，最终变成了一场值得自我表扬的‘自愿赔偿’。

text:
$파랭이 820k dyor

0x8175810d00f9356a8f87a4a7b8ff7660087c7777

okx wallet:https://t.co/CyNxP0FRKG

It originated from a post written in Korean:

“오늘 하루 또 거칠었습니다. 회개하고 다시 깨끗한 파랭이로 태어나겠습니드아!!!!”

Translation: “Today was another rough day. I shall repent and be reborn as a pure, clean little blue supporter once again!!!!”

The accompanying image shows a blue cartoon character dressed in white robes like an angel or saint, complete with a halo and wings.

“파랭이” is a cute, playful Korean term for “a blue person.” In South Korean politics, blue is the symbolic color of the Democratic Party of Korea and the progressive camp, including supporters of Lee Jae-myung. In this context, it means becoming a clean, pure supporter of the blue political camp again.

The post is a form of self-deprecating humor following an online political argument. The person is essentially saying, “Today I got caught up in another round of heated arguments. I need to repent and become a pure blue supporter again,” using the saint-like image for comedic effect.

On October 11, 2026, South Korean President Lee Jae-myung quoted this post.

The message of his quote was that the essence of politics is to win the understanding, empathy, and consent of more citizens. Insulting people, mocking them, and spreading fake news on social media might feel satisfying in the moment, but in the eyes of the public, you have already lost.

True victory comes from making arguments and persuading others based on facts and with courtesy, using what is currently being called “좌아하게”—a playful expression blending the idea of being left-wing with being elegant or graceful.

He called on his supporters to work together to maintain a clean public-discussion space and directly cited the post about “repenting and being reborn as a pure blue supporter” as an example.

最近看到一个回测。有人从 2012 年开始，每年只做一件事，买入上一年度标普 500 涨幅最高的股票，持有一年，然后换成下一只冠军股。

据说这么做，100 美元最终变成了 17.6 万美元，整整 1760 倍。

2023 年的冠军是英伟达，2024 年又涨了约 180%；2024 年的冠军是 Palantir，全年涨了 341%，结果 2025 年又涨了 135%；2025 年冠军换成 Sandisk，全年涨了 559%，2026 年到 10 月初又翻了好几倍。

这让我想到一个问题，为什么我们总觉得一只股票涨了三五倍，就应该差不多到头了？

我感觉很多人，包括我自己，都容易低估一个产业的利润最终会向少数几家公司集中到什么程度。

英伟达如此，Palantir 也是如此。Sandisk 的上涨还叠加了存储周期和供需变化，商业逻辑各不相同，但它们都有一个共同点：当基本面不断超出预期时，市场需要反复修改对它们的定价。

很多人热衷于寻找下一个英伟达，觉得现在的英伟达已经太贵了。但过去几年，美股似乎一直在提醒我们，一家已经被所有人发现的公司，依然可能被严重低估。

当然，满仓追逐上一年的冠军股，风险也非常极端。尤其是这种漂亮得不像话的回测，必须仔细检查选股口径、成分股变动和最大回撤。

不过我感兴趣的也不是这套策略能不能复制。

我觉得它揭示了一个很有意思的市场错觉，我们太习惯用过去的涨幅来衡量一只股票未来的空间，却很少认真想过，市场究竟需要多长时间，才能真正理解一家公司的盈利上限。

不只是亚洲，

@0xJohannes_把他自己在欧洲官方经销商的实体店买的 Ledger 给拆了，
发现里面也有不属于原本 Ledger 的线材，
同样的，这个设备也通过了 Genuine Check 。

他个人认为这有可能是比较旧版本的植入物，新的版本可能藏在屏幕后面。
不过这台设备里面的钱并没有被盗。

不过，也有另一个 X 用户留言指出，
照片里的设备看起来只是旧版本的 Nano X，
Ledger 第 4 版硬件的电池用的是线材连接，不是弹簧触点。
他还分析真正的植入物需要有额外的硬件接到屏幕数据线上，而照片里看不到。

另外，又有人拆了另一台设备，是 Stax 型号。
据说植入板上有不属于原版的 Nordic nRF9151 蜂窝通信模块，和一根藏起来的天线。
这块植入物可支援 4G的网络，不需要另外靠手机或电脑就可以把数据传出去。
暂时还不知道这台设备来源，是欧洲还是亚洲。

Ledger 官网也说了，如果安全芯片没被动过，是无法检测到物理改装，所以通过 Genuine Check 并不代表 100 % 安全。

Ledger 暂时没有承认和否认欧洲的事件，
只是重申所有已确认的个案都来自 CryptoBilis 渠道，官网直销渠道并没有受影响。

text:
Have been diving deep down the quantum rabbit hole these past days, trying to wrap my head around the whole ecosystem both on the crypto side (PQ-secure assets) as well as on the equity side (quantum computing).

This thread will cover both landscapes.

Still very much in the process tho, so treat this as v0.1, the lists are not final, and if I'm missing a name or looking at something the wrong way, please tell me. CT hivemind > me alone.

Lets start with crypto: here's my map (mcap/FDV, 7d and 30d moves, distance from ATH):

1) Opt-in PQ on mainnet

- $NEAR ($7.6B, +15% 7d, +145% 30d, 72% off ATH):

The biggest chain where you can actually sign post-quantum today. Since the 2.13 upgrade on July 20th, any account can rotate to an ML-DSA-65 key with a single tx, same address, same assets. That works bc NEAR accounts were never tied to one key in the first place, which is exactly the design ETH and BTC wish they had right now. It's voluntary tho, so the number that matters is how many accounts actually rotate, and I haven't found it yet. NEAR also became the distribution layer for the whole theme, QTC trades on near(.)com. Just don't credit the full 30d move to quantum, intents and the issuance cut proposal are in there too.

→ DYOR: @nearprotocol

- $ALGO ($1.2B, flat 7d, +40% 30d, 96% off ATH):

The one I slept on. Algorand has the longest PQ track record of any major: Falcon-signed State Proofs since 2022, the first Falcon-authorised mainnet tx in Nov 2025, and since August native Falcon-1024 accounts, supported in Pera. You rekey an existing account and keep your address. What's not done is the chain itself: consensus still runs on classical keys, a PQ VRF paper is due early 2027 and "broad quantum resilience" is the goal for end of 2027. So your funds can be protected today, the network underneath not yet. Still further along than everything in section 3.

→ DYOR: @algorand

- $CKB ($82M mcap, $84M FDV, +26% 7d, +56% 30d, 96% off ATH):

Nervos has a structural edge here: the cell model lets any signature scheme live as a lock script, so adding a new one needs no fork. A SPHINCS+ lock is live on mainnet, audited, and usable through the Quantum Purse wallet. SPHINCS+ is hash-based, so CKB also sits on the right side of the Vitalik argument. Two caveats: the default lock is still secp256k1, so almost nobody is protected by default, and onchain demand is weak (~16.6K txs a day, no real DeFi TVL). Volume ran several times its normal level this week, that's the narrative trading, not the chain.

→ DYOR: @nervosnetwork

- $TSC ($26M, +8% 7d, flat 30d, 20% off ATH):

TensorCash is a weird one, in a good way. It's a Bitcoin Core fork where the proof of work is AI inference, miners run an open LLM and every answer comes with a proof. The quantum part: an ML-DSA-65 address type exists from block zero, opt-in. And the team is refreshingly honest that nobody has actually spent from one of those addresses yet. AI x PQ in one PoW coin is a fun combo, but volume sits on SafeTrade at under $100K a day. Watching, too early for more.

→ DYOR: @Tensorcash

2) PQ-native chains

- $QRL ($93M, +43% 7d, +71% 30d, 69% off ATH):

The OG. Live since 2018 and signing with XMSS from day one, a hash-based scheme, so security rests on hash functions only. That's the family Vitalik said he prefers in his October 7th post, which is a big part of why it caught a bid. The catch is what comes next: QRL 2.0 (Zond) moves to PoS and an EVM, and validators will sign with ML-DSA-87, a.k.a. lattice. So the chain people buy as the hash-based hedge is moving its consensus onto exactly the thing the hash crowd worries about. Zond is on testnet, audits were 50% done in June, mainnet date still TBD. And it's thin: ~$60K daily volume on a $93M cap.

→ DYOR: @QRLedger

- $QTC ($39M mcap, $801M FDV, +43% 7d, +187% 30d, 25% off ATH):

Quantus is a one-month-old PoW chain (mainnet 9 Sep) with ML-DSA signatures from block 0 and ZK privacy on top. Bitcoin-style 21M cap, Balaji led the last round, and it trades on near(.)com through NEAR Intents. The tech is real, but the price is a float story: only ~1.3% of the 21M cap circulates, so at the full cap you pay close to $3B for a chain with no measurable usage yet, and 27% of supply is a premine that starts unlocking in Sep 2027. It's also all-in on lattice, so it's the most exposed name if the AI-vs-lattice worry ever plays out.

→ DYOR: @QuantusNetwork

- $ABEL ($13M mcap, $20M FDV, +34% 7d, +37% 30d, 94% off ATH):

Abelian is basically the "what if Zcash, but quantum-safe" pitch: a PoW L1 with lattice-based crypto (built on Dilithium and Kyber per its own description) and a privacy coin where you choose the level, from full privacy to privacy with accountability. Post-quantum plus privacy in one asset is a combo almost nobody else has live yet. The problem is purely market structure: it trades on MEXC only, with a miniscule volume of around $20K a day. A few k moves the price, in both directions.

→ DYOR: @PQabelian

- $CELL ($2.6M, +25% 7d, +79% 30d, 99% off ATH):

Cellframe is a 2021-era L1 framework for building chains and services, with Falcon and Dilithium integrated and SPHINCS+ sitting in the SDK. It's 99% off ATH, so the market wrote it off long ago. What it does have is venues (Gate, MEXC, Pancake, Uniswap), which is probs why it's the micro cap that catches the bid whenever the narrative runs. I couldn't find any specific news behind the weekend pump tho, and for now I couldn't confirm from their docs which scheme is the default on mainnet either. So for me def a beta play until proven otherwise.

→ DYOR: @cellframenet

- $XNT ($1.5M, +119% 7d, +293% 30d, 37% off ATH):

Neptune Privacy is the purest hash-only story on the list: PoW, private by default, everything built on zk-STARKs and hash-based crypto, no lattice and no elliptic curves in the proofs. On paper that's the cleanest answer to Vitalik's argument. In practice tho, it's a community fork of Neptune Cash where the original cryptographers stayed with the other chain, while nobody (or at least not I) knows who actually runs XNT, and the codebase it inherited had two chain-level bugs within about six months. Given the low mcap and $50K daily volume, it's mostly a lottery ticket imo.

→ DYOR: @NeptunePrivacy

3) Announced, testnet or draft

- $BTC ($1.68T, -3% 7d, +8% 30d, 34% off ATH):

Bitcoin might be considered the reason this trade exists: most to lose, slowest to move. BIP-360 is the proposal everyone points to, a new output type that works like Taproot minus the key path, so your public key stays hidden while coins just sit there. That only covers the "long exposure" attack. The authors say themselves that it doesn't protect coins at the moment you spend, that needs actual PQ signatures. It's a draft, it needs a soft fork and there's no activation path. Meanwhile roughly 6.26M BTC sit in addresses with exposed pubkeys.

→ DYOR: BIP-360

- $ETH ($312B, -6% 7d, +1% 30d, 48% off ATH):

Ethereum deff has one of the most serious research efforts but also the longest timeline. Their own roadmap page says L1 upgrades "could be completed by 2029", and that migrating the execution layer (a.k.a. your wallet) takes years beyond that. Around ten client teams are already building post-quantum consensus clients in the meantime tho. So the work is real, but if you believe Drake's "months, not years" worst case, 2029 is not a comforting number. That gap between the roadmap and the fear is what's driving a lot of the other tokens on this list.

→ DYOR: pq(.)ethereum(.)org

- $TRX ($31.5B, -1% 7d, -2% 30d, 23% off ATH):

Probs the most underdiscussed one. Tron has been running PQ signatures on its public Nile testnet since 30 June, and not just for transactions: Falcon-512 and ML-DSA-44 for txs, block signing, node handshakes and smart contract verification. Mainnet needs a separate committee vote per scheme and wallets and exchanges on board first, no date. The cost is real, signatures are big enough to mean 10 to 30x more data per tx. But this is the biggest USDT chain out there, and it's the one name in this section the quantum bid hasn't touched at all.

→ DYOR: @trondao

- $ZEC ($22.2B, -2% 7d, +14% 30d, 59% off ATH):

Covered ZEC in the privacy post, so just the quantum bit: PQ signature opcodes are planned for January, hash-based, and only for the transparent side, where around 70% of supply still sits. The shielded pool needs its own separate migration. No activation date confirmed yet. Worth noting how fast that came together after the bunker mode week tho, the Zcash devs react quicker than most.

→ DYOR: @zcash

- $SUI ($4.6B mcap, $11.2B FDV, -9% 7d, +54% 30d, 79% off ATH):

The clearest dated plan among the majors. Native ML-DSA-65 accounts on testnet by end of 2026 and on mainnet in Q1 2027, plus hash-based vaults for cold storage this year. The part I like: you keep your address and the new key derives from the same seed phrase, so for the user it's a wallet update, not a migration. Nothing is live yet, audits are still running and the team itself calls the dates open. But if they hit Q1, Sui is one of the first majors with PQ accounts as a native feature.

→ DYOR: @SuiNetwork

- $STRK ($780M mcap, $1.05B FDV, +78% 7d, +260% 30d, 98% off ATH):

The leader of the trade, and the one where price is furthest ahead of facts. The base is legit: STARK proofs are hash-based already, and the roadmap swaps the remaining pieces (Pedersen hashes out, Falcon-512 consensus signatures in). The 2027 "first fully quantum-resistant network" target comes from Starknet's own posts. But the L1 move that sent it flying is something they're "actively considering", not something that can be taken as a fact. And the last phase depends on Ethereum's own PQ transition as long as it stays an L2. A 3.6x month prices in a lot of that.

→ DYOR: @Starknet

- $APT ($769M mcap, $1.07B FDV, +8% 7d, +44% 30d, 96% off ATH):

Aptos picked the most conservative option on the menu: SLH-DSA, pure hash-based, big signatures but no lattice assumptions. AIP-137 is accepted, so the design is settled. The honest part is in the proposal itself, which says there is "no urgency to deploy this on any of the networks" over the next year. So think of it as a fire extinguisher on the wall: ready when needed, not a catalyst with a specific date for now.

→ DYOR: @Aptos_Network

- $XTZ ($356M, -4% 7d, +26% 30d, 96% off ATH):

Funnily, Tezos did something nobody else has: it stood up a full post-quantum chain on a testnet (Quantumnet, 24 Sep). Not just accounts with ML-DSA-44, also hash-based block attestations aggregated with STARKs and a new data availability scheme. They even left their private transactions out bc those aren't quantum-safe. The devs are explicit that this is not a preview of a mainnet upgrade, each piece has to go through governance separately. Then again, Tezos governance actually ships upgrades, so I wouldn't dismiss it.

→ DYOR: @tezos

- $MON ($306M mcap, $2.6B FDV, -21% 7d, +10% 30d, 47% off ATH):

Disclosure, I'm long. Monad published its PQ roadmap on 28 Sep, nine days before bunker mode made it fashionable. Step one is about user funds: accounts add a quantum-resistant key and retire the old one while keeping the same address, so nobody has to move anything. A PQ version of the consensus is in development in parallel. All of it is design, none of it is live, and there's a major unlock on 24 Nov. The bet is simply that STRK did a 3.6x month on a similar-stage roadmap while MON is down 21% on the week.

→ DYOR: @monad

4) PQ vaults and infra

- $QONE ($0.5M mcap, $3.8M FDV, -8% 7d, -19% 30d, 29% off ATH):

Might be one for the Hyperliquid maxis. qVAULT is a non-custodial vault on HyperEVM that puts a second, Falcon-based signature on top of your normal wallet key, and afaik it's the only way to hold HYPE behind a PQ signature today. It only protects what's inside the vault tho, HyperEVM accounts themselves stay ECDSA. The product is more interesting than the token for now tho: half a million mcap, barely trades, and down while the sector ran.

→ DYOR: @qlabsofficial

- $NAORIS ($18M mcap, $120M FDV, -10% 7d, -15% 30d, 82% off ATH):

Naoris pitches a decentralised cybersecurity mesh for enterprises and governments, running on its own post-quantum L1 that went to mainnet on 1 April, invite-only for now still tho. What bugs me a bit is: everything I read says "NIST-approved cryptography" without ever naming the schemes specifically. For a project whose entire product is PQ security, that's the first thing I'd want spelled out. It's also bleeding in the hottest quantum month so far, with 85% of supply not circulating yet.

→ DYOR: @NaorisProtocol

- $QANX ($20M mcap, $25M FDV, -6% 7d, -5% 30d, 94% off ATH):

QANplatform is an EVM-compatible L1 aimed at enterprises. The idea is neat: a cross-signer that attaches a Dilithium signature to your normal EVM transaction, so you keep your wallet and still get PQ protection. But it has been testnet-only for a long time, mainnet is still not live, and the token didn't move while everything with quantum in the name ran. Might be the market telling you what it thinks about the timeline.

→ DYOR: @QANplatform

5) Narrative beta

- $ZK ($173M mcap, $336M FDV, +25% 7d, +66% 30d, 95% off ATH):

Disclosure, long this one too, but I'm putting it here on purpose. ZKsync's Airbender prover is STARK-based, so the "post-quantum by design" line is true for that layer. But the proof gets wrapped in a pairing-based SNARK before it lands on Ethereum, and accounts are plain ECDSA. Neither of those is quantum-safe, and there's no dated roadmap to fix them. So it's a catalyst trade around the 10/21 teaser, not a proper PQ thesis (yet). If that announcement covers the wrapper and signatures, it moves up a section.

→ DYOR: @zksync

- $AZTEC ($59M mcap, $205M FDV, +15% 7d, +39% 30d, 50% off ATH):

Aztec sits here for now, but it's the one in this section most likely to move up. Today its privacy runs on elliptic-curve based proofs, so nothing about it is post-quantum yet. But Zac said on the 9th of October that an Aztec-specific security post and roadmap covering the AI and quantum threats is coming, spent the weekend at a post-quantum cryptography conference, and confirmed a security and roadmap update for this week. He also called bunker mode hyperbolic and warned against rushing into untested crypto, so I'd expect a careful plan rather than a flashy one. With V6 heading to mainnet at the same time, that post is the next main catalyst to watch.

→ DYOR: @aztecnetwork

That's the token side. Equities in the next post.

Again: not final, still digging. What am I missing, and where am I wrong?

1/2

text:
Now the equities side of the quantum trade. Same theme, completely different angle and market situation.

While the PQ tokens ripped over the last two weeks tho, the quantum computing stocks kept bleeding ($IONQ -12%, $QBTS -16%, $INFQ -24% from 25th of Sep to 9th of Oct).

Also, same disclaimer as before: v0.1, still researching, so pls tell me what I'm missing.

Numbers are 9 Oct closes: mkt cap, mkt cap / trailing sales, 1 month move, distance from 52w high.

1) Pure-play hardware

- $IONQ ($15.9B, 64x sales, +8% 1m, 53% off high):

The biggest and most liquid pure play, building trapped-ion machines. $80M revenue last quarter (+287% y/y), $3B in cash, and the only pure play selected for Stage C of DARPA's quantum program. For crypto people it's the most relevant name: IonQ co-authored the September estimate that breaking Bitcoin's curve would take ~19,400 physical qubits and ~26 days per attempt on its architecture, while saying clearly that no such machine exists. The flags: a lot of the growth is acquired, there's a short report from February, and insiders sold ~$450M of stock over two years. And it fell on the days the DARPA news came out, which tells you what this market cares about right now.

- $QNT ($10.9B, 473x sales, -15% 1m, 52% off high):

Quantinuum, the Honeywell spin-out, and on the numbers the technical leader: its Helios machine has the best published gate fidelity (99.92% on 98 qubits). It IPO'd in June at $60 and trades at ~$41 now, so everyone who bought the IPO is down 31%. You pay 473x sales on $23M of revenue for the best tech, with $2.1B of cash behind it. The near-term issue is supply: the IPO lock-up is reported to expire around December 1st, and Honeywell still holds ~48% of the votes.

- $QBTS ($5.4B, 437x sales, -13% 1m, 69% off high):

D-Wave is the odd one out. It sells quantum annealers, which are real machines with real customers, but annealing can't run Shor's algorithm, so it's irrelevant for the "breaks crypto" question. Revenue has been flat at ~$3M a quarter, and its own gate-model roadmap only reaches 10 logical qubits in 2030. At 437x sales you're paying a quantum multiple for a business that isn't growing rn.

- $RGTI ($4.7B, 351x sales, -8% 1m, 76% off high):

Rigetti builds superconducting chips, same approach as IBM and Google but without their budget. The newest 108-qubit system runs at ~99.1% two-qubit fidelity, which is behind the ion-trap guys. $13M of trailing revenue against a $4.7B cap, but $541M of cash and no debt, so it has years of runway. Pure high-beta narrative stock, moves hardest in both directions.

- $INFQ ($2.5B, 59x sales, -15% 1m, 48% off high):

Infleqtion is the one that looks most like an actual business. Neutral-atom computers plus quantum sensing (clocks, navigation), and the sensing side sells to defense customers today: $42M trailing revenue, +116% last quarter, cheapest multiple in the group. It also claimed 30 logical qubits on 80 physical ones in September, tho without publishing an error rate. Came public via SPAC in February, so keep an eye on the share supply.

- $QUBT ($1.7B, 171x sales, -5% 1m, 69% off high):

Quantum Computing Inc is basically a cash box with a call option attached. It raised a ton of equity near the highs, and ~77% of the market cap is cash now. The revenue ($9.8M) mostly comes from companies it bought this year, and the photonic chip foundry is the least proven product on this list. Downside is cushioned by the cash, upside needs the tech to show up.

- $XNDU ($1.2B, 164x sales, -57% 1m, 91% off high):

Xanadu is the cautionary tale. Photonic approach, respected research team, listed via SPAC in March. Then ~294M shares got registered for resale in May and the stock never recovered, it's down 91% from the high. Nothing broke in the tech. It's just what happens when supply hits a story stock, and it's the scenario to keep in mind for every lock-up on this list.

2) PQC security

- $LAES ($487M, 20x sales, 76% off high):

SEALSQ sells post-quantum secure chips, so it's the closest thing in equities to a direct play on the PQ migration (somebody has to make the hardware that runs the new signatures). $25M trailing revenue at 20x sales, which looks almost reasonable next to the hardware names, but it's loss-making and the PQC chip cycle is a multi-year story.

- $ARQQ ($286M, 262x sales, 72% off high):

Arqit does quantum-safe encryption software. The problem is one number: ~$1.1M of trailing revenue. 262x sales for a company that small is mainly a story, not a business yet.

3) Big tech programs

- $IBM ($214B):

The most concrete roadmap in the industry and the one to track for Q-day timing. The target is Starling in 2029 with 200 logical qubits. For context, the latest estimates for breaking 256-bit elliptic curves need roughly 1,200 to 1,450 logical qubits, so even an on-time Starling is an order of magnitude short. Also in DARPA Stage C. Earnings 21 Oct, developer conference 11 to 13 Nov, where they like to show new chips.

- $GOOGL ($4.3T):

Google's Willow chip (105 qubits) was the first to show error correction actually getting better as you scale up, which was the open question for the whole field. And a Google-led paper this March is the one that cut the estimate for breaking ECC-256 to under 500K physical qubits, which kicked off a lot of the current panic. Most important lab for the thesis, zero impact on the stock.

- $MSFT ($3.97T):

Microsoft bets on topological qubits, a totally different approach that would be far more stable if it works. Whether it works is openly disputed tho, plenty of physicists don't buy that the Majorana results show what Microsoft says they show. High-risk, high-reward science project inside a $4T company. Also in DARPA Stage C.

- $AMZN ($2.83T):

Amazon mostly rents out other people's quantum computers through Braket, and has its own Ocelot chip in the lab. It's the picks-and-shovels cloud angle, and a rounding error in the valuation.

- $NVDA ($5.54T):

Nvidia doesn't build qubits at all. It sells the classical side: quantum computers need a lot of classical compute next to them for control and error correction, and CUDA-Q is Nvidia's software layer for exactly that. If hybrid quantum-classical is how this plays out, they win regardless of which qubit type does.

4) Owners and foundries

- $HON ($65.8B):

Honeywell still holds ~48% of Quantinuum's voting power after the IPO. So it's the diluted, boring way to own the technical leader, inside an industrial conglomerate.

- $GFS ($26.5B, 3.8x sales):

GlobalFoundries is the fab angle. A real chip business at a normal multiple, with a reported CHIPS Act quantum award behind it. Quantum is optionality here, not the reason to own it.

5) Software

- $HQ ($0.9B):

Horizon Quantum builds software tools that are meant to work across hardware types. Listed via SPAC in March, and I couldn't get clean revenue numbers, so there's too little data for me to have a view yet.

6) ETF

- QTUM ($5.7B AUM, 0.40% fee):

The lazy option. But look at the holdings before you call it a quantum bet, most of it is semis and cloud names, so the quantum exposure is pretty diluted by all the other stuff.

NFA tho. DYOR.

2/2

quoted_text:
While half of CT was partying in Singapore, the rest of the timeline was arguing about whether the math behind our crypto wallets could break within months.

Not (just) because of quantum computers, but also AI's rapidly increasing capabilities.

The initial warning came from one of Ethereum's lead researchers on Wednesday.

If he's right, 6.26M BTC might be first in line to be compromised. That's 31.2% of supply, and >$500B in dollar terms, sitting in addresses with exposed keys.

However, it's important to understand that nobody has broken anything so far. But the debate around the threat vector is already moving prices and roadmaps.

Missed what's happening?

Let me explain:

Your wallet is protected by a signature scheme called ECDSA.

It rests on one assumption: nobody can work backwards from your public key to your private key.

We've known since the 90s that a large enough quantum computer breaks that assumption. The comfort was always that such a machine is still years away. 

Hence, Ethereum plans to be quantum-safe around 2029. Bitcoin (so far) has no date at all.

That was the whole debate until Tuesday.

What changed?

On the 6th of October, OpenAI published 722 math papers written by an unreleased internal model. Not all of it is verified yet, but it was enough to rattle people who do math for a living.

A day later @drakefjustin, one of the Ethereum Foundation's lead researchers, wrote:

"It is now reasonable to brace for the possibility that ECDSA breaks before qday, in the worst case in months not years."

His logic: if AI can suddenly do decades of math in weeks, it might also find a shortcut that cracks wallet keys on normal hardware. No quantum computer even needed.

So he asked the industry to plan for "bunker mode". Meaning: move funds, starting with the biggest holders, to fresh addresses that have never sent a transaction.

Why fresh addresses?

Because until you spend from an address, the chain only shows a scrambled fingerprint of your public key, so there is nothing to attack.

The moment you sign a transaction, the key is public forever.

That's where the 6.26M BTC figure comes from (based on @glassnode data). Binance's cold storage is 83% exposed. Robinhood's is 100%. On Solana, every address is a public key by design.

But the most important question is: Is he right?

And the answer here might be more nuanced.

Because (as mentioned before), nobody has broken anything yet. So there is no proof.

Meanwhile, most cryptographers pushed back hard. Coinbase's head of cryptography called it "the very definition of FUD", with Ledger's CTO (not sure if that's gud or bad tho lol) and Adam Back saying the same. 

The @aztecnetwork co-founder @Zac_Aztec called it "hyperbolic" and warned that the worst reaction would be rushing into newer, less tested cryptography too quickly.

@VitalikButerin landed somewhere in the middle, (re)enforcing the point to NOT scramble to move funds today, but still take AI-driven math seriously.

Then he said the part that I personally think matters the most:

Chains have roughly two families of "post-quantum" signatures to switch to.

- Lattice-based (ML-DSA, Falcon). Compact, fast, the official standard. But built on structured math, a bit like the curves we use today.

- Hash-based (SPHINCS, XMSS). Relies on nothing but a hash function, the simplest building block we have. The catch: signatures get 30 to 120 times bigger.

Vitalik's point: if the fear is AI finding hidden structure in math, lattices are exposed to that same fear. In his view only hash-based holds up against both a quantum computer and an AI shortcut.

Okay. 

Now, let's have a look at who is doing what:

- Lattices: @NEARProtocol (live since July), Algorand, Quantus, Sui (planned), Monad (draft)

- Hash-based: Ethereum's roadmap, QRL, Zcash (targeting January), and the STARK proofs under @Starknet 

Based on Vitalik's point of view (which is not consensus btw), a chain can hence be safe against quantum computers but still sit in the group he worries about.

Zac (the above-mentioned Aztec founder) counters this, pointing out that nobody actually knows that hashes are safer from AI than curves. It's an assumption rather than a fact.

But enough about the tech side. 

Because the market (as you might have noticed) reacted too, and as so often, it bought the loudest story:

- $STRK is up 65% in a week. The catalyst was Starknet saying it is "actively considering becoming an L1" to be fully quantum-resistant by 2027. There is no proposal and no vote yet.

- $QRL, hash-based since 2018, is up 41%.

- $NEAR, which actually has post-quantum signing live on mainnet, is up 12%.

- BTC, ETH and ZEC are all down.

Announcements got paid more than shipped code tho for now.

My take:

ECDSA is most likely not breaking next month, and this week may well look like FUD in hindsight.

But every chain now has to answer how fast it can swap its cryptography if it has to. Chains where you can rotate keys without changing your address (like NEAR, @SuiNetwork, @Algorand and Starknet) have the easy path. Bitcoin, with no agreed plan and a third of supply exposed, has the hardest one.

If you want to be on the safe side, keep long-term holdings in addresses that have never signed a transaction, but don't rush it and fuck up along the way.

Some of the next things I'll watch: Aztec's security roadmap, whether or not Starknet actually migrates to an L1, and whatever comes out of the Ethereum researchers' meeting that runs through Monday.

NFA tho. DYOR.

AXIS对标传统市场的上市公司怎么估值。

@axisrobotics 业务的本质是解决机器人AI训练的数据瓶颈（Data Bottleneck），虽然没有一模一样的公司，但其业务估值主要可以拆成三个部分来看，众包模式+物理AI定位+仿真基础设施。

核心业务同类：众包模式

在传统 AI 领域，这种“靠全球网络/众包来收集和标注数据”的业务早就诞生了上市公司，比如澳股上市的Appen，全球最大的 AI 数据众包和标注平台之一。它拥有一个数百万人的全球远程工作者网络，帮微软、谷歌等巨头标注语音、图像和文本数据，由于传统 Web2 数据外包业务受大模型自研影响，其市值较几年前的高点大幅缩水，目前正在转型拓展中国等新兴市场，目前估值2亿美元。

暂未上市的超级独角兽 Scale AI ，作为行业标杆，虽然尚未正式 IPO，但它是最典型的 AI 数据标注基础设施，近期估值已达数百亿美元，它也开始大规模涉足自动驾驶与机器人仿真数据的生成，当然140亿的估值里有一部分可能是为了挖人给的溢价。

技术/产业同类：物理 AI 感知与仿真基础设施

ouster作为物理 AI 基础层硬件与感知软件的代表，过去一年其市值随物理 AI 概念升温增长了超过 60%，目前30亿美元估值。

Unity Software作为仿真引擎与虚拟环境巨头约 85 亿至 90 亿美元估值。

下游服务的应用：具身智能与机器人

这个行业作为热门赛道，估值泡沫是比较大的，比如优必选46 亿美元，Symbotic 57 亿美元，等等，当然这也意味着这行业是有钱付给数据供应商的，所以AXIS业务做好了也有机会水涨船高。

text:
In a utopian world, you don't need solution engineers.

The products you have is so simple and scalable that everyone can just integrate it in one click. You could even argue that having solution engs shows there's a gap in your product suite.

However, the interesting thing with protocols such as Morpho is that their raw capabilities far exceed what people want or what is easy to do now.

So you have a very long lead time during which you figure it out what actually the products are that are worth making based on market trends, what you think people truly want & what people ask (often they dont really know what they need exactly).

So you actually, need incredible solution engineers to identify repeated patterns, bridge the integrators' needs with existing products, while forwarding the integrators' true requirements to an incredible product team that must figure out what truly is worth building and how.

This is no simple task in practice and actually take a lot of effort from every team members: often pushing back on what the integrators or BDs wish. Which is uncomfortable and does not please everyone. This is the price to pay to create a truly safe and scalable network I guess.

We're learning a lot these days, especially as Midnight open an even larger design space VS Blue. But understanding how to collect the true requirements, feed that to the team, build only the relevant & scalable products and repeat that process until we onboard all types of loans on Midnight will be a gigantic accelerator to bring the trillions of loans onchain.

I want to clear a few things up, because two very different stories are getting blended together.

First, the card dashboard incident from Oct 5 is real. Someone accessed cardholder KYC data, and we take that seriously. It's right that people are talking about it. Funds were safe, and affected users have been notified. If you hold a Based card, please stay vigilant, as phishing attempts may use your real details. We will only contact you through in-app support. Any DM on X or Telegram claiming to be Based support is a scam.

The AI dashboard story being reshared alongside it is a separate incident from back in March.

That one was discovered by one of our die-hard users, who was always digging through our site to see what we were building next. It was an internal OpenClaw dashboard the team was experimenting with. It was never public-facing or launched. He flagged it, we shut it down, rotated the keys, and thanked him for catching it. The keys were for our internal AI gateway with usage caps. Card dashboard was kept separate.

We recognize that even internal experiments need to be handled with the right level of care. We appreciate the user who brought it to our attention, and we take these situations as opportunities to improve.

-
We've been through similar situations before, and each time, we've tried to clarify what happened. We understand that trust takes time to build, and people have every right to ask questions and expect clear answers from us.

What makes these situations difficult is that even after the facts are clarified, the original posts often continue to circulate while the follow-up receives much less attention. We hope to get the full context across this time, and we'll continue to be open and clear whenever concerns arise.

-
I also want to share a bit about how we've grown and where we're headed.

Based has been listed in Hyperliquid's docs since the early days, and we're proud to be featured on their site. But our growth hasn't come from the docs alone. Builder Codes were designed to help teams bring new users into Hyperliquid, and that's what we've focused on: introducing people to the ecosystem who might not otherwise have joined.

We're continuing to explore new ways to grow across Web2 and Web3, including community-led initiatives and UGC. Our goal is to keep bringing new users into the ecosystem while building products that give them more reasons to stay.

We know trust is earned through actions, not words. We'll keep listening, improving, and building.

AI agents can only help you if they know about you. And what they know is your data.

So who moves it, and who decides? That was the question at Builder Nights Seoul with @MetaMask, @lfdecentralized and @0xTicker.

@juliangordonhk8 opened on who is already building this. LF Decentralized Trust counts ten central banks among its members, including the Bank of Korea. It also hosts the standard Vana wrote for how personal data moves.

On the first panel, @francescoswiss and the MetaMask team talked about agents moving from trading to doing everyday things for you. For that, an agent needs your data, and you need to stay in charge of it.

On the second, @sheila_warren and the panel made a harder point. Regulators everywhere are talking about digital public infrastructure and decentralization. It’s a natural fit for Web3, but very few Web3 projects are in the room.

Web3 doesn’t need to invent new use cases. It needs to meet the ones that already exist.

Which projects do you see showing up for this work?

author: ccatalini
quoted_text:
i often hear people talk about RL as if it’s just “an algorithm” which might or might not be the “right one” and speculate that we might “find a better one”

the issue with this is that all algorithms have some implicit goal of “solving a problem” or “improving an objective” and RL is just what pops out when you take the gradient for your objective

if you’re doing any algorithm other than RL, you are giving up on optimizing your on your ultimate objective directly and leaning on a proxy instead. this is often useful, because your objective might be imprecise, and you might have access to some teacher signal (a static dataset, a teacher model, process evaluation) which trades off unbiased optimization for robustness or reducing sampling costs. but if what you care about can be made explicit, there aren’t any shortcuts. policy gradients are minimum variance unbiased estimators for progress.

text:
Bessis 今天写了十条关于 AI 和数学的判断，我最认同其中一句：数学的产物是清晰和理解。

一道难题被证明了，当然值得庆祝。但数学研究真正珍贵的部分，还有人们如何理解这个证明、从中发现新的联系，以及由此提出下一代问题。

我觉得更值得警惕的是，数学正在变成 AI 公司展示模型能力的竞技场。一个学科几代人积累的开放问题，在模型竞赛里成了可以批量攻克的 benchmark。模型公司获得了耀眼的成绩单，验证和理解这些成果的成本，却被留给了整个学术共同体。

而且这种成本很难量化。一个年轻数学家原本可以花五年探索自己的方向，现在却可能不得不先搞清楚，某个闭源模型生成的几百页证明，究竟有没有提前终结他的研究。

AI 改变数学已经没有太大悬念了，未来真正稀缺的会是理解。

当我们拥有生产海量新知识的能力，却没有同等的能力去消化它们，人类究竟是在加速科学，还是在不断积累自己都无法理解的答案？
author: sleepy0x13
quoted_text:
10 remarks on AI and math that can be true all at once:
1. The recent progress is stunning and exciting.
2. The Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis is arguably Fields-medal level.
3. Mathematics is being transformed and there is no way back.
4. OpenAI doesn't give a fuck about the future of mathematics.
5. Half-baked unreadable preprints claiming major results can effectively stall mathematical progress.
6. Some mathematicians are responding with naive, overly defensive comments.
7. The social-media wankers framing this as "OpenAI tramples gatekeeping" have no experience of mathematical research.
8. The product of mathematics is clarity and understanding. Not theorems, by themselves.
9. Mathematics is a critical infrastructure of human cognition. The human need for understanding isn't obsolete and it can't be offloaded to machines.
10. We haven't "solved" mathematics and we won't get there before the Sun burns out.

text:
曾经叱咤风云的“财经女侠”叶檀，最近做客了 币安会客厅。

这位复旦历史系博士出身、曾因高强度创业打拼而罹患乳腺癌晚期的硬核媒体人，在经历了生死考验和与生命和解后，对财富、投资和人性的理解变得极其通透。

在对话节目中，她给出了几条非常适合当下浮躁市场的清醒建议，无论是在加密市场还是传统市场，小编觉得都很适用：

1. 投资的第一性原理：小范围试错，但“试”不过三
永远不要做自己能力边界之外的投资。
进入新领域时，先小范围试错；如果连错三次，就说明这条路（或者这个赛道）根本不适合你，及时认怂止损。

2. 不懂没关系，但要找对人和研究对
要么你自己下苦功夫去深度研究，要么你能找到真正靠谱的人带路。
如果这两点你都不具备就盲目下场，那根本不叫投资，而是纯赌。
可能赢，但并不可取。
这点加密市场更明显，要么整合社媒和链上数据的所有公开信息来做分析，要么，你能混进核心圈。
i 人和 e 人各有出路，但就怕纯赌。

3. 摒弃买房投资
在当下的宏观周期里，房地产已经不再是单纯的投资品种，而是变成了“生活的必需消费品”，是提供安全感的“人生活的壳”。
买不买房，完全取决于你个人的生活需要和擅长领域，而不是指望它暴涨。

4.财富的终局是“内心的舒适”
早年为了公司狂飙突进，叶檀曾完全失去了生活；如今病后重生，她认为成功根本没有统一的世俗标准，关键在于“自己觉得舒适”。

在财富、经济和人性之间取得均衡，远比单纯追逐账户里不断跳动的数字更重要。

这个观点其实和最近孙哥在 Alan 播客里提到的思路是类似的，财富自由，其实是先获得心灵自由再谈财富，后者只是你达到自由状态的一种佐证和回报。

5. 敬畏市场，更要敬畏无常
在交易中，市场永远是对的。
而在生活中，意外不知道什么时候就会降临，“过好当下的每一天”才是对抗无常的唯一解法。

关于这一点，小编觉得如果生过病，或者经历过一些变故，更能体会。

经历过大起大落和生死关头的人，哪怕你不能感同身受，讲出的话也多少值得一听。

text:
🏰 The Network Fortress and the Paradox of Fake Decentralization 🏰

Imagine a kingdom proudly declaring that every citizen has the right to participate in the national governing council. The promise sounds incredibly democratic. However, a hidden law mandates that to enter the meeting room, each citizen must purchase a highly expensive, gold plated carriage with their own money. Ultimately, only the elite and the wealthiest families can afford to participate. That kingdom is absolutely not decentralized. It is simply an authoritarian regime disguised under the veil of democracy.

That is exactly the paradox currently playing out in the effort to scale modern Web3 infrastructure.

🔥 The Hidden Bandwidth Costs Killing Independent Nodes

We often measure decentralization by counting the number of validators on the network. But as transaction throughput increases, the legacy Gossipsub protocol begins to reveal its brutal inefficiency. It forces nodes to constantly download and rebroadcast massive amounts of redundant data packets.

This creates a silent financial burden. The monthly cost of maintaining high speed bandwidth and dedicated servers becomes completely overwhelming for independent solo operators. They are forced to shut down their machines and leave the ecosystem. Network power gradually consolidates into the hands of a few massive financial institutions that own gigantic data centers. When infrastructure demands excessively high maintenance costs, decentralization automatically collapses from the inside.

⚙️ Democratizing Infrastructure with Algorithms

This is exactly where Optimum executes a vital architectural intervention. By deploying Random Linear Network Coding, Optimum is not merely making the network technically faster. This platform is directly slashing a massive amount of redundant data circulating on the propagation layer.

Instead of requiring validators to constantly upgrade to wildly expensive server racks just to keep up with network speeds, the mump2p protocol compresses the entire message payload into lean algebraic equations. The hardware workload is minimized to the absolute limit, allowing the data stream to move smoother and lighter than ever before.

💡 The Core Vision of Network Power

The profound analytical lesson here is that protecting decentralization is not a philosophical debate. It is strictly a hardware cost optimization problem.

By completely resolving the bandwidth bottleneck, Optimum is actively shattering the financial wall that blocks out independent retail validators. They prove that the ecosystem does not need to force participants to buy massive infrastructure just to secure the blockchain. A truly decentralized system is one where superior mathematical engineering carries the physical heavy lifting on behalf of the user.

text:
Powerful quantum computers could pose a serious risk.

And preparing the world's infrastructure for quantum attacks will take longer than most people expect.

I came across this breakdown from @PaloAltoNtwks, and it got me thinking about how many systems we'd actually need to upgrade.

We're talking about:

→ Payment systems
→ Digital identities and authentication
→ Software updates and security checks
→ Older connected devices that may be difficult to update

With so much infrastructure to upgrade, I can see why NIST isn't waiting around. It finalized its first three quantum-resistant cryptography standards in 2024 and is already urging organizations to adopt them.

There's another concern, too.

Encrypted data stolen today could become readable years later, once quantum computers become powerful enough.

Lots of ground to cover, so best start early if you ask me.

We were able to fine tune an open weight model (Qwen3.5-9B) on proprietary internal data at @coinbase, and it out performed frontier models, at much lower cost and speed, for a specialized task (fraud prevention in this case).

I think we'll see more of this pattern inside companies. The frontier models are amazing generalists. But increasingly you'll see specialist models out perform on more narrow tasks, either working on teams, or by themselves.

We're making it easy to fine tune models internally for our employees. We even have a skill for it in our internal harness that makes it easy to spin these up and start training them:

"/fine-tune-and-serve-llm I want to fine-tune Qwen for payments risk review. help me get started"

I imagine we'll have some backend services that could be replaced entirely by this new architecture.

这篇我很推荐，尤其是现在做科研的人。

作者 Pierre Marion 提了一个很有意思的判断。LLM 如果真的把算公式、写代码、搜文献、做实验这些环节加速 10 倍甚至 100 倍，科研里最稀缺的东西会慢慢转向选什么问题、怎么建模、以及怎么判断结果有没有价值。

更值得警惕的是，AI 省下来的时间如果只是拿去发更多论文，最后很可能只是把 publish-or-perish 加速到失控。作者甚至直接判断，以论文数量和 h-index 为核心的评价体系正在失效。

作者最后给的方向是让 AI 扩大探索空间，把人的时间留给判断、品味、理解和培养下一代研究者。

以后科研能力可能像「你会不会驾驭一支极快的 AI 研究团队」，而不是一个人能亲手完成多少步骤。

text:
Oct Fed hike probability collapsed from 70% to 20%; Dec still ~80%

The probability of an October rate hike has collapsed from 70% to 20% following "dovish-hike" comments from Fed Vice Chair Jefferson and NY Fed President Williams, both signaling a case for hike deferral. That's per Edward K. Tom at @Cboe as of October 5, 2026.

But the December hike probability remains around 80%. Fed Funds futures aren't pricing a moderation or reversal of the tightening bias. They're pricing a delay. Tom puts it plainly: any shift in Fed path policy is "more about the timing of the next rate hike, rather than a moderation or reversal of the tightening bias."

That distinction matters for reading the vol response. VIX closed at 15.3, correlation at 8.0, and skew at 7th percentile lows. Equity markets treated near-term hike repricing as relief. The forward policy path is still tight.

The cross-asset vol table shows where rate uncertainty is showing up. $TLT and $IEF 1M implied vols sit at the 98th percentile of their 1-year range. $RTY implied-realized spread is at the 89th percentile. 

The rate vol signal is loud even as equity vol stayed contained.

text:
Hi @isaiah_p_taylor , some advice from someone who has been in many lawsuits (as plaintiff and defendant) and never lost a lawsuit and raised a lot less VC money than you but still some large rounds. 

- your biggest mistake wasn't taking Day One money, if you hadn't you'd be dead, so stop thinking it was
- your biggest mistake was initiating the lawsuit instead of letting any legal threats exhaust themselves. Defendants have huge advantage and a judge is not going to grant you declaratory relief. 
- You will lose @ the Summary Judgement stage and it will provide the clear body of evidence and judgement basis for Day One to win a final crushing blow, that gets them their ability to exercise pro rata.
- Given this is the case, you should just strike a deal now when the outcome is unclear and both sides can then come out congratulating each other rather than antagonising each other. 
- No matter how BAD you guys make each other look, there's ALWAYS room to take it all back and make each other look great - if you notice, @mashadrokova is clearly giving room for this in her messaging, she clearly wants you to win and doesn't like making you look bad.
- You should understand her fiduciary duty and obligation is to exercise this right that she paid for, she probably thinks your company is going to IPO for 20-30B and she doesn't want to reduce % ownership.
- Your second biggest mistake was airing this dispute on X, because now 50%+ of ppl are questioning whether you're a man of your word. 

Disputes that get made public suck because people get entrenched into their antagonistic positions of the opponents and think in negative sum mindset rather than positive sum capitalistic value creation mindset.

I've been there before & rooting for the best for you dude.

quoted_text:
here's how to make a cozy fishing game solo with Claude Opus 5.5 + Blender + 3D AI + Unity 6...

the trick is giving every tool one job, but there's a smart way to set it up:

- step 1: generate every 3D model with Tripo Smart Mesh P2: palms, rocks, the pier, the boat, the hut, the character
- step 2: connect Claude Code to Blender through MCP
- step 3: Opus 5.5 sets up each model in Blender: scale, pivots, materials, clean export
- step 4: Opus animates in Blender too: the character's walk, the cast, the rod, the boat on the water
- step 5: bring everything into Unity 6 and build the world: forest, river, waterfall, beach, pier
- step 6: add the systems one at a time: walking, fishing, bait choice, a time of day
- step 7: play it after every step and fix one thing at a time

who does what:
> Tripo: the 3D models
> Opus 5.5 + Blender: setup and animation
> Unity 6: the world and the game

one person, one stack, one game you'd actually want to play

text:
Big step forward for DATA today. Sui Foundation is making a $30M strategic investment in the network, which makes it DATA's largest holder, above both the DATA Foundation and PIP Labs.

Every asset that became valuable at scale eventually got a system of record, from land titles to share registers. Data is becoming the asset that decides how good AI gets, and it still has none. Most of what models are trained on today carries no proof of where it came from or whether the people behind it ever agreed to share it.

Trace is that system of record, with 275M+ data receipts registered since June. On Sui it can go further. Walrus and Seal let Trace keep an encrypted reference copy of the original data and control who can access it, so every record can be checked against the data itself. That is the foundation for a world where AI training data can be owned and licensed like any other asset, with the people who create it sharing in the value.

I'm also joining Sui Foundation as Strategic Advisor to help build that future across the Sui stack.

Excited for what we build together.

Today we’re launching Blobs - a new page to follow Ethereum blob activity in real time! 

Blobs also replaces DABEAT, which we’re sunsetting because @ethereum has plenty of unused blob capacity, and that capacity will only keep growing. We explain the decision in more detail in the article linked below.
author: l2beat

text:
So why are we sunsetting DABEAT?

For a project to benefit from the security of an alt-DA layer, Ethereum needs to verify that layer's attestations. Of the 38 projects posting data outside Ethereum, only three currently verify these attestations on Ethereum: @Celo, Lens @LC, and @Sophon.

We also believe Ethereum can support the growing data demand, especially as PeerDAS allows blob capacity to scale further.

Going forward, we'll focus our assessments on what Ethereum can enforce: whether a DA verifier is integrated, who controls its upgrades, and who can relay attestations. This also means validiums and optimiums can reach Stage 1 at most.

We've explained the full reasoning here: https://t.co/2JkBeobzVJ

text:
我发现一个问题，

我这样的人，很容易一不小心把每天过成一样的

我国庆后请了十几天年假，自从5号早上到省图去，已经持续八天了，每天都是早上一碗热干面豆浆、一瓶水，下午一瓶水，坐一天。上午做一整套卷子，中午复盘标错因，下午背书，晚上出去胡吃一顿，11点前准时睡觉。

上班快10年，休个假居然又把每天过成一样的了。其实我刚上班前两年，每天早上都是吃食堂的热干面，我们单位食堂就跟自助一样，东西很多，但我只吃热干面、豆浆。后来是同事发现了，然后我就改成了玉米、包子、蛋挞、豆浆，这样又持续了好几年。

我上高中的时候，吃我们学校门口的凉面三年，无论冬夏；上初中的时候吃学校旁边的千层饼三年，每天都一样。大学有几个从本科到读研都在一起的稳定饭搭子，所以不会重复。

一旦习惯某种生活，潜意识就不愿意改变，所以说我是一个物欲很低的人。即使后来撸空投赚到了一笔两笔三笔，我还是一个物欲很低的人，并且极度厌恶浪费。我妹早上吃饭，点一碗热干面吃两口，然后再点一碗粉吃两口，剩下的都倒掉，有一次刚好被我看到了，说了一路，现在不浪费粮食了。

不过我是一个多无趣的人啊，这样过一辈子，我脑海的片段估计还没有别人一年的片段多。

我现在每天在本子上写变则通，明天不去省图了，换个地方去——

author: ClementDelangue
quoted_text:
We were able to fine tune an open weight model (Qwen3.5-9B) on proprietary internal data at @coinbase, and it out performed frontier models, at much lower cost and speed, for a specialized task (fraud prevention in this case).

I think we'll see more of this pattern inside companies. The frontier models are amazing generalists. But increasingly you'll see specialist models out perform on more narrow tasks, either working on teams, or by themselves.

We're making it easy to fine tune models internally for our employees. We even have a skill for it in our internal harness that makes it easy to spin these up and start training them:

"/fine-tune-and-serve-llm I want to fine-tune Qwen for payments risk review. help me get started"

I imagine we'll have some backend services that could be replaced entirely by this new architecture.

美股代币化全链熄火：一场自嗨的金融错配，与真正的四条破局出路

从 Robinhood 链上的双雄 Pons 与 LONG，
到 Solana 上曾经爆火的 Stonks，
再到 BSC 上一拥而上的美股仿盘与 PancakeSwap 概念对……

几个月前，全链都在疯狂鼓吹同一个叙事：“美股代币化 + 链上资产配对，是打通万亿 Web2 资产的圣杯。”

但今天放眼全链，惨状如出一辙：
交易量暴跌 90% 以上，内盘死水一潭，深度见底，散户全线套牢。

很多人把这归咎于大盘环境差。
但如果只甩锅给行情，你永远看不清本质：
这不仅仅是流动性退潮的问题，而是现阶段全链推行的“Meme 配对美股”模式，在底层金融逻辑上陷入了不可调和的结构性错配。

近日，IMF（国际货币基金组织）发布专题研报，直接给这套模式下了病危通知书：
“Tokenized stocks are less liquid and more volatile than traditional stocks.”
（代币化股票在实际运行中，不仅没有带来预想中的流动性泛滥，反而呈现出流动性远低于传统股票、波动率却畸形放大的特征。）

今天撕开所有遮羞布，深度拆解这场实验为什么全线崩塌？以及未来究竟该如何破局？

一、核心诊断：为什么当前模式注定是一地鸡毛？

1. 致命的受众真空：Degen 嫌慢，股民嫌烦

无论是 Solana 的高频 Degen，还是 BSC 的土狗军团，这套模式都陷入了同一个死胡同：

· 链上玩家要的是什么？
要的是 10 分钟 50 倍的极致波动率和注意力博弈。让他在底池里配一个一年涨 30% 都算暴利的英伟达或标普，不仅拉低了赚钱赔率，还增加了计算成本。链上玩家连明天的盘面都不信，你让他守着纳斯达克做价值投资？

· 真实的美股投资者会来吗？
现实中想买美股的人，打开正规券商一键免佣下单，受官方 50 万美元保险保护，享有合法分红。
谁会为了买一点股票，冒着智能合约漏洞、跨链桥脱锚、DEX 滑点、甚至被貔貅盘割韭菜的风险，大费周章来链上买一个“影子股票”？

把“散户炒空气”和“传统老钱买股票”强行绑在同一个池子里，从第一天起就是项目方生造的伪需求。

2. 金融数学的诅咒：无法解决的双重无常损失

在实际做市中，全链协议都撞上了同一堵数学高墙：

传统的 Token/SOL、Token/BNB 或 Token/ETH 配对，资产同属加密大盘贝塔，同涨同跌，做市商尚可对冲。

但“土狗配美股”是做市商的噩梦：
一边是 7×24 小时情绪驱动的纯空气币，另一边是受全球宏观和财报驱动的实体公司，两者相关性几乎为零。任何单边行情都会给池子带来毁灭性的无常损失（IL）。

更荒谬的是时间差：
美股周末休市，预言机喂价静止；链上却在疯狂交易。
在 BSC 或 Solana 上，做市商根本不敢在周末放深厚流动性，因为周一美股一旦跳空，池子就会被套利机器人瞬间抽干。这就导致：号称 7×24 小时全天候交易，实际上一到周末流动性就薄如纸片。

二、终局思考：到底有没有解？美股代币化的四条真正破局出路

全链的崩盘并不代表美股上链是伪命题，而是宣告了“把美股当土狗发”的草莽阶段彻底死亡。

要想真正走出死局，行业只有以下 4 条自我救赎的进化路径：

1. 资产选品破局：先啃“加密国库股”，抛弃传统死板股
强行在链上推 $SPY、$AAPL 是徒劳的。真正的第一批链上美股，必须是 Crypto-treasury（加密国库型美股）——如持仓比特币的微策略（$MSTR）、Coinbase（$COIN）、Robinhood（$HOOD）以及背靠 Tether/Cantor 的 $XXIc 等。
这些资产天然自带币圈高贝塔，受众 100% 重叠，且在美股开市时存在巨大的链上链下基差套利空间，能天然吸引套利做市商主动注入流动性。

2. 功能定位破局：从“DEX 炒现货”转向“顶级生息抵押品（Collateral First）”
散户买卖美股，Web2 券商的体验无法被超越；但 Web2 券商给不了“全天候可编程杠杆”。
真正的破局是把美股代币做成 DeFi 借贷的超级抵押品：你在链上质押 10 万美元的代币化美股，既能拿原生股息分红，又能以此作为 80% 质押率的抵押品借出 USDC 去冲链上热点。这彻底盘活了资产的资本效率，才是 Crypto Native 无法拒绝的真效用。

3. 做市机制破局：废弃脆弱的 AMM，拥抱做市商即时对冲（RFQ / JIT 流动性）
用传统的 x*y=k 联合曲线配对非相关资产，在数学上已被证伪。
未来的底层必须转向类似 CowSwap 的“意图驱动（Intent-based）与询价做市（RFQ）”：散户链上下单，底层由 Wintermute、Jane Street 等传统做市商在链下实时对冲，链上只做交割与即时铸造（JIT）。彻底终结无常损失和周末的流动性真空。

4. 流量入口破局：由持牌交易所/券商自上而下“降维分发”
指望存量的土狗钱包自发形成美股生态是痴人说梦。
真正的拐点，只会发生在 Bybit、Coinbase、Robinhood 这类拥有数千万真实用户的平台，直接在客户端内提供“一键将美股股票提现为链上代币、无缝接入 DeFi”的时刻。不是把币圈人培养成股民，而是把股民手里的天量合规资产直接引入链上。

三、总结：

美股代币化的第一阶段（作为 Launchpad 噱头的空气玩具）已经宣告死亡。
潮水退去不是坏事，它至少让所有人看清：

代码是代码，股票是股票，空气依然是空气。

它的第二阶段，属于严肃的金融工程——只有完成“加密国库股 + 借贷生息抵押品 + 机构 RFQ 做市 + CEX 级原生分发”的协议，才配拿到通往万亿级链上华尔街的真正门票。

傻哥前几天梳理了行情，这两天梳理个股和板块。

有些心得，有些反思，随手分享了：：
1、几个月前当时不知道大科技便宜，市场也不算贵。大科技便宜就是市场还处在低位的特征。
2、股神Serenity的三驾马车： $CCXI 和 $AAOI、$SIVE，幸亏没参与啊。不然亏大了。
3、测试的几张票，amkr、aehr也在跌的。但日月光在涨。
4、价值股可能是比较好的阶段了，便宜的阶段了
5、大量不靠谱的能源企业下跌了，比如Xe、Flnc、OKLO、这些
6、过去几个月，量子计算领域式微了。Ionq， QNT这些都在走下坡路。
7、非大科技的细分互联网平台，如Upwork、Uber、Paypal这些，都在承压。
8、软件的确在修复，类似now， crm这些都有了大反弹。
9、NeoCloud最近还是比较点背。Oracle和Coreweave尤其难受，Nbis稍好点儿。
10、中概还是老大难，在美国资本市场有种越来越混不动的感觉，被降维打击的
11、垄断价值股如沃尔玛、开市客还是牛逼，PE估值竟然还保持高位。这种溢价，说明其还有拥趸的。
12、医药股辉瑞和礼来，都还不错。
13、港股的科技股真是惨啊，大部分票都是亏损的半卖半骗的meme。
14、白银也非常之惨。散户只记住了白银的爆拉，对白银暴跌已经选择性失忆了。他们的格局有些甚至不如山寨币庄家。

Ledger theft, day two. Since yesterday the thief has pushed ether through Tornado Cash three times, and each time on into Zcash's shielded pool. We followed every lot out the far side. Here is how, step by step.

1. THE SAME BUILD, THREE TIMES
An ether wallet pays a fresh splitter. The splitter pays four fresh wallets. The four drop it into Tornado Cash's 100, 10 and 1 ETH pools. Minutes, every time.

Run 1, yesterday 15:17: 1,254 ETH. Run 2, today 09:42: 1,291 ETH. Run 3, today 11:56: 450 ETH from 0xfa4EaBB840A33C156E600311433AE261CBfCb0e2, in the pools by 12:15.

2. OUT OF TORNADO CASH
The mixer breaks the link between a deposit and a withdrawal. We do not need the link. Our tooling fingerprints the withdrawal transactions themselves: how each one is constructed, who constructs it, and when. 

Yesterday's 65 withdrawals (1,084 ETH) and today's 96 (1,726 ETH) all carry the same signature. The six other withdrawals from those pools in today's windows do not. Run 3 came out from 12:18 into 0x0d697aa182801566d87adc86e68e95fd3b2f5f82 (213 ETH) and 0x676b16cc18542f37d202a1a79ac05463395496a4 (122 ETH), and 195 ETH of it was inside a cross-chain swap service by 12:38. Forty-two minutes, end to end.

3. INTO ZCASH, AND OUT AGAIN
The swap service turns the ether into shielded ZEC, where sender, amount and recipient vanish. But the service's own shielding of each lot is public, and from it we derive a value signature for that lot's exit, then scan every transparent exit from the pool. 108 of 108 exits across both days match their lot to the zatoshi. Not one other exit from the pool does. 

First lot today: in at 10:18:18, out at 11:06:16 in block 3512847 (8d26a9b095d4d28373527f7a6eb81a3be7f906d1e2190960c0512ff64f369418 and 738c6d1261e79766e4dd16bdbd38dced91b8e3a86ce41dcda83eda1f19208fbf), straight into a ZEC to USDC order.

Today so far: 20 lots ordered (2,379 ZEC, $2.9m), 14 out, 5 inside the pool, 1 still settling. Every exit feeds a ZEC to USDC order paying two wallets born at 11:11, 22 of the 28 paid by 12:43:
0x816D5Ee17DB1495d1409F135b98FF3edc5F3cDf8: 940,561 USDC
0xBA736A4b616e79867B6d586293966b552883f3F3: 852,258 USDC

Introducing QwenGyre, bringing elastic RL to extreme-long-horizon (XLong) agent training. ✨

It launches with two core designs: 🥳
- Elastic Scheduler: reallocates GPUs between rollout & training as demand shifts—live executions never interrupted. Up to 1.85× speedup over Colocate, 1.78× over Async.
- Trajectory Processor: turns branching executions (compaction, sub-agents, retries) into prefix-shared trajectory trees with bounded, deduplicated training samples. Partial progress after timeout still gets scored.

Scaled to Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B with ~700K tokens per rollout, QwenGyre lifts NL2RepoBench from 52.5% to 58.5% in 48 steps, cutting end-to-end training time by ~44% vs Async.

text: The frontier is private
author: williamallen
quoted_text:
Dusting off this tweet from April because this gap in shared understanding of LLM capability is *widening*. It's now less "two groups of people speaking past each other" and more a sharp funnel.

- Napkin math somewhere around 6B people (~75% of the population) have barely come in contact with LLMs at all.
- Around 1-2B (~20%) are casual and infrequent users of free-tier ChatGPT-like products. This group sees derpy chatbots and treats them a bit like a better Google search, a writing aid, or etc. Maybe an agent tries to book you a flight. I have non-tech friends who (reasonably, imo) say they have not much use for it at all. Even many professionals outside of math&code are in this tier. For example, execs and many other functions spend a lot of their time talking to other people, so while they understand what is happening intellectually, it is still second-hand and a bit abstract.
- Now we get to professional use of frontier-grade LLMs in math&code. Somewhere around 20M people (0.2%) see first-hand that large, complex projects that used to take them weeks/months can now be completed by agents with a prompt. Building apps, copying apps, translating apps, decompiling apps from binaries... This has all happened very quickly and recently - less than 1 year ago, I was writing code manually by hand, typing memorized computer code commands into a code editor character by character, occasionally pressing Tab to autocomplete a little chunk of code.
- And finally we get to the ~5,000 people (~0.00006%) with access to frontier-grade systems internally. The external world has seen the preview. It looks like swarms of thousands of agents collaborating over weeks on software mega projects: minting zero days, running cyber attacks and defenses at machine speeds, discovering new science, advancing the frontier of mathematics. Things that would have taken top professionals in the industry years of work. Meanwhile, human review and comprehension are starting to fall behind. For example, people are still involved in the "archeology" of the OpenAI-HF incident from many months ago. Mathematicians may be poring over the 722 manuscripts on frontier mathematics for a while.

The funnel is driven by a combination of factors:
1. The impact scales with ambition, problem size, and horizon. A question with a paragraph answer barely stresses the system. You need a reservoir of big, difficult problems that you really care about. This aspect drives the consumer / professional dimension of the funnel.
2. The jaggedness of the system (which I have written about a lot separately). Capability peaks in domains that are digital, verifiable and economically valuable. This is because LLM capability emerges from reinforcement learning on verifiable rewards on a curated environment mixture driven by revenue potential. This aspect primarily drives the area (e.g. math&code) dimension of the funnel.
3. Access. Free-tier, paid-tier, internal.

So this is the weirdness of the moment. The general public has mostly not interacted with these systems. When they have, it looks like a derpy chatbot. The majority of professionals still see only a modest uplift. And a small sliver of professionals are experiencing the vertigo of the curve going vertical. And it is all happening at the same time.

看中一个 App 的功能，可以让 AI 帮你拆解它的实现。

开源项目 REA，把逆向分析工具接进 Claude Code、Codex、Cursor 等 Agent：即使没有源码，也能追踪功能逻辑，再据此为自己的项目编写实现。

按项目说明，它可以：

• 拆 JavaScript / Electron：追踪模块、路由、IPC 和原生扩展关联
• 查原生二进制：提取伪代码、汇编、字符串和调用关系
• 返回证据与分析局限，让 Agent 继续追查、解释并验证实现

例如，追踪 Notion 的剪贴板功能，沿着渲染进程、preload、IPC，一路看到主进程如何处理富文本。

分析在本地运行；原生二进制分析仍需配置 Hopper、Ghidra 或 IDA，商业工具授权需自行取得。

适合做软件研究、互操作性开发，以及分析自己有权研究的软件。

I am getting lots of incoming questions about the public execution of Nidal Hasan, mostly because I have been outspoken on wanting public executions for over a decade.

My position is simple:  Executions should be public and brutal, not private and medicalized.  They are the ultimate example of the state's monopoly on violence, and the only way to keep that from running out of control is to confront voters with the trade they have made every single time, that they might have appropiate confidence or revulsion in the institution.

This is not new thinking.  George Washington thought the same.  The way we have shifted from hanging to firing squads to doctors quietly injecting chemicals that send our worst gently off to sleep is awful and dystopian, a total short-circuiting of important feedback mechanisms.  It makes needless executions more likely, not less so.  People who demean this as barbaric or yucky miss the whole point.  It doesn't somehow become torture or inhumane (as the UN is suddenly claiming) just because we decline to hide the act behind a curtain.

And then there are those who suggest any revel in the death of those who truly deserve it is an indicator of a broken or diseased mind.  To the contrary.  It is normal, good, and aligned with our natural and national order.  That it has not been done here in 60 years is an indictment in and of itself.

And that is without even getting into the fact that men were not hung for stealing horse, but that horses may not be stolen.

"I would to God that one of the most attrocious in each State was hung in Gibbets, up on a gallows five times as high as the one prepared by Haman. No punishment, in my opinion, is too great for the Man, who can build his greatness upon his Country’s ruin." 
- George Washington, 1778

text:
The recent hardware wallet supply-chain attack have raised a question of how much the design of a hardware wallet contributes to its security.

The reported attack didn't require breaking the secure element. It's a reminder that even when a secure element does its job, other components can introduce vulnerabilities.

When we designed Solflare Shield, we made a deliberate decision: keep the hardware as simple as possible, without compromising its core purpose.

Shield is a card-sized hardware wallet built around a secure element, with only the components necessary to protect private keys and authorize cryptographic operations.

1. Keeping the hardware minimal

Hardware components beyond the secure element can create additional opportunities for attackers, particularly when they introduce new interfaces or communication channels.
Shield has no screen, display interface, battery, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, or cellular modem. It's a passive NFC card that draws power from your phone during a tap.
This eliminates certain classes of hardware attacks, including the specific display interception mechanism.

2. Separating the wallet experience from key protection

Shield is designed to work with the Solflare app rather than operate as a standalone device. The app handles the interface and prepares transactions, while Shield's EAL6+ secure element performs cryptographic signing internally.
The tradeoff is that your phone acts as the screen. The recovery phrase is shown once in the Solflare app during setup, and transactions are reviewed there before you tap.
After setup, your private key stays on the card and is never stored on your phone or in the Solflare app.
This separation keeps the physical hardware focused on protecting keys and authorizing transactions, without requiring additional components to support the user interface.

3. Reducing supply-chain exposure

Hardware security also depends on what happens between manufacturing and delivery.
Shield is sold exclusively through the official Solflare Shop, without an authorized reseller network or third-party retail distribution.
Additional protections, including cryptographic authenticity verification, safeguards against unauthorized software replacement, and tamper-evident packaging, are designed to reduce the risk of compromised devices reaching users.
These measures reduce certain risks, but no distribution model or security mechanism can completely eliminate the possibility of physical tampering.

Security is a series of design decisions

Sophisticated attacks are a reminder that protecting private keys requires looking at the entire device, its components, and the supply chain behind it.

Different hardware wallets make different design tradeoffs, and no architecture is immune to every threat.

With Shield, we chose to prioritize simplicity, minimize unnecessary components and keep the hardware focused on protecting your keys.
