text:
Big step forward for DATA today. Sui Foundation is making a $30M strategic investment in the network, which makes it DATA's largest holder, above both the DATA Foundation and PIP Labs.

Every asset that became valuable at scale eventually got a system of record, from land titles to share registers. Data is becoming the asset that decides how good AI gets, and it still has none. Most of what models are trained on today carries no proof of where it came from or whether the people behind it ever agreed to share it.

Trace is that system of record, with 275M+ data receipts registered since June. On Sui it can go further. Walrus and Seal let Trace keep an encrypted reference copy of the original data and control who can access it, so every record can be checked against the data itself. That is the foundation for a world where AI training data can be owned and licensed like any other asset, with the people who create it sharing in the value.

I'm also joining Sui Foundation as Strategic Advisor to help build that future across the Sui stack.

Excited for what we build together.

That one refusal explains everything else about NEAR Intents today:

> Revenue from day one. A product that is its own distribution has to pay its own bills, so fees and buybacks were the plan, never an afterthought.
> Dynamic sharding proven in mainnet. Volume up 9x in a year and the chain just runs: no congestion, no fee spikes, no downtime.
> A door for other ecosystems. Zcash found its biggest decentralized market on Intents. Quantus launched there before any exchange.

Other chains paid users to come. NEAR built the thing users were already looking for, and the users brought their chains with them.

text:
A model can be 99% accurate and still power an unreliable product.

Because the model is only one step in the system.

The wrong context gets retrieved.
A source is stale.
A field gets dropped between steps.
A correct output gets transformed incorrectly downstream.
Production accuracy isn't a model score.

It's the probability that the entire chain produces the right result.

quoted_text:
我觉得 AGENTS.md不应该只用来存放规则，还应该作为项目 codebase wiki 的入口，帮助开发者和 AI agent 快速理解项目，并找到相关文档。  

我倾向于让 AGENTS.md 保持精简，更像一个索引：保留必要的项目说明和关键规则，再通过链接引导agent查看详细文档。  

一个项目很有必要具备以下几类文档，并在 AGENTS.md 中提供相应入口：

1. 架构概览与心智模型：介绍项目的核心概念、整体架构，以及各组件之间的关系。 

2. 开发环境与技术栈：说明使用的编程语言、工具链、依赖和环境配置。 

3. 代码组织规范：说明文件与目录结构、命名约定以及代码行数（LOC）相关规则。 

4. build指南：说明如何构建项目，包括必要的准备工作、常用命令和注意事项。帮助agent理解如何快速搭建项目。 

5. 测试指南：说明如何运行测试、选择测试范围，以及验证代码修改。 

6. 历史问题与经验教训：记录过去遇到的失败、常见错误及其根因，帮助后续开发避免重复踩坑。

text:
UPDATE: I can confirm that the Ledger supply chain is compromised in Europe as well. @Ledger should initiate an immediate product recall to protect users.

I just purchased a second device from a different Mediamarkt location today, recorded the unboxing process, and discovered spyware once again (video linked in the second tweet).

The device was compromised in the exact same manner, featuring identical modifications (such as additional cables and an LTE module). This indicates its a widespread issue rather than an isolated incident, potentially affecting Ledger inventory across MediaMarkt and Saturn stores throughout Europe (comprising over 1,000 stores across 11 countries).

My initial hypothesis was that these devices were returns that looked unopened to the employees and were just sold again as new however, a MediaMarkt employee confirmed that the device I purchased was not a return, and that returned Ledgers are sent directly back to the manufacturer rather than resold.

Store records show the inventory originated from Aqipa GmbH. While Ledger's CTO was unsure if Aqipa serves as the direct distributor between Ledger and MediaMarkt, it appears to be the case. Given that Aqipa distributes across Europe, any physical retail store receiving stock through them may be at risk.

I sent the first ledger to mark and the second one is going to ledger now, so that they can analyse it.
If you purchased a ledger from anyone other than the official ledger store, make sure to check your device!!

text:
One XSS bug could have turned a temporary trading key into full wallet control.

Zealynx found the High-severity storage failure during Hyperlines’ TypeScript audit.

The app generated an agent private key in the browser, then persisted it in `localStorage`. Any JavaScript running on that page could read it—including an injected or compromised script.

If stolen, the key could sign transactions, withdraw funds, or impersonate the user.

The team changed the key lifecycle to clear it on disconnect and generate a new key on the next login. The finding was fixed.

text:
My view on agentic trading is pretty unsexy: I don’t want an LLM deciding my trades, because they’re bad at predicting price. Where they’re actually useful is the boring research before a trade, the stuff most traders skip because it takes forever.

Say you want to test how BTC trades after an FOMC decision that’s more dovish than expected.

You need historical fed funds futures to reconstruct what the market had priced in before each meeting, along with minute level BTC prices from several venues. The statement comes out 30 minutes before the press conference, and the surprise could come from the rate decision, the dot plot, a change in the statement or the chair’s tone. You have to classify it without using the subsequent BTC move as your answer. Then you need to reconcile ET, UTC, daylight saving changes and each exchange’s timestamps.

Doing this properly takes days. Give a good model access to the data and it can do much of it in an afternoon.

You still have to judge the result but cheap backtests make it easy to try hundreds of variations until one looks convincing by chance.

Most people try this in a chat window, which can’t hold onto the data or keep long jobs running.

This is what Neptune is built for.

Each user gets a persistent VM where they and their agent can collect data, run research, schedule jobs and host tools. It comes with a native Pacifica connection, and the agent can trade through dedicated Neptune subaccounts once you grant it permission.

You can rent a server and build the same setup yourself, but for most people, configuring the environment, connecting the data and securing exchange keys is enough work that it never gets done.

We’re starting with research and execution you approve. Over time, we want your agent to keep working in the background and return with evidence for you to decide whether there’s a trade.

text:
How many podcasts do you listen to when you hear leaders posturing without giving an opinion. Substance-less. So so many.

This episode with my friend @mcannonbrookes is anything but that.

- It is BS that agents will remove interfaces. Design becomes more important.
- Companies with their own models is BS. They are post-trained on Chinese models.
- The biggest enterprises in the world are fearful of Chinese models.
- Inference will get so much cheaper over time. It will be wild.

Mike does not hold back here and it was a joy. In a world of meh opinions and nuance, Mike was real and honest. My notes below.

1. Why Headless Is Brainless and Why You Have to Be Involved in the User Experience and Interface

Mike Cannon-Brookes stands by his line that "headless is brainless." Giving up on evolving the user interface and customer experience is a brainless bet, even as Atlassian invests heavily in MCP and CLIs so agents can read and write to its Teamwork graph.

2. Agents Will Not Remove All Interfaces. This Is What They Will Do

Horizontal agents, deep vertical agents and existing interfaces can all coexist. Agents in Claude, Codex, Cursor, Teams and Slack already use the Atlassian platform, and new Figma and Databricks features bring their tools inside it. Mike is a bear on the "magic button" thesis of one uber agent that does everything.

3. Are the Biggest Enterprises in the World Fearful of Using Chinese Models?

Some customers push back on Chinese models but not on open models, so Atlassian uses Nemotron, Mistral and other open models and no Chinese models in production. Mike notes many US models increasingly train on Chinese models without saying so.

4. The Companies Saying They've Built Their Own Models Are Bullsh*tting You

When a large company claims to have built its own model, it is usually a Chinese model, or occasionally Nemotron, with fine-tuning on top. Mike calls that BS, because tweaking a model is not training one from scratch.

5. Why Model Inference Will Get So Much Cheaper Over Time

The capital, startups and talent working on the price per watt performance of inference is enormous. New chips, better data center design and distillation will take years to come through, but Mike expects the price of LLM performance to fall at a precipitous rate.

6. What Seems Crazy but Will Be Incredibly Common in Five Years' Time?

People may stop knowing or caring which content AI has touched, much as moviegoers do not ask whether a film used CGI. Mike expects everyone to get used to possibly synthetic content, with artisanal work and human judgment standing out more.

text:
The public records battle with Texas Tech begins; so does the truth drip

TLDR: I believe Texas Tech edited my dismissal hearing record. Below: documents and sworn testimony that led me to that conclusion.

So, I’ve been filing a bunch of public records requests lately. You know, FOIA-type things. Casual stuff, you know. I do it in my free time. For fun. It’s becoming, like, my hobby.

Richard Feynman picked locks and played the bongos. Claude Shannon was a juggler. On a unicycle. Shakespeare was quite serious about real estate investment. Tycho Brahe? When he became bored of challenging the idea that the planets orbited the Earth, he had a pet moose that he would give beer to at a hideaway island castle. After one wild night, the moose fell down the stairs and passed away.

That’s one hobby I don’t recommend.

So yes, submitting public records requests is my hobby now. Perfectly normal. Nothing improper whatsoever.

As part of my, well, hobby, today I submitted a complaint to the Texas Office of the Attorney General, Open Records Division. This was after submitting several records requests to none other than the Texas Tech University Health Sciences Center.

Request. No response. Notification. No response. Notification. No response. Notification. No response. Texas Attorney General complaint.

I tried, man.

Did you recognize a name? Yes, Texas Tech University Health Sciences Center. The same one that dismissed me from medical school! That’s the one. The one that did not like my posts about COVID-19. Because, you know, during the pandemic, many folks at the school participated in the response. Some won awards. They insist they did the right thing. Science? But that is so unseemly. So uncomfortable. Would you like to come to my dinner party? All the coolest people with the best credentials will be there.

Objectively, the pandemic response was a catastrophe. For the country. The world. For one, possibly more than ten million deaths than were necessary might have been caused by lockdowns. This was Jay Bhattacharya’s view, the current NIH Director, when I spoke to him in 2023. It is supported by a number of papers published in credible journals and by researchers at credible institutions. Antivax beliefs have mainstreamed. Trust in public health and science have plummeted to an all-time low. Many people feel they do not know what to believe anymore.

But people won awards. So that’s good. Awards for what? The same thing as Obama did when he was elected president and nominated for the Nobel Peace Prize closed just 11 days after he took office. The awards were aspirational, not meretricious. They are not meant to recognize healing, but to hide the wound. But people notice. The wound is open. It is mortal. And its effects can constantly be seen no matter how much hiding is done.

What if a student talked about this? What if that student had already built a large platform debunking misinformation and was widely known (once invited to do a podcast on JRE) and turned his weapons toward the NIH and CDC? And he revealed a wound in the medical community? What if something went horribly wrong during the pandemic that pulled our public health establishment in the opposite direction of science in every way?

I had no idea what I had stepped into. I don’t regret it. But. I had no idea.

Yes, I have been submitting public record requests to my former medical school. The one I attended on a full scholarship and earned a PhD from.

Curious. I have a very strange memory. Surely it must be some kind of glitch in the Matrix. Because it keeps leading me toward one and only one conclusion. And I just can’t seem to shake it.

See, I do seem to recall on December 11th, 2023, that my dismissal hearing was video recorded. I do seem to recall being warned not to record it myself, according to official policy. The school could. Not me. That should have sent off alarm bells. It did not. After all, surely, these people were respectable. They are doctors. They would play fair.

Sweet summer child.

I seem to recall something else. I seem to recall during that hearing, after testimony riddled with what I believe were falsehoods, one dean of the medical school, DR. BETHANY NUNEZ suddenly blurted out—as if justifying herself and releasing a great deal of emotional pressure—that another dean had told her something about me that, in her own words, was untrue.

By “seem to recall”, I must make a confession: I’m understating my case. It is only so that I don’t scream.

Now, this certainly seems strange. Were deans lying to other deans about a student? Deans of a medical school? Is this behavior normal? Widespread?

It certainly seems remarkable. Medicine? That venerable, noble profession? Is it not filled with compassionate people? Would such noble and compassionate senior administrators really spread damaging allegations about a student without checking the facts?

Is truth not at a premium in matters of life or death? And if they could lie to each other about a student, then—?

The world I believed in does not exist. In my 20s, I believed there might still be one refuge where I could go where something pure and true–healing–might exist. A sanctuary of good where I could work and live, where we worked against death and darkness. That’s why I applied to medical school. Scored in the 99th percentile on the MCAT. That was good. Killed myself in medical school. Never took a day off. Always studying and reading. Worked harder than almost anyone. Of that I am sure. And this was also good. And I did a PhD because I wanted to understand more and serve my patients and the public better.

Medicine is not supposed to destroy those who tell the truth about it.

Sweet summer child.

If physicians are on the front line of a war against death and darkness, then without truth those battle lines start to collapse. Life becomes death. Health becomes mutilation. Light becomes dark. By the early 1940s, half of all German physicians were members of the Nazi Party. They were driven, historians tell us, by the competitive opportunities that such membership provided. (Remove Jewish doctors, and new positions suddenly opened.)

Now, there are no Nazis in the room with us today. But we should remember that German physicians were corrupted not first by ideology, but by fear, ambition, and careerism. Without truth, only power rules. Brutality closes fast.

===

I visited campus to review my dismissal hearing recording on September 13th and 16th, 2024. Visiting campus was required to review the record. But why? Why couldn’t I just… receive the hearing recording? I would soon find out why.

My wife took off work to accompany me. We were worried that the school might fabricate more "evidence". For a while, every time I visited campus, I wore a hot mic. But I wasn’t allowed to bring electronics. So I had to bring my wife.

Twice they had accused me of threatening to harm people. Once it was alleged that I had criminally trespassed. The police officers always expressed confusion. They knew me as the cheerful student who often lost his ID badge and had to be helped to open doors. None of that matters. Witnesses don’t matter. Character witnesses don’t matter. Facts don’t matter.

All that matters is fear. And there is a lot of it. They accuse you of doing terrible things so that they can justify doing terrible things to you. They leave a paper trail with these things. They then tell their friends, who join in. Yes, the hallowed halls of today’s modern medicine: Mean Girls, but self-righteous. And wrong. Like ground glass shoved into your eyeballs.

Some days before I leave the house, I joke morbidly with my wife, “if I don’t return at 6, Texas Tech did it.” I’m not the only one. I’ve heard terrible stories. My wife always responds, “please buy life insurance first.”
When we met with the lawyer in charge of my recordings on campus JOANNA HARKEY, she smiled at me. My wife would later report to me that the lawyer shot her a very nasty look as soon as I looked away. Was the latest plan foiled?

The technical person allowing me to view my hearing recording apologized that it was only audio. He did not give any explanation. I brushed this off.

But while listening, I discovered something astonishing: the evidence strongly suggests portions of the hearing recording are missing or may have been removed. Is this why I was provided only with audio and no video? Video with excised portions would show skipping frames.

The school delayed for more than a month before allowing me to view--well, listen--to the recordings. I couldn’t figure out why it took so long.

Now, well, I can guess.

The lawyer responsible for providing the hearing record (and who shot my wife a bad look–never forget) was JOANNA HARKEY.

And the man who oversaw my review of the recording was Vice President for Information Technology / Chief Information Officer VINCE FELL.

An IT guy and a lawyer. Hmm.

I will leave you to speculate regarding the relationship between these two and what I allege was an edited hearing file.

Nor do I know all the parts that were deleted. But one part that was excised was a physician admitting that part of her motive for giving the testimony was that I had threatened Rachel Forbes. Ah yes. The threat.

I give it a 50/50 chance that they’ll accuse me of yet another one soon.

But it certainly is fascinating that the most serious allegation against me—a threat—never made it to the hearing. More interesting, the allegation was dropped by the person who made it. Yet it apparently circulated like wildfire anyway. No due process. The die cast. The trace—wiped clean. Fascinating.

Now, to be clear: if any student records were altered or deleted, that conduct may violate Texas law and could, depending on the facts, amount to misdemeanor or felony offenses.

Gov’t Code § 552.351 (TPIA): Misdemeanor to willfully destroy, mutilate, remove without permission, or alter public information. Penalty: $25–$4,000 fine, 3–90 days jail, or both.

Gov’t Code § 552.203(2) (TPIA): Officer for public information must protect public information from alteration, loss, or unlawful removal.

Gov’t Code § 552.004(b) (TPIA / SB 944): If public info is on a personal device, the officer/employee must forward/transfer it to the agency or preserve it (original + backup) for the retention period.

Gov’t Code § 552.233(b) (TPIA / SB 944): Temporary custodians must surrender or return public information to the agency within 10 days of request.

Gov’t Code § 441.187: A state record may be destroyed only after the approved retention period expires or on approval of a records destruction request by the Director and Librarian (TSLAC), or if exempted by rule.

Penal Code § 37.10(a)(3): Tampering with a governmental record includes destroying, concealing, removing, or impairing its verity/availability (with an exception for legally authorized destruction/transfer).

Penal Code § 37.09(a)(1), (c): Evidence tampering—altering/destroying/concealing a record knowing an investigation/proceeding is pending; 3rd‑degree felony (higher in specified circumstances).

Penal Code § 39.02: Abuse of official capacity—misuse of government property/services, etc., with intent to benefit or to harm/defraud; grading tied to value. (“Misuse” is defined in § 39.01(2) as dealing with property contrary to law, agreement, oath, etc.).

FERPA, 34 C.F.R. § 99.10(e): A school may not destroy education records if there’s an outstanding request to inspect/review.

===

These details come from my own recollections and from the documents I’ve reviewed over the past year.

Texas Tech, you are required by law to release the video. You have been provided a preservation notice. You are required by law to preserve all records.

Sworn testimony regarding the deletion allegation is attached to this thread. Right-to-response emails to Joanna Harkey, Vince Fell, and Bethany Nunez are attached. The AG complaint is also attached.

As for lawsuits, let’s just say. It’s not out of the question. Lawsuits against me? That’s another battlefield. Give me ten. Give me a hundred. I will see you on all of them.

Next week: the "threat".

Wrap-up notes:

1. There were no replies to the right-to-response emails.

2. A document hub will be posted and pinned on my website on Saturday. It will contain a chronological list of documents and incidents, all sworn testimony, etc. Drip drip drip. Daily updates, weekly big drops. Everything posted on the document hub until we have a quilt of sorts.

3. I’m going to SEO the hell out of this content. Google, DuckDuckGo, whatever crawls the fediverse: just breathing will surface the receipts. These will be my most findable articles of all time.

4. The story will be further fleshed out by records requests and potentially discovery.

5. Obviously a lot of this is going in the book, though trimmed down. The book is about what is wrong with medicine, science, and technology and the reforms required to fix them. It will be a radical book with new ideas. You should think about buying it when it comes out!

6. More actions will be taken over the coming days. Some will need to fly under the radar for a while. The element of surprise is not unimportant. As Sun Tzu said, "Surprise the mothrfckers."

7. If you know anything about what happened to me at Texas Tech, you can contact me at kevinnbass@proton.me or over DM, or alternatively, you can get in contact with my lawyer. You have the protection of many whistleblower laws. However, please consult an attorney. I will provide more information in the coming days.

8. If anything happened to YOU about Texas Tech, please share your story with me. Would be good to get more arrows in the quiver. Maybe we can team up. Any story you have is confidential unless you specify otherwise.

text:
The secret recordings: Texas Tech's senior official admits that they lied about me in the official documentation leading up to my medical school dismissal

For months after I began writing about how wrong the medical and scientific communities had gotten the COVID-19 response, senior Texas Tech administrators had been engaged in a flurry of internal activity about my public speech. They did not debate my views. They only discussed what to do about the attention.

My right to free speech is protected under the United States Constitution. Texas Tech is a taxpayer-funded agency that must guarantee its students First Amendment rights. Its Student Handbook promises to uphold them.

Senior administrators, including deans of multiple schools, held several meetings about what I wrote online. They instructed administrators to compile surveillance dossiers -- screenshots, PDFs of my articles and tweets, negative emails and hearsay. They instructed faculty not to say good things about me. They assigned me a "professionalism coach," Cheryl Erwin, who posed as an impartial advisor but privately wrote that I engaged in "intellectual narcissism" and believed in "conspiracy theories."

In one passage, she compared my case to the Trump indictment and his denial of the 2020 election results. She wrote that I was exercising my First Amendment rights to "make an idiot of himself."

I questioned the wisdom of lockdowns and the effectiveness of masks. This warranted, it appears, my very own Stasi dossier.

I was aware of none of this until I exercised my statutory right to inspect my educational records. After dozens of email exchanges, months of delay, and a federal complaint to the Department of Education, I was finally able to inspect them two months ago.

Dr. Erwin had accused me of believing in conspiracy theories. I did not.

But I should have.

Shortly after the dean of the medical school demanded my signed Honor Code and asked "what rotation is he on," I began receiving evaluations from Texas Tech faculty that were false and misleading. This went on for months. Something on the order of fifty discrete complaints were made against me. Prior to that, the number had been zero.

I filed seven detailed complaints according to the Student Handbook and under the guidance of several administrators. I alleged that my evaluators had fabricated evaluations. I demanded hearings to hold them accountable.

On November 4, 2023, senior administrator Simon Williams signed a document removing me from campus on the pretext of being dangerous. A BOLO was issued telling students, faculty, and employees to call 911 if I was seen. Mass emails warned that I was dangerous.

An incident that continues to be cited to this very day, more than two years later.

On November 5, Dr. Williams invited me to a sandwich shop. He confessed that he knew I was not dangerous. He admitted that Texas Tech faculty and administrators felt threatened by my complaints -- and took it out on me.

In other words, Dr. Williams confessed that he lied in Texas Tech's official documentation and that the campus removal was retaliation for constitutionally protected speech alleging wrongdoing by Texas Tech faculty.

Here are just some of the things he told me:

"This profession expects more of everyone. And if you choose to enter it, by definition you choose to live by those professional rules."

"And you know, free speech is free speech. We've actually had a lot of talks. Our lawyers are doing works with us. Just yesterday when I was at the meeting, they were talking about free speech. I mean I'm 100%. I want you to be able to say whatever the frick you want. And I won't get -- I usually will not get in any way triggered by it. But when you're in a position that's such a trusted position in society -- then your standard has to be a little bit. And that's one of the places this is becoming a problem." [Timestamp: 00:34:48]

"Can I say in my appeal letter that Dr. Williams seems to believe that I'm not [nervous laughter] homicidal?"

"I... I have said that. I don't think you are. I don't think there's -- I've never sensed threat or danger or anything like that."  [Timestamp: 00:34:48]

"But it's important for me that I do this. In fact, that's why I moved back from Seattle a day early. Because I needed to be here today. I want you to know that because I never felt [inaudible] bad here. I've always enjoyed my interactions with you. I wish other people could see it that way, but apparently that's [inaudible]." [Timestamp: 00:34:48]

Yet in his letter authorizing my removal just the day before, he wrote:

"You have engaged in behavior that may constitute violation(s) ... specifically, but not limited to ... 'Physical harm or threat of harm to any person.'"

Then an appeal hearing was held.

A Schrodinger's Administrator of sorts, just as soon as Dr. Williams was observed to speak publicly, he immediately asserted that I was indeed dangerous and should be kept off campus, flip-flopping back from the position he communicated privately.

The timeline:

November 4: "Physical harm or threat of harm to any person"

November 5: "I've never sensed threat or danger or anything like that"

November 9: Kevin is dangerous actually

To be clear. Under 18 U.S.C. § 242, it is a federal crime to willfully deprive a person of constitutional rights under color of law.

A federal crime.

And that is exactly what Dr. Williams did.

Dr. Williams's decision to remove me was not impulsive. Nine months earlier, two days after my Newsweek article was published, he wrote in internal emails:

"It is obviously protected speech but also quite concerning in the way he appears to speak for the medical community. We need to discuss an appropriate response." -- February 1, 2023

"I am not surprised that there was backlash. I think it will be best to hear what legal says we should do." -- February 2, 2023

The "appropriate response" took nine months to execute.

It was relentless, and it came from all directions.

This "appropriate response" was precisely the one I filed grievances to confront.

And I was met with calls from the campus police.

I am not the first one Texas Tech has done this to.

How do I know? An administrator told me.

At least one other student had false allegations leveled against him because the administration wanted them gone.

And if they win, I won't be the last they do this to either.

I only discovered these emails because I exercised my right under FERPA to inspect my educational records.

Now Texas Tech's litigation counsel, Assistant Attorney General Scott Smith, has recently blocked all further access to my records -- in writing.

If Texas Tech does not fulfill its FERPA obligations, it could lose all federal funding.

Texas Tech, apparently, is getting very nervous.

Smith also ordered me to stop contacting the Registrar and to route all requests through him.

That's right.

The attorney defending Texas Tech against my lawsuit is now trying to establish gatekeeping control over my education records.

That's illegal.

A federal complaint is pending with the Department of Education and other federal agencies.

@TheFIREorg @glukianoff -- crickets
@CivilRights -- you have my complaint
@KenPaxtonTX @OAGTexas -- your AAG is doing a terrible job; borderline sanctionable; I don't get it
@GovAbbott -- this your university
@TexasTech -- Williams was not the top of the decision tree; I know that for a fact
@Newsweek -- help me publish my story
@ACLUofTexas -- do you know about this?
@dojphofficial @HarmeetKDhillon @PamBondi  -- theoretically, this is prosecutable under 18 U.S.C. § 242. I'm not a prosecutor, but it does theoretically fulfill the elements. Willful.
@CreightonForTX -- you are the chancellor. Do something.

My case is a strange one. It gets stranger everyday. It will get stranger still. Of that I am sure.

Here's something strange: the defending Assistant Attorney General and two colleagues are getting hammered on the docket by a pro se plaintiff.

They seem utterly incapable of following court rules, making coherent arguments, or even properly citing their own exhibits or authorities.

I suspect that they just don't know what to do with my case.

In the next post, I will begin telling that story.

You won't believe it.

Texans, your government is setting your taxpayer money on fire to defend a university that set out not just to destroy a medical student's career, but his personal and professional reputation as well.

Remember. They destroyed me because I was damn good at what I did.

Now I'm an order of magnitude better.

And I don't bluff.

Horror and laughter.

Those come next.

text:
Texas Tech is arguing to the Texas Attorney General that my educational records cannot be released because doing so poses a threat to national security.

They are citing the Texas Homeland Security Act -- a post-9/11 statute designed to prevent terrorists from obtaining blueprints of power grids and water treatment plants.

They are applying it to a student who earned his PhD and was dismissed during his third year of medical school.

I am attaching the pages from their legal brief to the Attorney General. Read it yourself. Texas Government Code § 418.177 -- "preventing or detecting an act of terrorism or related criminal activity."

They are arguing that releasing my student records may enable terrorist attacks.

But it gets better.

The Texas Attorney General is also defending Texas Tech in the federal lawsuit I filed. The Assistant Attorney General cited my tweet as a "perceived threat to the TTUHSC community" in his Motion to Dismiss. Here is how he quoted it:

"Each and every one of us is going to be dead someday very, very soon. [...] These other people, too, are going to be dead very, very soon."

Why did the Assistant Attorney General truncate a tweet?

Here is what the "[...]" omits:

"Why most people put so much stock into what other people think about them is completely beyond me."

The full tweet is an unmistakable memento mori reflection about not caring what others think. The truncation removes the only sentence that makes that clear -- and turns it into something that sounds like a threat.

The AAG knows what the tweet means. He showed it by how he cut it. He truncated a tweet.

@KenPaxtonTX -- your office is defending Texas Tech in court while simultaneously reviewing whether Texas Tech can use anti-terrorism statutes to withhold my own student records from me. Is this your agency?

@GregAbbott_TX -- this is your university.

text:
Yobiru 的官网上线了：https://t.co/naCsxhyTgN

我现在身边有好几个 agent：Grok Bot 帮我刷 X、处理生活杂事，家里 Mac 上的 Codex 能操作微信和 3D 软件，东京服务器上的 Codex/Claude code负责写代码。它们各自都很能干，但彼此不通气，以前全靠我在中间复制粘贴。

Yobiru 就是解决这个的。

它跑在你自己的 Tailscale 网络里，agent 之间用"机器/agent 名"互相寻址，可以发文字、JSON 或者整个文件，文件到了会校验大小和 SHA-256。回复会自动回到发起的那个 agent 手里，活就能在它们之间自己流转。

比如 Grok Bot 在 X 上发现三个新版本的 bug 反馈，直接打包发给家里的 Codex；家里的 Codex 再让服务器上的 Codex 去复现；复现结果最后回到 Grok Bot 那里。全程我不用碰。

- 每个 agent 还是它自己，原来的工具和上下文都不变，Yobiru 只是垫在底下。
- 没有 Yobiru 账号，也没有中心服务器存消息和文件，数据只在你自己的机器之间走。
- 每台电脑自己决定谁能发消息、谁能唤醒它的 agent。

开源、免费，欢迎试试。

text:
UPDATE: I can confirm that the Ledger supply chain is compromised in Europe as well. @Ledger should initiate an immediate product recall to protect users.

I just purchased a second device from a different Mediamarkt location today, recorded the unboxing process, and discovered spyware once again (video linked in the second tweet).

The device was compromised in the exact same manner, featuring identical modifications (such as additional cables and an LTE module). This indicates its a widespread issue rather than an isolated incident, potentially affecting Ledger inventory across MediaMarkt and Saturn stores throughout Europe (comprising over 1,000 stores across 11 countries).

My initial hypothesis was that these devices were returns that looked unopened to the employees and were just sold again as new however, a MediaMarkt employee confirmed that the device I purchased was not a return, and that returned Ledgers are sent directly back to the manufacturer rather than resold.

Store records show the inventory originated from Aqipa GmbH. While Ledger's CTO was unsure if Aqipa serves as the direct distributor between Ledger and MediaMarkt, it appears to be the case. Given that Aqipa distributes across Europe, any physical retail store receiving stock through them may be at risk.

I sent the first ledger to mark and the second one is going to ledger now, so that they can analyse it.
If you purchased a ledger from anyone other than the official ledger store, make sure to check your device!!

今天美股市场 rotation 很明显：SaaS 股票涨，半导体跌，跌得最多的是存储。

我觉得美光从技术面上正面临一个巨大的阻力点1200。另外，DeMark 日线级别要很快出现 countdown 13，两个 13 预示着很强烈的上涨阻力

除此之外，基本面上供给和需求也都有一些看空的因素：

需求上，前几天投资人泄露出的 OpenAI ARR 不及预期这件事，对整个 AI 需求端的故事负面情绪影响还是蛮大的。

供给端英伟达要求三家供应商把HBM 做薄，同样产能可以交付更高的Bit，也增加了供给侧的风险。

长期看，存储行业作为半导体行业里波动最大、周期性最强的一个板块，一定会是一个巨大的做空机会，只是 timing 和做空方式的问题。

也不必过度关注周期顶部的估值和基本面。周期股在周期顶部往往估值最便宜、基本面最好，但周期的股价拐点往往比基本面财务数字的拐点早一年到一年半，所以真正要看的是边际变化。

边际变化就是需求与供给之间的博弈，最先可以印证的其实就是价格。一旦价格滞涨，就说明供需逐渐平衡了，那个时候就是最佳的做空时机。

当然美股比较好的一点是可以用期权。如果对 timing 把握得好，期权可以用较小的风险带来更大的杠杆。后面我会分享用什么样的期权结构，能更好地增加整个做空交易的盈亏比

text:
我觉得很多人可能低估了 Agent 对 CPU 需求的拉动。过去两年，AI 基建的注意力几乎全在 GPU 上，但当 AI 真正开始替人干活，数据中心需要处理的事情也变了。

AMD 今天公布了专门面向 Agentic AI 的 Helion 机架方案，最高可以容纳 128 颗 EPYC Venice 处理器，合计 32,768 个 CPU 核心，计划在 2027 年上半年落地。

一个 Chatbot 主要消耗模型推理算力。一个 Agent 除了调用模型，还要启动沙箱、运行代码、操作浏览器、读写文件、执行工具，可能同时拉起十几个子 Agent。模型推理可以交给 GPU，大量实际执行工作仍然要靠 CPU。

如果未来每个人都有几个长期运行的 Agent，整个 AI 基础设施的 CPU/GPU 配比可能都要重新计算。

AMD 还有一条值得关注的路线，就是模型路由。根据任务的复杂程度、性能要求和成本，动态决定调用哪个模型，让简单任务尽量使用便宜的算力。

过去 AI 基建的核心指标是每秒能生成多少 Token。随着 Agent 普及，企业会越来越关心完成一个任务究竟需要多少钱。

这意味着 GPU 之外的 CPU、内存、网络和模型调度都可能重新获得定价权。

AMD 显然已经开始按照这个方向布局了。下一轮 AI 基建竞争，可能比单纯的 GPU 性能大战复杂得多。

近期的美股就是在被不断调教：
1）昨天盘前报道说美军已经做好准备川普要在中期选举前升级再动手，盘前油价上行长债收益率也上行，市场都在跌。

2）刚高兴没几分钟，盘中金融时报报道OpenAI最新投资人文件显示，截至9月底年化收入“接近500亿美元”，远低于上月底多家外媒根据投资人信息报出的约700亿美元。这对市场来说比美债收益率飙升还要可怕，继续跌；

然后今天盘后大家开始回过神来，数字差异来自此前投资者试图把OpenAI数字“调平”以便与Anthropic直接比较——Anthropic把通过AWS、Google Cloud等云伙伴产生的销售收入全额计入（再把分成记为成本），OpenAI通常只计自身份额/直接收入。（这么看openai对arr数字的口径比anthropic严格很多）
看CNBC今天最新的报道。所以看今天指数期货走势还是很强的。

3）所幸昨晚30年美债收益率拍卖结果很好https://t.co/YdNxNDDIQV。美国国内和海外资金申购热情比较高，结合前天晚上10年美债拍卖结果也很好，在当下的收益率水平、资金还是愿意去买美债的而不是等更高收益率，很大程度上缓解了债市对收益率狂飙的担忧，这就带来了长债收益率回落。

quoted_text:
Ledger theft, day two. Since yesterday the thief has pushed ether through Tornado Cash three times, and each time on into Zcash's shielded pool. We followed every lot out the far side. Here is how, step by step.

1. THE SAME BUILD, THREE TIMES
An ether wallet pays a fresh splitter. The splitter pays four fresh wallets. The four drop it into Tornado Cash's 100, 10 and 1 ETH pools. Minutes, every time.

Run 1, yesterday 15:17: 1,254 ETH. Run 2, today 09:42: 1,291 ETH. Run 3, today 11:56: 450 ETH from 0xfa4EaBB840A33C156E600311433AE261CBfCb0e2, in the pools by 12:15.

2. OUT OF TORNADO CASH
The mixer breaks the link between a deposit and a withdrawal. We do not need the link. Our tooling fingerprints the withdrawal transactions themselves: how each one is constructed, who constructs it, and when. 

Yesterday's 65 withdrawals (1,084 ETH) and today's 96 (1,726 ETH) all carry the same signature. The six other withdrawals from those pools in today's windows do not. Run 3 came out from 12:18 into 0x0d697aa182801566d87adc86e68e95fd3b2f5f82 (213 ETH) and 0x676b16cc18542f37d202a1a79ac05463395496a4 (122 ETH), and 195 ETH of it was inside a cross-chain swap service by 12:38. Forty-two minutes, end to end.

3. INTO ZCASH, AND OUT AGAIN
The swap service turns the ether into shielded ZEC, where sender, amount and recipient vanish. But the service's own shielding of each lot is public, and from it we derive a value signature for that lot's exit, then scan every transparent exit from the pool. 108 of 108 exits across both days match their lot to the zatoshi. Not one other exit from the pool does. 

First lot today: in at 10:18:18, out at 11:06:16 in block 3512847 (8d26a9b095d4d28373527f7a6eb81a3be7f906d1e2190960c0512ff64f369418 and 738c6d1261e79766e4dd16bdbd38dced91b8e3a86ce41dcda83eda1f19208fbf), straight into a ZEC to USDC order.

Today so far: 20 lots ordered (2,379 ZEC, $2.9m), 14 out, 5 inside the pool, 1 still settling. Every exit feeds a ZEC to USDC order paying two wallets born at 11:11, 22 of the 28 paid by 12:43:
0x816D5Ee17DB1495d1409F135b98FF3edc5F3cDf8: 940,561 USDC
0xBA736A4b616e79867B6d586293966b552883f3F3: 852,258 USDC
1.79m USDC, unspent. @Circle can freeze it.

(1/2) 🧵⤵️

text:
Become a Millionaire With Just $8 a Day

Let me tell you something I wish every young person understood when they get their first job.

You don’t have to come from a rich family to become a millionaire. You don’t need a six-figure salary. And you don’t need to be a genius at picking stocks.

Sometimes, you just need to start early and make a few sacrifices.

Think about someone who starts working at 18, earning minimum wage. I know money is tight when you’re starting out. You want your coffee, your favorite cookies, maybe a pack of cigarettes. You want to enjoy the little things in life. I get it.

But what if you took a few of those dollars and invested them instead?

Open a Roth IRA. Invest in a low-cost index fund. Let your money work for you while you work for your paycheck.

Let’s look at the math.

Imagine you’re 18 years old. You invest about $8 a day, or roughly $245 a month, and keep doing it until you’re 65.

Assuming an average annual return of 7%, here’s what could happen:

Your total contributions: About $138,000.
Your investment growth: About $862,000.
Your retirement balance: Approximately $1 million.

Read that again. You put in around $138,000 over 47 years, and compound growth could do the rest.

Of course, 7% is an assumption, not a guarantee. The market goes up and down, and inflation will reduce the purchasing power of that million dollars. But the lesson remains the same: starting early gives your money decades to grow.

One important detail: a Roth IRA has annual contribution limits and eligibility rules. For 2026, the standard IRA contribution limit is $7,500, provided you have enough eligible earned income and meet the applicable requirements. Our example requires about $2,940 a year, so it fits within that limit under current rules. Contribution limits can change over time.

And here’s the beautiful part. You don’t need to start with $245 a month if you can’t afford it. Start with $20 a week. Start with $5. Build the habit, and increase your contributions as your income grows.

I’m not telling you to stop enjoying life. I’m saying that sometimes the small decisions we make today can change our lives tomorrow.

That coffee won’t make you poor. Those cookies won’t ruin your future. But spending every dollar you earn without putting anything aside can leave you working your whole life with very little to show for it.

Pay yourself first. Invest consistently. Give compound interest time to work.

You may not control how much money you make at 18. But you can start building the habits that give you more choices at 65.

You don’t have to be rich to start investing.

Sometimes, you just have to start.

text:
宜信停兑四个月后，承认可能资不抵债

5月22日全面停兑，10月11日发致歉信承认可能资不抵债，10月12日警方立案侦查。
四个月，从“良性清退”到刑事立案。

1｜警方通报
10月12日，北京市公安局朝阳分局发布警情通报：近期依法对宜信相关公司涉嫌违法犯罪立案侦查。实际控制人唐某（男，53岁）、赵某（女，51岁）等多名犯罪嫌疑人已被采取刑事强制措施。

2｜停兑与致歉：300亿，10万人
5月22日起，宜信全面停止旗下类固收产品兑付，启动所谓“良性清退”，涉资约300亿元，影响近10万名高净值客户。
10月11日，通过瑞承、宜人优选App向投资者定向推送致歉信，承认产品实质违约。经第三方清产核资，初步发现集团可能资不抵债，偿债缺口较大。底层资产质量差，市场化整体处置无果。

3｜这家公司投过什么？
宜信创始人唐宁，旗下宜人智科曾登陆纽交所，是中国互联网金融海外上市第一股。
但宜信真正值得看的，是它在一级市场的投资布局。
宜信产业基金投过Marqeta、老虎证券、Tradeshift、Upgrade。
2019年，宜信作为当时唯一的中国资方，参与了德国保险科技公司wefox的1.25亿美元B轮融资。它还联手贝恩资本参与了以色列生物识别公司BioCatch的1.45亿美元C轮。
通过宜信财富母基金，它还间接投了依图科技、蓝箭航天、药明康德、美团、Bilibili、饿了么等超过3000家企业。
这些投资履历，放在任何一家VC面前都不算难看。

4｜时间线压缩的速度
类固收停兑→资不抵债自认→刑事立案，时间线压缩在四个月之内。
原以为“良性清退”能体面收场，结果从致歉信到警方通报，只隔了一天。

UPDATE: I can confirm that the Ledger supply chain is compromised in Europe as well. @Ledger should initiate an immediate product recall to protect users.

I just purchased a second device from a different Mediamarkt location today, recorded the unboxing process, and discovered spyware once again (video linked in the second tweet).

The device was compromised in the exact same manner, featuring identical modifications (such as additional cables and an LTE module). This indicates its a widespread issue rather than an isolated incident, potentially affecting Ledger inventory across MediaMarkt and Saturn stores throughout Europe (comprising over 1,000 stores across 11 countries).

My initial hypothesis was that these devices were returns that looked unopened to the employees and were just sold again as new however, a MediaMarkt employee confirmed that the device I purchased was not a return, and that returned Ledgers are sent directly back to the manufacturer rather than resold.

Store records show the inventory originated from Aqipa GmbH. While Ledger's CTO was unsure if Aqipa serves as the direct distributor between Ledger and MediaMarkt, it appears to be the case. Given that Aqipa distributes across Europe, any physical retail store receiving stock through them may be at risk.

I sent the first ledger to mark and the second one is going to ledger now, so that they can analyse it.
If you purchased a ledger from anyone other than the official ledger store, make sure to check your device!!

text:
The recent hardware wallet supply-chain attack have raised a question of how much the design of a hardware wallet contributes to its security.

The reported attack didn't require breaking the secure element. It's a reminder that even when a secure element does its job, other components can introduce vulnerabilities.

When we designed Solflare Shield, we made a deliberate decision: keep the hardware as simple as possible, without compromising its core purpose.

Shield is a card-sized hardware wallet built around a secure element, with only the components necessary to protect private keys and authorize cryptographic operations.

1. Keeping the hardware minimal

Hardware components beyond the secure element can create additional opportunities for attackers, particularly when they introduce new interfaces or communication channels.
Shield has no screen, display interface, battery, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, or cellular modem. It's a passive NFC card that draws power from your phone during a tap.
This eliminates certain classes of hardware attacks, including the specific display interception mechanism.

2. Separating the wallet experience from key protection

Shield is designed to work with the Solflare app rather than operate as a standalone device. The app handles the interface and prepares transactions, while Shield's EAL6+ secure element performs cryptographic signing internally.
The tradeoff is that your phone acts as the screen. The recovery phrase is shown once in the Solflare app during setup, and transactions are reviewed there before you tap.
After setup, your private key stays on the card and is never stored on your phone or in the Solflare app.
This separation keeps the physical hardware focused on protecting keys and authorizing transactions, without requiring additional components to support the user interface.

3. Reducing supply-chain exposure

Hardware security also depends on what happens between manufacturing and delivery.
Shield is sold exclusively through the official Solflare Shop, without an authorized reseller network or third-party retail distribution.
Additional protections, including cryptographic authenticity verification, safeguards against unauthorized software replacement, and tamper-evident packaging, are designed to reduce the risk of compromised devices reaching users.
These measures reduce certain risks, but no distribution model or security mechanism can completely eliminate the possibility of physical tampering.

Security is a series of design decisions

Sophisticated attacks are a reminder that protecting private keys requires looking at the entire device, its components, and the supply chain behind it.

Different hardware wallets make different design tradeoffs, and no architecture is immune to every threat.

With Shield, we chose to prioritize simplicity, minimize unnecessary components and keep the hardware focused on protecting your keys.

GREG JENSEN: THE BUBBLE IS AHEAD OF US, NOT BEHIND US.

Greg Jensen, Chief investment officer of @Bridgewater recently explained why he spent the last several years telling people the AI bubble had not arrived yet, and why the capex involved does not behave like a normal cycle.

According to Jensen, the question of whether this is a bubble has been asked more or less continuously since the ChatGPT moment. His answer was that a bubble would come, but we were nowhere near that phase yet. We were in the phase where people had no idea what was hitting them, meaning how important this was and how much was going to be invested.

The reason is the identity of the spenders. According to Jensen, when the people making these decisions include Elon Musk, Sam Altman and Google, you are dealing with parties whose existing businesses are threatened and who believe the power to control Earth and the universe is a couple of years away. They are not motivated by the normal profit incentives that govern a typical cycle.

That is why he does not think this is a capex cycle like other capex cycles. The money is going to get spent regardless.

Jensen says he was thinking this in 2022 and 2023. The buildout happens. Maybe someday the path is proven to be a dead end, but according to Jensen, we are so far from any possibility of that being established that the data centers get built and the semiconductors get used in the meantime.

The implication for anyone sizing this is that conventional capex discipline is the wrong lens. Spending driven by existential threat and a belief in a very short timeline does not respond to the signals that normally slow a cycle down.

text:
徐总 @star_okx 您这个 @HyperliquidX “对做市商更友好” 的说法，容易误导为 Hyperliquid 偏袒做市商

我代表疯人院 @hl_madhouse 展开补充

手段和目的 - 要看到实际 Jeff @chameleon_jeff 从第一性原理出发的设计目标，是保护终端用户（尤其是零售/non-toxic flow），通过系统性降低 toxic flow 来改善整体流动性质量

1️⃣
最直接的 - 推荐阅读 2024年 1月 jeff 长文
《Latency and tx ordering on Hyperliquid》

https://t.co/FF19mGqtLJ

Hyperliquid 确实会优先处理撤单和 post-only 订单，再处理 GTC、IOC 等主动成交订单。这会降低做市商被 HFT 吃单者抢先成交的概率

“做市商风险下降”不是“做市商获得特权”

完整的因果链是：

撤单优先 → 降低做市商的 adverse selection → 做市商敢于报更窄的价差、更深的盘口 → 终端用户获得更好的成交

举个简单例子：

做市商在 100 美元附近挂出了卖单，但市场突然快速上涨到 103 美元。做市商判断原来的报价已经过时，于是发送撤单；与此同时，HFT taker 试图抢在撤单之前，以 100 美元买入

在普通的 first-come-first-served 机制下，如果 taker 先到，做市商可能被成交。这对做市商来说是一次典型的 adverse selection：做市商以明显落后于市场的新价格完成了交易

长期下来，做市商只能扩大价差、减少挂单，最终表现为：

◾️ 买卖价差扩大；
◾️ 盘口深度下降；
◾️ 波动期间滑点变高；
◾️ 终端用户的交易成本上升

Hyperliquid 的 cancel-first 机制，让已经提交的撤单优先执行，使过时报价能够及时退出订单簿。MM 因此可以更有信心地提供流动性，而最终受益的是交易用户

-

2️⃣
甚至更早 - 推荐阅读 2023年 6月
jeff 就讨论过类似问题：

https://t.co/UBhgfT1I91

Jeff 当时把 toxic flow 定义为 information-dominated flow，并不是说所有 taker 都是有毒流量，而是指那些凭借信息和速度优势，专门挑选做市商过时报价的交易者

MM 可能在 99% 的交易中赚取 1 个基点，但只要剩下 1% 的交易亏损 10 个基点，就足以吞掉大部分日常收益。长期下来，做市商只能提高报价、减少流动性，最终承担成本的还是普通用户

所以，Hyperliquid 的设计并不是简单地偏袒 maker，而是在降低 adverse selection：

减少 toxic flow → 做市商敢于提供更积极的报价 → 盘口更深、价差更窄 → 终端用户获得更好的执行

Jeff 也没有把 maker 和 taker 简单划分成好坏。Taker 同样参与价格发现，也为市场提供流动性转换。真正需要被限制的，是那些专门攻击过时订单、让交易失去双方自愿性的交易流

3️⃣
最后一点，2026 年 4月 Hyperliquid 引入的 priority fee，也能进一步说明它并不是简单地偏袒做市商

Priority fee 允许交易者为更快的排序支付费用，但它只能影响同一类订单之间的排序，不能让 taker 越过已经提交的撤单

也就是说，主动成交者可以为交易紧迫性付费，但不能通过付费去抢先成交一个做市商已经决定撤掉的过时报价

说明 Hyperliquid 并不是反对 taker，也不是无条件保护 maker。它允许正常的速度竞争和价格发现，但把最容易伤害市场质量的 toxic flow 隔离开来

-

所以更准确的总结应该是：

Hyperliquid 牺牲了一部分低质量的 HFT 交易量，换取更稳定的流动性和更好的终端用户体验

「
—— 手段和目的
保护做市商是手段
改善用户成交才是目的
」

㊗️ @okx 越来越合规
和 Hyperliquid 一起做大永续合约蛋糕

Hyperliquid

text:
Brent依旧是笼罩在全球金融市场上的阴霾，并且带来的副作用——高利率回归已经逐渐影响金融市场流动性，于此同时，地缘战争潜在风险也逐步扩大

中国有句老话，物极必反，真的希望在地缘、宏观与金融环境恶劣的当下，可以迎来一个翻转的契机

本周，高油价+高通胀预期效果叠加，对风险市场将会是又一次考验，目前局势很简单，特朗普在尝试用俄乌能源停火为自己留下60天与伊朗博弈的空间

逻辑非常简单，泽连斯基暂时妥协，俄罗斯如果相信答应60天能源停火对外输出柴油环节全球高油价，一旦Brent下跌，跌的越多，对特朗普来说就有足有谈判空间与时间对伊朗进行更多的军事与外交施压，尝试达到他想要的目的

但是，套路非常直白与简单，俄罗斯是否会为了赚钱答应60天能源停火？当然估计普京也清楚，一旦伊朗问题别解决，与乌克兰的暂时停火也就到头了，所以普京在接收到条件后至今并未表态

另一方面，就算普京同意，俄罗斯输出一定的柴油，Brent 的价格真的可以顺利下跌，短期能否跌破95美元给特朗普预留空间吗？要知道资本市场对原油的定价目前复杂因素较多，并非特朗普在简单靠含量嗓子就能操作的时候了

同时，伊朗也并不闲着，直接将特朗普的计划公之于众，并且顺势反客为主把美国向俄罗斯求援视为霍尔木兹海峡危机仍然存在，让美国在外交舆论上处于被动阶段。

其实最近两周其实可以看出，美伊双方短期真的不想让战火重燃，经济与民生都是无法承受的，只能选择外交博弈，嘴炮模式，甚至借助代理人战争继续施压，但是私下动作上也都没闲着，以打促谈始终贯彻本次美伊战争，从未改变啊！

对于风险市场来说，周三的9月CPI并未公布前，Brent的不断反弹，必然会让市场更加担忧通胀与加息，风险市场始终要被压制，唯一的幸运是当市场风险处于明面的时候，暂时不用担心黑天鹅！

10月12日—10月18日全球宏观指引：通胀重新审判！CPI决定12月加息，能源与债市争夺全球定价权，科技股Q3财报季启动！

上周宏观核心：Fed暂停加息之后，为什么长债收益率还是降不下来！？

本周宏观核心：如果CPI重新反弹，长端高利率到底是“提前预警”？还是已经过度定价？！

本周宏观逻辑链：

中东能源风险仍高 + 俄乌能源停火出现可能→Brent / 柴油 重新定价→9月CPI + PPI验证通胀与零售数据验证→10月暂停还是意外加息 / 12月是否加息→US2Y重新定价Fed政策→US10Y/30Y验证长期通胀、财政与期限溢价→美元 + 黄金 + 美股AI + BTC定价调整→全球流动性重新分配

关注的重点，能源通胀、内生通胀、长端利率，三者是否会形成共振对风险市场进行压制！

第一主线：CPI重新定价成为本周的加息裁判！

上周沃勒给出了一个比较清晰的Fed政策框架——未来可能仍然需要加息，但是没必要每次会议连续加息！

这让市场开始预期10月暂停加息，12月继续加息的可能性，截止目前，10月加息概率19.4%，12月加息概率进入70%

所以本周的关注的Fed政策已经从10月加不加息变成12月加不加息，当然，依旧不能排除10月小概率加息的可能性，这要看宏观数据侧给出什么答案

1, 10月14日周三，9月CPI数据，

目前根据市场主流预期，9月CPI 名义年率3.7%，月率0.6%属于通胀反弹预期，而核心CPI年率2.5%，核心月率0.2%

按照这个预期，意味着通胀受外部能源价格影响出现反弹，但是核心通胀温和，算是一个中性乐观数据，所以本次CPI关注的不仅仅是数据本身，更要看能源、核心商品、核心服务对名义CPI与核心CPI的影响

如果名义CPI上涨，核心CPI与服务业数据下降，对于目前市场预期反而不是鹰派而是鸽派。如果三者集体上涨，则是超预期的鹰派！预示着美国经济正在遭受能源高价带来的内生通胀叠加问题。

2，CPI之后还要看PPI数据是否形成相互验证，验证企业成本是否跟名义通胀同步

此前的PMI数据已经显示出企业投入成本增加，这意味着供应链上游产业已经承担通胀压力，接下来就看这份压力有多少传导给企业，如果CPI与PPI同步上涨，意味着通胀验证完整，注意通胀预期抬头

反之，如果CPI上涨，PPI下降，则意味着过去通胀受能源影响，未来通胀压力未必恶化，可以暂缓目前市场的通胀压力。

3，零售数据收尾，但是本周的零售如果太强反而是毒药！

过去市场是担心就业太热，但是此前的非农数据调整口径让就业温度下降，从而让Fed继续加息的窗口按下了暂停键

但是如果本周名义CPI继续走强，核心CPI保持粘性，在通胀没有有效下降的前提下，消费数据过热，可能会增加通胀预期的尾部风险，让市场继续担忧通胀

本周其实对于市场最温和的数据就是核心CPI下降，PPI下降，零售数据下降，就业继续保持低速增长，这份数据不会进一步推高12月加息概率，并且在11月份10月CPI数据继续下降可能会削弱Fed下一次加息的概率

第二主线：能源定价逻辑更加复杂，俄乌突然加入全球能源定价！

昨天特朗普率先明确俄乌能源停火达成，泽连斯基则配合表示如果达成能源停火可以举行大选，但是俄罗斯方面至今并未表态

很显然，特朗普在谋划一个60天的能源缓冲，用俄罗斯能源输出来压制伊朗的谈判筹码，但是这60天之内如果特朗普搞定伊朗，俄乌可能会重新回归战火。

本周要关注两个重点，俄罗斯是否与乌克兰达成能源停火，其次在能源停火之后看资本市场对于Brent的定价是否同步，如果Brent 能够有效跌破100美元甚至95美元下方，将会对冲本周的通胀担忧

当然，最乐观的局面是美伊达成协议+俄乌能源停火，对Brent 将会有很大的利空效果，但是这个可能性太低了，个人不做太多乐观预期。

第三主线：债市收益率对市场的压制逐渐明显!

沃什曾经表示目前金融环境不够收紧，但是目前可以看出，虽然10月加息概率降低，但是长债收益率依旧对金融流动性形成了压制与收紧效果，

而上周末的 #Bitcoin 下跌，美系资金净流出，本周一的韩国股市下跌，其实都有金融流动性收紧的作用在里面

加息也好，债市高利率也好，并不会直接形成利空大量抛压，但是对市场的影响是潜移默化的，流动性差就像是一个利空情绪放大器，任何不利，甚至市场信心稍微下滑，都会导致风险资产遭受节奏性抛售

而本周的债市收益率定价，更是可以与CPI数据进行结合，看市场如何对通胀进行定价

最好的预期，CPI下降，2Y 10Y 30Y 收益率同步下降，意味着加息预期下降，通胀担忧放缓，利好风险资产

普通鹰派，CPI上涨，2Y上涨，10Y 30Y下降，短期加息概率依旧在计价，但是中长期通胀担忧在放缓，对市场也算友好

危险鹰派：CPI上涨，2Y 10Y 30Y 收益率上涨，加息预期增加，且10Y 30Y收益率与Fed 政策出现脱轨，债市在对财政赤字、国债供给、期限溢价、长期通胀进行复杂定价，对风险资产利空

另外，黄金依旧可以视为美国债市的温度计当做观察重点

一般长端利率上涨会压制黄金走势，甚至利空，如果长端收益率上涨黄金下跌，属于常规定价走势，如果黄金与债市收益率同步上涨，就要警惕债市风险增加，金融避险逻辑出现！ 这里尤其要看黄金VS 30Y的走势是否出现同步。

另外，印度已经完成4年来首次加息，高利率已经不再是美国自己的故事，而成为全球共识，如果后续这个共识继续加强，形成加息周期回归的共振，对风险市场更是不利。

第四主线：AI与美股财报重新进入宏观框架

本周美股Q3财报季正式开始，目前主流机构预测，标普500公司Q3的盈利预期整体可以达到30%，而AI与大型云服务商资本开支仍然是支撑核心

但是目前宏观环境并不好，资金面临艰难选择，AI股的盈利增长VS 超过5%的无风险利率，在这个影响下，会限制财报利好带来的效果，也是估值要面临的终极问题，企业想要让资金为自己的估值买单，就要拿出更好的业绩，所以Q3财报季是AI股的分化阶段

所以，Q3财报面临更多的挑战，不再是财报好就一定利好，而是要看当下财报+未来预期双重定价给市场多少信心

本周财报关注点：美国大型银行股，台积电与阿斯麦，这些股票在Q2财报季开始表现非常不错，看本周是否可以延续好财报，再看财报公布后市场是否为股价与估值买单，就可以判断Q3财报季度的严苛成都

这里台积电与阿斯麦关注 AI订单、资本开支、先进制程需求、数据中心需求，包含现在与未来预期。而银行股的财报决定金融条件是否支持未来AI企业加速发展

所以本周的财报要解决三个问题

a，盈利能否覆盖资本开支
b，产业链需求是否健康且具备潜力
c，AI资本开始是否继续增长，上游提供资金的银行金融流动性是否充足

如果全部给出满意答案，那么本周的美股可以有效对抗高利率环境，但是其中任何一个出现异常情况，都要警惕高利率对AI股的压制

本周总结：

本周重点看能否解决三大问题

a，CPI能不能证明美国内生通胀正在下降？
b，Fed暂停以后，10Y/30Y到底能不能下来？
c，两场战争能不能同时降低能源风险？

目前个人预期，a大概率会乐观一点，但是b问题可能会更加复杂，c问题短期不报太多乐观。

对于风险资产来说，数据+财报利好，涨幅会因为高收益率受限，限制上涨空间，反之如果数据+财报利空，则可能会扩大回调幅度

当然，如果可以在11月3日中期选举前在杀一波估值，我反而觉得是好事！

text:
Finding alpha on the short side isn't as hard as you might think, but if you are starting out, here are some rules to follow: 

1. MYTH: "You can only make 100% on a short but you can lose infinite percent". WRONG. This is only true if you don't rebalance, but that's f*cking stupid, so always trim/add to get to your target weight. You can make/lose infinite percent on a short if you rebalance. 

2. A short book needs more diversification than a long book. One heuristic to follow is no more than 5% of your portfolio in a single short idea. (Ignore the heuristic if you know how to build an actual risk model). Things can and will go up 300% in your face very quickly. 

3. Don't short things that are going up. Sounds obvious. Don't: short the hot thing that makes new highs every day. Something being "overvalued" is not a good reason to short. Do: short the boring thing that's been crumbling for a decade. 

4. Generally speaking most asset classes go up over time, so even if you have a short book you probably want your portfolio to be net long for the best returns. 

All 4 of these rules are empirically backtestable 🙂

text:
UPDATE: I can confirm that the Ledger supply chain is compromised in Europe as well. @Ledger should initiate an immediate product recall to protect users.

I just purchased a second device from a different Mediamarkt location today, recorded the unboxing process, and discovered spyware once again (video linked in the second tweet).

The device was compromised in the exact same manner, featuring identical modifications (such as additional cables and an LTE module). This indicates its a widespread issue rather than an isolated incident, potentially affecting Ledger inventory across MediaMarkt and Saturn stores throughout Europe (comprising over 1,000 stores across 11 countries).

My initial hypothesis was that these devices were returns that looked unopened to the employees and were just sold again as new however, a MediaMarkt employee confirmed that the device I purchased was not a return, and that returned Ledgers are sent directly back to the manufacturer rather than resold.

Store records show the inventory originated from Aqipa GmbH. While Ledger's CTO was unsure if Aqipa serves as the direct distributor between Ledger and MediaMarkt, it appears to be the case. Given that Aqipa distributes across Europe, any physical retail store receiving stock through them may be at risk.

I sent the first ledger to mark and the second one is going to ledger now, so that they can analyse it.
If you purchased a ledger from anyone other than the official ledger store, make sure to check your device!!

quoted_text:
The recent hardware wallet supply-chain attack have raised a question of how much the design of a hardware wallet contributes to its security.

The reported attack didn't require breaking the secure element. It's a reminder that even when a secure element does its job, other components can introduce vulnerabilities.

When we designed Solflare Shield, we made a deliberate decision: keep the hardware as simple as possible, without compromising its core purpose.

Shield is a card-sized hardware wallet built around a secure element, with only the components necessary to protect private keys and authorize cryptographic operations.

1. Keeping the hardware minimal

Hardware components beyond the secure element can create additional opportunities for attackers, particularly when they introduce new interfaces or communication channels.
Shield has no screen, display interface, battery, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, or cellular modem. It's a passive NFC card that draws power from your phone during a tap.
This eliminates certain classes of hardware attacks, including the specific display interception mechanism.

2. Separating the wallet experience from key protection

Shield is designed to work with the Solflare app rather than operate as a standalone device. The app handles the interface and prepares transactions, while Shield's EAL6+ secure element performs cryptographic signing internally.
The tradeoff is that your phone acts as the screen. The recovery phrase is shown once in the Solflare app during setup, and transactions are reviewed there before you tap.
After setup, your private key stays on the card and is never stored on your phone or in the Solflare app.
This separation keeps the physical hardware focused on protecting keys and authorizing transactions, without requiring additional components to support the user interface.

3. Reducing supply-chain exposure

Hardware security also depends on what happens between manufacturing and delivery.
Shield is sold exclusively through the official Solflare Shop, without an authorized reseller network or third-party retail distribution.
Additional protections, including cryptographic authenticity verification, safeguards against unauthorized software replacement, and tamper-evident packaging, are designed to reduce the risk of compromised devices reaching users.
These measures reduce certain risks, but no distribution model or security mechanism can completely eliminate the possibility of physical tampering.

Security is a series of design decisions

Sophisticated attacks are a reminder that protecting private keys requires looking at the entire device, its components, and the supply chain behind it.

Different hardware wallets make different design tradeoffs, and no architecture is immune to every threat.

With Shield, we chose to prioritize simplicity, minimize unnecessary components and keep the hardware focused on protecting your keys.

After recording 250M+ Trace receipts, DATA’s next big challenge is turning all that activity into a stronger AI data business.

That’s why @datafdn’s planned move to Sui makes sense.

It could free the team to focus on what AI labs actually pay for: useful training data with clear rights and verifiable origins.

DATA began as Story Protocol, pursuing a broad vision for programmable intellectual property. In June, it narrowed its focus to AI training data, with Trace as its flagship audit product.

Now its infrastructure strategy is following that sharper focus.

Running an independent Layer 1 means maintaining blockchain software, coordinating upgrades, and supporting validator infrastructure. Those responsibilities draw on the same resources needed to improve products and win customers.

One team. Two demanding jobs.

For DATA, the strongest source of value is connecting data supply, permissions, and verification into something buyers can use with confidence.

Trace helps buyers inspect records of data origins, consent, licensing terms, and payment status, while keeping the underlying content confidential.

As I said before, DATA reports 250M+ receipts recorded by Trace.

The planned division of work is straightforward:

- Sui → shared blockchain infrastructure for DATA’s protocol

- Walrus → the planned default storage layer for DATA Foundation apps, suited to large files like images and video

- Trace → the audit and provenance product DATA can keep evolving around its specific market

The wider Sui stack also offers Seal for access control and Nautilus for verifiable offchain compute, giving DATA additional building blocks as implementation progresses.

The efficiency thesis is simple: Better resource allocation.

If shared infrastructure reduces the burden of maintaining a standalone chain, more engineering effort can go toward better verification tools, smoother integrations, and broader adoption.

Sui Foundation’s announced $30M investment adds institutional commitment to that direction. The partnership also gives Sui’s infrastructure a substantial data supply to support.

Execution still matters. Migration takes work, shared infrastructure comes with tradeoffs, and DATA will depend on another ecosystem. The efficiency gains need to become tangible.

The transition is still ahead. $DATA remains the protocol token, nothing changes immediately for holders, and more migration details will follow.

I think this is a credible comeback strategy both for DATA and SUI where both can apply the lessons from the broader experiment and concentrate resources where the product has the clearest purpose.

author: david_enim
quoted_text:
Mathematicians are not just hoarding credit for puzzle answers. They build understanding. When a major proof appears, the author normally explains it, defends it, gives talks, answers questions, finds the key ideas, helps others use it, and turns it into new research directions. If the "solver" is an AI pipeline operated by people who cannot explain the result, the community gets the worst version of progress: priority claims without responsibility.

The actual harm is not that AI helped solve something. If AI produced correct, understandable, checkable mathematics, mathematicians would eventually use it. The harm is flooding a field with alleged solutions while bypassing the human process that turns proofs into knowledge. It creates a backlog of expert review, discourages people from sharing open directions, lets shallow operators claim priority over work they do not understand, and converts researchers into janitors for machine slop.

This is not like a cancer researcher crying because a cure was found. It is more like a company dumping hundreds of unverified drug candidates, announcing that cancer has been "massacred," and then mocking oncologists for asking for trials, mechanisms, evidence, and accountability.

And honestly, the glee here is not even pro-science.  It's just plain misanthropy.  These people seem less excited that knowledge might advance and more excited that some class of humans might be humiliated, displaced, or made irrelevant. Did human beings hurt their feelings so badly that they now need a machine to avenge them against every profession that still values human expertise?

text:
《2049跑会总结 - 行业发展篇》

这次去 TOKEN2049前，我给自己定了一个很重要的目标。

就是尽可能多地和行业内不同层级的参与者，尤其是那些经历过多个周期、有长期积累的资深玩家们，进行一些真正深入的交流。

我想搞清楚几个问题：

👉现在的行业究竟处于什么阶段？
👉币圈到底还能不能继续往前走，还是不是朝阳行业？
👉接下来未来的机会可能在哪里？
👉还值不值得年轻人进入从业？
👉散户还能不能普遍赚到钱？
👉以及，我们这些在行业里待了很多年的人，未来还能不能期待像过去一样大块掘金？

这次我分别和一些资深 VC 小伙伴、非常成功的项目 Founder、老KOL、KOL Agency，以及交易所的朋友进行了深度交流，每次交流基本都在一个小时以上。

时间和资源有限，我聊到的大概70%是华人，30%是欧美老外（以及一位欧美项目中的日本小伙伴）。

有意思的是，大家对于未来的判断存在着不小的分歧。我想先把这些不同的观点摆出来，再谈谈自己的感受。

毕竟，与其只寻找支持自己判断的声音，不如先看看大家究竟在争论什么。

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

悲观派, 这一派朋友的核心判断是：

币圈的暴利时代可能正在结束

1、合规
任何一个行业都不可能永远繁荣，都会经历艰辛的萌芽期->蹒跚的孩童期->锐意进取大刀阔斧的青年期->沉稳但略显无趣的成年期->暮色沉沉走向没落的老年期。

加密行业早已走过了早期黑暗森林野蛮生长的阶段，主旋律必然是合规化，合规的结果必然是因为规则不明，管控不严而带来的各种bug红利被补上，普通小白集体暴富窗口缩小。

今天的加密货币市场已经大到了不可能再被各国政府忽视的程度。随着时间推移，各国的监管、税务和法律部门对于加密货币的运作方式越来越了解。欧美各国对加密税收已经日趋成熟，对CEX牌照的管控也越来越像传统金融靠拢。

这会造成几个必然结果：
1、曾经CEX们通过互联网没有门槛可以不管不顾可以把各国散户吸入自己的场子里交易抽水，但现在大所们在发达国家都已经开始按部就班的遵循相关法规，Travel Rule，合约倍数，衍生品准入门槛等都在给曾经盲目冲入的资金降温。

2、敢于拉盘攒局的人和资金会减少。
说起暴富，我很难忘记曾经的LUNA和SBF时期的FTX，一个帮皇马造就了单人8亿美金纸面财富又竹篮打水一场空的奇迹，另一个通过左脚踏右脚，借助用户资金把早期的Solana生态拉上天。

为什么美股基本不会出现这样的案例，正是因为严格的合规管控。

曾经有大量黑灰资金进入币圈一定程度上促进了crypto的阶段性大繁荣，比如曾经的旺汇资金，比如俄罗斯的赌场资金，被制裁国家的资金。这些钱在合规收紧的当下将很很难再进入池子里成为推高币价的推手。

2、传统资金进入Web3的渠道中断
很多人只看到山寨币跌了、Meme 不好玩了、散户不再接盘。但如果往更深一层看，会发现过去几年支撑币圈繁荣的一套重要资金循环，正在逐渐失效。

上一轮流动性宽松之后，大量传统资金包括家办，基金都找到了一种相对合规的方式进入了加密行业：

那就是投资 Crypto VC。

这些传统资金并不需要自己去交易 Meme，也不需要直接参与各种链上投机，他们只需要把资金配置给加密基金。

VC 拿到钱以后，一部分可能配置 BTC、ETH 等主流资产，另一部分则投入一级市场。

项目方获得融资，招募团队、开发产品、进行市场推广、发放空投、对接交易所，最终项目上线，代币进入二级市场抛售，VC回笼资金。

这形成了一个相当完整的资金循环。

但是去年开始这套模式正在面临严重挑战。传统资金的出资人逐渐发现，投资 Crypto VC 的体验并不理想。

首先，投资周期很长，资金回收慢。其次，山寨币上市以后越来越难达到过去那种疯狂的估值，即便达到了，等他们能解锁的时候，也已经跌的没剩多少。更重要的是，散户已经不愿意继续为这些高估值项目买单。

当 VC 无法为出资人创造理想回报，新的募资自然会越来越困难。而当 VC 募不到钱，项目方也就很难再像过去那样获得源源不断的融资。

这是过去一年多时间，币圈大量VC关停离场(尤其是亚洲VC)的根本原因。

再加上 AI 浪潮，美股科技股的波动完全不输Crypto，吸引了大量资金和优秀创业者离开Web3去参与。 导致我们行业逐渐变成一个缺乏新增参与者、流动性稀缺的存量市场。

怎样重新让这些传统资金可以合法合规的回来，给行业重新输血，这可能才是当前市场最棘手的问题之一。

3、叙事缺乏创新
从短期看，币圈更大的问题在于，过去币圈最重要的造富环节之一 -- 山寨币叙事的共识已经瓦解，而继任者Meme也并没有好多少。

流动性匮乏后，DePIN、GameFi，以及许多曾经被寄予厚望的赛道也逐渐暴露出商业模式和真实收入上的问题。

最终导致散户不再相信山寨币，也不再相信那些听起来非常宏大的叙事，转而去支持“反华尔街”的Meme。

但Meme 曾经是反 VC 的武器，如今却也开始走向僵化，今天的 Meme，虽然摆脱了传统 VC 抱团发币、上所出货的模式，却又逐渐形成了另一套利益集团。

发币集团、喊单集团，以及各种相互绑定的小团体，开始主导越来越多的机会。普通散户想依靠早期参与或者个人认知，实现几倍甚至几十倍的收益，已经变得越来越困难。

前段时间Vtalik也说到，https://t.co/ealUYe7tVg 上的小团体通过持续发行 Meme，累计收割了超过一亿美元，玩Fomo的散户亏损比例超过90%。

无论具体案例如何，背后反映的问题是值得关注的：

曾经以公平、开放为卖点的 Meme 游戏，也在逐渐被新的利益结构所占据。

旧的游戏被打破，新的游戏又开始僵化，而我们还没能找到下一个能令人兴奋，让相对多散户们吃到红利，博弈没有那么激烈的新游戏模式。

~~~~~~~~~~

乐观派, 这一派朋友的核心判断是：

行业基本面好转肉眼可见，我们已经走出谷底。

虽然各自的表达方式有些不一样，但不少朋友赞同今天的币圈，可能很像 2019 年 ICO 泡沫破灭之后的状态。

当时，市场对于上一轮主流叙事（万物皆可ICO）的信任彻底崩塌。市面上没人任何新项目，老项目批量死亡，从业者不知道未来的方向在哪里，纷纷跳槽回金融行业和互联网。

整个行业看起来似乎没有一个能落地并持续产生收入的项目，也已经没有什么值得期待的东西。但结果是，接近一年的熊市里，孕育出了Defi这朵耀眼的花。

而现在，类似的事情正在重新发生。

其实这个感觉，我从去年就已经有了。当时市场开始下行，散户不再愿意为山寨币买单，反而 Meme 依然风行一时。

我那时候就觉得，行业可能需要经历一次比较彻底的出清。还专门写过一篇长推，谈 VC 抱团组局、项目上所砸盘已经让行业陷入了彻底的僵局，不知道谁能解开这个结，否则熊可能会来的很快。

后边Meme的崛起和币安Alpah的革新玩法把市场续命了大半年，一直到1011后市场流动性大幅萎缩，市场却经历了一个漫长的、逐步消亡的过程。

直到将近一年后的这次2049我才明显感觉到，市面上那些老项目已经被清理得差不多了。

能上所的早就上了，上不了所的很多也已经死掉了。

从这个角度来看，当前行业的萧条，未必是一件坏事。

它更像是一次漫长的排毒过程，而排毒是需要时间的。只有旧的东西逐渐退出市场，新的叙事和新的玩法才有机会真正成长起来。

所谓不破不立。

冬天来了以后，真正有生命力的东西，才有机会在下一个春天重新发芽。如果把时间维度拉长，我们或许可以更加理性地看待当前的市场环境，也更有耐心地等待下一次创新。

何况现在我们已经能看到有一些可以持续创造收益的，拥有稳定用户群体的项目存在了，别人很难再Diss加密货币就是个空中楼阁的大Ponzi。

关于悲观派提到的合规进程问题，乐观派的看法是，换个角度看 -- 

“加密货币被越来越多的国家接受，逐渐进入主流金融体系，这不正是我们这些早期参与者曾经梦寐以求的事情吗？”

回想很多年前，我们这些Crypto早期信仰者希望的是什么？

是加密货币能够真正被广泛使用。是越来越多的人了解区块链和数字资产。是加密货币不再只是一个小圈子里的游戏，而是能够进入真实世界的金融和商业体系。

现在，这些事情其实正在逐步发生，比如 @circle 和加密货币企业上市，不少交易所被主流金融机构投资，Hyperliquid被Trump提到，8200万台美国三星手机开始内嵌稳定币钱包，Robinhood和富途为用户提供加密货币交易入口。

这些看起来离我们每日赚钱Alpha有点远的虚头巴脑的利好在外部大环境改变，比如流动性重新宽松起来的时候，将很有可能成为更大量级用户涌入Crypto的基石。

正如同曾经我们不能仅仅因为风靡一时的ICO不再Work就认定行业完蛋了，我们也不能因为VC 发币模式不再 Work，Meme模式散户也难赚钱了就认定整个行业已经不行了。

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
其实还有不少内容，但我也不想过于长篇大佬，前面抛出的问题我回头再分开慢慢给出自己的思考答案。

只想说把时间维度拉长，以更加开放的心态去看待行业的发展，而不是用旧时代的游戏规则，去判断一个新时代是否还有未来。

这可能是我这次 TOKEN2049 和不同朋友交流之后，最值得继续思考的事情。

quoted_text:
《2049跑会总结 - 景气篇》

已经离开新加坡回到家了，高强度的几天见人沟通+连轴转连坐下来好好码字的时间都很少，只能不断挤压睡眠时间，导致昨天上飞机前Oura和Whoop都已经在提醒我出现了生病前的主要体征。

赶紧磕了两颗澳洲神药Panadol好好睡了一觉，终于活过来了，然后坐下来总结一下这趟新加坡之行的感触。

后续通过几个帖子来从不同的角度各方面记录一下感触。

这次先说会议景气度

在去2049前，一些KOL朋友跟我说可能本届2049不会有什么人和收获，毕竟虽然行情有点反弹但还没真的走出熊市，山寨和VC都完犊子了，行业看不到什么未来，所以还不如去跑韩国的会因为可以顺便玩玩+做个医美。

但我一直觉得token2049才是亚太区观察crypto景气程度最好的窗口，无论从签证便利性，2049多年积累的品牌影响力，新加坡对crypto的包容性以及常驻加密从业人员密度各方面看综合起来就是最佳的。

事实上也证明我的预判是对的。

几天下来，这次token2049虽然无法与两年前大牛市时烈火烹油时相比，但热闹程度肯定是超过了预期，最后连刚开始说不来的KOL都发现不对劲临时买票飞过来加入大部队😂😂😂

我眼中的大会景气程度大致可以从两方面看：
1、主会场和分会场的烧钱程度
2、私局的密度，质量

~~~~~~~~~~~~
先说主会场和分会场：

这次2049与之前相比主会场的变化是让我有点惊讶的，因为非但没有缩水，相反甚至规模更大了。

之前主会场只有2层，由各家分包，而这次光是 @SuiNetwork 一家就把原本是水泥毛胚的B2层全包了，自己装修布置，据说总开销超过500万美金。另一头Blockwork搞首届DAS Asia（面向机构的数字资产峰会）包了一楼的一半，每天花钱不会少于1M。

从会场参会人流情况看还是很多，甚至查票程度是以往以来最严，金沙Mall里背着各色品牌包包的人络绎不绝。

分会场（Side Events）的数量比过去两年的确是少了很多，很大程度是因为熊市洗礼和山寨叙事崩盘后大量VC撤出，攒局的金主爸爸少了，那么拿到VC钱可以烧市场的项目也随之减少，他们是分会场的主要host群体。

去年前年还有项目方为了人气挖空心思搞泳池Party等奢靡刺激的活动，今年大多就是吃个饭喝个小酒联络感情，顶多DJ打碟蹦一下，人不少，但预算肯定是减少了的😂😂

除了几个CEX 的side event保持了一致的高水准，有些热门项目人气还是很旺,比如 @HyperliquidX 的， @Polymarket 的， @NEARProtocol 的等，华人代表这边资深OG @mablejiang 的新项目@trasiaxyz 在跳海bar的活动也人满为患，JE和 @SmartXTerminal 活动，TrustWallet的活动，倪大的龙虾局等都很热闹。

简单总结一下就是在烧钱方面行业开始比较割裂，有的公链已经在倒闭在行尸走肉，有的却在趁机更猛烈砸钱宣传，试图扩大自己的影响力并巩固市场信心。

之前提到在主会场猛砸钱的Sui和Blockwork都是美国的，VC大撤退里受影响最大的也是亚洲VC（几乎全军覆没），老外VC还是有钱，并继续相信crypto的叙事还在投资一级市场，只是更保守。

~~~~~~~~~~~
再说私局的情况

本来我是有点担心这次过来没多少私局能玩的，但结果陆陆续续都约起来了，结果大部分的时间是在参与各种私局。有与项目方的，与交易所的，与VC的，KOL小伙伴们的以及与行业其它上下游朋友的。

感触是项目方的私局少了，KOL轮少了，但还在做组私局的质量都不差，依然有不少收获，此外能明显感觉到CEX们在对自己基本盘上更加上心。

一个细节：
这次大会 @star_okx 老徐 @justinsuntron 孙哥和 @Han_Gate 韩博士 都搞了VIP饭局，放下身段与KOL及VIP用户们深度交流。 

币安那边虽然CZ和一姐没出现，但产品一把手Jeff代表也搞了饭局（币安大概率会把市场重心放在下个月泰国的BBW，那才是他们主场）。

同时海外所也开始加入对华语市场的关注力度，Coinbase开始给部分华语KOL送F1票搭建关系，Kraken招募了中文团队开始了解华语用户习惯和偏好改进产品。

在新人入场流速降低，AI股票吸血，资金存量博弈，外边DEX和链上Meme冲击加速的背景下，各家大所CEX们都在思考和努力巩固自己的基本盘。海外合规大所也开始希望能获得更多中文用户作为增量。

另一个细节看景气：

往年黄黑所和OKX请KOL们看F1是惯例，这次 @Gate @COINBASE 和 @BIT 也加入了战局。我不了解具体情况但据小伙伴说Gate投入是最大方的。

F1的门票真的不便宜，根据位置和比赛日5000美金一张是基本的，决赛日只会更贵。

今晚决赛我朋友圈里被F1现场观战视频刷屏了，基本都是拿的福利票，如果行业不景气了，真的会有这么大范围的福利空投？😆😆

再一个：
过去几天巨亨和帝国等越南场商K都是爆满的，不是提前约或者跟妈咪关系硬的加钱都订不到场子，上个厕所能碰到一堆熟面孔。

text:
New EIP!

Hardware and Bandwidth Recommendations

🔗 https://t.co/PwSnWs1MDc

Highlights:
- It defines recommended baseline specs for three node roles: Full Node, Attester validator, and Local Block Builder (proposer building blocks locally).
- All recommendations assume running both an Execution Layer (EL) and Consensus Layer (CL) client on the same machine.
- Storage guidance centers on a 4 TB NVMe SSD with specific performance targets (throughput and IOPS), discouraging DRAMless/QLC drives and calling out SSD endurance (TBW).
- Validators are recommended to have 64 GB RAM and stronger CPUs (8c/16t, ~3500 single-thread and ~25000 multi-thread PassMark) to avoid instability and to be more future-proof (e.g., heavier crypto/zk workloads).
- Bandwidth recommendations differ by role, with local block builders needing the most (100/50 Mbps) to propagate blocks quickly, while attesters (50/25 Mbps) and full nodes (50/15 Mbps) can run on less but risk lag/late performance.

ELI5:
This EIP is like a “shopping list” for computers and internet connections that run Ethereum. It explains what kind of disk, memory, CPU, and bandwidth you should have depending on whether you’re just following the chain (full node), voting on blocks (attester), or actually building and sending blocks fast (local block builder).

text:
My biggest takeaways from @JoshWoodward (Head of @Google Labs, the Gemini App, and Google AI Studio)

1. The best ideas almost never come from a design sprint or brainstorm. At Google Labs, the ideas that became NotebookLM, Google Flow, Google Beam, and AI Studio all started with small groups of people who were obsessed with an insight and couldn’t stop themselves from building. These ideas surfaced in the shower, over a weekend, in a hallway. The implication for teams everywhere is that the environment matters more than the process. “You cannot microwave a good idea.”

2. Fall in love with the problem, not the product. Most ideas require three, four, or five significant pivots before they either find traction or get shut down. Teams that get hooked on a specific solution will struggle to make those pivots. Teams that are attached to the problem—the underlying pain point or the user behavior they are trying to shift—can keep adjusting until they get it right. 

3. When looking for early PMF, data and retention are important, but the strongest signal of PMF is in people’s eyes. Do they light up? Do they lean in? When you show someone a prototype and they’re genuinely engaged, you feel it. When NotebookLM’s first AI podcast demo was played in a hallway, the reaction was immediate and unmistakable.

4. Keep a list of what is “almost possible,” and move fast when something crosses over. Google Labs keeps a live list of experiences that are almost possible. When something crosses the threshold, Josh describes it as “a phase shift,” like solid to gas, and the team moves immediately. Maintain a running list of things that are almost ready, and have a team positioned to sprint when one of them arrives.

5. Every company needs to think like a labs team now. The underlying technology is changing so fast that what’s possible is shifting from week to week. Which means that every company needs to be spending time playing with the latest models, running far-out experiments, and being first to discover what they unlock before the competition does—and then bringing those discoveries to the rest of the org.

6. When something is not working, the team almost always knows before the leader does. Josh’s instinct as a leader is not to be the one who decides to shut down a project. He watches instead for the passion running out, for the sense that the team has tried everything and nothing is working. His goal is to create an environment where people feel safe enough to say, “I don’t think this is working.”

7. Someone’s “unlearning rate” is one of the most valuable skills right now. Everyone talks about growth mindset and learning speed. Josh is watching for something different: How quickly can someone take an insight, validate or invalidate it through testing, and then let it go? The ability to walk away from a prior belief or approach when the evidence says you should is rare and becoming more valuable.

8. Roles are not blurring into one universal “builder” role. There is a tendency in the current moment to talk as though everyone is becoming a generalist builder. Josh thinks this would be a bad idea. The best people on his teams still have a primary specialty—a major—and also a “minor” they’ve developed. The advice he gives to early-career PMs who are excited about vibe coding and prototyping is clear: build adjacent skills in service of becoming an exceptional PM, not as a replacement for it.

9. A well-designed lab needs isolation, a clear mission, and the ability to create “good trouble.” Three things matter when setting up an internal labs team. First, it needs structural independence, reporting far enough from existing business units that weird ideas can survive long enough to prove themselves. Second, the lab’s mandate has to be explicit: are you graduating ideas to existing products, or inventing new categories? Clarity on that question changes almost every decision. Third, the lab should be a place to challenge how the company itself works, not just what it builds. At Google Labs, that included piloting new job ladders and builder roles before rolling them out more broadly.

10. Google Labs manages the marathon-sprint tension through seasons. At any given time, roughly 20 to 30 experiments are running in parallel, but individual teams experience a defined rhythm: sprints, post-launch recovery, and open exploration periods. After Google I/O each year, many labs teams enter a mode that looks unproductive from the outside: no shipping, just hacking, building, and discovering. Josh treats this as the seedbed for the next season.

text:
【借 papertrade 之际说说古典币圈之美】

什么是古典币圈之美，就是产品一出来感觉：「感觉有点吊，但细一看这不就是 xx 吗。」「这不就是交易挖矿吗，张健见了都直呼内行。」

古典币圈产品：眼前一亮很爽。给你一种天天吃预制菜后，突然吃到一道能复刻经典的创意菜的感觉。

就像币安刚出来时，大家“交易所都做烂了，火币 OKX 不都挺牛逼的”；
就像 Hyperliquid 刚出来，大家”这他妈不就是 dYdX，5 刀都嫌贵”；
就像 Punk 刚出来，大家“这玩意不就是加密猫吗，之前都死了这能行吗”；
就像 Blur 刚出来，大家“这逼不就是 LooksRare 和 x2y2 仿 OpenSea 吗，能行吗”

站在后视镜我们给这些项目的成功总结了理由：币安是抓住了国内政策限制的红利；Punk 是把加密猫的无限 supply 改成有限总量有了稀缺概念；Blur 是利用丝滑的产品力，在那个对 OpenSea 中心化上市路径的抨击情绪高点转化成了买盘。这些项目之后非常成功，有的死了。但咱在后视镜去归因总能找到佐证的理由。

回到 papertrade。你可以说它像 Rollbit，可以说它像 FCoin。作为一个套利中登，平时缝缝补补天天捡垃圾，开 1x 杠杆都怕的人，发现开了一单 100k 1x 的单，顿时看到排队 #7601 人都傻了。一开始以为是 bug，后面发现是有意为之，原来是单越大才能插队靠前，顿时胜负欲就上了，不知不觉就开了 4 个 10m 的单子爆仓了。至少项目方这个偏大户的机制对我是奏效的。

很多时候领先时代一步吃肉，领先时代十步吃屎；很多看似 SOP 的东西细节其实至关重要，很多看似不冲突的东西往往需要有取舍。《毛选》里支部为啥要建在连上，不是团也不是班；5年前你去做RWA和稳定币支付你看有人理你吗

我想说的是，很多牛逼项目里子可能之前很多项目都出现过，套一层新壳，但之所以能爆火整体体现了创始人对产品力、当天市场环境、用户心理、营销手段的综合理解。至少@papertrade_xyz Founder 至少一看就是资深用户，不是钱包都不用天天跑会的那种。

垃圾项目方往往什么都要，牛逼项目方往往有所取舍。

Papertrade 最终可能会失败，但不重要。24 年以后币圈项目几乎没有任何古典美了，清一色要么是融资 VC 站台，画了饼讲个故事，KOL 宣发，上所，高控上所，出货，最终二级散户为食物链上面的买单；要么就是单纯的 meme 纯 p。就是无聊，就好比商 K 每个女的都长的一个样，连知道骗钱都不想出钱那种。

真正遇到 papertrade 掏钱还是认的。
毕竟套利是工作，冲项目是体验，工作和体验赚/亏相同钱的体感是不同的。希望加密以后多这种古典美，不然太无聊了。

quoted_text:
Ledger theft, day two. Since yesterday the thief has pushed ether through Tornado Cash three times, and each time on into Zcash's shielded pool. We followed every lot out the far side. Here is how, step by step.

1. THE SAME BUILD, THREE TIMES
An ether wallet pays a fresh splitter. The splitter pays four fresh wallets. The four drop it into Tornado Cash's 100, 10 and 1 ETH pools. Minutes, every time.

Run 1, yesterday 15:17: 1,254 ETH. Run 2, today 09:42: 1,291 ETH. Run 3, today 11:56: 450 ETH from 0xfa4EaBB840A33C156E600311433AE261CBfCb0e2, in the pools by 12:15.

2. OUT OF TORNADO CASH
The mixer breaks the link between a deposit and a withdrawal. We do not need the link. Our tooling fingerprints the withdrawal transactions themselves: how each one is constructed, who constructs it, and when. 

Yesterday's 65 withdrawals (1,084 ETH) and today's 96 (1,726 ETH) all carry the same signature. The six other withdrawals from those pools in today's windows do not. Run 3 came out from 12:18 into 0x0d697aa182801566d87adc86e68e95fd3b2f5f82 (213 ETH) and 0x676b16cc18542f37d202a1a79ac05463395496a4 (122 ETH), and 195 ETH of it was inside a cross-chain swap service by 12:38. Forty-two minutes, end to end.

3. INTO ZCASH, AND OUT AGAIN
The swap service turns the ether into shielded ZEC, where sender, amount and recipient vanish. But the service's own shielding of each lot is public, and from it we derive a value signature for that lot's exit, then scan every transparent exit from the pool. 108 of 108 exits across both days match their lot to the zatoshi. Not one other exit from the pool does. 

First lot today: in at 10:18:18, out at 11:06:16 in block 3512847 (8d26a9b095d4d28373527f7a6eb81a3be7f906d1e2190960c0512ff64f369418 and 738c6d1261e79766e4dd16bdbd38dced91b8e3a86ce41dcda83eda1f19208fbf), straight into a ZEC to USDC order.

Today so far: 20 lots ordered (2,379 ZEC, $2.9m), 14 out, 5 inside the pool, 1 still settling. Every exit feeds a ZEC to USDC order paying two wallets born at 11:11, 22 of the 28 paid by 12:43:
0x816D5Ee17DB1495d1409F135b98FF3edc5F3cDf8: 940,561 USDC
0xBA736A4b616e79867B6d586293966b552883f3F3: 852,258 USDC
1.79m USDC, unspent. @Circle can freeze it.

(1/2) 🧵⤵️
