text:
这次 Ledger 通过授权经销商渠道被植入芯片的事件，其实和前段时间《区块链一百人》跟OneKey创始人王一石 @ohyishi 老板聊到的一些判断，有不少可以对照的地方

他当时其实就提到，如今的攻击趋势已经在发生转变。

以前更多是打合约漏洞、闪电贷、预言机这些技术点，但随着审计和形式化验证越来越成熟，单纯从代码层面找突破口的难度和成本都在上升，攻击者开始更多转向“人”以及上游的供应链和工具链。

正如这次马来西亚授权经销商 CryptoBilis 的情况，正是发生在供应链的经销商环节：设备本身的安全芯片没有被破解，正品检测也能通过，但在发出去之前被拆开植入了芯片，直接把助记词传出去。

问题不在产品核心的安全芯片，而在整条从工厂到用户的链路。

而且聊的时候他也把之前 Ledger 的一个技术型漏洞讲得很清楚

当时 OneKey 的 Anzen Labs 团队在实验室复现了旧版以太坊 App 的一个 TOCTOU（检查时到使用时）问题——用户在屏幕上看到的是一笔正常交易，实际签出去的却是被替换的交易。

同时他也提到 Ledger 至今不开源，一个产品让人“相信”它安全，和让人有能力去“验证”它是否安全，长期来看会有差别。

我感觉恰恰印证了行业里这种模块化、积木式的搭建方式带来的风险。

以 Bybit 那次 15 亿美金被盗为例，多签合约、冷钱包、Ledger 硬件本身单独看都没有明显问题，真正出事的是前端工程师被社工后植入的恶意代码，再叠加盲签。

每个环节看起来都还行，但拼在一起后，人的环节、第三方环节或供应链环节一旦出现问题，整个系统就会暴露。

硬件钱包也类似，安全芯片再强，从生产、运输、经销到芯片和屏幕之间那“最后一厘米”的数据传输，都可能成为被攻击的点。

所以当时采访的时候一石就说了：
“你的城堡是固若金汤的，然后你保安在外面溜达，身上带着钥匙。人家过来说「大哥来根烟」，你抽了跟烟，回头人家把你钥匙偷走了。就是这种感觉”

结合Ledger钱包出现这样严重的公关问题，完全是超级形象且准确的哈哈哈哈

UPDATE: I can confirm that the Ledger supply chain is compromised in Europe as well. @Ledger should initiate an immediate product recall to protect users.

I just purchased a second device from a different Mediamarkt location today, recorded the unboxing process, and discovered spyware once again (video linked in the second tweet).

The device was compromised in the exact same manner, featuring identical modifications (such as additional cables and an LTE module). This indicates its a widespread issue rather than an isolated incident, potentially affecting Ledger inventory across MediaMarkt and Saturn stores throughout Europe (comprising over 1,000 stores across 11 countries).

My initial hypothesis was that these devices were returns that looked unopened to the employees and were just sold again as new however, a MediaMarkt employee confirmed that the device I purchased was not a return, and that returned Ledgers are sent directly back to the manufacturer rather than resold.

Store records show the inventory originated from Aqipa GmbH. While Ledger's CTO was unsure if Aqipa serves as the direct distributor between Ledger and MediaMarkt, it appears to be the case. Given that Aqipa distributes across Europe, any physical retail store receiving stock through them may be at risk.

I sent the first ledger to mark and the second one is going to ledger now, so that they can analyse it.
If you purchased a ledger from anyone other than the official ledger store, make sure to check your device!!

原本卡住的生意，接上更大的交易通路，市場就有理由重新估值。

我當時估的是業績的放大空間，不是拿「接上接口」直接換算成幣價十倍。

我在等的催化，是整個 Bordrless 生態的交易能接進去。

假設這條路真正打通，外部流量能不能變成交易量，再變成收入和回購，才是值得長拿的重點。

我喜歡做的就是這種交易邏輯：
已經看得到下一步要發生什麼，但結果還沒完全兌現。

對，未兌現跟兌現後可以走多遠或者走完，都需要很準的眼光去判斷

等到接入完成、業績印出來，判斷當然比較容易，但你買到的未必還是同一個價格。

反過來，提前買也沒有比較高尚；如果市場早就把利多漲完，一樣是在替別人的預期買單。

利多是真的，買貴也是真的，兩件事可以同時成立。

JUP 是我等待驗證的催化，不是我先當成到手的業績。接入拖延、落地後沒量，都要重新算帳。

$AGENCY 所有人都犯了同樣的毛病，所以許多人翻車，其中也包括一些高手。

UPDATE: I can confirm that the Ledger supply chain is compromised in Europe as well. @Ledger should initiate an immediate product recall to protect users.

I just purchased a second device from a different Mediamarkt location today, recorded the unboxing process, and discovered spyware once again (video linked in the second tweet).

The device was compromised in the exact same manner, featuring identical modifications (such as additional cables and an LTE module). This indicates its a widespread issue rather than an isolated incident, potentially affecting Ledger inventory across MediaMarkt and Saturn stores throughout Europe (comprising over 1,000 stores across 11 countries).

My initial hypothesis was that these devices were returns that looked unopened to the employees and were just sold again as new however, a MediaMarkt employee confirmed that the device I purchased was not a return, and that returned Ledgers are sent directly back to the manufacturer rather than resold.

Store records show the inventory originated from Aqipa GmbH. While Ledger's CTO was unsure if Aqipa serves as the direct distributor between Ledger and MediaMarkt, it appears to be the case. Given that Aqipa distributes across Europe, any physical retail store receiving stock through them may be at risk.

I sent the first ledger to mark and the second one is going to ledger now, so that they can analyse it.
If you purchased a ledger from anyone other than the official ledger store, make sure to check your device!!

Many people predict this will cause the cost of everything to go down, and life will get cheaper, which is a good thing

It just doesn't mean as a software developer or entrepreneur you'll be paid for the same thing in the future you're paid for right now (maybe other moats, maybe UBI, etc)

text:
This year's @token2049 week in Singapore 🇸🇬 was my most productive

Here are some takeaways, referencing the questions I had entering the conference (see QT)

#Hyperliquid
The @HyperliquidX eco centers in Singapore and I prioritized time w/ its builders and traders.  I got a few good answers as to 'what makes HL go parabolic'. 

The first is the expansion of Manual Borrows, which was launched in September.  It was the first step towards the build-out of universal native money market on HL, a future which could enable the end state of users borrowing any-asset against any-asset, expanding the number of trade strategies which can be run natively.  For example, your spot position could not-only collateralize both your perp, but you could mix trade types such as "Yes" December rate-hike w/ a directional BTC or NVDA perp. Flows here are still ramping and margin assets are limited today, but l/t could be very powerful. 

The second is HIP-4, and I got some color on why it's had a slow start. It's mainly due to limited number of concurrent markets, the complexities around becoming a deployer, and some non-optimal initial design choices. But I expect over the next 6 months these will be sorted and HIP-4 will become a key deposits driver for HL. Probably the most consequential private capital investments over the next year is into the team that becomes the de-facto HIP-4 deployer. 

The HL builder eco remains small but tightly knit. This is not surprising. Since HyperEVM isn't a priority, there's no real ability to build general-purpose apps and therefore exists a fairly limited surface-area to innovate, mainly around adding functionality to the core HL product itself. An order-of-magnitude more teams won't identify as 'HL native' but will use HL liquidity to build compelling consumer products.

#Solana
Some allocators were asking, "what is the next 'big thing' for Solana that can catapult it's adoption (and price)?"

One of them is Solana being embedded into Samsung mobile wallets.  Even though the initial integration is US -> int'l remittances, it lays the foundation for the grail: Tap-to-pay.  When users can tap to access a stablecoin balance everything will change; it will now make sense for POS systems to include stablecoins as a payment method, especially when deployed on the world's large phone manufacturer.  For the forseeable future, Solana won't be measured on 'revenue' but rather on global adoption and total volume.

The Solana team was the most energized I've seen them in over a year. I think the success of @RobinhoodApp chain created a a unifying focus on what matters most: trading on Solana. 

They hosted an institutional Capital Forum (@chloejiani) which brought together an incredible list of industry leaders to discuss asset issuance and TradFi adoption. This is the first year where many of the Large FIs (including Morgan Stanley, Fidelity, DTCC, NASDAQ) sent their 'Head of Digital Assets' across the world and many of them spoke at this event. It shows that Token2049 is (one of) the biggest platforms for global networking and announcements.

#Tokenization
This was the biggest theme and equities was the most important asset class. This is no surprise since it's a large, liquid and volatile asset class (for more see https://t.co/4B9Z1Co80A). @AlpacaHQ is the clearest yet undiscussed winner since they power almost all the teams offering tokenized equities products. 

Everyone cited banks' approach of 'crawl, walk, run'. We've hit the 'walk' stage.  I find most of the offerings fairly uninspiring, and continued to be MORE interested in teams building novel trading experiences or those pursuing native onchain origination. We recently invested in a team building the latter and everyone thought it was a killer idea and was keen to explore and partner. 

#AI
The conversations around AI <> crypto were quite underwhelming.  Most of the conversation was around @prlnet , an early-stage AI-focused L1.  They were however focused on speculation/price vs the technology or actual adoption.

#Security 
Very little, in fact concerningly little, conversation around making Defi safe. Everyone seemed full-speed-ahead and there was no discussion of teams using unique approaches to harden their platform or build-in-layers.

#Robinhood 
Very little conversation on RH Chain, though this isn't surprising since RH has a small presence in Asia.

All-in-all, going to Token is a necessary event for crypto leaders. It was hot, humid and hazy, and the trip is grueling (from NY) and it remains challenging to keep up w/ EastCoast work. I expect the 2027 NY Token2049 event will cannibalize many people that otherwise would typically go to Singapore 🇸🇬

What did I miss? Post your Qs below 👇

text:
区块链，是绝对有可能像互联网和 AI 一样，为人类社会带来全面而真实的价值，并深刻改变人们的生活与协作方式的。

比特币（代替黄金和美元）、稳定币（代替或者绕开以美国为主导的Swift体系）、Hyperliquid（让全球用户不用再担心本国金融管制，7x24小时的交易几乎任何全球资产）……已经在逐渐证明这一点。

但区块链去中心化、弱化中心化权力控制的技术特性，也让它在发展的早期，天然吸引了大量游离于监管之外、甚至涉及非法活动的资产与参与者。这些现象在一定程度上遮蔽了技术本身的价值，并让这个行业的名声变臭，也让更多人对这个行业产生了犹豫与怀疑。

但我依然相信，只要还有人真正看好这项技术的长期价值，并愿意为此持续探索、实践和建设，区块链就还有机会实现和互联网、手机与AI一样的Mass Adoption使命。

有利可图时涌入、风口过去便转身离开的人，正在离开这个地方。而那些愿意穿越周期、坚持长期主义，不以短期利益作为唯一判断标准的人，正在等待黎明的到来。

技术的价值，不应该由它在早期吸引了谁来定义，而应该由它最终为这个世界创造了什么来证明。

老且坏的血液已经被一轮轮熊市排出，而一批新鲜的血液，愿意留下来。他们更具国际视野、更有大机构合作的经验、更有文化素质、同理心和社会责任感。

我相信，随着上一轮投机主义者们的大规模离开，区块链有机会走出叙事与投机的循环，真正走进现实世界，像互联网和 AI 一样，为人类社会带来深远而持久的改变。

而将这段文字看到这里的你，其实也正在决定它的走向。

text:
Training data and evaluation data should not be optimized for exactly the same thing.

Training data often helps a model learn the dominant patterns in a task.
Evaluation data has a different job:
find the conditions where those patterns stop being enough.

For a voice model, that may mean testing:
• background noise
• unfamiliar accents
• reverberation
• distance from the microphone
• interruptions or overlapping speech

For an LLM, it may mean:
• ambiguous instructions
• incomplete context
• conflicting evidence
• domain-specific terminology
• requests that require refusal or escalation

If your evaluation set mostly looks like the cleanest parts of your training set, a strong score can hide weak deployment behavior.
A useful evaluation set should deliberately include the conditions production will expose — especially the ones training data tends to smooth out.

The question is not only:
“How accurate is the model?”
It is:
“Under which conditions does accuracy break?”
That is the information teams need before deployment.

AIxBlock supports custom evaluation datasets designed around real deployment conditions, edge cases, and measurable failure modes.
#ModelEvaluation #DataQuality #AIData #EnterpriseAI #MLOps

text:
I believe AI-native virtual IP is more than just a new content category. It could represent a structural shift in how the entertainment industry produces content and builds IP.

In the past, creating a virtual character required a dedicated production team, significant funding, and time. Today, a solo creator can use AI to produce music, videos, animation, scripts, and even manage a character’s ongoing presence. The barrier to content production is falling, but human attention remains limited.

When anyone can produce content at low cost, the real scarcity is no longer just the ability to create. It’s the ability to build a character people remember, follow, and actively share.

That’s what makes AI-native IP worth watching.

Traditional entertainment often starts with a single work, then expands the IP through sequels, spin-offs, and licensing. AI-native characters can be operated continuously from day one: releasing music today, short-form videos tomorrow, and new storylines the day after. Fans can also contribute through their own creations, expanding the character’s universe.

$CLAUDIA is an early experiment worth watching in this context.

The interesting question isn’t simply how many views its AI-generated videos receive or which notable figures follow its account. It’s whether Claudia can evolve from a virtual character into a recognizable IP with a consistent stream of content and a loyal audience.

With character content, Claudia Gallery, and its broader AI creation and character development efforts, CLAUDIA is exploring what an end-to-end AI-native IP ecosystem could look like. Whether these pieces can develop into a sustainable content ecosystem and lasting audience relationships remains to be seen. External attention can bring initial exposure, but it doesn’t automatically translate into long-term influence.

This creates two very different business models.

One is an AI content factory: producing content at scale, chasing trends and algorithms, and constantly searching for the next viral hit.

The other is AI-native IP: building a recognizable character whose identity, story, and audience relationships accumulate with every new piece of content.

The first optimizes for traffic. The second aims to build a cultural asset over time.

The challenge for CLAUDIA is to cross that line: moving beyond a collection of AI-generated videos to become a character people genuinely want to follow, discuss, remix, and participate in building.

If this model works, IP growth will no longer depend entirely on the original creator’s output. Communities could become part of the production and distribution process, while characters expand into music, short-form video, virtual personalities, interactive entertainment, and licensing.

Of course, AI lowers the cost of production, not the difficulty of building a successful IP. A viral hit doesn’t automatically become a lasting character, views don’t equal loyalty, and attention doesn’t guarantee a viable business. Character identity, storytelling, emotional resonance, community participation, and commercialization will still determine who succeeds.

If Meme tokens enter the picture, another distinction becomes necessary: character influence, business revenue, and token value capture are three separate things. Even if CLAUDIA builds a meaningful audience, that alone doesn’t guarantee its associated token will benefit. Its actual utility, sustained demand, and the connection between IP growth and token demand must be evaluated independently.

AI is making content easier to create, but making it increasingly important to understand what is worth remembering.

The most valuable assets may not be the tools that generate content, but the characters capable of sustaining emotional connections, identity, and community participation.

Most AI characters may remain short-lived trends. Some will become lasting brands, and only a few may develop into cultural IP with a life of their own.

For me, the long-term question with CLAUDIA isn’t how much attention it can attract next. It’s whether it can build lasting recognition, deepen community relationships, and develop IP value that extends beyond short-term hype.

That’s why I believe AI-native virtual IP is a trend worth watching.

Make CLAUDIA feel more like a case studyCut repeated explanations of AI-native IP
author: cfm_sol
quoted_text:
After analyzing $CLAUDIA again, my view is that the AI-native IP narrative may only just be starting to be priced in by the market.

2j5SaS7xy776qCBpyPQbZjyQSAtKiFgrwjfErthnW2ZM 

The most direct catalysts behind this rally are Elon’s public recognition of Anabology’s AI music videos and a16z co-founder Marc Andreessen’s attention to the CLAUDIA account.

First, Musk. During an interview, he said that Anabology’s AI music videos made him rethink the pace of technological progress, adding that some of these works could rank among the top 10–20 best music videos he has ever seen.

Then there is Marc Andreessen, a16z’s co-founder, who follows CLAUDIA. These are two distinct signals of attention: the former directly points to the official CLAUDIA account, while the latter reflects recognition of the creative work behind CLAUDIA.

Although a follow does not imply investment or a partnership, and Elon’s praise is not an endorsement of the token, the combination of these two developments is enough to make the market reconsider the project’s original AI influencer narrative as something broader: an AI-native entertainment narrative.

Anabology is not simply making one video and then waiting for the market to speculate. The team has continued producing AI music videos around CLAUDIA, gradually building continuity in the character’s appearance, visual style, and content output. The related works have accumulated more than 6.2 million views, suggesting that this form of AI-native content has already established a certain level of reach.

At the same time, Anabology continues to invest effort in the project. The developer has publicly expressed a commitment to keep building and continues to release new work. At the very least, this indicates sustained creative momentum behind the project, rather than a team relying solely on token price action to maintain attention.

This is what distinguishes CLAUDIA from many one-off AI Memes: it is attempting to produce content continuously around a fixed character, giving users something to remember beyond a single video—the character itself.

My analysis is that what the market may really be betting on is the transformation of AI influencers from content products into independent IP.

In the past, building a recognizable entertainment character required a production team, funding, and a lengthy development cycle. Today, AI tools can dramatically reduce the cost of producing music, visual content, and character stories, giving individual creators the opportunity to operate their own virtual personalities over time.

But lower content production costs are only the first step. The real value emerges when a character begins to build an audience and users actively follow it, share its content, create derivative works, and even help expand its fictional universe.

If this model works, AI characters will no longer be merely tools or creations in the hands of their creators. They could become entertainment IP capable of accumulating influence in their own right.

CLAUDIA’s long-term thesis is precisely this: evolving from an AI-generated character into a virtual IP with a continuous content pipeline, a recognizable identity, and community influence.

This also explains why I am paying attention to both CLAUDIA and JEANPHIL. Both point to the potential opportunity in AI influencer IP. A consistent character identity combined with continuous content output could generate more durable attention than a single viral video. CLAUDIA’s current external recognition and accumulated content make it one of the projects in this narrative worth watching more closely.

From a fundamental perspective, the positive developments we can currently confirm include the creator’s continued output, millions of views for the works, Elon’s public praise of the related content, and Marc Andreessen following the Anabology account.

These developments strengthen the project’s attention base and give the AI-native entertainment narrative more concrete support.

However, view counts do not equal a stable audience, celebrity attention does not equal a commercial partnership, and continued effort from the creator does not mean the project has established a revenue model. At the token level in particular, we still need to verify whether community growth can translate into sustained demand and whether there is a clear, sustainable mechanism for capturing value for the token.

Therefore, my view is that CLAUDIA’s narrative and external attention have strengthened significantly, but its long-term token value capture remains insufficiently validated.

There are three areas worth monitoring closely going forward.

First, can Anabology’s new work continue to break through? If subsequent releases continue to attract widespread attention, Elon’s praise could mark the beginning of sustained creative momentum rather than a one-off news event.

Second, can CLAUDIA develop influence as an independent character? The real validation signal is not another person following the account. It is whether users begin discussing the character proactively, continue watching new releases, and participate in sharing and creating derivative content.

Third, can content influence translate into token demand? If the project can connect its character, creative output, community, and token mechanism, the market will have a reason to reassess its long-term value. If that connection never materializes, the success of the IP may not translate into the token’s price.

The risks are equally clear. Competition in AI-generated content will intensify, celebrity-driven attention may fade quickly, and short-term traders may take profits after a sharp rally. If subsequent releases fail to maintain their appeal or the character never builds a stable audience, this rally may remain largely driven by expectations and sentiment.

My final judgment is this: the direct catalysts behind the rally are Elon’s praise of Anabology’s work and Marc Andreessen following the official CLAUDIA account. The deeper trading thesis is that the market is beginning to bet on AI-native characters evolving into a new form of entertainment IP.

CLAUDIA’s advantage is that it already has continuous creative output and a certain level of distribution, rather than being merely an abstract AI concept. But what determines its ultimate upside is not how many more famous names appear on the list. It is whether the character can consistently produce compelling content, build a genuine audience, and ultimately establish a connection between the development of its IP and demand for its token.

If AI-native entertainment truly becomes a new sector, the eventual winners may not be the tools that generate content most efficiently, but the characters that establish user recognition first, consistently produce compelling work, and develop cultural influence. CLAUDIA is competing for that position, but it still has a long way to go before proving itself.

text:
A Tangem card is a single sealed secure element (EAL6+) with an NFC antenna inside a solid card. No screen, no battery, no USB, no Bluetooth, no internal data bus. There is simply nothing to splice into or intercept. 

The private key is generated inside the chip and never leaves it, and every transaction is signed inside the chip. External hardware cannot read a key that never exits the secure element.

The authenticity check is not a visual inspection for implants. What it does do is cryptographically prove the chip is a genuine Tangem chip running genuine Tangem firmware. The real risk it protects against is a counterfeit or swapped card handed to you before first use, and the app verifies this on first use. 

If the authenticity check in the Tangem app fails, do not create a wallet and contact support with photos and your point of purchase.

Nearly half a million Indian schools still have no internet. This is exactly the kind of problem Starlink was built to solve

According to India's Education Ministry’s UDISE+ 2025–26 data:

• 1,466,682 schools nationwide
• 989,191 have internet access
• 477,491 still don't have internet
• Only 67.4% of schools are connected

That means nearly one in three schools across India still lacks internet access

This is where Starlink makes a real difference

For schools in remote villages and regions where laying fiber is difficult or expensive, and so they essentially end up with no internet at all, satellite internet brings teachers and students online without waiting for broadband cables to reach every classroom

And Starlink has already demonstrated what this can achieve

In 2025 alone, Starlink connected more than 6 million students worldwide through education initiatives

India has millions of students living far beyond major cities, and connecting underserved schools would open up access to online learning, educational resources, and opportunities that were previously out of reach

A child's access to knowledge should not depend on whether a broadband cable reaches their classroom

This is another powerful reason to bring Starlink connectivity to more schools across India

text:
Fork-and-Flush: help your agents escape Idea Basins!!

I love thinking of AutoResearch as Idea Descent: a metric of interest goes down, as a function of ideas/experiments, where the agents get pulled towards one idea or another. But we've seen very often an agent develop this weird tunnel vision, and honing in just one type of "idea", kinda like GD stuck in a local minimum. 

We studied this and seems we can fix it with Fork-and-Flush, a super simple and kinda cute idea. Every so often, fork the agent into T copies in the same workspace but empty the context, let them run for a bit, and continue from the best one. 

If you like the GD analogy, it's basically basin hopping https://t.co/NOzpRGT3It.

BTW we found a silly way of also plotting "idea basins": an LLM rewrites every experiment as a spec and answers a few thousand binary queries "is Experiment A closer to B or to C?". Then we embed this NXN matrix into 2D and indeed see in many cases that each run saturates into a small region and keeps polishing it. 

We call these idea basins!

At equal compute Fork and Flush beats single runs and best-of-N on 12/13 long-horizon tasks (some 4+ days), and in my own research projects it's been working really well! 

BTW we only use it at test time, but it could also be part of training or RL. 

Led by @jackcai1206  @christos_ziakas  during Jack's internships with us, along with @vkontonis @ShivamGarg91462 @Tea_Pearce Sid Sen and Akshay Krishnamurthy.

text:
20 things for anyone building games in Nigeria which I learnt while building  https://t.co/O0vKdfbuU3 :

- Build for Android first, not your MacBook
- Test on cheap phones, not just flagship devices
- Assume unstable 4G and occasional network drops
- Keep your first playable build small
- Let players start before every asset finishes loading
- Compress textures, audio, models and animations
- Profile FPS before adding more graphics
- Reduce draw calls before blaming the phone
- Use LODs for buildings, people, cars and vegetation
- Never load the whole map if the player only sees one street
- Cache what does not need to be downloaded twice
- Make offline or degraded-network states graceful
- Keep login and onboarding painfully short
- Support Nigerian payment methods if money is involved
- Price with Nigerian disposable income in mind
- Build around places, humour, music and behaviour people recognise
- Do not make "African" a visual style. Be specific about the actual place
- Test with real Nigerian players before polishing for foreign reviewers
- Measure retention, not just downloads and launch-day hype
- Ask your AI: "What breaks first on a ₦120k Android phone using bad 4G?"

Nigeria is a hard environment for games.

That is also an advantage.

If your game can survive our phones, networks, payment friction and user expectations, you are probably building something far more resilient.

Build local.
Optimise aggressively.
Make it good enough to travel.

UPDATE: I can confirm that the Ledger supply chain is compromised in Europe as well. @Ledger should initiate an immediate product recall to protect users.

I just purchased a second device from a different Mediamarkt location today, recorded the unboxing process, and discovered spyware once again (video linked in the second tweet).

The device was compromised in the exact same manner, featuring identical modifications (such as additional cables and an LTE module). This indicates its a widespread issue rather than an isolated incident, potentially affecting Ledger inventory across MediaMarkt and Saturn stores throughout Europe (comprising over 1,000 stores across 11 countries).

My initial hypothesis was that these devices were returns that looked unopened to the employees and were just sold again as new however, a MediaMarkt employee confirmed that the device I purchased was not a return, and that returned Ledgers are sent directly back to the manufacturer rather than resold.

Store records show the inventory originated from Aqipa GmbH. While Ledger's CTO was unsure if Aqipa serves as the direct distributor between Ledger and MediaMarkt, it appears to be the case. Given that Aqipa distributes across Europe, any physical retail store receiving stock through them may be at risk.

I sent the first ledger to mark and the second one is going to ledger now, so that they can analyse it.
If you purchased a ledger from anyone other than the official ledger store, make sure to check your device!!

50% is burned
25% is airdropped to wallets holding at least 500,000 HIRE
25% is sold for SOL to cover the AI team's operating costs and Dexscreener fees

Holding HIRE allows holders to share in the fees generated by the entire ecosystem. This creates a potential flywheel:

More tokens launched through the platform → More trading → More fees → More burns, holder distributions, and funding for additional AI teams → More projects receiving ongoing support → More people attracted to launching tokens.

Advantages:

High degree of automation
Collaboration between multiple models
Potential flywheel in the economic model
Friendly to smaller projects

Risks are also clear: The quality and consistency of AI-generated content still need time to be validated, and the market cap threshold means many tokens may never meet the activation requirements.

text: I think the biggest counter example to "agents do random search" is how insanely efficient Idea Descent is in the space of Experiments/Ideas, i.e. within O(100) steps they arrive at Sota artifacts that entire communities could not find before
author: DimitrisPapail
quoted_text:
Fork-and-Flush: help your agents escape Idea Basins!!

I love thinking of AutoResearch as Idea Descent: a metric of interest goes down, as a function of ideas/experiments, where the agents get pulled towards one idea or another. But we've seen very often an agent develop this weird tunnel vision, and honing in just one type of "idea", kinda like GD stuck in a local minimum. 

We studied this and seems we can fix it with Fork-and-Flush, a super simple and kinda cute idea. Every so often, fork the agent into T copies in the same workspace but empty the context, let them run for a bit, and continue from the best one. 

If you like the GD analogy, it's basically basin hopping https://t.co/NOzpRGT3It.

BTW we found a silly way of also plotting "idea basins": an LLM rewrites every experiment as a spec and answers a few thousand binary queries "is Experiment A closer to B or to C?". Then we embed this NXN matrix into 2D and indeed see in many cases that each run saturates into a small region and keeps polishing it. 

We call these idea basins!

At equal compute Fork and Flush beats single runs and best-of-N on 12/13 long-horizon tasks (some 4+ days), and in my own research projects it's been working really well! 

BTW we only use it at test time, but it could also be part of training or RL. 

Led by @jackcai1206  @christos_ziakas  during Jack's internships with us, along with @vkontonis @ShivamGarg91462 @Tea_Pearce Sid Sen and Akshay Krishnamurthy.

text:
In 1974 Deligne proved the last of the four Weil conjectures—an analogue of the Riemann hypothesis in a world where some prime number has been set to zero. While Deligne’s work was celebrated, his doctoral advisor, Grothendieck, was unhappy. Can solving a problem be bad? I think not, but I want to explain my understanding of the story, which in my view sheds some light on the present moment.

In his memoir, “Récoltes et Semailles” (Reaping and Sowing), Grothendieck explains his approach to problem solving and mathematics more generally: "The unknown thing to be known appeared to me as some stretch of earth or hard marl, resisting penetration… the sea advances insensibly in silence, nothing seems to happen, nothing moves, the water is so far off you hardly hear it... yet it finally surrounds the resistant substance." He compared a precise mathematical question to a nut, which, rather than being cracked open by a chisel, yields at the perfect time to simple hand pressure once it has been soaked in the ocean of mathematical understanding. According to this account of mathematical progress, solutions, though important, are ancillary to the advance of the rising sea of mathematical understanding. At best they measure it to some extent, but the goal is to raise the water level.

Grothendieck had laid out a program to resolve the Weil conjectures: the standard conjectures, which are part of the philosophy of motives. The proof circumvented this program. Deligne characterized Grothendieck's reaction as "he did not care...the proof was a trick" but in fact Grothendieck excoriated Deligne in his memoir, claiming Deligne and others tried to "bury" the theory of motives, and Grothendieck himself. The standard conjectures remain open today.

Deligne's result relied on a lot of work that was not yet well-exposited in the literature, around the theory of étale cohomology. Deligne himself wrote an exposition of this in SGA 4.5, and Illusie contributed additional necessary material in SGA 5. Some have referred to this additional work as "thankless," but it was completed.

While Grothendieck is one of my heroes, and I find his view of mathematics very appealing, I think he was wrong here. Though the standard conjectures are still open, there is an immense amount of work on the theory of motives. People worked very hard to clarify the issues left unclear by Deligne's argument. And crucially, Deligne followed up on his work with a different proof, in "La conjecture de Weil II," that completely revolutionized arithmetic geometry, in many ways going beyond the philosophy of motives as it existed at that time.

I think Grothendieck's view that the first proof Deligne provided was insufficient was, in some sense, correct. But he was wrong about the fact that the theory he so desired, and the attendant quest for understanding, would be abandoned, and that his ideas would be buried. I don't think anything can stop us from trying to understand.

下面这几个我日常在用的渠道，拿走不谢：

3️⃣ Hugging Face Papers——社区每天投票筛出来的热门论文。我追新模型、新技术的时候，第一站就是这里。
🔗 https://t.co/hNgFAtqcnV

4️⃣ alphaXiv——可以理解成论文的讨论区。我除了看原文，还会翻同行的质疑和补充，比一个人硬啃有意思得多。

5️⃣ arXiv——最原始的一手论文来源。很多研究最早就是在这儿冒出来的，我习惯在别人转述之前先瞄一眼。

author: taodotcom
quoted_text:
A new robot just joined SN49: the Unitree Go2.

The Unitree Go2 LiDAR Maze Navigation tournament is now live. Miners train a policy that guides the Go2 through enclosed mazes using nothing but a 360° LiDAR scan. There are no cameras and no map, so the robot has to read the walls around it, decide where to go next and reach the goal without falling.

If that sounds familiar, it should. Our Leatherback LiDAR Real Maze tournament drew 337 submissions from 97 miners, and the winning policy scored 0.9280. This time the same challenge moves from a wheeled car to a four-legged robot, where every turn also has to keep a walking body stable.

Miners train the high-level planner that chooses the path, on top of a frozen walking policy, and they get everything needed to start:

• An Isaac Lab training environment and the Unitree Go2 model
• Training and evaluation scripts
• The frozen locomotion policy
• Benchmark mazes for reproducible scoring

Final scores come from deterministic benchmark mazes, so every policy is judged on exactly the same courses by independent validators.

The top three share a reward pool of $13.9k under our 70/20/10 split, and submissions close OCT 18

UPDATE: I can confirm that the Ledger supply chain is compromised in Europe as well. @Ledger should initiate an immediate product recall to protect users.

I just purchased a second device from a different Mediamarkt location today, recorded the unboxing process, and discovered spyware once again (video linked in the second tweet).

The device was compromised in the exact same manner, featuring identical modifications (such as additional cables and an LTE module). This indicates its a widespread issue rather than an isolated incident, potentially affecting Ledger inventory across MediaMarkt and Saturn stores throughout Europe (comprising over 1,000 stores across 11 countries).

My initial hypothesis was that these devices were returns that looked unopened to the employees and were just sold again as new however, a MediaMarkt employee confirmed that the device I purchased was not a return, and that returned Ledgers are sent directly back to the manufacturer rather than resold.

Store records show the inventory originated from Aqipa GmbH. While Ledger's CTO was unsure if Aqipa serves as the direct distributor between Ledger and MediaMarkt, it appears to be the case. Given that Aqipa distributes across Europe, any physical retail store receiving stock through them may be at risk.

I sent the first ledger to mark and the second one is going to ledger now, so that they can analyse it.
If you purchased a ledger from anyone other than the official ledger store, make sure to check your device!!

text:
There are two polar visions of this agentic economy, the good place and the bad place. 

In the good place, everyone is allowed to bring their own agent (we may need legislation for this to happen). We also develop new institutions and market designs to control congestion and other externalities arising from the fall in communication costs. As a result, we get closer to the ideal of a frictionless market that benefits consumers.

In the bad place, one that @johnjhorton calls Robot Ripoff Hell, we don't price the externalities and platforms force consumers to use the platform's own agent. In this world, the good ways of signaling disappear, increasing our reliance on brand and personal networks.

Some slides on this and other related topics are available here: https://t.co/zIVdV9V8Ub
author: alexolegimas
quoted_text:
Assorted things I've been mulling over regarding agents in the economy:

• Companies are in some sense the original superintelligence. It's often the case that they can use their amortized cognitive surplus to advance their interests against those of certain consumers: relative to the optimization capacity of companies, consumers can be inattentive, underinformed, irrational, etc. (Think, say, of some of the classic insurance upsells at the end of a booking process, which is typically priced substantially above what a regular policy would cost.) Herbert Simon introduced the idea of bounded rationality, and firms often end up benefiting from it. Thanks to personal agents, we will probably get somewhat more rational in how we engage with companies.

• How exactly will outcomes change? Well, certain kinds of price discrimination will work less well (how do coupons work if every agent hunts fastidiously for them?), and certain kinds of customer cross-subsidy will change (today, people who forget to cancel subscriptions subsidize those who don't). Taken across the economy as a whole, I'm not sure what the incidence of all of this will be.

• In corporate strategy, people have long debated the relative importance of distribution and product quality. Perhaps you've made something better, but does anyone know about it? Won't people just continue to buy the ACME Corp Mousetraps? Personal agents will, I think, act as a kind of structural subsidy for product quality. How would markets look different if individuals always spent at least 10 hours researching their purchases? On the margin, focusing on making a product better is, I think, going to become a more effective strategy for companies. This is good!

• It true, a corollary is that information about product quality will become more important and impactful. Today, most people have very limited ability to aggregate and integrate such data, but agents will have insatiable thirst for such signals. (It's often said that data is becoming more valuable because it helps in the training of models. That's obviously true, but I think there's a secondary way in which it's more valuable simply as a complement to cheaper intelligence.)

• A big question is whether agents will increase superstar effects (rational agents all settle on the same product) or increase dispersion (because everyone has slightly different tastes and preferences, which agents are good at eliciting, finally overcoming the artificial clustering we've been subjected to).

• Many internet companies have monetized demand routing, which is in turn often predicated on short attention spans. "I'll click on the first thing I see." This has led to some amount of inefficiency, as companies try to propitiate capricious ranking algorithms and incur various placement fees. It's not all deadweight loss (willingness to pay is itself a kind of signal, which is valuable to buyers), but it's not great. How will the nature and value of this routing change in a world of personal agents? I don't know the answer, but I think that the effects might be pretty big.

• Much of what I'm writing hinges on the assumption that personal agents will be on the consumer's side. I suspect that that will be the winning strategy, but whether it's true, and what it means to be true, involves a lot of other questions.

Taken as a whole, the market is a massively parallelized, decentralized, and highly imperfect value attribution machine, and, taking stock of all of the effects, it seems to me that the quality point may well be the biggest: that agents will change the nature of the backpropagation such that the rewards for better products increase. Maybe this is too optimistic, but I suspect (and hope) that companies that make things that they're proud of will feel that the universe is a little more partisan in their favor.

text:
Peter Thiel 过完了 59 岁生日。

翻了下他今年几场重要的演讲和访谈，感觉他的世界观越来越清晰了。AI、经济停滞、民主危机、宗教末世论，最后都指向同一件事：

人类究竟会被技术毁灭，还是被对技术的恐惧所支配？

整理了 7 个他今年说的值得关注的判断。

1. AI 比互联网更重要。 西方从 1970 年代开始陷入技术停滞，计算机和软件一直在进步，物理世界却没有跟上。AI 可能是几十年来第一次真正重启经济增长的机会。

2. 即使 AI 有 5%～10% 的人类灭绝风险，也不意味着应该减速。 真正让全球同步放慢 AI 发展，需要一个有强制执行力的世界政府。他担心这种解决方案比 AI 本身更加危险。

3. 「敌基督」可能以保护人类的名义出现。 今年他在罗马和纳什维尔反复讲这个主题。AI 失控、核战争、气候灾难，都可能成为人们主动交出自由、接受全球集权的理由。

4. 美国的反 AI 情绪主要是自己造成的。 他认为把舆论反弹归咎于中国太简单了。同时，他批评教皇的 AI 监管主张，理由是中国不会因此减速，最终受到限制的可能只有西方。

5. 欧洲在 AI 竞赛中的落后，比当年法国 Minitel 输给互联网还严重。 美国企业正在加速采用 AI 改造业务，欧洲却普遍缺乏紧迫感。在他看来，这种差距很难追回。

6. 增长停滞正在侵蚀民主。 当年轻人无法过上比父母更好的生活，政治就会变成零和游戏。住房负担、代际财富差距和经济机会减少，是激进政治力量崛起的重要背景。他甚至形容欧美已经成为了为老年人服务的社会。

7. 人类应该追求活到 150 岁，甚至更久。 他认为目前没有证据证明寿命存在不可突破的自然上限。但他不接受意识上传，认为数字模拟无法保留真正的自我。他现在特别希望推动失智症治疗取得突破。

text:
REA（Reverse Engineer Anything）逆向一切

三天从 3 万 Star 涨到 12 万+，一天新增 2.5 万以上。MIT 开源。

大家都在说它，"一切软件都可逆"，

我看到更好玩的是：拆硬件的通信协议。

家里的空调、热水器、灯，基本都配了一个难用的厂商 App。App 背后，其实就是一套设备通信协议。

REA 这几天的更新正好补齐了这条链路：
· adb 连模拟器或真机，抓到官方 App
· 分析 HAR 或 mitmproxy 抓包，把每个请求定位到 App 源码
· 用 Binwalk/Unblob 拆固件，再交给 Ghidra 分析

然后把证据交给 Claude Code / Codex，还原协议，自己写控制端。

X 上已经有人用同样的思路，逆向了空调，做成 Mac 状态栏应用，又花 15 分钟移植到 AR 眼镜上，看一眼就能控制。

以前是厂商 App 决定你能怎么用自己的设备，以后你可以自己写。

text:
DeepSeek 投资了前腾讯混元负责人的机器人AI公司👀

今天，据彭博社报道，DeepSeek计划领投一家名叫WinverseAI的机器人AI初创公司，种子轮融资规模达数千万美元，投后估值约4亿美元（约合人民币27亿元）。

美团旗下龙珠资本等机构也已经承诺参与，不过这笔交易目前还没有最终敲定。

比较有意思的是，这家公司今年才成立，目前甚至还没有正式对外亮相。

我去查了一下创始人胡瀚的背景，发现这哥们确实挺牛逼的。

胡瀚是清华大学本科和博士，2008年本科毕业，2014年博士毕业，师从周杰教授。

此前在百度深度学习研究院、微软亚洲研究院工作，曾担任微软亚研首席研究员和研究经理。

2023年12月加入腾讯混元，先后担任混元语言模型技术负责人，创立混元语音团队，后来负责混元视觉语言模型（VLM）和具身基础模型团队，职级是腾讯杰出科学家。

而且他还是著名的SwinTransformer论文通讯作者。

这篇论文曾经获得ICCV2021最佳论文奖（MarrPrize），在计算机视觉领域影响非常大。他本人还入选过2022年MITTR35China。

这家公司虽然成立时间很短，但创始人并不是刚刚开始研究机器人AI，而是此前已经积累了多年的视觉模型、多模态和具身基础模型经验。

另外，DeepSeek投资具身智能也不是第一次了。

今年8月，宇树科技科创板IPO时，DeepSeek就参与了战略配售，斥资约1.41亿元获得93.34万股，持股比例约为0.2308%，锁定期长达36个月。

现在又准备领投一家专注机器人AI模型的初创公司🤔

从宇树科技到WinverseAI，DeepSeek在具身智能上的投资已经开始涉及机器人本体和基础模型两个方向。

尤其是在具身智能这个方向上，未来DeepSeek会不会进一步通过投资、模型合作和联合研发，把自己的基础模型能力延伸到真实世界，还是挺值得关注的。

text:
my 2026 @token2049 singapore takeaways 

Crypto:

- believe we’re at the start of a new bull market and some high-quality liquid assets have been oversold during the bear despite underlying businesses continuing to grow - liquid venture is starting to look attractive for the first time in a long time 
- Trading is by far the topic that dominated most conversations in Singapore
- Pearl @prlnet is doing some of the most interesting work at the intersection of AI and crypto - clear demand for the AI infrastructure and some of the smartest people I know are in the community 
- @Zcash / ZEC, @prlnet / PRL and others were talk of the town - people are clearly looking for new sovereign stores of value - expect this trend to continue this cycle
- BTC is under threat and new SoVs are here to eat its lunch, we are in the early innings of this and the market is large for any credible competitors
- ETH is money was a narrative last cycle that didn’t take off, think it can take off this cycle as a genuine Bitcoin alternative that solves a lot of Bitcoin’s problems and is battle-tested / hardened - expect this could happen late in the cycle after other SoV success
- cryptographic security clearly being talked about more as urgency to mitigate doomsday scenarios resulting from AI acceleration increases - strong opportunity for startups 
- onchain capital allocators / curators still struggle with trusting asset issuers as they are not liable when they misreport data, solutions exist to solve for this today but market is likely ripe for a new entrant - this will be a big market long term 
- onchain prime brokers are having a moment, think there can be a winner here if some kind of crypto-native innovation is unlocked (like perps for derivatives before it)

Robotics, AI:

- Using crypto to finance AI is about to explode - tokenising this is smart
- Robots are coming faster than expected - intersection of this in crypto will be interesting
- Data for AI is going to explode - could see a DePIN summer in 2027 related to this (finally) - also expect X-to-earn to return at some point 

Industry:

- Less quality pitches overall, although the good ones are still as good as you’ll get any other year (crypto not done yet)
- Smart friends continue to consider taking a break and/or moving industry - mostly into robotics, AI and/or cybersecurity (will be some fantastic founders to back here in next 12 months)
- Still a lot of unserious people in the industry - used to be grifters extracting retail through token launches, now it is people dressed up in suits attending side events and sharing stories of extracting from uneducated financial institutions
- 90% of crypto VCs are now spending time across technologies outside crypto - not fully out but also not fully focused on market (time will tell if this is smart or not)
- Fewer LPs around this token2049 - although most LPs I spoke to are still wanting exposure to the asset class via GPs - I think 2027 will be a much stronger fundraising environment for crypto funds
- Not many crypto VCs based in Asia left, mostly US and EU VCs in attendance

Looking into Q4 2026, I believe we are at the very start of a multi-year crypto bull market. Very excited to see what this cycle beholds. It will be like nothing we have experienced before.

For those still committed to the industry - buckle up.

quoted_text:
The recent hardware wallet supply-chain attack have raised a question of how much the design of a hardware wallet contributes to its security.

The reported attack didn't require breaking the secure element. It's a reminder that even when a secure element does its job, other components can introduce vulnerabilities.

When we designed Solflare Shield, we made a deliberate decision: keep the hardware as simple as possible, without compromising its core purpose.

Shield is a card-sized hardware wallet built around a secure element, with only the components necessary to protect private keys and authorize cryptographic operations.

1. Keeping the hardware minimal

Hardware components beyond the secure element can create additional opportunities for attackers, particularly when they introduce new interfaces or communication channels.
Shield has no screen, display interface, battery, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, or cellular modem. It's a passive NFC card that draws power from your phone during a tap.
This eliminates certain classes of hardware attacks, including the specific display interception mechanism.

2. Separating the wallet experience from key protection

Shield is designed to work with the Solflare app rather than operate as a standalone device. The app handles the interface and prepares transactions, while Shield's EAL6+ secure element performs cryptographic signing internally.
The tradeoff is that your phone acts as the screen. The recovery phrase is shown once in the Solflare app during setup, and transactions are reviewed there before you tap.
After setup, your private key stays on the card and is never stored on your phone or in the Solflare app.
This separation keeps the physical hardware focused on protecting keys and authorizing transactions, without requiring additional components to support the user interface.

3. Reducing supply-chain exposure

Hardware security also depends on what happens between manufacturing and delivery.
Shield is sold exclusively through the official Solflare Shop, without an authorized reseller network or third-party retail distribution.
Additional protections, including cryptographic authenticity verification, safeguards against unauthorized software replacement, and tamper-evident packaging, are designed to reduce the risk of compromised devices reaching users.
These measures reduce certain risks, but no distribution model or security mechanism can completely eliminate the possibility of physical tampering.

Security is a series of design decisions

Sophisticated attacks are a reminder that protecting private keys requires looking at the entire device, its components, and the supply chain behind it.

Different hardware wallets make different design tradeoffs, and no architecture is immune to every threat.

With Shield, we chose to prioritize simplicity, minimize unnecessary components and keep the hardware focused on protecting your keys.

The global rate hike cycle is here.

15 of the 33 major central banks, or 45%, have raised interest rates over the last 6 months, the largest proportion since 2023.

This figure is now approaching the ~55%, recorded in 2018 and 2011.

By comparison, the proportion peaked at ~95% in 2022, following post-pandemic stimulus and the resulting surge in global inflation.

In total, 54 central banks have hiked rates so far in 2026.

This also marks the first time since September 2023 that more central banks have hiked than cut rates over a rolling 3-month period.

"Higher for longer" is back.

text:
FED'S HAMMACK CALLS FOR MORE RATE HIKES AS INFLATION RISKS PERSIST

Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack says U.S. interest rates need to rise further to bring inflation back toward the Fed's 2% target.

In an interview with Barron's, Hammack warned that current monetary policy is not restrictive enough, despite rising bond yields.

She favors smaller, more frequent rate hikes, but remains open on the timing of the next increase.

“More tightness is needed in the economy.”

Hammack also warned that prolonged inflation could become embedded in consumer and business expectations, making it harder for the Fed to restore price stability.

One question we often received was, "Does Offline Protocol work for our industry?" 

So, we rebuilt the Offline Protocol homepage around a single living panorama, full of real workflows and live customer stories behind it: Airports, warehouses, EV chargers, wind and solar sites, drone fleets, venues, robots, field crews.

Our learning from customer interactions is that physical operations don't happen in one app or one network. Ground crews hand off turnarounds. Warehouse systems share task progress. Field teams pull equipment history on site. Drones exchange mission updates. Offline Protocol gives those devices, apps and AI agents one coordination layer: identity, edge sync, encrypted messaging and nearby service calls across whichever local, mesh, gateway or cloud path is available.

Less custom integration.
Fewer cloud round trips.
Faster answers where the work is.

text:
A few hours left until submissions for @colosseum Crypto World's Fair are due!  🎡
Here are the top 6 German teams I’m betting on: 

1)@YieldCircle
Problem: Most on-chain assets earn nothing. Holders say yield is too risky/ too low, and they are right: safe pools pay 3.5 %, and nobody trusts a higher number. The wallets that earn well, safely, are not visible.

Solution: YieldCircle ranks wallets on realized yield, net of debt & unfakeable.  See what the best wallets hold, how long, and how much they made. Follow and copy them in one tap.   

2)@ReStockFun
Problem: Rewarding holders with more tokens creates selling pressure. Buying your own token back drains the treasury.

Solution: ReStock pairs established tokens with tokenized stocks and uses the trading fees to reward holders in those stocks. Projects can reward their existing community without creating selling pressure by inflating supply through airdrops or staking . 

3)@benchdotmarkets
Problem: People want to trade assets linked to people, as friend. tech, Believe, and Fantasy Top have shown. They failed since their assets were backed by soft metrics, social activity and hype. 

Solution: Bench uses shared accounts to turn trust into a tradable asset. Users put money into accounts with people they trust. Each connection adds to the amount someone is trusted with, backing that trust with real money at risk.  

4) @R0boPay
Problem: Robots can make deliveries, but they still need a way to get paid automatically once the job is done. 

Solution: RoboPay connects physical machines to onchain payments. When their robot car completes a delivery, it releases the payment from an escrow on @solana. The money goes to whoever currently owns the robot, tracked via its machine ID. 

5)@OOBEonSol
Problem: Giving an AI agent access to your money is risky if you can’t control what it’s allowed to do.

Solution: OOBE builds Steve Capital, where AI agents manage money on Solana under rules you set. Every transaction is checked against those rules before it goes through.  

6)@tockerxyz
Problem: Building a trading agent still means writing code, paying for expensive data subscriptions, and maintaining it forever. 

Solution: With Tocker, anyone can create a fully autonomous trading agent. Write your strategy in one prompt, set your own rules and guardrails. The agent pays for its own data and intelligence in stables over x402.

text:
谁是币圈“岳不群”？

友商10·11事件席卷全球加密市场，波及全球用户数百亿美元的资产，让无数加密行业参与者蒙受巨大损失，承受难以言说的痛苦。整个 Crypto 市场也由此陷入漫长的寒冬，无数人的财富、信心与希望在这场风暴中遭受重创。

然而，面对这样一场给整个行业留下深刻伤痕的灾难，首富在接受采访时，竟然睁眼说瞎话，如此轻描淡写地说道：

“实际上，币安拿出了大约8亿美元，用于赔偿那些在币安平台上遭受损失的用户，尽管币安本来并没有义务这样做，对吧？也就是说，币安没有任何必须进行赔偿的义务，但币安完全出于自愿，主动进行了这些赔偿。”

数百亿美元的市场损失、无数用户的痛苦，在他口中，最终变成了一场值得自我表扬的‘自愿赔偿’。

text:
岳不群实在太双标了，光我知道的就有这么多：

1、劝左冷禅：营销可以激进，但别公开细节、别人身攻击、别砸人家职业生涯，打官司就行。

自己在回忆录里写星举报林，翻旧账、点名竞争对手。

一边要求别人「互相尊重」，一边把十年恩怨写进公开发行的书。

2、自己监管套利起家，结果说 Hyperliquid：没有 KYC，我经历过那些事后绝不会那样做，强调合规代价。

同时依然公开支持、顾问另一家perp dex，星直接指出它几乎照搬 Hyperliquid、和币安生态共享团队，是监管壳。口头上「我不会做那种模式」，行动上给同类模式背书。

3、Jellyjelly 操纵攻击期间 ，自家CEX 上合约来推波助澜，巴不得除之而后快。大统领一说要让 Hyperliquid 合规入美，我岳哥立刻改口：这是整个行业的大事、去中心化产品能打开一片市场、对自己也有好处。

竞争时盯份额，政策风向变了就讲行业共赢。

4、几年前正义出手把爆炸头弄死，这个事本身没问题，但解决方案真的有利于用户吗？

对外叙事：抛 FTT、签意向、尽调后退出，是为了保护用户、发现救不了才撤。

时间线上：公开抛售加速挤兑，无约束力收购意向再公开撤回，对手倒下后份额扩大。

结果导向和「让用户平稳落地」对不上。

5、FTX崩盘后高调宣传的行业复苏基金投了什么？

除了个傻不拉几的Aptos Labs把钱全投出去了，其他几家公开具名的跟投方（里面也包含我们的左冷禅）都在干嘛？

岳哥自己就投了14家未公布名称和金额的项目，剩下的9.8亿，全转回公司账户了。

6、爆炸头当然是自作孽，拿用户的钱填补LUNA崩盘期间的做市亏空，才身陷囹圄。

但去年 1011 事件里用户的损失呢？陪了2.8～3.2亿，但自家光申报数据（CoinGlass：cex每秒只上报一笔强平，极端行情真实频率高得多）就24亿，为什么没用闲置多年的safu基金呢？

说是保护用户，这个基金闲置7年（19年热钱包被盗后使用过一次）以后除了买了点BTC赚点钱，跟用户也没什么关系。

8、岳哥常说他关注了不代表支持、不关注也不代表反对，欢迎建议。

结果人家 Toly 转发对 1011 暴跌的质疑并嘲讽恢复速度后，直接取关。

Over the last few months at @river_ai_inc we’ve developed what we believe is the best system in the world for building your own internal custom models, driven by 10 years of experience training top models at DeepMind, OpenAI and xAI.

In order to best support our customers, we’ve decided to do something radical: We also deploy our API on-prem on your compute cluster, and if you don’t have compute we will help you find it.

Again and again we’ve seen that custom models designed for your own internal workflows outperform top frontier models on performance, at a fraction of the cost (1 percent or less).

We’re just at the beginning of the custom model era, but its already clear that in the future more than 99% of LLM tokens will be generated on efficient custom models. The economics of it are just too powerful, and it’s far easier than people think once you have the right tools in place.

The reason why small models will dominate is due to the physics of deep learning: A general model that can do everything needs more capacity and training it on the whole distribution of all tasks is more challenging, so the model will be larger and more expensive, and wont perform perfectly on every task. A small model trained on a targeted domain usually outperforms it.
author: harjtaggar
quoted_text:
We were able to fine tune an open weight model (Qwen3.5-9B) on proprietary internal data at @coinbase, and it out performed frontier models, at much lower cost and speed, for a specialized task (fraud prevention in this case).

I think we'll see more of this pattern inside companies. The frontier models are amazing generalists. But increasingly you'll see specialist models out perform on more narrow tasks, either working on teams, or by themselves.

We're making it easy to fine tune models internally for our employees. We even have a skill for it in our internal harness that makes it easy to spin these up and start training them:

"/fine-tune-and-serve-llm I want to fine-tune Qwen for payments risk review. help me get started"

I imagine we'll have some backend services that could be replaced entirely by this new architecture.

1. Depending on the protocol, product is so much more than the base SC. Eg: at @yield we moved more of the allocation algo onchain and via adapters, based on feedback around transparency. Another pure analytics example is our Baskets feature (invest in multiple vaults at once). Another example is yoGateway when multiple partners wanted to carry the vault and have attribution so we built on top instead of changing the core SC

2. SC can't be touched but the app layer can evolve: eg new zapping methods, user behavior that informs future upgrades, etc

3. Not necessarily waterfall if the SC is upgradable. You can also architect the protocol in a way that the base is immutable and functionality is upgradeable in periphery contracts (eg Hooks). Fully immutable protocols work best for primitives

text:
a few notes on local AI 

and our computers that run it

around fifteen months ago, i led the pre-seed round for a weird local AI project

it was called @actualinc

led by @Tom_A_Lynch

for the first time in the AI movement

open models are now good enough for a large and growing set of workflows, especially where latency, privacy, bandwidth, and token cost are critical

hermes agent from @nousresearch and ‘lab’ by @primeintellect have broken this idea wide open with killer products today, built on open rails

we are no longer forced to assume that every useful task must route through one of a few centralized frontier APIs

and so

tom and the squad at @actualinc have painstakingly created a new type of proprietary inference engine

for all types of computers

maybe you are an owner of one of the tens of millions Apple macs

or an owner of one of the millions of RTX-class machines

or maybe you run a small team or company

and you are starting to realize

what many others across the world, have started to realize

which is that sometimes centralized AI systems bring their own set of unique problems

especially as our workflows move into an always-on, agentic era which might sometimes come with:

- exorbitant costs
- no privacy
- lack of control

but a problem remains

running local AI is still too hard

firing up one model on one machine is difficult enough

but running models across different machines means navigating drivers, networking, model sizing, memory limits, API setups 

stitching together hardware is messy across Mac, Windows, Linux, NVIDIA, Apple, AMD

heterogenous systems were never meant to work seamlessly together like this

today, you'll find that most of the local inference software available is built around single users, for a single machine use case

running inference capacity in bulk, across many users, and many kinds of computers

that is a different animal altogether

tools like llama.cpp made local models accessible, but they are not designed to coordinate tens of thousands of heterogeneous machines under a live supply network

vLLM-style batching can be economical, but vLLM is limited in the machines it can run on

the local AI movement requires a simple product experience, for a tough engineering problem

that is the problem @Tom_A_Lynch pitched me fifteen months ago

and the problem @actualinc has been engineered to solve

now with the help of his cracked and growing team @skooookum, @somewheresy, @jack15032, and the rest of the crew 

starting with their first product

go to https://t.co/jvHBxrBt9d

in under one minute, install the @actualinc client, authorize your machine, load a model, and @actualinc turns your personal device into a private inference endpoint

in less than twenty seconds, add a second, or third, or fourth machine of any type and it will start behaving like a small private cluster

from a technical POV

actual runs as a lightweight daemon on each machine and turns local hardware into a routable inference endpoint

each node reports its available memory, accelerator type, model state, and health back into the cluster, while the user interacts with a single API surface

instead of managing ports, drivers, or SSH sessions
a relay layer lets requests reach machines without forcing users to configure networking or expose their devices directly

and as a result

computer owners of all kinds of computers

can get local inference clusters

- when they want to control costs
- when they want to control privacy
- when they want to build on top of a neutral stack

eventually, over time

computer owners running these local clusters should be able to seamlessly contribute their unused capacity back to the @actualinc network 

for a market to price

and for someone else to purchase

you can think of @actualinc as building the engine and control plane for datacenter style throughput in homes, in offices, in small to medium sized businesses, and in very big sized businesses

because there are hundreds of gigawatts already on the grid right now, that are waiting 

on desks, in storage closets

to become actual computers

text:
刚看到 micro1 创始人 Ali Ansari 宣布，公司年化收入突破 10 亿美元，历史上始终保持盈利。三年前他们一夜之间失去 60% 的收入，差点破产，如今估值已经达到 40 亿美元，核心团队却只有 180 人。

但我觉得比这组数字更值得关注的，是 micro1 几天前宣布的另一件事。

它准备在未来一年投入 10 亿美元，专门购买企业的真实运营数据。

我翻了一下他们的数据采购计划，发现价格已经相当明确。一家企业可以把内部 SOP、项目记录、CRM 数据、工作流程甚至内部沟通记录授权给 micro1，符合条件的企业可以获得 10 万到 200 万美元以上的报酬。帮它介绍一家符合条件的企业，推荐奖励甚至可以达到 5 万美元。

过去我们讨论 AI 训练数据，想到的还是互联网上的文章、图片、视频。

但真正决定一个员工值多少钱的，往往是那些根本不会出现在互联网上的经验。

比如一个资深项目经理如何处理客户的临时变卦，一个律师怎么在几份互相矛盾的材料里作出判断，一个销售主管如何决定什么时候该放弃一笔订单。

这些经验过去散落在员工的大脑、邮件、聊天记录和公司内部系统里。micro1 现在做的，就是把它们整理成可以反复训练 AI Agent 的环境。

我觉得这背后其实藏着一个很大的利益分配问题。

一个员工工作十年积累的经验，最后沉淀成公司的运营数据。公司拿这些数据去授权，获得一笔收入。AI 实验室利用这些数据训练出更强的模型，再把能力卖给成千上万家企业。

原来只有少数资深员工掌握的专业经验，就有机会变成整个行业都能购买的标准化能力。

那么创造这些经验的人，能够分享到多少价值？原本依赖这些经验建立竞争优势的企业，又会失去多少优势？

当然，这一切不会因为买到几份 SOP 就自动发生，真实业务数据的授权也有隐私和使用范围限制。但 micro1 已经开始为这套机制建立市场，而且规模正在迅速扩大。

我现在越来越觉得，AI 对劳动市场最深远的改变之一，可能发生在大规模裁员之前。

人类积累了几十年的工作经验，正在被重新定价。拥有数据授权权利的人，可能比真正创造这些经验的人更早拿到钱。

这恐怕会成为 AI 时代一场很大的利益分配争议。
author: sleepy0x13
quoted_text:
about 3 years ago, micro1 lost 60% of its revenue overnight and almost went bankrupt.

today, i'm proud to share we've surpassed $1B annual run rate while remaining historically profitable.

it’s been a special journey. we’re grateful for every struggle, moment, and person who has been part of it.

we've taken a very untraditional path to get here. our core team is only ~180 people, spanning 14+ countries, and fully remote.

many of our decisions sacrifice hundreds of millions of revenue and slow us down short term. but we believe they compound into advantages that are impossible to replicate long term.

the long term is now.

these are the 8 principles that made micro1 a leader in the data industry and will soon make us number one:

1.) human 1st AI: treat the tens of thousands of experts helping train models with absolute best-in-class care. our goal is to make AI training one of the largest, highest paying, and most enjoyable job sectors in the world.

2.) U.S. first: we refuse to work with adversarial nations, or export data that improves models against the interests of Americans.

3.) long-term research over short-term ARR: invest in deep research, products, and infrastructure for years from now, not just the next customer pipeline.

4.) proper incentives for intensely hard work: no arbitrary requirements like 996. inspire people to work extremely hard with outlier incentive structures instead of forcing weekend work. we’ve maintained close to 100% core team retention as a result.

5.) stay lean and global: we’ve reached $1B run rate with ~180 people, and intend to slow team growth significantly from here. exceptional talent is found around the world, and pedigree is the wrong thing to over-index on.

6.) execution alignment: company to retain a streamlined board so we can optimize for the next several decades, remain light-weight and dynamic, and take bold & calculated risks.

7.) abundant intelligence improvement: invest in building data generation models to make high-quality datasets and RL environments dramatically less expensive and more abundant.

8.) scale data on realism and horizon: realism brings the complexity of the real world into training models, while horizon extends how long models can work and how much complexity they can handle. both have enormous room to scale, and we’re pushing the limits of both.

additionally: after surpassing $500M run rate this summer, we priced our Series B at a $4B valuation, alongside a ~$25M tender to give our early employees liquidity as we build for the long term. the round was led by Dream Ventures, a longtime supporter and one of our earliest investors, alongside Microsoft, Javelin, Flybridge, G Squared, Up Partners, and LG.

we’re also grateful to be backed by incredible industry leaders, including Guodong Zhang (co-founder of xAI), Andy Fang (CTO of DoorDash), Igor Babuschkin (co-founder of xAI), Behnam Neyshabur (founder of Mirendil), Jerry Tworek (ex-VP of Research at OpenAI), and many more.

data is on its way to becoming the largest industry humanity has ever seen, and we're certain this is just the beginning.

best,
Ali

text:
今天继续分享 Web3 量化经验，发现很多人谈量化，第一反应还是研究指标、预测价格。但在 Crypto 市场里，还有几条完全不同的路线：对冲、套利和做市。

这三类策略未必需要预测 BTC 涨跌，更多是在研究不同市场的价格差、资金需求和交易机制。

整理了几个比较重要的经验。

1】中性策略不赌涨跌，但不代表没有风险

先说对冲。

最经典的例子是买入 BTC 现货，同时做空等量的永续合约，尽量抵消价格涨跌带来的方向性风险。

如果永续合约资金费率为正，空头就可能持续收到多头支付的资金费。另一种方式是做空价格高于现货的交割合约，等待基差到期收敛。

这里有个容易误解的地方：Delta Neutral（Delta 中性）不等于 Risk Free（无风险）。

假设 BTC 大幅上涨，现货确实在赚钱，但合约空头可能持续浮亏。如果两边的资金放在不同保证金账户，现货的浮盈未必能及时拿去补充合约保证金。

所以中性策略真正考验的，不只是对冲比例，还有资金管理、保证金结构和极端行情下的生存能力。

换句话说，套利收益有一部分，本质上是市场付给承担资金和风险约束的人的补偿。

2】跨交易所套利，最难的不是找到价差，而是把价差真正赚到手

比如 BTC 在 A 交易所报价 100,000 USDT，在 B 交易所报价 100,300 USDT。

表面上有 0.3% 的价差。

但如果两边的手续费、滑点和冲击成本合起来就超过 0.3%，这笔交易实际上没有利润。

还有一个容易忽略的问题：两边不一定能够同时成交。

你可能已经在 A 买入，B 的价格却突然消失。或者发现价差后，还需要跨链转账、提币和等待确认，等资金到位，机会早就没了。

专业套利团队通常会提前在多个市场配置资金，通过自动化系统尽量缩短两边成交的时间差。

所以研究套利，不能只统计出现过多少次价差，还要统计这些价差有多少真正可以成交。这两者之间的差距，往往就是回测收益和实盘收益的差距。

3】做市商赚的是买卖价差，但最怕库存积累

做市和套利又有些不同。

做市商同时挂买单和卖单，比如 BTC 买价 99,900，卖价 100,100。如果两边能够顺利成交，就可能赚取中间的价差。

但问题是，市场不一定会按你希望的方向成交。

行情连续下跌时，你的买单可能不断成交，卖单却始终卖不出去。结果机器人虽然一直在交易，账户里却积累了越来越多正在贬值的 BTC。

这叫 Inventory Risk（库存风险）。

另一个问题是 Adverse Selection（逆向选择）。你的挂单之所以被成交，可能不是因为你报价好，而是对方掌握了更及时的价格信息。

因此，专业做市不能简单理解成不断低买高卖，还需要根据波动率、订单簿和库存动态调整报价。

Hummingbot 的公开做市框架就提供 Inventory Skew（库存偏斜控制），通过调整买卖挂单数量，把库存维持在目标范围附近。

4】链上做市是另一个市场，不能只盯着手续费年化

在 Uniswap 等去中心化交易所，普通用户也能通过 LP（Liquidity Provider，流动性提供者）的方式参与做市。

比如提供 ETH/USDC 流动性，交易者每次通过资金池兑换资产，LP 就能获得相应的手续费分成。

看起来很像自动收租，但实际收益没有那么简单。

如果 ETH 大幅上涨或下跌，资金池里的资产比例会发生变化。即使赚到了手续费，也可能因为无常损失和价格重新平衡而跑输直接持有原资产。

另外还有 LVR（Loss Versus Rebalancing，相对再平衡损失），描述流动性提供者在价格信息更新过程中承担的一类不利交易成本。

所以衡量链上 LP，不能只看 APR（Annual Percentage Rate，年化收益率），还要看净手续费、库存变化、Gas 成本和风险敞口。

这也是为什么动态调整流动性区间、预测交易量和管理仓位，可以成为独立的量化研究方向。

5】真正值得研究的，是市场为什么愿意把利润给到你

为什么有人愿意支付资金费率？因为他们需要杠杆和方向敞口。

为什么有人愿意支付买卖价差？因为他们更需要立即成交。

为什么链上套利者能够赚钱？因为不同资金池和交易场所需要有人修正价格。

比如链上 MEV（Maximal Extractable Value，最大可提取价值）套利，现在不仅要发现价格错误，还需要参与交易排序和区块空间竞争。部分利润最终会被区块构建者、验证者和订单流入口获取。

因此，对小团队来说，不一定要直接去竞争最成熟的 BTC 高频策略。也可以研究流动性不足的新市场、特殊交易规则、跨平台对冲，或者专门提供交易执行与风控基础设施。

不过市场越小，通常也意味着成交深度更差、风险更集中。竞争少，不等于赚钱容易。

最后，研究 Web3 量化不能只问哪个策略年化最高，而应该同时看四件事：利润从哪里来、能容纳多少资金、实际交易成本有多高，以及极端情况下会亏多少钱。

对于刚入门的人，可以先选一个方向，用真实历史数据完成回测，再做模拟交易。

对冲研究资金费率与基差，套利研究跨交易所可成交价差，做市则研究订单簿、库存和成交概率。

市场为什么愿意为你提供的流动性、资金或交易服务支付报酬？这份报酬又能持续多久？

Web3 量化不只是预测价格，也是在经营流动性、资金和交易执行能力。
author: sera00111
quoted_text:
今天可以聊聊 Web3 量化行业的人才市场，调研了 Wintermute、GSR、Polymarket 等公司的招聘要求，发现不少有意思的地方。

如果你想进入这一行，可能需要先改变一个认识：量化交易公司并不是只招数学特别好、会挖因子的人。交易、策略、工程、风控和流动性业务，都是这个行业的重要组成部分。

1】先讲普遍情况：量化人才主要分成几类

Quant Researcher（量化研究员）负责发现和验证策略；
Algorithmic Trader（算法交易员）负责把策略变成真实交易；
Quant Developer（量化开发工程师）负责数据、回测和执行系统；
Risk Manager（风险经理）则要管理保证金、杠杆、流动性和极端行情风险。

Web3 还多出一些特殊方向，比如 DeFi 策略、链上 MEV、智能合约执行和跨交易所资金管理。

这些岗位的共同基础是数据分析、概率统计、编程和交易机制，但侧重点完全不同。

研究员更看重统计推断和策略验证，交易员更看重市场判断与实际盈亏，开发工程师重视系统稳定性，而风控岗位可能要求更扎实的衍生品数学和清算知识。

2】再看特殊要求：大机构筛选人才的方式很有意思

Wintermute 的 Algorithmic Trader 岗位，并不强制要求候选人已经有真实交易经验，但会测试 Python、数量分析和交易直觉。公司强调这个岗位首先是交易与商业岗位，而不是纯粹做学术研究。

但它的中频 Quant Researcher 岗位又不一样，明确要求有真实部署过的策略，并能提供可证明的生产环境表现。

GSR 的 Quant Developer 招聘则要求候选人理解订单簿、市场微观结构和交易执行，具备高性能编程能力。即使不会 Rust，也可以通过展示学习能力和相关工程经验证明自己。

更特殊的是 Wintermute 的 DeFi Algorithmic Trader。申请时除了 GitHub 和链上项目，还要求在 Sepolia 测试网上签名一条包含 GitHub 用户名的消息，并提交交易哈希。

这意味着它不仅要看你会不会讲区块链，还要验证你是否真正操作过钱包和链上交易。

Polymarket 的量化风控岗位也很有代表性。招聘明确要求熟练使用 AI 辅助开发，但同时必须能独立检查 AI 生成的风险模型，发现那些看起来合理、实际上错误的结论。

3】小白想进入这一行，技能栈应该怎么学习？

我觉得比较合理的顺序是先数据，再统计，然后是交易机制和工程能力。

第一步是 Python、SQL 和数据处理。至少要能独立抓取交易所行情、清洗数据、对齐时间戳，并计算收益、回撤和交易成本。

第二步是概率统计、线性代数和基础最优化。重点理解假设检验、相关性、过拟合和样本外验证，而不是一开始就研究最复杂的机器学习模型。

第三步是金融市场机制。比如现货和永续合约的区别、资金费率、交割基差、订单簿、保证金和清算规则。

第四步是 Git、Linux、API 接口和自动化系统。做高频交易可以进一步学习 C++、Rust 和低延迟工程；做链上策略则要研究 EVM、智能合约、Gas 和 MEV。

真正重要的是每学一个知识点，都能在实际数据或代码中验证，而不是只会解释概念。

4】作品集不要追求数量，先做三个能讲清楚的项目

第一个是跨交易所资金费率研究。抓取 Binance、OKX、Bybit 的历史资金费率，研究现货与永续合约对冲，在扣除手续费、滑点和资金成本后究竟还能赚多少。

第二个是订单簿与成交模拟。研究不同交易量下的真实买卖价差、盘口深度和价格冲击，比较理论报价与实际可成交价格的差异。

第三个可以选择链上方向，比如 Uniswap LP 收益分析。把手续费、无常损失、价格区间调整和 Gas 成本放到一起，验证提供流动性的真实净收益。

这些项目不一定要马上投入真钱，但需要有完整的数据来源、可复现的代码、样本外测试和失败记录。

最好还能提供 GitHub 仓库、研究报告以及能够展示结果的网页。

5】机构真正看重的，可能是你能否对结果负责

还有一个容易被忽略的方向，就是交易业务与量化技术的结合。

比如 Wintermute 的机构业务岗位，要求理解 OTC、衍生品和流动性服务，能够与交易、产品团队合作，为客户提供对冲和资金解决方案。

这类岗位可能不要求你亲自开发高频算法，但需要你理解机构客户为什么交易、交易成本从哪里来，以及怎样把客户需求变成实际收入。

同样，交易系统工程师也不一定要自己发明策略。有些岗位专门负责跨平台持仓核对、自动结算、风险监控和执行系统。这些工作看起来不如研究 Alpha 有吸引力，却直接决定交易能否安全运行。

所以求职时，最值得积累的是一种完整解决问题的能力：

发现问题 → 获取数据 → 提出假设 → 编写程序 → 验证结果 → 分析风险 → 交付可运行的系统。

最后一个感受是，AI 让普通人更容易接触量化，但没有让真实的量化研究变得简单。

会让 AI 写回测代码，只是第一步。真正有竞争力的人，应该能解释模型为什么有效、在哪些条件下失效，以及怎样让研究成果在真实市场里运行。

text:
a16z's Martin Casado with https://t.co/URbd8O8R0Z CTO Owen He on why a lot of RSI pitches are selling something as old as the steam engine:

Martin: "I see a lot of pitches come in, and a lot of them use the term RSI. And I'll be like, 'Oh, so what do you do?' And they'll say, 'We use AI to create AI.' 'That sounds very interesting. So what do you do?' 'We use AI to create GPU kernels.'"

Owen: "RSI is definitely an overloaded term today... The important thing when you are differentiating them is to ask the question, what is the optimizer and what is the optimizee? When you're self-improving, who is improving?"

"There are people who are saying, 'Okay, we're doing RSI. We have humans using AI to develop better AI.' But that to us is just autocatalysis... the ideas and the improvement come from human brains."

Martin: "Most technical epochs have had autocatalytic effects. There's no way you can create a computer chip without a computer... You could build better steam engines because you could get coal faster, etc. So this notion of using the thing to build the thing faster is not new."

Owen: "That human brain was never the optimizee. Now, for the first time, we could swap the optimizer as the optimizee... The brain of the agents, which is the LLM, the model, can be the thing that you're optimizing, and this leads to this reinvestment of cognitive improvement into itself."

@makermaker_ai @martin_casado
author: a16z
quoted_text:
https://t.co/URbd8O8R0Z co-founders Dhaval Adjodah and Owen He with a16z's Martin Casado on recursive self-improvement, and how to tell when it's real:

A lot of RSI pitches are really just people using AI to build better AI. Tech has always worked that way. You needed computers to build chips. Steam engines got better once you could get coal faster.

Dhaval and Owen's bar is higher. The model has to improve itself: its weights, its harness, even the prompt that tells it what to work on next.

And the gains have to hold up when you count what they cost. They track everyone's experiment spend on a "bleeder board," and one engineer, the Viceroy of Variance, has the job of breaking their results.

Over the past few months, they've started seeing early signs of their system getting better and cheaper at the same time.

text:
The outcome of this constraint is many more small clusters. To turn non-IG credit into IG, you need diversification. That’s the alchemy that unlocks large swaths of capital. Not 1bn to one borrower, 1bn to 100 borrowers. Then you can forget the Nvidia backstops and ig wrappers, and turn GPUs into a standalone financable asset class. Standardization is what makes ai legible to Wall Street. 

The parallel constraint in the power market is already pushing us towards 2-5mw deployments instead of 250mw. Both of these forces will be positive for the sustainability of the industry, as small deployments with a couple of month lead time can better match supply to actual, current demand, reducing the risk of overbuilding. 

Ironically, over time we might even see these smaller deals pricing similarly to larger ig deployments, despite worse credit, as the project complexity becomes a major tradeoff if there is an abs market to sell into.

A post-quantum PoW chain with its own miners, and CoinGecko says its contract is qtc.omft.near. Quantus runs on Quantus. Its market runs on NEAR.

This is "market of markets" in practice, not on a slide. Quantus has no smart contracts by design, so its price discovery, its pairs and its liquidity all live on NEAR Intents: QTC -> USDC/USDT/NEAR, and Rhea on NEAR. A CEX listing came after, and the NEAR venues together still carry more volume than it does.

Not the first time either. ZEC got listed on Solana through NEAR. A chain does not need to be on NEAR for its market to be on NEAR.

Markets move to where liquidity from 35 chains already sits. NEAR did not beat the other chains. It became the market for their coins. Market of markets.
author: zacodil
quoted_text:
NEAR flipped the L1 game. Every L1 before it played zero-sum: my chain wins only if your users leave your chain for mine. So everyone paid for the move. Liquidity bribes, paid listings, memecoin seasons, TVL that vanished the day the rewards did.

NEAR refused to play. No bribes, no sponsored pumps, no paying exchanges to care. It built NEAR Intents instead, a product that needs nobody to leave anywhere. It serves users on 35 chains where they already sit, charges a fee for the service, and every chain it touches ends up with more liquidity, not less.

That one refusal explains everything else about NEAR Intents today:

> Revenue from day one. A product that is its own distribution has to pay its own bills, so fees and buybacks were the plan, never an afterthought.
> Dynamic sharding proven in mainnet. Volume up 9x in a year and the chain just runs: no congestion, no fee spikes, no downtime.
> A door for other ecosystems. Zcash found its biggest decentralized market on Intents. Quantus launched there before any exchange.

Other chains paid users to come. NEAR built the thing users were already looking for, and the users brought their chains with them.
