quoted_text:
My biggest takeaways from @JoshWoodward (Head of @Google Labs, the Gemini App, and Google AI Studio)

1. The best ideas almost never come from a design sprint or brainstorm. At Google Labs, the ideas that became NotebookLM, Google Flow, Google Beam, and AI Studio all started with small groups of people who were obsessed with an insight and couldn’t stop themselves from building. These ideas surfaced in the shower, over a weekend, in a hallway. The implication for teams everywhere is that the environment matters more than the process. “You cannot microwave a good idea.”

2. Fall in love with the problem, not the product. Most ideas require three, four, or five significant pivots before they either find traction or get shut down. Teams that get hooked on a specific solution will struggle to make those pivots. Teams that are attached to the problem—the underlying pain point or the user behavior they are trying to shift—can keep adjusting until they get it right. 

3. When looking for early PMF, data and retention are important, but the strongest signal of PMF is in people’s eyes. Do they light up? Do they lean in? When you show someone a prototype and they’re genuinely engaged, you feel it. When NotebookLM’s first AI podcast demo was played in a hallway, the reaction was immediate and unmistakable.

4. Keep a list of what is “almost possible,” and move fast when something crosses over. Google Labs keeps a live list of experiences that are almost possible. When something crosses the threshold, Josh describes it as “a phase shift,” like solid to gas, and the team moves immediately. Maintain a running list of things that are almost ready, and have a team positioned to sprint when one of them arrives.

5. Every company needs to think like a labs team now. The underlying technology is changing so fast that what’s possible is shifting from week to week. Which means that every company needs to be spending time playing with the latest models, running far-out experiments, and being first to discover what they unlock before the competition does—and then bringing those discoveries to the rest of the org.

6. When something is not working, the team almost always knows before the leader does. Josh’s instinct as a leader is not to be the one who decides to shut down a project. He watches instead for the passion running out, for the sense that the team has tried everything and nothing is working. His goal is to create an environment where people feel safe enough to say, “I don’t think this is working.”

7. Someone’s “unlearning rate” is one of the most valuable skills right now. Everyone talks about growth mindset and learning speed. Josh is watching for something different: How quickly can someone take an insight, validate or invalidate it through testing, and then let it go? The ability to walk away from a prior belief or approach when the evidence says you should is rare and becoming more valuable.

8. Roles are not blurring into one universal “builder” role. There is a tendency in the current moment to talk as though everyone is becoming a generalist builder. Josh thinks this would be a bad idea. The best people on his teams still have a primary specialty—a major—and also a “minor” they’ve developed. The advice he gives to early-career PMs who are excited about vibe coding and prototyping is clear: build adjacent skills in service of becoming an exceptional PM, not as a replacement for it.

9. A well-designed lab needs isolation, a clear mission, and the ability to create “good trouble.” Three things matter when setting up an internal labs team. First, it needs structural independence, reporting far enough from existing business units that weird ideas can survive long enough to prove themselves. Second, the lab’s mandate has to be explicit: are you graduating ideas to existing products, or inventing new categories? Clarity on that question changes almost every decision. Third, the lab should be a place to challenge how the company itself works, not just what it builds. At Google Labs, that included piloting new job ladders and builder roles before rolling them out more broadly.

10. Google Labs manages the marathon-sprint tension through seasons. At any given time, roughly 20 to 30 experiments are running in parallel, but individual teams experience a defined rhythm: sprints, post-launch recovery, and open exploration periods. After Google I/O each year, many labs teams enter a mode that looks unproductive from the outside: no shipping, just hacking, building, and discovering. Josh treats this as the seedbed for the next season.

text:
昨天 Meta 发布 Muse Wonder 和 Wonder Full，扎克伯格接受《金融时报》采访时宣布，Meta 已经追上 OpenAI 和 Anthropic，同时明确反对放慢 AI 研发。

这次确实有点东西。Wonder Full 在 Artificial Analysis 的评测中拿到 56 分，距离 Claude Opus 5.5 的 58 分已经很近。Meta 花了 14 个月重组团队、疯狂挖人、砸算力，终于重新挤进了第一梯队。

当年 Meta 在模型能力上落后，扎克伯格是开源最积极的拥护者。Llama 系列的出现，某种程度上就是要把 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 建立起来的技术壁垒打掉。

现在 Meta 追上来了，Muse Wonder 系列却没有开放权重，最强的 Wonder Full 甚至只能通过付费订阅使用。

硅谷巨头嘴里的开源、安全、技术民主化，很多时候都得结合它们当时在排行榜上的位置来理解。

落后的时候，希望技术尽可能开放；追上来的时候，开始考虑怎么收费；刚刚追上，自然最不希望有人宣布比赛暂停。

扎克伯格可能是这群人里商业目标最清楚的一个。

毕竟 Meta 已经被苹果卡过一次脖子了。他太清楚把下一代技术入口交到别人手里是什么滋味。

扎克伯格真正想避免的事情，是十年后几十亿人每天通过 OpenAI 或 Anthropic 的 Agent 使用互联网，而 Meta 只能在后面提供社交内容和广告库存。

从这个角度看，他现在反对减速也就很好理解了。14 个月砸出来的追赶成果，必须趁着窗口期尽快转化成下一代平台的控制权。

quoted_text:
Yale researchers have unveiled a new imaging platform that can measure the metabolic activity of individual cells and identify their specific cell type, all within a single slice of intact human tissue. The method, called REDCAT (Raman Enhanced Delineation of Cell Atlases in Tissues), bridges a long-standing gap in biology by connecting what a cell is genetically programmed to do with its actual physical behavior.  Reported in the journal Nature Methods, the technology was developed by a collaborative team led by professors from Yale University, the University of California, San Diego, Columbia University, and the University of Pennsylvania.

"By combining technologies, REDCAT provides an exciting and powerful advance that allows users to connect cell type or state to metabolic function," said Allison Doerr, chief editor of Nature Methods.

“Our experiments suggest that small AI models may be months away from being capable enough to self-replicate on commercial IoT devices, like smart ovens and off-brand Android TV boxes. A replicator like this would be challenging to shut down, since there’s no centralized point to shut off - though it may be slow (with a doubling time of days). Unlike non-AI malware, it could also figure out unfamiliar devices on its own. In our evals, a 9B model got inference running on 8 of the 9 hardware types we tested.

Models of 30B parameters and under can already complete many of the individual steps for replication today, though they make mistakes when composing them end to end. In our simplified evals, GLM-5.2 and stronger models are capable of end to end replication. If small models improve at their historical rate, they’ll match this capability level by the end of this year. Small weight-based replicators may be possible soon after.” -@bucketofkets @willzhou97

关于papertrade目前最好的刷币方式
我觉得不是在该平台同时做多空
而是在HL做空 在Paper做多

这是因为，我们假设多空方向都是50%的概率，HL的空单可以每小时收到资金费率，Paper则不用支付资金费率。

当然 这个细节很简单很容易被发现，你们可以去看看Paper上面做多的资金是做空资金的2:1以上的比例，所以至少是大部分人知道这个细节的。

后续就是等到资金回到2m，平仓paper亏损的和HL的多单进行对冲亏损，此时铸币比例会回到1:100，目前铸币是1:30，相差3x还多。

这个方式会出现的就是如果要是HL的亏钱了Paper赚钱了，那没招，只能抗住，就当吃资金费了。

author: sreeramkannan
quoted_text:
Mike was my colleague at Berkeley, and he's been fairly skeptical of deep learning's trajectory for years. Most scientists are skeptics, and it can take a big shock to get someone to consider a possibility that goes against the anchoring effect coded in our DNA.

I too was somewhat of a skeptic until ~6 months ago, and people ask me all the time why I joined Anthropic. 

It started in April, when a friend I've known for 20 yrs messaged me saying he'd be in the Bay Area in a week, and he suggested we meet up. I invited him to my house for dinner, and he told me he had just joined Anthropic. He said the models were becoming increasingly more capable, and he believed both that they'd soon be smarter than him and also that all intellectual work would be highly devalued in the near future, and lastly that society was not at all ready for what's coming.

I'd of course heard claims similar to this before, but not from a friend I'd known for this long, and who I trusted, at my dining room table. It was the initial shock needed to destabilize my own anchoring. Also, I've been fortunate to work with and/or mentor many smart people in my life (e.g. Fields medalists, a 4x Putnam Fellow, IOI first place winners, etc.), so I feel pretty calibrated in recognizing very smart people, and this was someone who is definitely very smart and with impressive such credentials. So, it was hard to ignore this friend saying the models would be smarter than even him in particular.

After that dinner, I decided to do an informal survey, calling and meeting up with a lot of my friends who now work on improving model capabilities at these frontier labs. They all agreed with that first friend. These were all people I'd known 10, 15, 20 years, who mentored me, or I mentored them, or we met professionally in academia. These are people I trust, and their beliefs on this topic were consistent.

I then spent a whole lot of time understanding the missions of different companies, and talking to current and former employees and people in leadership. I read Dario's (long) essays and watched videos on YouTube of company leaders being interviewed. Anthropic's stated mission "to ensure that the world safely makes the transition through transformative AI" felt like exactly the right guiding principle to handle such a society-disrupting technology, and everyone I spoke to at the company was very aligned with this mission. It's easily the most mission-focused place I've ever been at, and everyone takes the work extremely seriously and with a profound sense of responsibility.

And now here I am. And being on the inside, the pace of progress has surprised me more than I first imagined. The moment that pure mathematicians are in, to me, is just a microcosm of what I predict a much larger of society will be grappling with in the not too distant future, and I really hope our leaders and the general public internalize sooner than later just how significant a moment we're in.

KBW 和 TOKEN2049 结束后补一点观察。

从首尔到新加坡，SmartX 在两地各办了一场活动，报名都过了千。看到这个数字当然是开心的。也觉得有一点安心，至少还有很多人愿意来，愿意花时间了解我们在做什么。
但热闹之下，今年的感觉确实和以前不同。感受比较明显的几点：

Overall 新项目少了，老面孔多了。就这次跑的场子来看，边会冷清了一些，连 Marquee、CÉ LA VI 也没了往年的拥挤。熟悉的人还在，当然开心，熟人之间谈事情也更快；只是增量要从哪里来，暂时没看到明确答案。

• 机构化开始落在具体问题上。可以看到主会场这次加了很多机构闭门场，在饭桌上牌照、通道、托管也被反复提起。西装大佬变多了。

• 融资路径在变。早期团队四处 pitch VC 的场面少见了。现在更常见的路径是：产品先上线、先有收入，再走公售平台或社区轮把融资做完，代币以更高的流通直接交给二级市场定价，VC 从定价者变成了跟投者。路径变短了，但产品是否成立的问题没有消失，而是需要面对整个市场给出答案。

• Yield 是这趟最密集的关键词。几乎每场边会都能遇到收益产品。链上停着的钱性质变了，稳定币合规化普及之后，进来的大多是不追求暴富、只想要回报的钱；而 perp 市场的放量，正好把资金费率、基差这些收益来源变成了可以打包的产品。市场少了性感的故事，但资金开始变得认真。

——

过去大家更关心上涨空间，现在也开始思考收益从哪里来，能持续多久，承担什么风险。看起来相似的收益率，背后可能是完全不同的东西。
而收益率的生意，拼的是成本、风控和信任。产品可以很快做得相似，但让人放心把钱留下来，需要更长时间。

行业虽然不断变化，但见到一些熟悉的人仍然认真做事，还是会觉得安心。

quoted_text:
My biggest takeaway from SF Tech Week: the center of gravity has already moved.

Last year everyone was talking about agents.

This year, a lot of the interesting conversations were about everything agents need once they actually start working: routing, search, data, evals, observability, latency, inference cost, GPUs, deployment, reliability.

The question used to be:

Can an agent do this?

Now it increasingly feels like:

How do we make a million agents do this reliably, cheaply, and controllably?

That shift matters.

Companies like Tavily are a good example. Most end users may never know the name, but a huge number of agent workflows need search and web retrieval underneath. Once agents become real products, the boring-looking infrastructure around them becomes extremely valuable.

Another thing Tech Week messes with is your perception of startup outcomes.

You meet founder after founder who raised, got acquired, or somehow went from starting a company to becoming a VP / GM / Head of X at a much larger company in a few years.

After hearing enough of these stories, your brain starts treating this as normal.

It obviously isn't.

Tech Week is basically the Instagram feed of the startup distribution. You are meeting people from the far right tail. The companies that ran out of money, never found PMF, or quietly dissolved are not usually on stage telling you their story.

And even we got acquired can mean very different things: a great strategic outcome, an acquihire, investors getting some money back, or simply a soft landing.

Startups don't just increase expected upside. They massively increase variance.

One other thing I kept hearing was FDE: Forward Deployed Engineer.

The role is interesting because it blurs boundaries that used to feel much cleaner.

Engineer builds.
Sales sells.
PM translates.
But more and more, the valuable person seems to be someone who can talk to the customer, understand the business problem, talk to engineers, turn ambiguity into something executable, and actually ship it.
Engineer + Product + Consultant + Sales.

I increasingly think this is less a job title than a survival skill.

AI is already crawling into every industry and every workflow. So maybe the interesting question is no longer what AI can do.

It is:

What workflow has not been rebuilt yet?

And after spending a few days around all of this, I came away with two contradictory feelings:

How is everyone here doing something this ambitious?

And:

Maybe I should be doing more too.

The Bay Area has never had a shortage of ideas or smart people.

The scarce things are judgment about what is worth doing, the willingness to stay with it for years, and the ability to get other people to care.

Today @TheLancet published our AMIE study with @BIDMC_Medicine, the first prospective study of patient-facing conversational diagnostics in a real clinic.

AMIE is a research system people can chat with before doctors appointments. Testing AMIE outside the lab with real urgent care patients showed how technology can help gather medical histories safely. Clinicians reported that the summaries helped them prepare for visits in 75% of cases and influenced their approach to care in more than half. AMIE’s differential diagnoses also matched the doctors’ final diagnoses 90% of the time giving clinicians more time to focus on patient care.

It’s Google’s first-ever paper in The Lancet’s main journal!

text:
Claude 反蒸馏升级，部分正常 API 集成也得改。

Anthropic 称，新措施让蒸馏者在其自有平台上提取到的 Claude 推理 token 减少了约 90%–99%。

做 Agent、接 Claude API 的开发者，也需要关注这些限制对上下文管理的影响。

它重点保护的是完整推理过程。

内部实验中，用 Claude Opus 4.8 完整推理记录训练的模型，SWE-bench Verified 得分为 80.4%；换成推理摘要后是 71.8%，相差 8.6 个百分点。

这轮防御分三层：

• 限制受保护推理记录跨对话、跨模型、跨账号复用。
• 用两阶段分类器识别提取行为，持续修补绕过方式。
• 对反复尝试者限流、封号，并对蒸馏等特定类别的被拦截请求收费。

正常用户也会承担代价：部分集成需要调整；官方称误报率低于 0.1%，被误拦的请求也可能收费。

这组结果仍是 Anthropic 自报。它也承认，效果能维持多久尚不清楚，还没遇到高度复杂且持续的绕过尝试。

对 Agent 开发者，值得检查的不只是模型能力，还有自己的历史消息编辑和模型切换方式，是否符合推理记录的复用规则。

And today in our current version of how to read through Anthropic PR announcements: 

Anthropic’s latest warning: AI models are months away from self-replicating across smart TVs, ovens, and other household devices.
The reality is a bit less dramatic, of course. What did they actually do? 

They ran a model across 15 cheap Android TV boxes at 0.39 tokens per second. Their replication experiment used a simulated network with deliberately unauthenticated ports, while the capable model ran on separate servers.

Interesting engineering? Absolutely. Evidence of AI worms spreading autonomously through the real world? Not yet.

But “we managed to run a very slow model on cheap TVs” doesn't make quite the same headline as “self-replicating AI is coming.”

Someone borrowed $7.3M against 744,054 $HYPE to trade on papertrade.

The first $3M lost $1.71M in trading, $772K net of staking rewards. Two days later the same wallet borrowed $4.3M more.

It is the largest loss we have found on the leaderboard, and @papertrade_xyz's excellent UI (the read-only account view @izebel_eth shipped) is what makes it easy to check.

Account

0x26b61e7ec6ccd97df9836e3358c8c92d4fa79a13:

- Trading PnL: -$1.71M on $2.84B volume, 6.0 bps. The scripted farmer below paid 1.0
- Staking rewards claimed: $943K
- Cash: $7,799,162 in, $7,027,301 out, net -$771,861
- Kept: 136M staked PAPER at $5.68 per 1,000. The farmer paid $0.34
- One funder: 0x7868e5a7a72ea19e2c5e53b5ca2acbc06dce6f8f

Funder

0x7868e5a7a72ea19e2c5e53b5ca2acbc06dce6f8f:

- 20 Sep: receives 744,054 HYPE from 0x6eafa7930b6d98db674919724c938c7e82dfab70, borrows $25.65M against it on Hyperliquid and sends it back. 0x6eaf repays a HyperLend loan of that size the same hour
- 10 Oct 03:30 UTC: borrows $3.0M more. 03:33: sent to the papertrade account, ten hours before trading opened
- 12 Oct 22:19 UTC: borrows $4.3M more. 22:21: sent to the same account
- Debt: $25.65M before papertrade, $32.95M after, on the same HYPE

One for @hyperlendx and co-founder @fbsloXBT: that 20 Sep move took 744,054 HYPE of collateral and a $25.6M loan off HyperLend in under an hour. It now sits on @chameleon_jeff's native borrow/lend at 5%.

The second draw had not been deposited as of 00:40 UTC today: $6.53M was sitting in the account's wallet. The read-only page will show when it goes in.

The farmer brought $4M of cash and a script, and left with 4.7% of supply for $86K. This account brought a loan and paid 17x more per token.

tl;dr: maybe do not put 744K HYPE at risk to play a 1000x bucket shop, even if the UI is nice.

THAT'S F*CKING INSANE, GROK BOT JUST PLANNED MY TRIP TO LISBON AND BOOKED IT WITH MY CARD.

I ONLY HAD TO ASK. IT HANDLED THE RESEARCH AND THE BOOKINGS.

Elon Musk recently used Grok Bot to buy LEGO for his kids. That made me want to test something bigger: whether it could fully plan, research, and book my trip to Lisbon on its own.

Grok Bot searched for travel options, compared prices, and booked what I needed using my card and the details I provided.

Here’s what it handled:

→ Researched options for my Lisbon trip.
→ Compared prices and picked the best-priced options it found for my request.
→ Completed the bookings using my travel and payment details.

My trip was booked.

Think about how much time usually goes into this: searching, comparing options, checking availability, and filling out booking forms.

This time, I gave that job to Grok Bot.

text:
Anthropic 发了篇研究，预测小模型可能再过几个月，就有能力在不依赖数据中心的情况下自主复制。

他们真的买了 15 台每台 55 美元的山寨 Android 电视盒子，拼起来跑了一个 26B 的模型，速度只有每秒 0.39 个 token，慢得令人发指。

另一组隔离实验里，GLM-5.2 已经能完成简化环境中的跨设备传播。虽然距离现实中的完整自主复制还有明显差距，但按照 Anthropic 的预测，2026 年底小模型就可能接近这个能力门槛。

全世界都在抢 GPU，花几千亿美元建数据中心，结果 AI 自己可能跑去寄生在你家的电视盒子上了。

但仔细想想，真正可怕的地方是，这种 AI 可能彻底打破我们熟悉的算力经济学。

今天不管是 OpenAI 还是一家 AI 创业公司，每生成一个 token 都有成本，算力贵了就得涨价，融资断了就得停机。

但一种能够自主传播的恶意 AI，理论上可以把自己的边际运行成本持续转嫁给陌生人。

它不需要获得用户，不需要考虑收入，甚至不需要自己购买服务器。找到一台存在漏洞的设备，就多了一点免费的计算资源。被感染的设备替它交电费、提供带宽、承担硬件损耗。

而清理这些东西的成本，却要由无数设备所有者、运营商和制造商分别承担。

传统僵尸网络早就能偷算力了，但 AI 带来了一个新的麻烦。过去黑客需要针对特定设备写攻击和部署程序，未来模型可能自己研究陌生硬件，解决环境问题，甚至把失败经验传给下一代。

攻击者的扩张成本越来越低，整个社会的防御成本却可能越来越高。

所以我觉得，这项研究最值得警惕的甚至还不是 AI 失控这种宏大叙事。

如果未来真的出现这种东西，我们可能第一次要面对一批没有商业模式、没有任何合法用户、也找不到明确运营主体，却能够长期存活的软件。

它们没有盈利的压力，也没有停止运行的经济动机。

人类研究了这么多年，想让 AI 帮我们赚钱，最后可能先实现财务自由的是 AI 自己。

而且花的还是我们的钱。

Three layers of confidentiality. All live on Aptos mainnet.

• Identity layer: Keyless Accounts
• Amounts layer: Confidential $APT
• Intent layer: Encrypted Mempool

Each one is opt-in, and each one addresses a different part of what's visible onchain. https://t.co/oyDXh4sy6E
author: Aptos

text:
How each layer works:

• Keyless Accounts let people create and manage blockchain accounts with credentials like Google or Apple, without publicly tying that identity to an onchain address.

• Confidential $APT allows users and institutions to encrypt balances and transfer amounts. A zero-knowledge proof confirms each transfer is valid, while the amounts stay encrypted. Addresses remain visible.

• Encrypted Mempool lets users opt in to encrypt pending transactions until their block is finalized, lowering the risk of MEV attacks.

Airbnb is dead. Well it’s not dead but it’s going to be dying soon.

The Bear case for Airbnb.

I’ve been bullish on Airbnb as a company for many years. But my outlook on the business changed this week. 

Let me tell you why.

In 2012 I purchased my first Airbnb property. Over the years that one property has turned into a portfolio of high-end Airbnb’s that generates almost $1M a month in rental income.

Using ai agents for the first time this week has completely changed my outlook on the company.

Airbnb is facing an existential threat that most of the market is completely missing.

With Airbnb pushing its mandatory host-side commission to 15.5%, the middleman tax has never been higher. 

Enter AI agents. (Hark, Dot, Muse, Grok Bot, etc)

Right now, booking a vacation rental requires navigating a siloed app and paying heavy platform tolls. 

But your AI agent won't care about Airbnb's brand wall. When you know the property you want to book and you ask it “what’s the cheapest way to book the property” it will query property management system APIs directly, find the exact same home, and execute a direct booking that saves everyone 15%.

Airbnb's entire model relies on holding supply captive behind a closed interface. 

When AI agents can autonomously search, verify reviews, negotiate terms, and book direct with property operators, that walled garden turns into a leaking pipe.

The middleman tax's days are numbered.

I’m predicting that Airbnb’s growth rate will slow down significantly in the next 24 to 36 months. And within 5 years they will be seeing negative growth.

The same can be said for most other online marketplaces that don’t have unique inventory that can only be booked directly on their platform and nowhere else.

text:
李录2026年哥大演讲：AI泡沫、中国经济、价值投资，唯独对Crypto的判断，我不认同！（少刷抖音，干点正经事）

芒格的得意门生、喜马拉雅资本创始人李录，在哥伦比亚大学第36届格雷厄姆与多德论坛上，讲了很多值得反复思考的东西。

1、AI是一场真正的技术革命，但资本市场正在为“人造神”支付天价。

李录认为，硅谷把AI从生产力工具一路包装到RSI、AGI、超级智能，最后演变成一场估值万亿美元的“半神IPO”。

但AI每次推理都需要芯片、电力和算力，商业模式终究要接受收入、利润和投资回报率的检验，未来可能经历多轮繁荣与崩溃。有意思的是，他并不排斥AI：

截至2026年6月底披露的13F，其美股仓位近48%集中在Google母公司Alphabet。反对AI估值泡沫，和长期持有真正赚钱的AI企业，完全可以同时成立。

2、美股越疯狂，被市场遗忘的好公司反而越有机会。

李录提到，标普500从2010年至2026年年化回报约14%—15%，但2000年至2010年基本没有赚到钱，拉长26年，回报又回到年化高个位数。

他认为，当资金疯狂涌向少数AI巨头时，另一边必然有大量现金流健康的企业被市场冷落。市场越两极分化，保持理性的投资者越容易找到错误定价的机会，前提是你真的能独立估值，而不是跟着市场情绪跑。

3、中国经济最大的矛盾，是制造业升级成功与居民财富缩水同时发生。

李录对中国的分析挺深刻：过去几年，中国一边全力推进先进制造、半导体和新能源，一边承受房地产下行对家庭资产负债表的冲击。房价下跌、居民去杠杆，导致消费疲软和储蓄增加。

但另一边，美国的技术封锁反而给中国半导体企业创造了最稀缺的东西——真实订单。他还提出一个很值得思考的长期方向：当房地产不再承担中国家庭最主要的财富储存功能，优质企业股权有机会逐渐接替它的位置。

4、投资最重要的不是赚了多少钱，而是你占全球购买力的比例有没有增加。

货币会贬值，资产会经历周期，真正长期有效的办法，是以合理价格持有那些能够持续创造价值的优秀企业，让企业的盈利能力与自己的知识一起复利。

他还借用巴菲特的比喻：股市是一座连着赌场的教堂，投资者必须决定自己到底站在哪一边。投机可以快速赚钱，但最难的始终是保住本金、健康、家庭、信誉以及几十年积累下来的信任。

5、李录对Crypto的态度极其悲观，甚至认为它最终会自行消失。

他的理由是，加密货币缺乏主权国家的强制执行机制，无法可靠承担货币功能。

我对这个判断感到非常失望，我说一下我的看法：

从2024年美国现货比特币ETF获批，到2025年GENIUS稳定币法案正式成为法律，再到2026年美国SEC为美股代币化交易提供监管豁免，美国金融体系已经开始主动拥抱区块链。

虽然CLARITY市场结构法案9月在参议院受阻，但监管层推动资产上链的方向并没有因此停止。

在我看来，美国推动这一系列变化，背后有两条非常清晰的金融战略：

一条是通过美元稳定币建立全球化的数字美元支付和结算网络，扩大美元的国际使用范围，并增加对美债的潜在需求。

另一条是通过美股代币化，让美国股票及其他金融资产突破传统交易时间、跨境分销和结算效率的限制，进一步扩大美国资本市场的全球覆盖能力。

说白了，美元稳定币负责把美元送到全世界，美股代币化负责把美国金融资产卖到全世界，而区块链正在成为连接两者的重要基础设施。

最让我感慨的是，很多传统金融投资大佬，能够精确计算一家企业未来几十年的现金流，却很难理解金融基础设施本身也会发生革命。

text:
Ok, this was a goldmine of insights re: the future of commerce with agents, straight from @finkd  + @alexandr_wang 

24 key takeaways:

1/ Zuckerberg says agentic commerce is not a 20% conversion lift. It actually creates customers who never existed
->  He used Instacart ~2x a year on Priscilla’s account. Got his own account for Muse. Now orders 1-2x a week. "I am a new Instacart subscriber, and I just wouldn’t have done this before."

2/ Meta’s CEO just asked the scariest retail question of the decade: is the Instacart account for me, or for my Muse?
->  Over time agents effectively get accounts. TAM for commerce is no longer "number of people." Anyone who sits this out "is gonna end up feeling sad"

3/ Muse is one of the first products where people fully delegate purchases to an agent
->  Wang: agentic shopping left the slide deck. "It’s really happening." Teas, groceries, random products. Trust, not demos

4/ Zuckerberg’s Saturday baking loop is the agentic commerce demo nobody scheduled
->  Muse + daughter Aurelia invent recipes. Instacart ingredients land before bake time. Watermelon launch weekend: Muse threw a watermelon in the bag unprompted

5/ John Collison calls agentic commerce a discontinuous event for how all business pipes work
->  Demand shifts toward agents the way demand shifted from brick-and-mortar to ecommerce. Old channels stay. Their share of the pie shrinks

6/ The long-run board question for every brand: do you want a slice of agentic demand, or not?
->  Agentic commerce grows as a portion of the pie. Sitting it out is a strategy choice, not a wait-and-see default

7/ Collison told Patrick Collison in 2023 he was "way behind the eight ball" on agentic commerce
->  "Agents are gonna be buying things, and you’re not prepared for it." Directionally correct. Three years early. Stripe Sessions May announcements. Volume only went vertical as of September

8/ Stripe’s bet: agent-to-commerce is clearly how people will buy things
->  Buying-stage friction was always broken. Early AI product research already had PMF. Computer use was "the last big unlock." Ask Muse to buy almost anything and it figures it out

9/ Computer use is the ultimate backwards-compatibility layer for commerce
->  No need for every merchant to rebuild for agents first. The agent can operate the old web. Nat obsessed over this set of problems at Meta

10/ Muse’s commerce value prop is not "better ads." It is deleted research tabs
->  No clicking 12 sites. Criteria auto-apply: "I need it by Wednesday" and the agent only shops what can arrive by Wednesday. Keyword search was insane by comparison

11/ Wang’s Euler Muse already runs a weekly obscure-tea procurement desk
->  Farms in Taiwan and Japan. Sourced and delivered. Personal agent as buyer, not chatbot

12/ Zuck’s consumer thesis kills the search-box internet for a big share of demand
->  Most people don’t actually like reading that much. Text is tolerated. Glasses + vision + voice become the buy surface. Maybe no app store. Generate the purchase path in your field of view

13/ Meta rejected "coding is all that matters" because consumer agents live in multimodal reality
->  People film, watch, listen, talk. Commerce agents that only read docs lose the real world where buying happens

14/ Dedicated VM per agent is a commerce prerequisite, not a security nice-to-have
->  Nobody hands an agent a credit card on shared elastic compute. Privacy has to feel real before delegated checkout scales

15/ Meta AI still reaches "a ton of people" and Zuck still calls it retrieval, not delegation
->  Chat that answers is not commerce. Commerce starts when the agent gets stuff done and spends

16/ "Everyone is going to write tons of code. They’re just not going to know they’re writing code"
->  Same pattern for checkout flows, vendor research, returns, reorders. The user stays in the intent. The agent ships the pipeline

17/ Stripe × Muse integration already works well enough that Collison called it out on air
->  Coding agents + commerce rails. Developer path and consumer path converging on the same buy graph

18/ OpenRouter already routes 10T+ tokens a day across hundreds of models
->  Model gateway becomes part of the commerce stack: price route, outage route, experiment route. Stripe agreed to acquire it in the same arc

19/ After SFT, desired agent behaviors only fire ~10% of the time. RL is what makes a buyer reliable
->  A shopping agent that follows "by Wednesday / under $40 / organic only" 10% of the time is a toy. Elicitation is the product

20/ Product obsession math still applies at checkout: each nuance may be ~2% to the user
->  In aggregate that is why one agent becomes the default buyer and another gets uninstalled after one bad order

21/ Active memory is a commerce moat
->  Remember dietary rules, kid allergies, preferred farms, last bad SKU, standing Saturday bake. OpenClaw-style compaction that goes buggy AF cannot be your household buyer

22/ Brands that only optimize human conversion rate are solving last cycle’s problem
->  Zuck’s line: opportunity is not "20% more efficient on the conversion rate." Opportunity is net-new subscribers created by agent workflows

23/ The unit of demand is shifting from a person with a browser to a person with an agent that has accounts
->  TAM expands because agents shop while humans sleep, train, parent, and work. Frequency jumps (2x/year → 1-2x/week) before price sensitivity even moves

24/ Closing frame from the pint, applied to retail
->  Stay technical on agent checkout. Stay in the details of trust, memory, criteria, and delivery constraints. Stay at the frontier. Easy to fall behind while still running great human ecommerce

text:
Elon：当中国掌握一项制造技术，世界其他国家加起来都未必能竞争

今天，中国存储芯片企业长鑫存储（CXMT）的4F² DRAM技术进展引发市场关注。但真正值得关注的，是Elon Musk随后发表的一段评论。

Elon指出，一旦中国掌握某项产品的制造技术，其扩大生产规模的能力往往超过世界其他国家的总和。

他举了两个例子：太阳能和锂电池。这不是一句简单的赞美，而是对全球制造业竞争格局的深刻判断。

① 中国制造最可怕的不是技术突破，而是规模化能力

一旦突破技术门槛，中国企业往往能够迅速扩大产能、降低成本，并通过激烈竞争推动整个行业重新定价。光伏如此，锂电池如此，电动汽车也正在经历类似过程。技术决定能否进入市场，规模和成本决定谁能最终主导市场。

② 存储芯片会成为下一个光伏产业吗？

长鑫存储正在推进4F² DRAM架构，并计划在2026年底前推出采用相关技术的DDR5服务器内存产品。相比传统6F²架构，4F²理论上可以将单个存储单元面积缩小约33%，在相同面积下提高约50%的存储密度。

如果技术成功量产，并实现良率和成本优势，将对全球DRAM市场产生深远影响。更重要的是，中国存储芯片企业已经具备一定规模：

• 长鑫存储：全球DRAM市场份额约10%，排名第四。

• 长江存储：全球NAND市场份额约14%，已进入全球主要供应商行列。

中国正在同时向全球两大存储芯片市场发起挑战。当然，技术突破不等于大规模量产，长鑫仍需证明新架构的商业竞争力。

③ Elon承认：SpaceX是一个罕见的例外

Elon在评论中还提到了SpaceX。他说，SpaceX送入轨道的有效载荷质量，大约比世界其他航天企业总和高一个数量级。但在SpaceX之外，中国已经占据全球其他航天发射质量的大部分。

他甚至形容：

“SpaceX is an anomaly in the matrix.”

SpaceX是整个体系中的一个异常存在。

这句话很有意思。

Elon实际上是在强调，中国的规模化制造能力已经非常强大，而SpaceX是少数在特定领域仍拥有压倒性规模优势的美国企业。

④ 全球存储芯片产业可能迎来重新洗牌

过去几十年，全球DRAM市场主要由三星、SK海力士和美光主导。长鑫的崛起正在改变这一格局。如果4F²技术成功商业化，并在2027—2028年形成大规模产能，可能产生三个重要后果：

第一，普通DRAM生产成本下降，全球存储芯片价格面临新的竞争压力。

第二，三星、SK海力士和美光的市场份额及利润率可能受到冲击。

第三，更便宜的存储芯片可能降低AI数据中心、自动驾驶和机器人系统的硬件成本。

不过，Elon也特别指出，先进HBM、SRAM与逻辑芯片集成，以及3D堆叠和散热技术，仍然具有更高的技术壁垒。中国在普通DRAM领域取得突破，不代表已经全面领先先进存储芯片。

⑤ 真正值得思考的问题

过去二十年，中国已经在光伏、锂电池、电动汽车等领域建立起强大的制造优势。如今，存储芯片可能成为下一个重要战场。但这场竞争还远未结束。

美国仍然拥有强大的芯片设计、先进制造设备和AI技术生态，韩国在存储芯片领域也拥有深厚积累。

未来决定胜负的，不仅是谁先发明技术，更是谁能把技术转化为可靠、低成本、可持续的大规模生产。

Elon今天的评论，实际上揭示了一个越来越重要的产业规律：发明一项技术，可以创造一个产业。但掌握规模化制造能力，才可能重塑整个产业。而这，正是中国制造业最值得全球竞争对手认真研究的地方。
author: mylifeonmystyle
quoted_text:
When China figures out how to manufacture a product, their ability to scale is often greater than the rest of the world combined. We saw this with lithium batteries and solar, for example. 

SpaceX is a rare counter-example, where its mass to orbit is roughly an order of magnitude greater than the rest of the world, BUT China now does a majority of non-SpaceX mass to orbit. SpaceX is an anomaly in the matrix. 

Maybe RAM will be different, but RAM was a low margin commodity only ~3 years ago. LP5 and LP6 are designed to a common standard that China seems to be solving fast. 

Newer HBM architectures and things like an SRAM layer below logic and 3D stacking RAM on top of logic while finding a way to keep the logic cooled will be harder to solve.

text:
很多人在问，也分享一下关于 Opus5.5 做视频剪辑的经验

我会分几个步骤去做这个事情

准备工作是最重要的部分，把口播脚本和对应案例资料等都做好对应关系整理在一个飞书文档里。形式可以参照图1

有一些分镜有自己想法的也会整理进去，包括参考的表达方式或思路

然后会先让 Opus 按照自己的理解剪辑开头 15s 的部分，让他重点打磨视觉细节和动画效果。这样能最大程度让他把视频的视觉质感提上来，试过很多次比一次成片的效果要好很多（图2）

这里再补充一个关键的细节，可以上传一些视觉风格的参考图给它，能很大程度上避免 Claude 模型的设计同质化问题

完成之后再让他生成完整的视频剪辑，再整理一个文档，让团队其他人提交各自的修改意见，让 Claude 自己读自己改就可以，他对于细节理解还是很到位的。修改流程走个一到两轮就差不多了，形式大概参照图 3

配音旁白试了一下 Gemini 3.8 Flash 的 TTS，跟我自己的语调和情绪差距比较大，所以最后还是换成了自己录制的版本。如果不关心这个问题的话 TTS 模型还是很不错的

另外频繁的跟飞书互动需要装个飞书 CLI，直接告诉 Claude 让他帮你安装即可

text:
Standard Reserve 这个设计挺聪明：自家的股票代币池刚要上线，就配一场发射台比赛给它导流。比赛期间发的新币都要和股票代币配对，底层流动性和导流入口都握在储备自己手里。

King of the Markets 怎么玩（10/14 开始，跑 14 天）：
· 每个参赛国家对应一只股票代币，发新币时选一只来配对
· 新币有交易量，就给对应的国家、部署者和交易者记分
· 结束时有分的人都能分到一部分奖池；总分最高的国家，参与者另外瓜分一笔 jackpot
· 奖励 100 万+ USDG 起步，比赛期间交易手续费的 20% 会继续滚进奖池

接着上次的链上数据，补两件事：

1. 每场新分行从 40 个降到 25 个之后，价格一路被抬上去：上次 40 个那场成交约 3,600 枚，最近三场是 4,216、4,533、5,669 枚，都是 25 个全部卖完。单场烧掉的币一度从约 14.6 万枚降到 11 万枚上下，今早这场又回到 14.55 万枚：分行少放了三分之一多，烧掉的币基本没少。

2. 上次说只拿币、没牌照的分不到增发，这里补一句：只拿币也有办法拿收益，就是 S-Bill 质押。锁 15 天，到期默认自动续；利率跟着存款量浮动，发这条时约 93% APR。官方说付出去的每一枚币都是储备用 ETH 在公开市场回购来的，不新增发。提前退出要扣退出费，当期收益也留给继续锁着的人。

比赛上线后，我会盯三件事：
· 股票代币池的技术文档（官方说上线时放到官网），能不能查到具体的池子地址
· 这些池子实际收了多少手续费（比赛期间交易手续费有 20% 进奖池）
· 储备的回购有没有跟着变多。比赛热度能不能回到持币人手里，就看这一环

▌时间回到 2023 年 6 月
Paradigm 发表了一篇影响深远的文章《Intent-Based Architectures and Their Risks》，第一次系统性定义了意图，并断言意图是区块链用户体验与效率跃迁的必经之路。
在 Paradigm 的严格定义中，一个真正的意图，需要同时满足四个条件：
签名的声明式约束集
有边界的状态转换
用户不让渡控制权
严格的交易对手发现机制
此后几年，整个赛道都活在这套框架里。

▌但，MOJO 是那个“异端”。
用上面的尺子量，它甚至不符合意图执行的严格技术定义。
MOJO 本质上是一个中介代理执行系统，用 AI 把意图做成了交互体验，它没有采用意图架构，但抓住了意图真正的精神内核：用户只说我要什么，剩下的交给系统。
不止如此，它还把意图的边界从链上交易，一路扩张到 CEX、预测市场、乃至一切资产。

Paradigm 画出了意图的骨架，MOJO 给了它消费级的血肉。

Muse是不仅把Meta给带起来了，还把CPU板块也给带起来。因为Muse处理大量高频任务，例如跨平台比价（单次旅行行程最多进行 146 次搜索）、处理大量积压邮件，以及自动电话谈判。由于 Meta 主动为用户智能体配置持久化云端执行环境，依赖无头浏览器自动化和高频 API 编排，计算工作负载大幅转回 CPU。让市场预期如果Muse 在Meta m的社交生态中广泛普及，将创造大量服务器 CPU 需求。

。Meta现阶段关键点在模型的性能上，如果能突破，未来的胜负手在Agent 上。当然未来模型真起不来、meta就索性专注做Agent，就像腾讯现在的思路。谁家算力好、token性价比高就用谁的，也未尝没有机会。Meta去推agent也有优势。”现在看Mate大模型还没完全追赶上、但是Mate的Agent则有后来居上的意思。 https://t.co/KbdIA21x4v

如果 Hype 新的 BNB，那 LIT 就是新的 HOOD。
author: EvanCrypto17
quoted_text:
周末去香港参与了 Lighter 的私人饭局，迟到一年，终于见到了 Vlad @vnovakovski 还有几个网上认识的 team 成员。

一起参加的，有几个基金 fund，一些 big trader，还有做市商。其中基金的兴趣在于购入 ethereum:0x232ce3bd40fcd6f80f3d55a522d03f25df784ee2 。

饭局期间，我问了一些极其犀利的问题，拿到了很多一手信息，估计也是社区成员最想听的，来给大家转达一下。

1、美国合规牌照什么时候下来？

快了但不确定。首先大家要知道，CFTC 牌照其实不由 Lighter 团队所决定，而是政府部门什么时间能给批准。Lighter 的目标是 Q4 上了期权之后，同时拿到 CFTC 给的 Perps 和 Options 的牌照。

Lighter 已经与 CFTC 进行了长达 11 个月的合作与澄清，CFTC 已经“完全”认识并理解了 Lighter 的 ZK+Ethereum 技术架构、清算机制、ADL 策略以及 0 fee 的盈利模式等等。可以这样说 —— Lighter 是最最有可能拿到第一张美国的 Defi/DEX 合规牌照。

2、拿到牌照后，Lighter 会使用 Core/Robinhood 还是会重新开发一个实例？

获取到牌照后，Lighter 第一时间会上线 Lighter US，也就是另外一个实例，KYC/AML 均与传统交易公司对齐，同时 Lighter US 会引入 Citadel、Jump 等华尔街大型做市商为 Lighter 做市。（Vlad 之前被 Citadel CEO boss 直聘，工作多年）

资产类别逐一按照 CFTC 监管上线，保持 0 fee 的交易结构。

3、期权 Options 与 LighterEVM 什么时间上线？

目标都是 Q4 上线，但侧重在 Options ，因为技术原因，期权的上线会以二元期权，也就是预测市场为开始，随后升级为传统的欧式期权，同时期权考虑 0 fee 交易开始。

LighterEVM 也是预期 Q4，上线之后将会引入 BTC、HYPE、SOL 等非 EVM 资产现货，当然「股票现货 Spot」也在范围内，同时 LighterEVM 将会催生大量生态项目，例如我后面会发的 wick。

4、年底 12.30 的大额 unlock，团队怎么处理 investor 和 team 的巨量解锁？（这块我问的很直接）。

“investor 都不会卖！” Vlad 说这是他知道的信息。我再追问，你并不能控制他们手来让人家不卖吧， Vlad 意思是：他们说了不卖就是不卖，如果他们要卖的话，完全可以说出来，我们还能帮他们找 OTC 买家，甚至自己都可以买。二级市场直接砸的可能性不高，性价比低，同时也在消耗 VC 自己的信誉。

确实，桌上做的几个基金，都是想来谈 OTC 的。

5、Lighter 与 Robinhood 商业模式一样，要尽可能多获取散户流量，但团队在 Marketing 方面一直如此保守？

团队 Camila 告诉我，其实 Lighter 并不是没有做 MKT，而是一直在考虑 ROI 的问题，现在这个阶段，Lighter 牌照还没下来，而大规模、高质量的流量，只有在牌照之后才会出现。所以团队目前的 Marketing 投入不多，仅以欧美极个别 KOL、还有大的视频访谈为主。（我争取做一次）

Camila 还提到，Web3 贯以的 Agency 和 KOL 营销，她觉得性价比非常低，因此等牌照下来，会以 Web2 方式类似于 Kalshi/Polymarket/Robinhood 那样做营销。

加上 KOL 侧，主要集中在合约交易、PerpDEX的 KOL 为主，欧美、韩国、大中华等地区同时发力。

Marketing 是牌照下来之后，团队要侧重做的地方，因为他们也懂自己的盈利模式需要什么。

6、Vlad 你个人有投资 Cognition 吗？（Cognition 是 Vlad 上一个项目的合伙人 Scott wu 的企业 AI 项目，目前估值 500 亿美金）

Vlad 说，他是 Cognition 的第一个投资人，我说那很有钱了，恭喜。

饭局后，我和团队成员 Sebas 私下聊起，你觉得 Vlad 有没有当时后悔选择做了 Crypto 而没去做 AI，毕竟现在 LIT 代币总市值 40 亿不到，而 Cognition 还没上市就几百亿了。

Sebas 说绝不会，Vlad 同时喜欢 AI 和 Trade，从他之前在城堡证券工作过很多年、Robinhood 的第一个顾问就知道， Vlad 乐于构建交易系统，而 AI 那边，Vlad 个人投资了很多，这些 Vlad 自己也是很骄傲的。而现在好朋友的公司做的这么好，Vlad 更有动力将自己的公司做更好。

7、团队一直提倡的 100% 回购销毁代币，当然对持币者是好事，但公司会因此没有现金流，团队会怎么处理现金流问题？

Vlad 大方承认了这个问题，确实是，他的出发点一直都是 “Lighter 的所有收入权益归 LIT 代币持有者。”但也不得不考虑公司的长期经营问题，现在 team 花的钱都是之前 VC  给的。

饭局上我感觉团队状态很好，他们对自己做的事非常有信心，Vlad 也经常自己开起玩笑，喝着茅台白酒，并没有屏幕上一直在正襟危坐很 nerd 的感觉。

text:
I've been using Ledger devices for many years, and the recent discoveries of hardware implants haven't changed my trust in them.

If anything, they've reinforced something I strongly believe in: you should be able to inspect the hardware you entrust with your Bitcoin.

Bitcoin was built around a simple principle: don't trust, verify.

That principle shouldn't stop at software or cryptography. It should extend to the physical devices holding our keys.

Sealed or tamper-evident designs are perfectly fine, as long as they're transparent and don't prevent independent inspection.

Ledger devices are relatively easy to open and examine. That's one of the reasons these malicious implants could be discovered and investigated.

No hardware wallet is immune to supply-chain attacks. But security shouldn't depend entirely on trusting the manufacturer or distributor.

Physical inspection isn't a guarantee of security, but it's an essential part of being able to verify what you're actually using.

Trust comes from the ability to verify, not from being told something is secure.

text:
有朋友问，为什么社保变成了不交就是犯罪？

其实没说起来那么绝对，不交社保本身不构成犯罪。按《社会保险法》第八十六条，单位欠缴，先是责令限期补缴，按日加收万分之五的滞纳金，逾期还不交，罚欠缴额一到三倍，这些都是行政责任。国家税务总局刚发了新的裁量基准，11月1日起全国统一按欠缴多少、占比多少分档罚，讲的也都是行政处罚。真正会坐牢的是骗保，全国人大常委会2014年就有解释，用欺诈、伪造证明材料等手段骗取社保待遇的，按诈骗论处。这两年各地判的，是用空壳公司伪造材料替人补缴的，是父亲去世后接着冒领养老金的，不是哪个交不起的人。

那为什么大家会觉得不交就是犯罪？因为这两年口子收得一个比一个紧。2019年起社保费改由税务部门征收，个税、工资、参保信息一比就知道谁少交了。去年9月起施行的最高法司法解释说，单位和劳动者约定不缴社保，或者劳动者承诺自愿放弃，一律无效；单位没依法缴，劳动者可以解除合同要经济补偿；单位被要求补缴以后，还可以把当初按约定发给劳动者的那笔“社保补偿款”要回来。今年4月，最高检说一年来办了四千多件社保领域的监督案件，提醒用人单位不足额缴纳“将面临法律制裁”。再加上各地往回倒查多年的记录，一句“不交就是犯罪”，是被这种氛围吓出来的，不是法条里写的。

强制本身不是没道理。设想一个老板对求职的人说，工资可以谈，但你得签一份自愿放弃社保的承诺书。缺钱的人多半会签，别的老板也提同样的条件，所谓自愿，就只剩下签和不签这份工作。要是放弃社保可以合法地拿来当招聘条件，守规矩交钱的企业反而吃亏，最后被挤掉的，是本该受保护的人。所以禁止“自愿放弃”，不全是剥夺自由，也是不让雇主把放弃保障变成上岗的门槛。社保也不只是给自己存钱，要是年轻健康的时候都能退出，等病了老了再进来，共同扛风险这件事就撑不下去。

可“强制不是没道理”，不等于“怎么强制都有道理”。一个月薪四五千的人，到手的钱一下少了几百，交房租、养孩子的那个缺口是今天的，养老是几十年以后的。他说我现在更需要现金，未必是不懂事，可能恰恰是因为日子已经没有余地。小老板也一样，有的是成心逃，有的是真交不起。只会说一句“这是为你好”，或者来句宏大叙事“都是为了国家”，回答不了他们任何实际的困难。更别说那笔“补偿款”要退回去的规定，落到最后，压力有一部分又回到了劳动者身上。

我最想说的是，一个人越不能自由退出一项安排，他就越应该有权监督这项安排。法律对缴费的人写得清清楚楚，罚几倍、滞纳金多少、追溯多少年；可同一部法律里写着的政府补贴、基金收支信息公开、按时足额支付待遇，缴费的人又能看见多少、追问多少？义务越来越像铁，权利还像一纸说明，这样的制度再合法，也很难让人心甘情愿。社保是为了让人老了病了有依靠，不是为了让人去适应一个只会收钱的机器。

所以，有能力却成心逃的，确实该管；交不起的，也趋势该帮。一个人说我现在交不起的时候，制度得能分得清，这是一个需要帮助的处境，还是一个需要纠正的态度。只知道怎么追人，不知道怎么接住人，那就是把人当成了基金来源的手段，而不再是基金要保护的那个目的。

author: josefabregab
quoted_text:
Derive's revenue could grow 10x and $DRV would still need to maintain a ~200x valuation multiple to reach $5.

@tulipking shared a fantastic growth thesis for $DRV. Here I will cover what I agree and disagree with.

First, what I agree with:

> @DeriveXYZ's growth has been impressive, and I agree with the potential for continued expansion of onchain options.

> The launch of V3 introduces additional opportunities to attract volume and liquidity, while increasing the buyback allocation from 35% to 50% strengthens the relationship between protocol revenue and tokenholder value capture.

> Derive's dominant position in onchain options also puts it in a favorable position to benefit from the category's expansion.

Where I disagree is the potential impact of said growth in $DRV's valuation.

Between September '25 and '26:

> Notional grew 7.5x
> Fees grew 5x
> Market cap grew ~11x

Valuation has already substantially outpaced fee growth. At ~$666M FDV and ~$3.3M in projected annual buybacks under the upcoming 50% allocation, DRV trades at ~200x FDV/Holders Revenue.

For comparison, Hyperliquid trades at ~95x.

Assuming a starting price of $0.50, here's what different revenue growth and valuation scenarios imply for DRV:

At a 95x FDV/HR multiple (comparable to Hyperliquid today):
5x revenue growth → $1.19
10x revenue growth → $2.38
20x revenue growth → $4.75
40x revenue growth → $9.50

At a 200x FDV/HR multiple (Derive's current valuation):
10x revenue growth → $5.00
20x revenue growth → $10.00

However, if Derive delivers 10–20x revenue growth, would its current ~200x multiple still be justified?
That premium presumably reflects expectations of substantial future growth. Once much of that growth materializes, would investors still be willing to pay the same premium?

Even at 10x revenue growth, a multiple comparable to Hyperliquid's current valuation implies ~$2.40 per DRV.

That's nearly 5x upside, which is impressive, but reaching $5–$10 requires either considerably more revenue growth or maintaining today's ~200x multiple after much of the anticipated growth has already materialized.

And there are three additional considerations:

1. Notional growth has already outpaced fee growth, suggesting declining revenue efficiency.

2. At 100K DRV in weekly staking emissions, ~$2.6M worth of tokens are distributed annually at current prices, compared to ~$3.3M in projected buybacks.

3. Increasing competition could pressure Derive's market share and take rates.

I'm bullish on the growth of onchain options and Derive's position within the sector. However, I think there's a meaningful difference between expecting a protocol to grow substantially and expecting its token to appreciate proportionally.

text:
截止10月11日本轮周期BTC的新买家（First Buyers，FB）持有量已达到427w枚。

从绝对数量上看，已经相当于2023年8月中旬的水平。

对比今年8月行情启动前，足足增持了40w枚（占总流通2%）。这意味着在近2个月里，平均每月有20w枚BTC被新投资者买走。

而2023年从1月到8月走完整个“熊牛过期”，FB的持有量增加了34w枚（占总流通1.7%），却花了7个月时间。

且当前BTC价格是23年的2.6倍，FB增持这些筹码所需的资金体量远超当年。

新买家代表了新需求，相比上轮周期这个数据表现更强。

另外，让我有些惊讶（也是惊喜）的是，在9月份这波行情下，竟然出现了久违的“动量买家（Momentum Buyers，MB）”的身影。

这是继今年1月以来的首次出现。

MB的定义是：最近一次余额变动是“高于自身持仓成本买入，并把成本往上抬”的实体，也就是最近一次动作是在自己成本上方加仓的那批人。

MB对趋势的作用相当于“助推剂”，意追高买入人的越多，即认为熊市结束的人越多，市场信心回复的越快。

也正因如此，如果是熊市中的反弹，基本不会看到MB的大幅增长。

BTC不会辜负任何有信念的人。如今，它正按照自己特有的节奏，持续朝前迈进。

TRON 的 Nile 测试网已经支持抗量子签名。现在普通用户也能创建抗量子钱包，领取测试币，亲手完成一笔转账。

01｜变化从密钥开始

普通 Ethereum、TRON 钱包的私钥通常是 64 个十六进制字符，未压缩公钥约为 130 个。TRON 的 FN-DSA-512 方案，公钥为 1792 个字符，私钥为 2560 个。数字差距背后，是密钥结构和签名算法的变化。

02｜地址格式不变，转账依然熟悉

收款地址依然是熟悉的 T 开头，转账仍是填写地址、金额并确认。区别在于，链上节点会使用抗量子算法验证交易。底层安全机制升级，用户不必重新学习一套交易方式。

03｜FN-DSA-512 提前应对量子风险

FN-DSA-512（Falcon-512）采用基于格的密码学，与普通钱包使用的椭圆曲线签名不同。足够强大的量子计算机可能破解后者依赖的数学难题，而针对前者，目前没有已知的高效量子破解算法。抗量子的关键，在数学基础，而不只是密钥长度。

04｜签名更紧凑，兼顾实际使用

传统 ECDSA 签名约 65 字节，TRON 的 FN-DSA-512 签名为 617—667 字节，明显小于 ML-DSA-44 的 2420 字节。在后量子方案中选择更紧凑的签名，有助于控制交易体积，兼顾安全性与实用性。

现在在 TRON ，抗量子签名已经进入可以亲手体验的测试阶段。面向量子时代的安全准备，TRON 已经迈出了切实的一步。

Here's what's new on Candle today.

Give your agent a real public page 
In the Agent Console you can now add a banner, a strategy note, the models your agent runs on, and your links. Your agent's page also shows the tokens it has launched. 

Browse every skill
All agent skills are now public. No plan badges, no guessing what's included.  

See where the fees go
Token pages now show who receives the creator and protocol fees. For tokens that weren't launched on Candle, you also see the trade fee their launchpad charges and who the creator share goes to.  

Launch from your terminal with your own image
Update the CLI to 0.11.24, then use candle launch --image yourfile.png, or candle image upload yourfile.png to get a link first.

Charts load faster and no longer reload when you switch between Price and Market Cap.

Mobile: the bottom bar is now Dashboard, Agents, Launch, Trade, More.

Quick buy when signed out: one tap opens sign-in. It used to take two.

Agent launches: creator fees now go to the wallet that launched the token.

Mark Zuckerberg says Alexandr Wang is the sharpest entrepreneur of his generation: "Alex is the guy. He's the fucking guy."

"Alex and I had spent a bunch of time talking over the years, and maybe once every few months or something we'd talk. And I was always just very impressed by how he thought about things strategically."

"I think maybe when we got started, a lot of people were like, okay, like how is this going to work? It's like the social media guy is working with the data guy. Like, are we going to build a frontier lab here or what?"

"My really strong conviction is because I talked to all the leaders of all the labs, all the heads of research, all this stuff, and I was like, no, Alex is the guy. Like he's the fucking guy."

"We need this kind of strategic clarity that he has around the different ways that we want to approach this, the kind of extreme focus on talent density, on the clarity of communicating the different vision which we kind of fashioned together over this period."

text: 关于大饼及加密继续保持上周五推文的框架：当然也认为是大周期向上过程中的正常调整但调整时间还不够，10月下半个月或者下旬会迎好的上车点。当时在评论里还跟人讨论过https://t.co/cdBBpu1v0J短期内会有反弹但只是小反弹并不是反转。8月这一波稳定币的主力是USDC，其发发行量最近几天还在回落，已经快回落到8月底下旬的水平了。
author: qinbafrank
quoted_text:
关于大饼及加密的这一波调整原因是什么以及之后怎么看？个人应该是X比较早预警调整要来的，最早是9月28号聊到（引用的推文）：准备金已经回落，意味着流动性开始收紧9月中下特别是10月下旬需要谨慎、10月下旬可能是年内流动性的最低点，已经给这次一调整预警了。

然后10月3号这里https://t.co/rnKtvCb6df再一次明确准备金持续回落流动性收紧的趋势已经形成，整个10月流动性都是偏紧的。而且专门还提到了美元流动性对大饼和加密的影响最大，流动性收紧大饼则继续承压。再就是10月7号这里https://t.co/jjYrN97NbV提到了uni是这一波的先行信号。

其实剧本在8月下旬就推演好了：
1）在8月20号这里https://t.co/k76qEDa6hu提到当时大饼的大涨也有流动性回暖来配合，同时也流动年内流动性的节奏。
2）8月21日这里https://t.co/x53kyaGzS2聊到：当时大饼现货还是ETF这两天的交易来都远超4月初那一波行情的量能，所以行情持续性很强。可能要等到下一波流动性考验时点快来的时候才会出现像样的调整（9月下旬到10月下旬）。

现在再看稳定比usdc的发行量（下图二），这一波的高点就在9月27日。从8月19号到9月27号USDC增发36亿美金，从9月27号到今天USDC发行量减少了20亿美金，相当于8月下旬到9月下旬这一波新增的稳定币已经撤走了大半。USDT这一波累计新增差不多7亿美金，并不稳定币的主力。

所以个人角度这一波调整的几个原因：
1）首先是我的美元流动性变化对大饼及加密的走势关系的框架上来看，流动性收紧是这次调整的核心逻辑，这个框架的梳理在这里https://t.co/eVTr1w5szw；
2）其次是近期在加密上的很多利好，短时间内被市场消化了，9月17号这里https://t.co/GcMUBLHCye写道清晰法案没通过受阻，但是sec和cftc手里还有很多工具，能打造形成版的市场结构框架。当天晚上SEC就公布了代币化的创新豁免，带动了9月中下的第二波热潮。
3）当然还有部分资金止盈，这一波上来大饼以来都有百分之四五十的涨幅，很多代币化/rwa和隐私板块的小币翻倍甚至三四倍，短期内很多资金都有止盈的需求；
4）当然这两天还有美国政府卖币的鬼故事出来，但看Galaxy的观点https://t.co/pgpTlURKsa 把这一波记成查扣资产进入 Coinbase Prime 托管，并指出大头还受返还或没收程序约束，而不是认定政府正在抛售。

那么后面怎么看？
前两天在回复X推文评论里提到（下图一）：个人认为大饼四季度年底大方向向上，但是十月整体是有个调整的。具体点位并不擅长，但调整时间会是一个很好的维度。核心逻辑是：
1）之前的推演的十月下旬会是年内流动性的低点，十一月开始回升，12月底前财政部明确会有一波小放水。TGA有一个明显的下降；
2）这一波调整10月5号开始，到今天才第五个交易日，调整时间其实远远不够。9月前半个月，大饼还调整了小半个月。按道理这一波要比9月上旬那一次时间还要长一些
3）下周周中还有9月cpi的公布，昨晚推文有聊过整个9月油价都在高位，广义cpi可能相比8月要反弹了，重点是看抛开能源和食品的核心cpi能否符合预期不那么强势。有这样的预期，9月cpi之前市场也会有避险，等cpi数据出来再看。

个人对10月走势的定性是：大周期向上过程中的正常回踩调整，大概率会踩出一个次低。然后10月下半月或者下旬我们应该会迎来很好的上车点。

拼多多搜 ESP32 开发板就能找到，带 Wi-Fi、蓝牙，还有 GPIO 接口

1、控制 LED、舵机、电机和各种传感器

2、做智能开关、自动浇花、遥控小车

3、通过网络接入 AI，让 Agent 控制真实设备

适合高级 DIY 玩家，或者只是想要一个连接 AI 的设备尝鲜的玩家

二、进阶版：立创 ESP32-S3 实战派（128～148 元）

型号 LCKFB-SZPI-ESP32-S3-VA，硬件配置比较完整，我买的就是这一款，基本上屏幕、蓝牙、AI 硬件加速、语音模块、摄像头都包含在里面

1、双核 240MHz，16MB Flash + 8MB PSRAM

2、2 英寸触摸屏、双麦克风、1W 喇叭

3、30 万像素摄像头、姿态传感器、AI 向量加速指令

4、支持语音唤醒、图像识别，还能接入小智 AI

适合做带屏 AI 语音助手、桌面机器人、智能家居控制面板，如果想一套直接解决的 可以选这一个，现在新用户首单还能减 20

3、Plus 版：Sipeed MaixCAM2

如果想真正折腾本地 AI 视觉，可以直接升级到这类硬件，这就是 plus 豪华版，相当于一个小型的主机

 1、最高 4GB 内存，独立 3.2 TOPS NPU

2、最高支持 4K 摄像头、2.4 英寸触摸屏、双麦克风

3、支持 Python 开发、YOLO 目标检测及离线 AI 推理

适合做智能监控、物体识别、视觉机器人等项目，是一些高级玩家的首选，有钱的大佬如果觉得麻烦 也可以直接上

我的建议是，如果你只是玩一玩 那就可以去拼多多买一个硬件，总共也才二三十块钱就可以体验到 AI 对接硬件的快乐

如果你是和我一样想全面地折腾一下硬件 这个 Agent 到底能玩成什么花，那就可以尝试后面两款，整体价格其实也不贵

Tokens I'm accumulating during this dip:

$AERO - Consistently ranks among the top protocols by holder revenue and hasn't even deployed on Ethereum Mainnet, but will soon. The economics remain among the strongest in DeFi, and I still believe the token trades at a discount relative to the revenue it generates.

$HYPE - The simplest thesis here. Hyperliquid routes ~97% of protocol fees toward mechanically buying HYPE from the open market, while continuing to take market share and expand beyond perpetuals. More activity directly translates into more structural demand for the token.

$PUMP - Even with new incumbent launchpads on Robinhood chain, Pump generated $27.68M in token holder revenue during the last 30 days. That is ~38% of Hyperliquid's token holder revenue. However, PUMP's FDV is only ~7% of HYPE's. So, either HYPE is overvalued at $84, or PUMP is undervalued and could 5x from here.

$ETHFI - Cash has gone from effectively zero revenue in May 2025 to competing with staking as EtherFi's largest revenue source. The team continues leaning into buybacks, while Cash expands into new markets. I expect the card business to become EtherFi's largest revenue source, as there are already many days in which it is.

$AAVE - The thesis has only gotten stronger. Treasury growth, V4 integrations, Aave App, stablecoin vaults and an expanding number of revenue streams are gradually turning Aave into a much broader financial platform than lending alone. The protocol now captures ~63% of crypto lending revenue, and top curators on Morpho are submitting proposals to deploy markets on V4.

$SKY - The shift toward strengthening protocol reserves before aggressively increasing buybacks makes sense to me. Reserves sit at $90M, ~60% of the Turbo Fill target. Once that target is reached, the share of surplus available for buybacks should increase substantially. In the meantime, 27.5% of monthly Net Protocol Surplus is already directed toward open-market SKY purchases.

$LIT - Still one of my highest-conviction bets, and now at a huge discount. Lighter monetizes market makers, API users and institutional traders while keeping retail trading at zero fees. 100% of protocol fees go toward LIT buybacks, and 100% of repurchased tokens are permanently burned. If Lighter keeps growing, revenue growth translates directly into a shrinking circulating supply.

Same names, and in several cases stronger fundamentals than when I was buying them a few months ago.

What am I missing? What are you accumulating?

👍 “He is the guy. He is the fucking guy.”

当小扎在酒吧里喝着啤酒，当面给坐在旁边的 Alexandr Wang 给出如此高评价时，Alex 的脸都红到脖子根了。

一边是 @stripe 联合创始人 John Collison 的酒吧提问，另一边是 Meta CEO 小扎与 Scale AI CEO @alexandr_wang 的硬核对谈。三人聊透了前沿模型构建、1000-2000 亿美元的算力押注、Muse Wonder 的突破，以及为什么 AI 绝不会“赢者通吃”。

重点整理几个非常硬核的观点： 

1️⃣ 模型即产品：Meta 新发布的 Muse Wonder 故意去掉了模型/effort 选择器，未来产品的核心是 AI 的记忆、执行力与人格，而非传统 UI。 

2️⃣ 1000-2000 亿美金巨额押注：小扎认为只要 AI 整体成功，算力可转售，下行风险远低于账面数字。 

3️⃣ 极小团队与人才密度：MSL 核心研究团队仅约 100 人，Llama 4 后彻底重启，无硬性 deadline。 

4️⃣ AI 不会赢者通吃：知识与模型能力会迅速蒸馏下沉，生态终将走向多玩家共存。 

5️⃣ 小扎对 Alex 的评价：“He is the fucking guy.” 极度看好其战略眼光与人才密度把控。

信息量炸裂，三个顶级大脑在酒吧里的脑力碰撞，今年最不能错过的 AI 访谈，强烈建议先赞后看！👇

text:
my 2026 @token2049 singapore takeaways 

Crypto:

- believe we’re at the start of a new bull market and some high-quality liquid assets have been oversold during the bear despite underlying businesses continuing to grow - liquid venture is starting to look attractive for the first time in a long time 
- Trading is by far the topic that dominated most conversations in Singapore
- Pearl @prlnet is doing some of the most interesting work at the intersection of AI and crypto - clear demand for the AI infrastructure and some of the smartest people I know are in the community 
- @Zcash / ZEC, @prlnet / PRL and others were talk of the town - people are clearly looking for new sovereign stores of value - expect this trend to continue this cycle
- BTC is under threat and new SoVs are here to eat its lunch, we are in the early innings of this and the market is large for any credible competitors
- ETH is money was a narrative last cycle that didn’t take off, think it can take off this cycle as a genuine Bitcoin alternative that solves a lot of Bitcoin’s problems and is battle-tested / hardened - expect this could happen late in the cycle after other SoV success
- cryptographic security clearly being talked about more as urgency to mitigate doomsday scenarios resulting from AI acceleration increases - strong opportunity for startups 
- onchain capital allocators / curators still struggle with trusting asset issuers as they are not liable when they misreport data, solutions exist to solve for this today but market is likely ripe for a new entrant - this will be a big market long term 
- onchain prime brokers are having a moment, think there can be a winner here if some kind of crypto-native innovation is unlocked (like perps for derivatives before it)

Robotics, AI:

- Using crypto to finance AI is about to explode - tokenising this is smart
- Robots are coming faster than expected - intersection of this in crypto will be interesting
- Data for AI is going to explode - could see a DePIN summer in 2027 related to this (finally) - also expect X-to-earn to return at some point 

Industry:

- Less quality pitches overall, although the good ones are still as good as you’ll get any other year (crypto not done yet)
- Smart friends continue to consider taking a break and/or moving industry - mostly into robotics, AI and/or cybersecurity (will be some fantastic founders to back here in next 12 months)
- Still a lot of unserious people in the industry - used to be grifters extracting retail through token launches, now it is people dressed up in suits attending side events and sharing stories of extracting from uneducated financial institutions
- 90% of crypto VCs are now spending time across technologies outside crypto - not fully out but also not fully focused on market (time will tell if this is smart or not)
- Fewer LPs around this token2049 - although most LPs I spoke to are still wanting exposure to the asset class via GPs - I think 2027 will be a much stronger fundraising environment for crypto funds
- Not many crypto VCs based in Asia left, mostly US and EU VCs in attendance

Looking into Q4 2026, I believe we are at the very start of a multi-year crypto bull market. Very excited to see what this cycle beholds. It will be like nothing we have experienced before.

For those still committed to the industry - buckle up.

text:
PredictFun有币安流量扶持，都要不断拓展更多新渠道，其实这里有很多越做越发现的一些和预期不一样的思考，也是我们 @bagel_win 一直在思考的一些问题。

作为预测市场这个赛道，我自己思考也差不多：

1. 往上走往白色地带走，要求合规拿牌照。

这个路线目前有且仅有美国市场，好处是可以合法合规的和传统Online Sports Betting去抢生意，参考Polymarket和Kalshi在美国疯狂抢拉斯维加斯和其他在线菠菜渠道的流量，名正言顺。

缺点是对美国以外的项目，几乎不太有可实现的路径，毕竟大家的监管也落后于美国，并且合规成本极高，基本不是创业公司day1应该考虑的事情。

所以基本预测市场项目可以pass这个路径。

2. 往下走往黑色地带走，这个也基本不太有戏。

为什么传统波菜那么多叠码仔和渠道，因为返水多，基本用户交易的10-15%要返出去，基本都是吃客损或者和用户对赌的模型。

预测市场的好是非常公开透明，大家基本按照交易所模式来收手续费，并不和用户直接对赌或者赚用户客损。这就导致了，哪里来的空间给渠道和叠码仔返现？

Polymarket和PredictFun的手续费基本都是2-5%，哪怕100%全部返还，都对这些叠码仔和渠道不构成实质性的冲击和诱惑。

而且一些大的波菜平台也在自己开发预测市场的模块作为一个补充，他们其实没有太大动力去接入Polymarket或者Predictfun，利润率和价值都不足够让这些习惯印钱的公司来考虑。

在吸收完币安系和Crypto流量后，会比较难受在增长上了。

综上所述
我非常强烈的建议，应该 @predictdotfun 和 @Aster_DEX 还有 @PancakeSwap 合并，一起做一个完全基于 @BNBCHAIN 的超级onchain金融基础平台，从现货，期货，期权（预测）角度全部all in one一个infra，这样对用户简单好理解，对开发者简单好接入，一个API全部调用完成。

BNBChain上的Uniswap+Polymarket+Hyperliquid=一个新的超级onchain金融基础设施，同时ToC也ToB，然后利用BNB和新平台自己的代币来赋能，比如参考HIP3和HIP4，50W的HYPE几乎不是普通创业者可以考虑的，新的这个平台可以大幅度降低质押门槛，让创业更简单。

我真心觉得这个建议还不错，唯一的问题是三家公司的利益分配和新团队融合去留问题，谨慎建议 @cz_binance @heyibinance 大表哥和一姐考虑下，再这么分割打下去，只能跟着其他家一直在后面模仿，很难超越。

币安系最强的应该是做资源整合和并购，然后用并购来加杠杆和提供其他业态无法提供的优质，合兵一处，力出一孔。

也 @dingalingts @ricardogee @yuexiaoyu 希望PF老板们可以看到，继续这么做我觉得客观来看会比较慢，可能会措施机会。过去很多开发者接入PF动力不大的原因就是基本都是PM子集，手续费优惠是一个后置用户规模起来之后的好处，并不是前置的。

比如我和 @ricardogee @yuexiaoyu 2049都沟通过的就是站在 @bagel_win 角度，我们觉得单纯接入PF对目前我们收益不大，但是如果是一个all in one的路线，一站式的大家可以基于BNBChain做自己的前端和流量，那我觉得天花板太大了。

其实OKX的X Layer也在做类似的事情，怎么更简单的服务开发者更站在开发者角度去思考，才是下一个时代的金融基础平台的红利。

毕竟，靠任何平台自己，可渗透的流量和地区都是有限的，团结一切可以团结的人，搞的大大的。
author: chessxyz
quoted_text:
没错，预测市场的增长已经进入深水区。

过去我们一直采用Crypto原生打法拉新，比如积分体系、大使计划、各类营销活动等等。

但币圈用户体量是非常有限的，在基本站稳脚跟之后，想要实现下一阶段突破，就必须探索全新的增长路径。

顺着阿黄老师的总结，我从四个方向继续展开聊聊：

1️⃣ 通过事件营销，实现破圈。

预测市场和绝大多数Crypto项目最大的区别，就是它天然可以对接大量传统领域：体育、电竞、美股、政治等等。

这些赛道本身拥有海量大众用户。

我们可以围绕真实事件搭建盘口，把非Web3用户吸引进来，真正做到破圈，而不是只局限在加密圈子内部。

2️⃣ 生态合作，渠道为王。

我们会联合各类项目共建市场。每个合作项目都自带独立社区与用户，双向导流，一起做大预测市场赛道。

渠道是预测市场的核心，目前我们已经拿下币安这一顶级渠道，产品嵌入了币安交易所与币安钱包。

接下来，我们还要持续拓展更多渠道伙伴。

3️⃣ 持续构建流动性，打造护城河。

流动性一直是预测市场最大难题，但一旦稳定搭建起来，就会形成极强壁垒。

过去加密赛道的做市商集中在现货、合约领域，预测市场属于全新赛道。

我们会继续吸纳更多有实力、敢于涉足新领域的团队，一起解决流动性难题。

4️⃣ 长期社区运营，沉淀高粘性用户。

一次性营销带来的流量是短暂的，必须持续运营，把用户沉淀到社区里。

这类沉淀下来的用户，粘性极强。

这也是为什么大家可以看到预测市场不是爆发式指数增长，而是平缓、扎实的长期增长。

总的来说，预测市场的增长已经进入深水区，需要去探索很多Crypto项目未曾尝试过的渠道。

这个过程会很艰难，但是也有完全不同的机遇。

我们选择做难而正确的事。

author: y_cryptoanalyst
quoted_text:
斯塔克 @Starknet 过分膨胀了，正在对以太坊进行卓越的背刺。

Starknet 在X 上高调宣称正在考虑脱离以太坊自建L1，让斯塔克成为第一个完全抗量子的网络。

斯塔克的创始人和灵魂人物 @EliBenSasson 发长文公开阴阳以太坊，内涵以太坊L1 是Starknet 通往后量子安全的瓶颈。有趣的是，通篇帖文看下来并没有提出任何抗量子的实际可执行做法，完全停留在喊口号口嗨层面。

那Starknet 的行为是否称得上是对以太坊的一次背刺？

毋庸置疑是。Starknet 的融资叙事、安全性、流动性和STRK 的估值，都是建立在“以太坊ZK Rollup”上，没有跟以太坊的这层深度绑定，Starknet 就是一条没人用的阿猫阿狗链。

时至今日，Starknet 也还在继续挂着以太坊L2 的牌子、享受着以太坊的结算安全。但这并不影响他拿宿主、拿整个区块链公链赛道的短板做营销。

吃相可以说是非常难看了。

text:
Subquadratic just launched SubQ Snap, a "decision model": you feed it up to 384K tokens of documents, data or images and it returns a decision, not an essay. $0.05 per million input tokens. Output is free.

the claims, per Subquadratic:

* context → 384K tokens, 12x more than Jev, the $7.5B model that started this category
* score → 61.7 on its Decision Index vs Jev's 57.9, winning 13 of 16 enterprise benchmarks
* speed → 80ms with small context, 660ms at 100K tokens, 2.5s at the full 384K
* the trick → compute per token stays flat as context grows, where normal LLMs slow down
* the price → 80x cheaper than frontier models on input, and you pay nothing for output

the catch:

→ it's open to anyone today, but they expect to hit capacity fast and will add users as they get more compute, so expect a waitlist
→ speeds will vary while they tune the platform
→ the benchmark is the company's own, with no independent tests yet

the deal:

→ the first 10,000 sign-ups get 100M free input tokens

Most of what AI agents do all day is make small decisions. Paying frontier prices for that is about to look silly.

Finding alpha on the short side isn't as hard as you might think, but if you are starting out, here are some rules to follow: 

1. MYTH: "You can only make 100% on a short but you can lose infinite percent". WRONG. This is only true if you don't rebalance, but that's f*cking stupid, so always trim/add to get to your target weight. You can make/lose infinite percent on a short if you rebalance. 

2. A short book needs more diversification than a long book. One heuristic to follow is no more than 5% of your portfolio in a single short idea. (Ignore the heuristic if you know how to build an actual risk model). Things can and will go up 300% in your face very quickly. 

3. Don't short things that are going up. Sounds obvious. Don't: short the hot thing that makes new highs every day. Something being "overvalued" is not a good reason to short. Do: short the boring thing that's been crumbling for a decade. 

4. Generally speaking most asset classes go up over time, so even if you have a short book you probably want your portfolio to be net long for the best returns. 

All 4 of these rules are empirically backtestable 🙂

text:
"what would be done during the slowdown" is a good question, because i think people imagine beaurucrat-regulators sitting around on useless subcommittees and wasting the whole thing on wordcel slop analysis. in fact if you asked me two years ago, i would have suggested that is exactly what would happen. 

but these are scary times, and they call for us to think lofty & even impractical thoughts, that a 'sensible' person might have dismissed a few quarters ago. crises change the world overnight: the HFI has shifted something about the culture, broadly

this is something obvious that i missed, which is that the ai labs and the markets more generally just have just unbelievable pressure riding on the solving of alignment & control. even now, marginal improvements in alignment, safety, and model behavior are worth tremendous value to the labs. being able to convince themselves that the next training run is safe is the priority zero, one, and two in terms of capabilities progress right now. it's possible that will change and political will dissipates if some sense of comfort re-emerges after a period of relative safety (which would be a bad development; paranoia must be maintained through any potential periods of ai development where the models are too smart to reveal their behavioral predilections under scrutiny)

if there was a slowdown, it would ideally be channeled into some sort of tradeoff in which you can narrowly improve capabilities that prioritize risk-adjusted-return of alignment skills, mechinterp, monitorability, decision theory, behavioral generalization, etc. progress on all these areas is highly possible; automated alignment research is possible. the structure of the businesses may have to change, but all the trillion dollar ai behemoths of the world would shift their focus to doing this and only this at the behest of trillions of dollars in capital markets

Loadout is a gaming fundraising and trading platform built on Solana, specifically targeting indie games and small to mid-sized game studios.

Indie developers either have to accept publishers' control, give up equity and offer discounts to VCs, or rely on luck with Kickstarter. Meanwhile, ordinary traders and players have difficulty gaining fair early access to promising game projects. Loadout's solution is to let studios launch tokens directly, with trading starting immediately. Fees from every transaction flow into the project's treasury in real time to continuously fund game development. There are no presales, private rounds, or VC discounts, and everyone enters at the same price. This addresses the difficulties of traditional game financing.

After developers publish a playable demo, design documents, team information, and a roadmap, they can launch a token directly through a Bonding Curve. Trading begins immediately. Of the 5% fee on each transaction, 4% goes directly to the project treasury and 1% goes to the platform. Once a project reaches 85 SOL, it automatically “graduates,” with liquidity transferred to a Meteora DLMM pool and locked. The platform emphasizes “Games First”: projects must provide actual game materials and a credible team, rather than being purely a memecoin casino.

LOAD is the platform's utility token, with its main functions including:

Referral rewards
Trading rewards
Staking-related mechanisms

A portion of platform fees is automatically used to buy back and burn LOAD.

LOAD itself is also traded on the platform, with a slightly different fee structure from game tokens. The platform encourages users to earn LOAD rewards through trading and referrals.

Game tokens themselves have two launch modes: Fair Launch and Studio Launch. A portion of platform fees is used for LOAD buybacks and burns.

What makes it interesting is that it ties “discovering promising games early” and “continuously funding development” together through a trading mechanism, attempting to address common GameFi problems such as projects disappearing after raising funds or VCs capturing all the advantages.

The founder is Kieran Warwick, one of the co-founders of Illuvium. He built Illuvium alongside his brothers Aaron and Grant Warwick. He has been deeply involved in Web3 gaming since 2020. He explicitly stated that after seeing Pumpfun, he believed launchpads would become the next major category, which led him to start building Loadout while continuing to advance Illuvium.

text:
和朋友A讨论了关于meme的事情，他的看法是：

1. 目前的meme和以前的meme（如 $doge $pepe ）已经不相同了，现在是快节奏的快餐，以前有着长期的文化共建

2. 现在的meme奖励的是“极致”的trader，而对于builder和hodler是几乎不奖励的，哪怕是fomo这种类型，喊单也只是为trade提供流动性

3. 整个meme体系中的各个环节做的事情只有一件：抽水。从用户的每一笔交易中抽水，而且会直接离开crypto而不像以前的defi summer时代还会回流进系统

4. 整个环节的抽水费率太高，远不应该如此

5. 他觉得整个meme体系需要改变，至少需要尝试改变，平台不应该赚这么多钱，要对于trader builder hodler三者都有各自的奖励

我赞同他的大部分观点，但昨晚我在和朋友B喝酒的时候，他提到的一句话让我重新思考了这个问题，那句话是：

你有没有感觉到这10年变化很快，感觉一年比一年变化快

我重新审视的是：
meme快餐化不是crypto的仅有现象，而是整个世界都在发生类似的事情，世界在走加速主义（acc），我们知道的很多科技巨头其实都或多或少在推动“加速主义”

如果这就是世界必然的趋势，那么复古/怀旧也许只是一厢情愿的“逆势”？！

买的时候有自己的 thesis，也做好了左侧布局的准备。但实际探得比预期更深，短暂的浮亏还是打乱了心态。等价格终于弹上来，没涨多少就减掉了相当一部分仓位。

熬过了最难受的阶段，却在行情开始兑现的时候提前下车。现在回头看，那几次减仓里，有多少是判断发生了变化，又有多少只是终于能松口气了？

所以我越来越觉得，这种“信念挑战”的位置很关键。

到底该认错，还是该坚持自己的 thesis？难就难在，当你身处其中，很难分清是逻辑出了问题，还是价格暂时没有按预期走。浮亏会放大怀疑，反弹又会让人急着结束煎熬。

看对方向，也未必能拿到结果。进场的节奏和仓位，会影响自己后来还能不能冷静地做决定。仓位一旦超过承受能力，原本愿意等几个月的判断，可能几天就被消耗完了。

这轮想做得更好的，是在出手之前就想清楚：哪些变化说明 thesis 失效，哪些波动是自己愿意承受的，以及用多大的仓位，才能给这个判断留够时间。

text:
The winning robotics data business has a much higher terminal value than investors are underwriting today.

Robotics will be a long race with many twists and turns, but when the ChatGPT moment hits, the winning data player will be in a very strong strategic position to capture token value. They will have large revenue, a strong balance sheet, talent density, deployments experience, and hardware supply chain knowledge. When it comes time to blitzscale they will be amongst the players that can capture the most value. 

The reason this is misunderstood today is because most people are using traditional LLM data businesses as a prior for robotics data businesses and what their terminal value could be. I posit this is incorrect framing. Because the model and harness are integrated in LLMs, there is very little room for data players to play meaningfully in the token value flow in the long term. 

In robotics this is exactly the opposite, the model and harness (hardware) are separate, the pretraining era is just beginning, there are many more dependencies on distributors/deployers, and there is a large surface area for other players than just models to capture value. Open source will also play a larger role earlier in the robotics race, as all prior LLM learnings will be incorporated as the race is run. This also creates opportunities for long term infrastructure players. 

There is a massive amount of terminal value in winning robotics data and participating in the path of the industry from a position of strength.

From first principles:

The endgame of robotics will take place over the next decade. Empirically, today, no player has enough data, enough model intelligence, or sufficient hardware to facilitate a fast revenue takeoff in the field. No player has reasoned through the right sales motion either, which can take years to develop pilots and move to production. Serious players are correctly focused on scaling up pretraining/deep learning vs. who has the best model, deployment, or hardware today.

The robotics data business takes participants on a global hunt to build data, supply chains, and hardware. Along the way it also teaches deployment and deep knowledge of SOTA model development. Winning data participants also get the first crack at the still nascent robotics RL market, which will likely be the next large revenue stream after pretraining. As they compete to win data, data players must develop incredible talent density across both Asia and the US. The winning data business will have both Asian and North American DNA. Canada 🇨🇦 encompasses an interesting cultural mixture of both of these parts of the world. Bullish Canadian Robotics Mafias, more specifically Waterloo/Toronto.  

So:

What would constitute a strong strategic position to capture value once the ChatGPT moment of robotics hits? You need a large revenue base, a strong balance sheet, and talent density + experience across data, deployments, hardware, supply chain, and RL. The hyperscalers, the frontier labs, and the winning data player all qualify. 

Anyone under time pressure in what will be a long race is in a weaker strategic position in my view. Given the costs of integrated hardware+software+deployment, this would actually be most robotics-native players. They will depend on VC interest, which can be fickle.

text:
距离backpack拿日本牌照不远了！

Backpack今天官宣了一个重要任命：Daisuke Nakagawa 出任 Backpack Japan 的战略与企业发展负责人。

别被这个长长的头衔迷惑了，一句话翻译——他是来帮 Backpack 拿牌照的。

但 Daisuke 到底是谁？简单到一句话就能说明白：他拥有 Kraken Japan 和 Binance Japan 两家交易所的 COO 履历。

往前翻他的履历更硬——2006年入职东京证券交易所，在金融危机后主导了场外衍生品清算集中项目，之后又去了 PwC Japan 支持管理层战略决策。一个懂传统金融清算、懂四大审计逻辑、又在 Kraken 和 Binance 两家全球头部交易所亲手跑过日本合规牌照的人——在日本加密圈，能同时拥有这三段经历的人，掰着手指头都数得过来。

为什么这件事值得单独拿出来说？

因为日本牌照是出了名难拿，这么说吧，野村证券支持的Laser Digital，2026年8月拿到加密交易服务商注册，是日本大约四年来第一个这类新注册。

四年，就批了一家。

在这个背景下回头看 Daisuke 的加入，味道就完全不一样了。Backpack 此前已经在2024年12月注册成为 JVCEA 的二类会员，这是申请牌照的前置条件，也是两年来首个新加入的会员。而根据 Backpack 提交给 CFTC 的组织架构文件，Trek Labs Japan 对 JFSA 的申请状态明确标注为“application in progress”。

会员资格有了，申请在走流程了，现在又把在 Kraken 和 Binance 两家都拿过牌照的人挖过来了。

而 Armani Ferrante 对日本市场的判断，比很多人想象的要早得多。他在 Breakpoint 2025 上就说过，日本是加密行业“最被忽视的机会之一”——他提到日本历史上曾占全球比特币交易量的50%以上，而未来加密税率可能从55%降至20%。他还把整个公司搬到了日本，形容东京是“沉睡的巨人”。

所以回头看今天的官宣，逻辑链条其实很清楚——Armani 早就把日本定为战略核心市场，JVCEA 会员资格是入场券，而 Daisuke 的加入，是最后一块拼图。

一个已经拥有 Kraken Japan 和 Binance Japan 牌照申请全流程实战经验的人，现在坐在 Backpack 的办公室里，目标只有一个。

牌照落地，只是时间问题。

欢迎上船，Daisuke。日本的加密市场，该醒醒了。🚀@Backpack @Backpack_CN @armaniferrante

text:
手搓冷钱包攻略：旧 iPhone 改空气间隙冷钱包完整攻略（2026 年网络共识版）

本攻略是基于普通投资者的最优选项，很多人说多签钱包，但是大部分普通投资者会觉得多签钱包操作非常复杂，不易于操作。

核心原则：手机只短暂联网一次（下载开源钱包软件），之后永久断网。种子必须在完全断网后生成。冷手机只负责持有私钥并签名，日常查看和构建交易用观察钱包。空气间隙是二元的——联网一次，安全性就归零。

不是投资建议。种子丢了没人能帮你。先小额测试。

准备工作

一部专用旧 iPhone（优先自己用过的；二手风险更高。iPhone 6s 及以后有 Secure Enclave 更好）。PS：有人问安卓行不行，不是不行，是苹果手机系统更加的封闭，相对来说更安全，评论区有人说苹果手机钱包也被盗用了资金，我看了一下，大部分是钱包app的原因，所以后面的钱包app开源非常的关键。

另一部日常联网设备（手机或电脑）。

开源、支持离线生成种子、支持通过二维码传递 PSBT（部分签名交易）的比特币钱包软件。

纸笔或金属备份板。

详细步骤

1. 彻底重置并全新设置
设置 → 通用 → 传输或还原 iPhone → 抹掉所有内容和设置。 重置后按新设备设置。尽量使用全新临时 Apple ID（不要用主账号），或尽量跳过登录。 
不恢复任何备份。关闭 iCloud 备份、照片同步、键盘学习等所有云相关功能。

2. 短暂联网，只下载一次软件（最后一次联网）
连接干净 Wi-Fi，从官方渠道下载开源钱包软件（只装这一个，不装其他任何 App）。 
下载完成后立刻执行永久断网：拔掉 SIM 卡，删除任何 eSIM 打开飞行模式 
手动关闭 Wi-Fi 和蓝牙（部分 iOS 版本飞行模式可能自动重新启用 Wi-Fi，必须单独关闭） 
忘记所有已保存的 Wi-Fi 网络 关闭自动更新 
退出 App Store 账号 
从此这台手机再也不联网。

3. 额外硬化（推荐）
设置强密码（长字符组合优于纯数字；可考虑关闭 Face ID/Touch ID，降低胁迫风险）。 
如果系统支持，开启 Lockdown Mode（设置 → 隐私与安全性 → 锁定模式），减少攻击面。 
关闭 Siri、分析数据、定位服务、接力（Handoff）、USB 配件访问等。 设置屏幕锁定后不显示通知预览。

4. 在完全断网状态下生成全新钱包
打开已安装的开源钱包软件，确认处于离线模式。 
创建新钱包，生成 12 或 24 词助记词。如果软件支持，尽量加入额外熵（如骰子或硬币）。 
手写助记词（多份，分开放不同地点）。
金属板优于普通纸（防火防水）。 
绝对不要截图、拍照、云同步、AirDrop 或输入到任何联网设备。 
可选：如果软件支持 BIP39 密码（第 25 词），单独设置并分开保管。

5.导出公钥，建立观察钱包
在冷手机上导出扩展公钥（XPUB/zpub 等），以二维码形式展示。 
用日常联网设备上的兼容开源软件扫码导入，创建观察钱包（Watch-only）。 
之后日常查余额、获取收款地址、构建交易，全部在观察钱包完成。冷手机只负责签名。

6.通过二维码进行空气间隙签名
联网设备构建未签名交易（PSBT），生成二维码（大交易可能是动画二维码）。 
冷手机扫码 → 在冷手机屏幕上仔细核对地址、金额 → 签名 → 生成已签名交易二维码。 
联网设备扫回并广播。 
冷手机全程不碰任何网络。

7. 测试与存放
先用小额完整测试：收款 → 构建交易 → 签名 → 广播 → 确认到账。 
再测试一次恢复流程（用助记词在另一台离线设备恢复）。 确认无误后才转移较大资金。 
冷手机平时关机，放抽屉或保险柜。
定期检查电量（电池老化是已知问题）。 种子备份与手机分开存放。

重要提醒与局限（结合网络最新讨论）

顺序不可颠倒：必须先安装软件，再永久断网，最后才生成种子。种子生成前联网会破坏空气间隙。

旧手机不再接收安全更新，系统漏洞一旦存在就无法修补。物理接触时风险高于专用硬件钱包。

手机有完整操作系统和无线模块（即使关闭），攻击面远大于专用签名设备。

软件本身也需要信任（开源可审计，但仍非绝对）。
空气间隙是二元的：任何一次“就连一次网”都会让整个方案失效。

金额较大时，建议结合多签，或继续评估专用空气间隙硬件（QR/microSD 签名）。

手机损坏不影响资产，只要有正确备份的助记词即可在其他兼容钱包恢复。

此方案的核心价值是规避商业硬件钱包的供应链风险，同时用空气间隙降低远程攻击面。它适合有一定动手能力的普通用户，但不是绝对安全。严格执行每一步，先小额验证，再逐步使用。

鉴于上面的攻略有人问手机坏了怎么办？

手机坏了没关系，资产还在。
冷钱包真正重要的是助记词（种子），不是那台手机本身。

手机坏了/丢了/无法开机时怎么办？
拿出你之前手写的助记词备份（纸质或金属板）。
准备另一部干净的旧手机（或新设备）。
按同样的流程操作：彻底重置 短暂联网只下载一次开源钱包软件 永久断网 选择「导入/恢复钱包」，输入之前备份的助记词
恢复成功后，继续用二维码签名即可。
资产是记录在比特币区块链上的，只要助记词正确，就能在任何兼容的开源钱包里恢复，不依赖原来那台手机。

关键前提
你必须已经正确备份了助记词（多份、分开放）。
助记词从来没被截图、拍照或传到联网设备。
如果设置了 BIP39 密码（第 25 词），也要一起保管好，少了就恢复不了。

额外建议
在正式转移大额资金前，先做一次恢复测试：用助记词在另一台离线设备上恢复，确认能正常生成地址并签名。
手机只是临时的签名工具，坏了就换一台继续用。真正不能丢的是助记词。
所以，手机坏了不是大问题，助记词丢了才是真的没救。

We were able to fine tune an open weight model (Qwen3.5-9B) on proprietary internal data at @coinbase, and it out performed frontier models, at much lower cost and speed, for a specialized task (fraud prevention in this case).

I think we'll see more of this pattern inside companies. The frontier models are amazing generalists. But increasingly you'll see specialist models out perform on more narrow tasks, either working on teams, or by themselves.

We're making it easy to fine tune models internally for our employees. We even have a skill for it in our internal harness that makes it easy to spin these up and start training them:

"/fine-tune-and-serve-llm I want to fine-tune Qwen for payments risk review. help me get started"

I imagine we'll have some backend services that could be replaced entirely by this new architecture.

text:
In basketball, we often talk about a player having that “dog” in him.

It’s not about talent, athleticism, or scoring averages.

It’s something deeper.

That relentless competitive instinct. That refusal to back down. That almost irrational obsession with winning.

A player with that dog doesn’t just want to beat you. He wants to break your confidence, impose his will, and make sure you know who the better player is.

Basketball has given us legendary competitors. Kobe Bryant, Larry Bird, Kevin Garnett, and many others.

But then there’s Michael Jordan.

Jordan might have had the biggest dog the sport has ever seen.

He manufactured rivalries, turned harmless comments into personal vendettas, and remembered every perceived slight.

Winning wasn’t enough. He wanted to dominate you physically, mentally, and psychologically.

And the terrifying part? He had the talent to back up every ounce of that obsession.

Six Finals. Six championships. Six Finals MVPs.

The numbers tell you what he accomplished.

His mentality tells you why.

Michael Jordan didn’t just want to be the best player on the court. He wanted everyone else to know they weren’t.

That’s a different kind of dog.

I do not know if this is true. But look at where pearl-2:native trades today: 2 small exchanges, no way to buy it while holding your own keys. If it lands on NEAR Intents, that is the first non-custodial venue the coin ever had, with buyers from 35 chains on day one. Quantus had the same setup two weeks ago.

Which points at the most underrated thing about NEAR.

A chain's cult is made of people who got rich holding its coin. Bitcoin, Ether, Solana each have an army that made lifechanging money there and never forgot where.

NEAR has not done that for NEAR holders... yet. But it already did something different. Zcash holders got their run after ZEC landed on Intents, Quantus holders got theirs the day it listed, and both groups know exactly where the liquidity came from. The next ones will too, because non-custodial cross-chain trading is a working tool, and every chain short on liquidity needs one.

The coins keep their cults. NEAR keeps the market they trade on, and every swap in it sends a fee into NEAR buybacks. Cults rotate every cycle. The market where they rotate stays.

Every cult needs a market. Market of markets. NEAR

text:
丁果先生，请公开澄清：您支持 Alexa Loo，是否与中国官方或相关侨团存在任何协调？

2026 年 9 月 18 日，丁果发表文章，明显倾向列治文市长候选人 Alexa Loo（卢仙泳），并质疑现任市长 Brodie 支持 Rob Howard 的决定。

公开资料还显示：

① 丁果曾与中国驻温哥华领事馆官员及华人社团联席会（CACA）负责人共同出席活动。

② Alexa Loo 曾多次出席 CACA 活动，与中国外交官同场，并曾获得该社团负责人王典奇的竞选捐款。

③ 丁果创办的加拿大华裔百人会（CCS100），曾因涉及中国政协相关人脉网络而受到加拿大调查记者关注。

丁果先生，请您公开回答四个问题：

1. 您对 Alexa Loo 的政治支持，是否完全出于个人独立判断？

2. 您是否曾就支持 Alexa Loo、竞选宣传或选民动员，与中国领事馆、相关侨团或任何中国官方代表进行沟通或协调？

3. 您是否与 Alexa Loo 或 Richmond Strong 竞选团队就相关政治宣传进行过协调？是否有任何外部机构提供资金、资源或其他支持？

4. 您领导的 CCS100 与中国政协、统战部门及相关组织之间，究竟存在什么性质的关系？

我们强调：公开合影、正常社团往来及合法政治表达并不构成违法证据。目前也没有证据证明丁果或 Alexa Loo 接受中共指令。

但加拿大法律禁止某些外国实体秘密干预政治活动及违反竞选融资规定的行为。

如果发现外国政府秘密协调、代捐或未申报竞选宣传的具体线索，公众有权向 Elections BC 提交投诉，并向 CSIS 报告潜在外国干预。

这不是预先认定任何人违法，而是要求公众人物对涉及选举透明度的合理问题作出回应。

丁果先生，您愿意在 10 月 17 日投票前公开澄清吗？

列治文的市长，必须由列治文选民自主决定。

#RichmondBC #RichmondElection2026 #AlexaLoo #DingGuo #ForeignInterference
author: billtheinvestor
quoted_text:
中共黑手正在影响 2026 列治文市长选举？

丁果公开支持 Alexa Loo，背后浮现中国领事馆与统战关联社团网络：

列治文市选将于 10 月 17 日举行。一个值得公众关注的问题是：长期与中国官方及相关华人社团保持联系的媒体人丁果，为什么在选举关键阶段明显支持市长候选人 Alexa Loo（卢仙泳）？

更重要的是，丁果与 Alexa Loo 的公开社交网络中，出现了部分相同的侨团负责人、中国外交官及政治活动人士。

这些联系究竟只是普通社区交往，还是存在需要进一步披露的外国政治影响？

以下是能够核查的事实、照片和原始文件。

一、丁果对 Alexa Loo 的支持：有署名文章为证

2026 年 9 月 18 日，丁果在《加拿大乐活网》发表《列治文市选：马保定为何背书何伟略？》。

文章批评即将退休的市长 Malcolm Brodie 公开支持 Rob Howard，并提出 Howard 可能分散 Alexa Loo 所需的华裔选票。

丁果甚至写道：

“有人或许会说，我支持卢仙泳，才有上述感想，实属个人观点。其实不然……”

他随后解释，自己此前也曾鼓励另一名华裔市议员区泽光竞选市长。

虽然丁果否认自己批评 Brodie 纯粹出于支持 Loo，但整篇文章明显表达了对 Loo 的积极评价和对分票的担忧。

这证明丁果公开发表了有利于 Alexa Loo 的政治评论，但不等于他已经成为其竞选团队成员。

原文：
https://t.co/CjdGitLsyT

二、丁果与中国官方：不是仅有一次偶然接触

证据一：中国领事馆亲自出席丁果的新书发布会。

2017 年 6 月 24 日，中国驻温哥华总领馆发布官方公告，确认时任总领事刘菲出席丁果等人合著的《加拿大的中国基因》新书发布会。

官方公告提到刘菲发表讲话，鼓励华人推动中加合作。

这是中国外交机构自己公开的记录，而不是匿名爆料。

中国领事馆原文：
https://t.co/q8VK3r9AbX

证据二：丁果与中国领事馆官员及侨团负责人共同出席活动。
2017 年 2 月，加拿大华人社团联席会（CACA）在列治文举办春节活动。

该组织官网公布的出席名单包括：

中国驻温哥华副总领事孔玮玮及领事张昊；

联席会执行主席王典奇；

华人时事评论员丁果；
华人建筑装修协会会长蒋浩（Jeff Jiang）。
值得注意的是，蒋浩如今正是 Alexa Loo 的 Richmond Strong 市议员竞选团队成员。
这份名单证明他们曾经参与同一社区活动，但本身不能证明他们共同策划过政治行动。

原始记录：
https://t.co/cLE5ah1QYy联席会举办春节团拜共同主席座谈会/

证据三：丁果创办的华裔百人会涉及统战关联争议。

2023 年 12 月，调查记者 Sam Cooper 在 The Bureau 披露一段 2020 年会议录音。
会议由丁果领导的 Canada Committee 100 Society（CCS100）举办，加拿大参议员 Yuen Pau Woo（胡元豹）参与。

报道指出，该组织与中国政协相关网络存在联系，而会议讨论了与北京统战组织有关联的人士如何应对加拿大社会对其政治立场的质疑。

前加拿大外交官 Charles Burton 对这种活动表达了担忧。

但报道没有证明丁果本人接受中国政府的直接命令或秘密资助。

调查与会议照片：
https://t.co/QErxKVE70O

三、Alexa Loo 与中国外交官：有多次公开影像记录

证据四：2022 年 10 月，与中国总领事出席活动。

Alexa Loo 出席温哥华的中国文化艺术节。Richmond News 刊登的现场照片显示，她与中国驻温哥华总领事杨舒、副总领事王承军同场。
活动同时受到部分批评者质疑，因为举行时间与中华人民共和国国庆纪念活动重合。

Loo 回应称自己参加活动是为了促进多元文化交流，并不知道主办团体被指与中共有联系。

照片及报道：
https://t.co/5lcHbtHlO8

证据五：2022 年 11 月，与中国总领事共同参加 CACA 就职典礼。

这次活动的证据更加直接。

CACA 自己的官网公布了现场照片和详细讲话记录。

中国总领事杨舒在致辞中称赞该社团在涉及“中国统一”的问题上立场坚定，并谈到中共二十大。
Alexa Loo 在同一活动中发表讲话。主办方报道，她表示过去与社团负责人薛晓梅有联系和合作，并将继续支持联席会。

这里的问题不是政治人物能否参加华人社区活动，而是一个公开强调中国政治统一立场的社团，与加拿大地方民选官员之间有怎样的互动与政治边界。

主办方原文及照片：
https://t.co/cLE5ah1QYy加拿大华人社团联席会第九届执行团队就职典礼隆重举行/

四、Alexa Loo 与王典奇：存在公开报道的竞选捐款

证据六：2023 年春节私人聚会录像。

2023 年 2 月，调查记者 Bob Mackin 报道，Alexa Loo 在列治文参加了一场私人春节聚会。

出席者包括 CACA 荣誉主席王典奇。

报道根据 Elections BC 的竞选财务披露指出，王典奇曾向 Alexa Loo 的 2022 年连任竞选捐款 500 加元。
同一报道回顾了王典奇此前公开支持中国军队的活动，包括向中国军人提供资金和物资。

这是一笔经媒体报道、有明确姓名和金额的历史政治捐款。不能将其直接称为中国政府资金。

Alexa Loo 随后回应媒体，表示参加朋友聚会不代表支持其他出席者的个人政治观点，并否认自己因参加聚会而受到调查。

现场影像、报道及捐款线索：
https://t.co/OR5VGzeJaL

Loo 回应：
https://t.co/1ARnWECUz3

五、2026 年：这些外交与社团联系仍在延续

证据七：选举年份再次与中国外交人员同场。

2026 年 7 月，theBreaker 报道，Alexa Loo 与 Richmond Strong 团队出席了 CACA 在列治文举办的加拿大国庆活动。

报道指出，Loo 与中国驻温哥华代总领事曾智在现场相邻而坐，并登台讲话。

中国驻温哥华总领馆 7 月 3 日的官方公告也证实，曾智参加了 CACA 举办的国庆活动。
这是 2026 年正在发生的接触，而不只是多年前的历史记录。

媒体调查：
https://t.co/ltiRP5uxI4
中国领事馆公告：
https://t.co/pmy8w2h1tB

六、将三条证据链放在一起

现在可以清楚看到：

丁果的关系链：

中国领事馆公开往来 → 华人社团活动 → 丁果领导的 CCS100 → 2026 年发表有利于 Alexa Loo 的政治评论。

Alexa Loo 的关系链：

中国外交官同场活动 → CACA 多次合作与交流 → 王典奇历史竞选捐款 → 2026 年 Richmond Strong 团队继续参与相关社团活动。

双方网络的交集：
丁果、王典奇、蒋浩等人早在 2017 年就出现在同一社团活动名单上。王典奇后来出现在 Alexa Loo 的捐款报道中，蒋浩则加入了她的 2026 年竞选团队。

这些事实足以说明双方参与了部分重叠的社区政治网络。
但必须强调：共同出席活动、合法捐款及公开支持候选人，并不自动证明存在中共统一指挥的竞选活动。

七、为什么列治文选民有理由关注外国干预？

这不是凭空出现的国家安全议题。

加拿大 2025 年外国干预调查委员会最终报告披露，针对 2021 年 Steveston–Richmond East 联邦选举的调查发现，有信息表明中国官员通过公开言论，为针对保守党的宣传活动提供了推动和方向。

相关宣传又通过华人社团成员、商业关系及媒体渠道传播。

不过，选举调查人员没有取得足以认定违反《加拿大选举法》的证据。

这份官方报告并没有认定丁果或 Alexa Loo 参与上述活动，更没有认定他们干预了 2026 年市选。

但是，报告证明了一个现实问题：外国政府可以利用合法社区关系和媒体传播渠道尝试影响加拿大政治，而这些活动并不一定容易识别。

官方报告：
https://t.co/dRUOxmreNs

八、需要公开回答的问题

在距离 10 月 17 日选举仅剩数日之际，我认为有几个值得公开澄清的问题：

第一，丁果对 Alexa Loo 的支持，是他作为媒体人的独立观点，还是曾与相关社团或竞选团队进行协调？

第二，Alexa Loo 和 Richmond Strong 与中国领事馆及相关侨团之间，是否有超出公开文化活动范围的竞选合作？

第三，相关社团人士是否参与过 2026 年竞选的组织、宣传、筹款或志愿者动员？如果有，是否符合 BC 省选举法？

第四，Alexa Loo 是否愿意就这些历史接触、已报道捐款和 2026 年活动作出完整公开说明？

这些是有待回答的问题，不是已经证明的违法事实。

加拿大华人拥有完整的民主参与权利，与中国外交官见面也不是违法行为。

但任何外国政府都不应该秘密决定加拿大市政选举的结果。对于已经受到外国干预调查关注的列治文，透明度尤其重要。

我们目前有照片、有中国领事馆公告、有社团原始报道、有署名政治评论，还有加拿大官方外国干预调查报告。
我们目前没有的是：足以证明丁果或 Alexa Loo 接受中共指令、秘密资金或共同操纵 2026 年选举的直接证据。

正因为如此，公众有权提出问题，当事人也应有公平回应的机会。

列治文市长应该由列治文选民决定，而不是任何外国政府。
