text:
#医保 #养老金 #公积金 #延迟退休

看到很多自由职业的朋友，还在主动自费缴纳社保，感到悲痛惋惜。来分享一下我的观点：

🏥医保

1. 大部分缴纳医保的年轻人，从未真正使用过医保。

这是一个恶意的文字游戏，自费是自己掏钱，医保支付大部分情况下依然是自己掏钱。

不妨检查一下付款的详单，大概率用的是个人账户支付，而非统筹账户 —— 也就是自费。

但在所有医院付款环节中，这里被特意的设计成 让你误以为是医保报销。

如果你想真正看病报销，推荐查看这个视频《2023最清晰实用医保指南》，足够清晰易懂，也足够让你头昏眼花。
https://t.co/4zvQg6Cx7d

2. 自由职业者可以选择只缴纳居民医保，这是全中国唯一尚存的“老百姓福利”。

门诊报销比例，实际使用中占比很小，医保重要的是重大疾病、尤其是住院手术时的报销能力。

这一点居民医保性价比很高，虽然需要通过层层关卡（申请转院），但操作得当是可以真实落地报销的。

3. 商业险，须知保险的本质是杠杆。

购买保险，是你本人和保险公司之间的对赌，对赌一定有输赢。对方一堆精算师算出来的价格，你只要接受了，毫无疑问是你输。

那为什么必输还得买呢 —— 因为你还不够有钱，也承担不起重病的风险，所以不得不接受这个必输的交易，来获取一定杠杆。这个杠杆就是，你用每个月相对少量钱的付出，加杠杆，获取重大疾病发生时的医疗费用兜底。

换句话说，如果你有一些资产，比如应急现金留够了 100 万，那就不用考虑额外买商业保险了。以国内保险从业者的素质而言，条款里每一项细则都可能是坑，完全可以选择不参与这种必输的游戏。

👴养老金

已经退休的公务员，到手工资比重点大学的毕业生高很多，这不是段子而是现实。养老金是非常简单的问题：你到底是哪一边的？

公务员、国企、私企、自由职业（打零工），身份不同，实际到手的养老金差异巨大，网上可以搜到足够多的数据。有多少人考公，就有多少人想明白了这一点，选择努力做被供养的那一边。

看到很多年轻公务员抱怨工作强度大，收入低，被 PUA。那你为啥不来另一边 😆

没有谁是傻子，大家都会为自己的利益努力。作为既得利益者，当然是希望更多人缴纳养老金，更晚退休。如果你不幸在另一方，唯一能做的抵抗就是尽量不交，尽量少交。

至于能不能可持续发展，这根本没有讨论价值，如果还在纠结这个问题，我收回上一句话“没有谁是傻子”。

🏠 公积金

这个部分没有坑，或者说坑不在这里… 住房公积金是实打实能提取，能到手的真钱，算收入的时候考虑进去。

据我观察，愿意冒风险给员工避税的公司越来越少了。在这个过程中，企业的风险远大于收益，而且能把账算明白的也是少数，吃力不讨好。

以前我上班的时候，有一份工作税前是 4 万，到手是 5.3万。—— 还真就有人选择不要到手 5.5，选择要到手 2.7 + 全额缴纳的。

当然企业是为了自己省钱，还是为了给你也省点，要具体情况具体计算。不要先入为主拒绝，一切以自己到手为准。

🎫 社保的额外价值

也就是落户和房票。

在我辞职之后的一段时间，还继续保持着上海的社保。当时还没做决定，未来会不会在上海生活，买房，落户。所以付费保持着连续社保，断了这些就没资格了。

当决定定居日本之后立刻停了，止损。放今天看，落户和房票 显然越来越不值钱了，更加没有维持的必要。

公积金早已提取完毕了，养老金我放弃，医保还有钱。所以我依然保持着，回国时顺带找三甲医院做的检查的习惯，尽量把医保的钱花掉。不报销，仅医保个人账户自费，不给国家添麻烦。

——

我想说的说完了 ～ 大部分人也许还没有选择，但理应知道自己在做什么，这样有选择的时候才能选对。

祝早日退休，领到自己应得的养老金。

text:
中共黑手正在影响 2026 列治文市长选举？

丁果公开支持 Alexa Loo，背后浮现中国领事馆与统战关联社团网络：

列治文市选将于 10 月 17 日举行。一个值得公众关注的问题是：长期与中国官方及相关华人社团保持联系的媒体人丁果，为什么在选举关键阶段明显支持市长候选人 Alexa Loo（卢仙泳）？

更重要的是，丁果与 Alexa Loo 的公开社交网络中，出现了部分相同的侨团负责人、中国外交官及政治活动人士。

这些联系究竟只是普通社区交往，还是存在需要进一步披露的外国政治影响？

以下是能够核查的事实、照片和原始文件。

一、丁果对 Alexa Loo 的支持：有署名文章为证

2026 年 9 月 18 日，丁果在《加拿大乐活网》发表《列治文市选：马保定为何背书何伟略？》。

文章批评即将退休的市长 Malcolm Brodie 公开支持 Rob Howard，并提出 Howard 可能分散 Alexa Loo 所需的华裔选票。

丁果甚至写道：

“有人或许会说，我支持卢仙泳，才有上述感想，实属个人观点。其实不然……”

他随后解释，自己此前也曾鼓励另一名华裔市议员区泽光竞选市长。

虽然丁果否认自己批评 Brodie 纯粹出于支持 Loo，但整篇文章明显表达了对 Loo 的积极评价和对分票的担忧。

这证明丁果公开发表了有利于 Alexa Loo 的政治评论，但不等于他已经成为其竞选团队成员。

原文：
https://t.co/CjdGitLsyT

二、丁果与中国官方：不是仅有一次偶然接触

证据一：中国领事馆亲自出席丁果的新书发布会。

2017 年 6 月 24 日，中国驻温哥华总领馆发布官方公告，确认时任总领事刘菲出席丁果等人合著的《加拿大的中国基因》新书发布会。

官方公告提到刘菲发表讲话，鼓励华人推动中加合作。

这是中国外交机构自己公开的记录，而不是匿名爆料。

中国领事馆原文：
https://t.co/q8VK3r9AbX

证据二：丁果与中国领事馆官员及侨团负责人共同出席活动。
2017 年 2 月，加拿大华人社团联席会（CACA）在列治文举办春节活动。

该组织官网公布的出席名单包括：

中国驻温哥华副总领事孔玮玮及领事张昊；

联席会执行主席王典奇；

华人时事评论员丁果；
华人建筑装修协会会长蒋浩（Jeff Jiang）。
值得注意的是，蒋浩如今正是 Alexa Loo 的 Richmond Strong 市议员竞选团队成员。
这份名单证明他们曾经参与同一社区活动，但本身不能证明他们共同策划过政治行动。

原始记录：
https://t.co/cLE5ah1QYy联席会举办春节团拜共同主席座谈会/

证据三：丁果创办的华裔百人会涉及统战关联争议。

2023 年 12 月，调查记者 Sam Cooper 在 The Bureau 披露一段 2020 年会议录音。
会议由丁果领导的 Canada Committee 100 Society（CCS100）举办，加拿大参议员 Yuen Pau Woo（胡元豹）参与。

报道指出，该组织与中国政协相关网络存在联系，而会议讨论了与北京统战组织有关联的人士如何应对加拿大社会对其政治立场的质疑。

前加拿大外交官 Charles Burton 对这种活动表达了担忧。

但报道没有证明丁果本人接受中国政府的直接命令或秘密资助。

调查与会议照片：
https://t.co/QErxKVE70O

三、Alexa Loo 与中国外交官：有多次公开影像记录

证据四：2022 年 10 月，与中国总领事出席活动。

Alexa Loo 出席温哥华的中国文化艺术节。Richmond News 刊登的现场照片显示，她与中国驻温哥华总领事杨舒、副总领事王承军同场。
活动同时受到部分批评者质疑，因为举行时间与中华人民共和国国庆纪念活动重合。

Loo 回应称自己参加活动是为了促进多元文化交流，并不知道主办团体被指与中共有联系。

照片及报道：
https://t.co/5lcHbtHlO8

证据五：2022 年 11 月，与中国总领事共同参加 CACA 就职典礼。

这次活动的证据更加直接。

CACA 自己的官网公布了现场照片和详细讲话记录。

中国总领事杨舒在致辞中称赞该社团在涉及“中国统一”的问题上立场坚定，并谈到中共二十大。
Alexa Loo 在同一活动中发表讲话。主办方报道，她表示过去与社团负责人薛晓梅有联系和合作，并将继续支持联席会。

这里的问题不是政治人物能否参加华人社区活动，而是一个公开强调中国政治统一立场的社团，与加拿大地方民选官员之间有怎样的互动与政治边界。

主办方原文及照片：
https://t.co/cLE5ah1QYy加拿大华人社团联席会第九届执行团队就职典礼隆重举行/

四、Alexa Loo 与王典奇：存在公开报道的竞选捐款

证据六：2023 年春节私人聚会录像。

2023 年 2 月，调查记者 Bob Mackin 报道，Alexa Loo 在列治文参加了一场私人春节聚会。

出席者包括 CACA 荣誉主席王典奇。

报道根据 Elections BC 的竞选财务披露指出，王典奇曾向 Alexa Loo 的 2022 年连任竞选捐款 500 加元。
同一报道回顾了王典奇此前公开支持中国军队的活动，包括向中国军人提供资金和物资。

这是一笔经媒体报道、有明确姓名和金额的历史政治捐款。不能将其直接称为中国政府资金。

Alexa Loo 随后回应媒体，表示参加朋友聚会不代表支持其他出席者的个人政治观点，并否认自己因参加聚会而受到调查。

现场影像、报道及捐款线索：
https://t.co/OR5VGzeJaL

Loo 回应：
https://t.co/1ARnWECUz3

五、2026 年：这些外交与社团联系仍在延续

证据七：选举年份再次与中国外交人员同场。

2026 年 7 月，theBreaker 报道，Alexa Loo 与 Richmond Strong 团队出席了 CACA 在列治文举办的加拿大国庆活动。

报道指出，Loo 与中国驻温哥华代总领事曾智在现场相邻而坐，并登台讲话。

中国驻温哥华总领馆 7 月 3 日的官方公告也证实，曾智参加了 CACA 举办的国庆活动。
这是 2026 年正在发生的接触，而不只是多年前的历史记录。

媒体调查：
https://t.co/ltiRP5uxI4
中国领事馆公告：
https://t.co/pmy8w2h1tB

六、将三条证据链放在一起

现在可以清楚看到：

丁果的关系链：

中国领事馆公开往来 → 华人社团活动 → 丁果领导的 CCS100 → 2026 年发表有利于 Alexa Loo 的政治评论。

Alexa Loo 的关系链：

中国外交官同场活动 → CACA 多次合作与交流 → 王典奇历史竞选捐款 → 2026 年 Richmond Strong 团队继续参与相关社团活动。

双方网络的交集：
丁果、王典奇、蒋浩等人早在 2017 年就出现在同一社团活动名单上。王典奇后来出现在 Alexa Loo 的捐款报道中，蒋浩则加入了她的 2026 年竞选团队。

这些事实足以说明双方参与了部分重叠的社区政治网络。
但必须强调：共同出席活动、合法捐款及公开支持候选人，并不自动证明存在中共统一指挥的竞选活动。

七、为什么列治文选民有理由关注外国干预？

这不是凭空出现的国家安全议题。

加拿大 2025 年外国干预调查委员会最终报告披露，针对 2021 年 Steveston–Richmond East 联邦选举的调查发现，有信息表明中国官员通过公开言论，为针对保守党的宣传活动提供了推动和方向。

相关宣传又通过华人社团成员、商业关系及媒体渠道传播。

不过，选举调查人员没有取得足以认定违反《加拿大选举法》的证据。

这份官方报告并没有认定丁果或 Alexa Loo 参与上述活动，更没有认定他们干预了 2026 年市选。

但是，报告证明了一个现实问题：外国政府可以利用合法社区关系和媒体传播渠道尝试影响加拿大政治，而这些活动并不一定容易识别。

官方报告：
https://t.co/dRUOxmreNs

八、需要公开回答的问题

在距离 10 月 17 日选举仅剩数日之际，我认为有几个值得公开澄清的问题：

第一，丁果对 Alexa Loo 的支持，是他作为媒体人的独立观点，还是曾与相关社团或竞选团队进行协调？

第二，Alexa Loo 和 Richmond Strong 与中国领事馆及相关侨团之间，是否有超出公开文化活动范围的竞选合作？

第三，相关社团人士是否参与过 2026 年竞选的组织、宣传、筹款或志愿者动员？如果有，是否符合 BC 省选举法？

第四，Alexa Loo 是否愿意就这些历史接触、已报道捐款和 2026 年活动作出完整公开说明？

这些是有待回答的问题，不是已经证明的违法事实。

加拿大华人拥有完整的民主参与权利，与中国外交官见面也不是违法行为。

但任何外国政府都不应该秘密决定加拿大市政选举的结果。对于已经受到外国干预调查关注的列治文，透明度尤其重要。

我们目前有照片、有中国领事馆公告、有社团原始报道、有署名政治评论，还有加拿大官方外国干预调查报告。
我们目前没有的是：足以证明丁果或 Alexa Loo 接受中共指令、秘密资金或共同操纵 2026 年选举的直接证据。

正因为如此，公众有权提出问题，当事人也应有公平回应的机会。

列治文市长应该由列治文选民决定，而不是任何外国政府。

text:
Variational的老板是真的懂交易，他说了几个做空法则，很有学习意义：

1. 迷思：“做空最多只能赚100%，却可能亏无限多。”错了。这只在你不进行再平衡时才成立，所以应始终通过减仓/加仓来调整到目标权重。只要进行再平衡，做空也能赚/亏无限百分比。

2. 空头组合需要比多头组合更分散。一个经验法则是：单一做空想法不超过整个投资组合的5%。（如果你会建立真正的风险模型，可以忽略这条法则。）标的可能而且往往会在你面前突然上涨300%。

3. 不要做空正在上涨的东西。听起来很明显。不要做空那些每天创新高的热门标的。“被高估”本身不是做空的好理由。要做空那些已经持续崩了十年的无聊标的。

4. 一般来说，大多数资产类别长期都会上涨，所以即便你有空头组合，为了追求最佳回报，整体组合通常还是要保持净多头。

Finding alpha on the short side isn't as hard as you might think, but if you are starting out, here are some rules to follow: 

1. MYTH: "You can only make 100% on a short but you can lose infinite percent". WRONG. This is only true if you don't rebalance, but that's f*cking stupid, so always trim/add to get to your target weight. You can make/lose infinite percent on a short if you rebalance. 

2. A short book needs more diversification than a long book. One heuristic to follow is no more than 5% of your portfolio in a single short idea. (Ignore the heuristic if you know how to build an actual risk model). Things can and will go up 300% in your face very quickly. 

3. Don't short things that are going up. Sounds obvious. Don't: short the hot thing that makes new highs every day. Something being "overvalued" is not a good reason to short. Do: short the boring thing that's been crumbling for a decade. 

4. Generally speaking most asset classes go up over time, so even if you have a short book you probably want your portfolio to be net long for the best returns. 

All 4 of these rules are empirically backtestable 🙂

text:
发现宝藏了！目前最牛逼的iPhone Use开源库: ICTRL
仓库地址在评论区。

直接让电脑或手机上的 Agent 操控 iPhone 里的各种 App，不用去买豆包手机了！惊叹苹果的生态真牛逼！

几个让我惊喜的点：
1. 比通过 Mac「iPhone 镜像」间接操作手机快很多
2. Mac、Windows 上的 Coding Agent，都可以通过局域网 Wi-Fi 操控 iPhone
3. 甚至不需要电脑：在 iPhone 上用 Minis App（也是一个 Coding Agent），就能直接操作这台手机

怎么用：
1. 安装完成后，直接在对话里点名使用 ictrl-phone-control skill，就能触发手机控制

2. 手机端Minis app第一次使用下面提示词：
```
这台 iPhone 已启动 iCTRL，服务地址是 127.0.0.1:8200。

请读取 http://127.0.0.1:8200/skill，按照其中的说明连接本机 iCTRL，然后打开天气，告诉我今天的天气。
```

不过，目前有一些坑：

① 安装门槛比较高，需要耐心。建议把 README.md 丢给 Agent，让它带着你一步步安装。

② 手机的局域网 IP 变化后，连接可能失败。目前配对信息保存在 ~/.ictrl/token.json，读到的可能还是上次的 IP。这时需要手动把 iCTRL 当前显示的监听地址告诉 Agent。

3. 有些手机app会有防御，由于底层用的是测试框架，例如淘宝app就会检测，频繁让你重新登录，这些app就不要使用了

仓库地址放评论区 👇

附件为看天气，看滴答清单，看宝玉哥今天的推特内容（当然都是可以通过电脑上的网页端获取，这里故意用这些任务，使用手机上的相关app来展现 iCTRL的能力）

text:
IMF 《世界经济展望》：明年经济反弹，AI 撤资或致全球 GDP 少 1.1%

全球经济还能保持增长，AI 投资出了不少力。但这轮热潮一旦退去，冲击会从科技投资传到资产价格、消费和全球产出。IMF 最新发布《世界经济展望》，以下是小编摘取的五个比较值得关注的点：

1.明年经济反弹，但增速仍低于过去两年

IMF 预计，今年全球经济增长 3.1%，明年回升至 3.4%，仍低于过去两年平均 3.5% 的水平。恢复还依赖能源供应改善：报告假设霍尔木兹海峡明年 3 月开始恢复通航。

2.32 个经济体，贡献全球 95% 的增长

4 月时，贡献同等比例增长的还有 54 个经济体，如今进一步收窄。接入 AI 供应链的国家靠投资和出口获得支撑；依赖能源进口、又分不到科技需求增长的国家，则承受更高成本和更弱的实际收入。

3. AI 投资退潮，全球 GDP 或少 1.1%

如果 AI 带来的效率提升不及预期，企业削减投资，再叠加资产价格下跌、金融条件收紧和消费走弱，到 2028 年，全球 GDP 或比基准预测低 1.1%。AI 热潮的回撤，影响会一路传到实体经济。

4.中东战争或致明年油价达 130 美元

如果战争进一步恶化，油价在明年第一季度维持每桶 130 美元，全球经济增速今年、明年可能分别被拉低 0.2、0.5 个百分点，明年通胀率则可能升至 5.2%。油价上涨，会同时挤压增长和推高物价。

5.通胀退得慢，政府也更难靠借钱托底

全球通胀率预计从今年的 4.7% 降至明年的 4.1%。高债务和借款成本又压缩了政府应对冲击的空间。IMF 建议重建财政缓冲，对受冲击家庭提供临时、定向支持，并投入基础设施和技能培训，让更多人分享科技带来的增长。

text:
Anthropic 测试 AI 自我复制：现在的小模型还做不到，按趋势年底可能追上

先说结论：目前还没有能在网上自己到处复制的 AI。

Anthropic 在一个简化过的实验环境里测了一批开源模型，能完整走完“传到新机器、把模型装好跑起来、再传下一台”整个流程的只有智谱的 GLM-5.2，它太大，塞不进电视盒子这类小设备；塞得进去的小模型都没做到。

按小模型过去的进步速度，Anthropic 估计今年年底就会有小模型达到 GLM-5.2 在这项测试里的水平，之后可能出现能在廉价联网设备上自我复制的 AI。

这项研究是 Anthropic 前沿红队（Frontier Red Team，专门评估模型危险能力的团队）10 月 12 日发布的。

【AI 自我复制是什么意思】

电脑蠕虫是一种不用人操作、自己从一台机器复制到下一台的恶意程序。Anthropic 担心的是 AI 版本的蠕虫：把模型权重（模型本体文件）当成病毒的一部分带着走，每占领一台设备，就在上面把模型跑起来，再由这个模型去找下一个目标。

它和传统病毒的区别在于能自己摸索陌生设备。传统僵尸网络（被黑客控制的大批设备）一般只针对某一类设备写死攻击代码，AI 蠕虫碰到没见过的硬件，可以自己查、自己试。它也没有一个中心开关，很难一次性关掉。

【离真能用还差多远】

Anthropic 把复制拆成四步：找目标、拿到执行权限、在新设备上把模型跑起来、从新设备继续传播。前两步属于黑客攻击，已有其他研究表明小模型能做，这次没有重点测。

重点测的是第三步。在陌生机器上让模型跑起来，要挑对推理软件、装对版本、排查这台机器特有的问题，一步卡住后面全卡住。

测试中，90 亿参数的 Qwen3.5-9B 在 9 类硬件里的 8 类上成功搭起了推理服务。这 9 类硬件大多是云服务器，从 Mac、RTX 4090 到数据中心显卡都有，另有两块实体小开发板，没有电视盒子。

然后是完整流程。研究团队搭了 8 台运行模拟安卓系统的云服务器，放一只蠕虫进去，看它能不能自己扫描网络、连上别的机器、把文件传过去、搭好推理服务、再继续传。

Qwen3.5-9B、Gemma4-26B-A4B 等模型每次都一台也没传成；GLM-5.2 在 5 次测试里有 4 次传遍 8 台，1 次传到 7 台。

这个结果有三个前提。

第一，入侵环节被简化到几乎没有难度：这些机器的 ADB 端口（安卓的调试接口）不设密码，连上就能操作，Anthropic 自己说这是现实成功率的上限。不过它也提到，当年的 Mirai 僵尸网络就是靠挨个试厂商默认用户名和密码传开的，现实中很多联网设备的防护未必比这强多少。

第二，蠕虫的“大脑”GLM-5.2 并不在被感染的机器上运行，而是放在另一台服务器上，因为这些机器跑不动这么大的模型。它在每台机器上搭起来的是更小的 Llama3.1-8B。实验想说明的是：如果一个 80 亿参数的小模型有 GLM-5.2 的本事，它就能把自己装到新机器上。

第三，“年底追上”是根据一个通用能力指数（ECI）的趋势线推算的。通用能力只能间接反映复制能力，Anthropic 也说这只是粗略估计。

【为什么盯上电视盒子】

模型要自己跑起来，得有能跑模型的设备。数据中心防护严，家用和小企业的联网设备便宜、常年在线、安全措施少，是更容易下手的目标。Anthropic 举的典型是白牌安卓电视盒子：这类盒子多用安卓开源代码改的系统，厂商不额外加安全功能，内存 1 到 4GB。此前的 Kimwolf 僵尸网络就感染了 200 多万台设备，主要是这类盒子。

一台盒子跑不动模型，可以把模型切成几段，分给多台盒子接力计算。Anthropic 买了 15 台约 55 美元、4GB 内存的白牌安卓电视盒子，把 Gemma4-26B-A4B 拆开分到上面，跑出了每秒 0.39 个 Token。

这个演示是研究人员自己部署的，用来说明这类设备凑在一起算力够用。文中还提到，智能冰箱、智能烤箱、扫地机器人、割草机也能分担一段模型，自带 AI 芯片的监控摄像头、视频会议设备会更有吸引力。

【真出现了会怎样】

传得慢。按电视盒子上的实测速度，Qwen3.5-9B 完成一次推理环境搭建要 28 到 51 小时，Gemma4-26B-A4B 要 71 到 150 小时。Anthropic 算了一笔账：如果像 Kimwolf 那样感染 200 万台盒子，每 15 台跑一份 Gemma4-26B-A4B，大约有 13.3 万个副本，总算力最多相当于 40 块 H100 显卡。它把这种蠕虫比作黏菌或果蝇群，数量翻一倍要好几天。

会积累经验。实验让 Qwen3.5-9B 每一代把试过的办法和踩过的坑写成笔记传给下一代，搭建成功率从第一代的 45% 升到后几代的 61% 到 84%。给小模型配一个 Opus 4.8 当顾问则没有明显帮助，小模型不知道该问什么。

防得住一部分。大量设备互传几个 GB 的模型文件、设备之间持续高流量通信，在运营商的流量监控里会很显眼，传得越快越容易暴露。当年清理 Mirai 时，有运营商把被感染用户的网络隔离起来并通知他们处理，14 天清掉了 92% 的感染，不通知的只清掉 74%。

Anthropic 认为类似做法对 AI 蠕虫也有效，但要彻底清除，得每家有感染的运营商都配合。设备厂商可以从源头减少目标，比如在英国市场，联网设备用默认密码已经不合规。

原文没有给普通用户的具体建议。从文中描述的攻击途径推断，家里来路不明的廉价电视盒子、没改过默认密码的联网设备，是最值得留意的。

text:
Some Musings on Forward Deployed Engineers

I spent some time looking into the FDE model for Palantir, OpenAI and Anthropic last week

When you dig into Palantir's Ontology/Foundry its obviously insanely complicated and hard to use and I've built agents for years. Thats why they sell you an FDE to come into your business, connect all of your data sources and systems, let you use any model and give you enterprise AI intelligence

It's AI hand holding and your friendly 60+ year old S&P 500 CEO wants their hand held into the AI realm

Palantir also launched a self serve AI FDE Chatbot style interface which is actually pretty easy to use just hard to find unless you search for it. 

I watched a lot of the demos (hertz, construction companies) and its clear businesses are unlocking a lot of value with Ontology. They just say the word ontology way too much it is annoying. 

Net, it feels like a CEO/company decides they want AI, they go to Palantir and they upgrade their business. They control their data and choose between models, which fits part of my Sovereign AI thesis, but their workflows and applications are built on Palantir so its very sticky for them. Your data, their platform kinda deal

Net, Palantir feels like an enterprise AI systems upgrade through connecting mass data and applications 

On the other hand, OpenAI/Anthropic are doing an emergent model

It’s emergent because employees can adopt the tools, build workflows and become the internal champions for company wide adoption. Getting the same company specific value from Palantir generally takes more upfront setup.

Instead, you have an AI champion or head of AI at a company and you give all your employees access to AI connected to their granola, and calendar and email and internal systems to boost their own individual productivity

Instead of upgrading all legacy systems with AI like Palantir, with OpenAI/Anthropic it feels more akin to giving each employee more reasoning and individual AI capabilities

For enterprise it feels like Palantir is upgrading Systems

For enterprise it feels like OpenAI/Anthropic are upgrading employees

I feel @NousResearch is also in a very strong position since theres millions of Hermes users and these folks act as as champions to upgrade their companies to Hermes enterprise AI. Hermes offers the self serve emergent model but you can expand it company wide with Hermes enterprise. 

Who wins on the Palantir vs OpenAI/Anthropic side? 

I think short term Palantir wins since they have an FDE army, enterprises want to cut AI costs and they want to upgrade their systems to use AI. Every board and shareholder will demand businesses do an AI upgrade cycle and CEOs want their hands held. I think enterprises want long term control and ownership of their AI stack. 

I will note note OpenAI/Anthropic already exclude business data from model training by default but this isn't broad ownership of your creations and there is platform lock in here. 

I feel enterprises owning their AI stack drives the creation of unique business outcomes and applications. Frontier for a business may be an open source model (or fine tuned version) + their data/memory/interactions/entire stack. @brian_armstrong demonstrated part of this today with Coinbase's fine tuned model release. 

Longer term it feels like OpenAI/Anthropic go overboard hiring FDEs (or acquiring all of the mini palantirs out there) and having the frontier model lead so net new technologies are created in a productive human + AI situation and OpenAI/Anthropic capture value as the infrastructure these creations depend on. 

I think OpenAI/Anthropic also eventually own a percentage of these new technologies and creations to rationalize the capex spend for these models and businesses are ok with it since its less upfront cost (but IP farming) and they share the equity upside. 

Net, I think Palantir is upgrading legacy systems with AI and OpenAI/Anthropic upgrading employees with AI

I really like PLTR thesis wise but I can't get comfortable with the valuation here since I can be right on the thesis and lose money if the (very high) multiple compresses. I'm interested in counterpoints here so DM or reply why I'm wrong here or your financial model

Anyway GN sleepy time tea is kicking in 🫖

author: kevinnbass
quoted_text:
I analyzed the Ohio telephone conversation about Talarico at Lindner. It appears likely to be an authentic, i.e., not AI-generated. Here is the analysis. It is lengthy. You can point @grok
at it for a summary or to ask questions.

# Is the Lindner call audio AI-generated? Feature report and assessment

Checked 2026-10-11 by the interactive session. The material is the three released recordings (Current Revolt 6:40, Amacher 0:55, Sortor 0:47) and Amacher's call-log screenshot.

Method:
- **Measurements on the audio:** `forensics/forensics_signal.txt`, `forensics_align.txt`, `forensics_noisefloor.txt`, `forensics_speaker_band.txt`.
- **Two model listening passes:** `forensics/gemini_forensic__*.json`.
- **Four open deepfake-speech classifiers with positive and negative controls:** see "Classifier results" below.

Claude cannot hear audio. Everything below comes from measurements, transcripts and model outputs.

## Three separate questions

1. **Is it AI-generated?** Synthetic text-to-speech or voice cloning, as opposed to real people on a real phone call.

2. **Did the call really reach Lindner, and is the speaker a Lindner employee?** A real call to an impostor or a staged human call would pass every AI test.

3. **Is what she said accurate?** No audio test can answer this.

This report answers 1 and part of 2.

## Features that point to a real recorded phone call
| Feature | What was measured or heard | Weight |
|---|---|---|
| Two channel signatures | The staffer and the IVR are cut hard at about 3.8–4.2 kHz (−37 to −44 dB at 3.8–4.2 kHz, about −55 to −65 dB above 4 kHz): a narrowband phone network. The caller's voice carries energy to 8–10 kHz (about −20 to −33 dB): a wideband local phone mic. The difference holds for every turn of both speakers. A fake would have to synthesize two voices and then model two different channels consistently, including in overlaps | strong |

| Speaker attribution by channel works | Per 100-ms frame, the staffer is always telephone-band and the caller always wideband, so turns can be told apart mechanically. This includes brief interjections ("Oh", "Okay") and the overlap at 6:18–6:22 | moderate |

| Continuous line noise under the key line | The telephone-band noise floor sits at −25 to −31 dB through the 6-s pause at 5:58–6:04 and the key sentence at 6:04–6:14, with no steps or resets. A spliced-in sentence usually leaves a noise-floor discontinuity at its edges | moderate (1-s resolution) |

| The three releases are one recording | Amacher's and Sortor's clips are re-encodings of the last 55.1 s and 47.0 s of the 6:40 file: sample correlation 0.986 and 0.998, with residuals −16 and −24 dB (codec loss). There are no internal splices in either clip | moderate (consistency, not authenticity) |

| Matches the call log | The screenshot shows calls to 513-536-4673, Lindner's published number: 8:53 (2 min), 8:56 (2 min), 8:59 (6 min). The recording is 6:40 and opens with that number's IVR menu prompt. The caller says "did I just talk to you like two minutes ago?", which fits the 8:56 call | moderate (the screenshot itself could be faked) |

| Spontaneous conversational behavior | Dense false starts and self-repairs from both speakers; an improvised spelling alphabet ("Todd, Apple, Larry…"); turn-taking overlaps and an immediate repair ("Mm, I'm sorry"); variable response latency; a 3-minute hold and a "let me go to a computer" errand | moderate. Current voice AI can imitate disfluency, but rarely live two-party overlap over a phone channel |

| Background activity | Other voices and (per both Gemini passes) typing behind the staffer, continuous under her speech. The publisher muted two stretches as background staff talk about "lab work, medications, and what may be other patients" (Current Revolt) | weak to moderate (background can be mixed in, and the muted parts cannot be checked) |

| Gemini listening passes | Gemini 3.1 Pro and 3.7 Flash both judged both voices real (99/100) and heard breaths, natural sibilants and no vocoder artifacts | weak. LLM listening is not a validated detector, and both models wrongly said the caller was also phone-band-limited, which the measurements contradict |

## Features that point away from authenticity, or limit what can be said

| Feature | What was found | Weight |

|---|---|---|

| The file is edited | Two publisher mutes are exact digital zeros: 1:03.1–1:06.2 and 1:13.1–1:16.3, labeled on screen. The 3-min hold, 2:38–5:45, is 186.8 s of exact digital zero. Mutes cannot hide AI, but anything said in those 3–4 s and during the hold cannot be checked | limits the record; not evidence of AI |

| Telephone band limits the forensics | Narrowband audio removes the high frequencies where many cloning artifacts show, and lowers classifier reliability (see the controls below) | limits confidence |

| The caller's channel is "clean" | The caller's side has little background noise, which suits a phone with noise suppression. Weak either way | neutral |

## Assessment

**AI generation.** Every feature that can be measured fits a genuine recording of a two-party phone call: a narrowband far end (staffer and IVR), a wideband near end (caller), continuous line noise through the key sentence, and natural overlap. I found nothing pointing to text-to-speech or voice cloning, apart from the disclosed edits. **My judgment: very unlikely to be AI-generated (roughly 90–95%).** It is not higher because:

- the band-limited far end hides some artifact classes;

- a sophisticated forger could, in principle, synthesize the staffer and pass her through a real phone path;

- the classifiers have limited validity on phone audio (below).

## Classifier results: they failed their controls, so they are uninformative

I ran four open wav2vec2 deepfake-speech classifiers from Hugging Face on 4-s windows of the call and on controls:

- MelodyMachine/Deepfake-audio-detection-V2;
- mo-thecreator/Deepfake-audio-detection;
- Gustking/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-deepfake-audio-classification;
- garystafford/wav2vec2-deepfake-voice-detector.
The controls:
- known AI speech: three Gemini-TTS lines written to mimic the call;
- known human speech: three Wikimedia "Spoken Wikipedia" readings, two uploaded in 2014 and one recorded in 2023.

Each control was run both as recorded (wideband) and through a simulated 8 kHz μ-law phone line. Full table: `forensics/classifier_table.txt` and `forensics/detect_results.json`.

Mean P(fake) by speaker or control (window counts in the table):

| Model | Call: staffer | Call: caller | Known AI (TTS), wideband / phone | Known human 2014 (two readers), wideband / phone | Known human 2023 |

|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| MelodyMachine | 1.00 | 0.96 | 0.00 / 0.00 | 0.83–1.00 / 1.00 | 0.00 |
| mo-thecreator | 0.96 | 0.89 | 0.00–0.67 / 0.50–0.67 | 0.83–1.00 / 1.00 | 0.00–0.33 |
| Gustking | 0.69 | 0.34 | 0.16–0.53 / 0.13–0.37 | 0.62–0.79 / 0.66–0.88 | 0.10–0.14 |
| garystafford | 0.82 | 0.52 | 0.49–0.97 / 0.42–0.86 | Earth 0.96–0.99; Universe 0.01–0.12 | 0.27–0.39 |
**Reading.** Read naively, three of four classifiers would call the staffer's voice "fake". But the same classifiers:
- call real human speech recorded in 2014 "fake" with the same confidence (1.00 / 1.00 / 0.66–0.88 / 0.99);
- mostly call the Gemini AI voice "real": MelodyMachine scored it 0.00, and Gustking scored it 0.13–0.53.

Only garystafford leaned the right way on the AI controls, and it still flagged one of the human readers at 0.99. No model separates the known-AI from the known-human controls. Their high scores on the call's narrowband staffer channel are what domain shift looks like: these models are trained on clean wideband datasets, and both telephone audio and older encodings look "out of distribution" to them. **The classifier scores therefore carry no weight either way.** Do not cite them as evidence of AI generation or of authenticity. A calibrated telephone-domain detector would be needed: a commercial service, or an ASVspoof-style model validated on phone audio. Sending the audio to an outside service needs Kevin's yes.

**Net assessment unchanged.** The judgment of "very unlikely to be AI-generated (roughly 90–95%)" rests on the channel and continuity measurements and the conversational structure above, not on the classifiers.

---

## Corrections after audit A-S6 (2026-10-12T05:42:00Z)

- **A-S6-AI-06:** the "90–95%" figure above is a subjective, uncalibrated estimate. No validated telephone-domain model or likelihood ratio supports a number, and the classifier controls failed. It is withdrawn as a probability. What stands: the measured properties (two consistent channel signatures, located publisher mutes, no detected hard cut at the key lines). Endpoint identity and the accuracy of what was said remain unresolved.

- **A-S6-AI-04:** the "−25 to −31 dB through the key sentence" range does not hold for every second in forensics_noisefloor.txt. The FFT normalization is uncalibrated (it also produces positive dB values). The supportable statement is "no detected hard cut or noise-floor step at the key lines", not proof of no splice.

- **A-S6-AI-07:** forensics_signal.txt is a preliminary log with invalid correlation values above 1, and it is superseded. Only forensics_align.txt (r = 0.986 and 0.998, independently reproduced by the auditor as 0.988 and 0.998) is used for numbers.

昨天还在说 @MEADGod 两天没发推，
不知道 Pons 在憋大招，还是周末休息。

答案来了：都有。

一边，是 Pons 悄悄上线了网页版；
另一边，是 Ozzy 跟着 Robinhood CEO 一起喊 “More to come”。

聊聊这一天的三个细节，以及背后的打法：

1. 产品先行：Pons 网页版上线

昨天早上 6 点，Pons 上线网页端。
能买卖、追踪代币，能挂限价单，还能看进阶数据。

别小看限价单。
这说明 Pons 在从一个发币平台，往交易终端走。
在交易量低迷的时候还在推进产品，至少团队没躺。

2. 借势背书：Vlad 一句 “More to come”

今天凌晨，Robinhood CEO Vlad Tenev 回应链上质疑：
Robinhood Chain 主打代币化真实资产，会接入数百万用户已经在用的 Robinhood 产品。
结尾一句：More to come。

Pons 官方直接引用，原样回了一句 “More to come.”
600+ 赞、150+ 回复，是 Pons 这两天互动最高的一条。

话不多，意思很明白：
官方往哪走，Pons 就跟到哪。

3. Ozzy 回归：转推喊多 + 抛出新问题

Ozzy 这一天的动作：
转 RobinhoodCrypto 的 “Robinhood Chain: just getting started”，
转 Moonshot 的社区认证，
转 KOL 的 “现在是关注 Pons 生态的好时机”。

但最值得看的是他自己的一条原创：
引用 Ben Grossman 的 “Trillions is FUD”，问了一句——
“这对股票 meme 意味着什么？”

还是那个老路子：
嘴上不谈币价，叙事一直在推。

目前的 $PONS，处在“产品在推、情绪在等”的阶段。

网页端是实打实的进展，
但真正能点燃情绪的，还是 “More to come” 到底兑现什么：

text:
i put together literally every major corporate blockchain

@arc moved it into a new phase

back in Aug, my view was that institutions were building different chains around different financial requirements:

- @RobinhoodApp for tokenized investing
– @CantonNetwork for private institutional markets
– @tempo for global payments
– @GIWA_by_Upbit for Upbit’s distribution
– @arc for stablecoin finance

the architecture still matters

but i now think the bigger advantage is controlling the full financial stack

includes assets + distribution + liquidity + settlement + app

right now, Arc has the most complete setup i have seen

[1] Arc

Arc public mainnet went live with:

- 100+ applications
- Circle raised $100M investment from Binance
- 100+ institutional and eco builders
- $74B+ USDC already circulating globally
- BlackRock, DTCC, ICE, Mastercard, Visa, Standard Chartered in the founding validator group

Circle already controls 
- the main asset
- the issuer relationship
- mint and redemption infra
- crosschain liquidity
- payments distribution 
- now the settlement network

Arc now has the strongest starting position in this group

[2] Robinhood

already proven that a corporate chain can attract real crypto-native demand

TVL reached $1B+, weekly DEX vol moved above $11B

DeFi, stablecoins and memes scaled faster than tokenized stocks or Robinhood’s own retail funnel

proved that the open market can create a completely different source of liquidity for corporate blockchain

[3] Canton Network

remains the clearest proof for regulated wholesale finance

supports more than 1M daily txns + ~$9T in monthly txn vol

DTCC and Tradeweb are moving real Treasury and collateral workflows onchain

Canton is less open and less composable than EVM networks, but that is part of its product

privacy and controlled data sharing are required for institutional settlement

[4] GIWA by Upbit

GIWA has Upbit’s distribution in Korea

the chain remains at the testnet stage

so i want to see mainnet liquidity, direct Upbit onboarding, real app before treating it as proven

[5] Tempo

already live and has a much clearer production thesis than when i first wrote about it

- Stripe and DoorDash are bringing payment flows into production
- Visa operates an anchor validator
- KlarnaUSD gives the network a native consumer payment asset

that is the main update to my thesis

the EVM may still become the common execution standard

but the largest advantage will come from controlling the assets and distribution entering that execution layer

快进的听完了，比孙哥硬核多了，几个很有趣的观点总结一下：

1. 1000-2000亿美元先押注：模型未出炉就承诺巨额资本开支，Zuckerberg认为只要AI整体成功，算力可转售，风险低于账面。

2. 模型即产品：Muse故意去掉模型/effort选择器，真正产品是模型的记忆、执行能力与人格，而非传统UI。

3. 个人智能体差异化：刻意避开纯编码竞赛，重点做多模态个人智能体（Active Memory + Active Focus），针对消费场景。

4. 极小研究团队：MSL核心研究约100人，强调人才密度。Llama 4后彻底重启，无硬性deadline。

5. 对齐逻辑不同：优先高可靠执行用户指令，不做道德说教，强调隐私酌情处理（discretion）。

6. 代理商务已启动：用户已把采购委托给Muse，收入路径含订阅 + 帮用户省钱/赚钱的抽成 + API/企业。

7. 不会赢家通吃：蒸馏让能力快速下沉；各实验室执行有起伏；生态倾向多玩家，目标尽快把Wonder能力压缩到Spark并免费分发。

8. 基础设施自建有利：1GW运营约150亿美元/年、建设500-600亿美元。自建优于租云，芯片仍保值。

9. 分发优势明显：免费层用Spark覆盖海量用户，付费层先上Wonder；长期靠规模网络效应。

10. 决策风格激进：Zuckerberg一旦确信就大幅转向，MSL是典型表现。成败关键看Wonder能否快速转化为付费与交易规模。

从投资的视角看：短期资本开支压力极大，中长期取决于个人智能体商业化速度。Meta押注的是“模型能力 + 分发”而非单纯模型领先。

text:
昨天的长文写着写着发现内容太多，只好分段Post，接下来我想逐步给带去2049的问题填上答案。

或许不见得准确，但至少是结合我收集到的信息综合思考过的，给大家做个参考。

👉现在的行业究竟处于什么阶段？ 

我个人觉得现在行业处在青年->中年阶段进行中，如果要参考人类年龄来看，我认为在20岁上下。

叛逆的小青年爆炸头头喇叭裤，一言不合要颠覆世界的时代已经过去，虽不至于立马穿上西装变成大人模样，但Crypto已经逐步与主流金融和社会在融合，而非彻底对立。

曾经我们认为BTC是法币的彻底对立，Defi是传统金融的完全颠覆，点对点加密支付才是人类的未来样子。

但现在是Defi在美股资产RWA上开花，BTC成了数字黄金，稳定币不断壮大，成了法币与Crypto之间最融洽的未来。

相比2021年，行业已经出现了重要变化， Coinbase、Circle，以及部分交易协议和DeFi项目，已经证明加密业务能够产生真实收入。

市场也开始更加重视协议收入、代币价值捕获、回购机制等因素。这意味着行业正在从单纯依靠叙事和流动性驱动，逐渐转向关注真实经济价值。

简单的说，已经开始不玩虚的了。

👉币圈到底还能不能继续往前走，还是不是朝阳行业？ 

朝阳不朝阳看的是增量，在之前币圈的总人口数量是相对有限的，大量的人和资金还被认知渠道和误解所拖累没有进圈，这就是增长潜力。

美国约62%的成年人持有股票，而曾经接触加密货币的成年人约为19%。这意味着加密货币已经进入主流社会的视野，但还没有成为大多数人的常规资产配置。

换句话说，大众普及程度仍然很低。

一个真正成熟的行业，通常具备三个特征：
1. 主要商业模式已经得到验证。
例如互联网行业发展到成熟阶段后，广告、电商、云计算、订阅服务等商业模式都能够持续创造利润。

Crypto 目前真正得到大规模验证的商业模式仍然集中在交易、稳定币、金融服务和部分链上基础设施。

大量应用尚未证明自己能够脱离投机需求长期生存。

2. 普通用户不需要理解底层技术。
今天人们使用互联网，不需要理解TCP/IP。
但使用Crypto，用户往往还需要面对钱包、Gas、私钥、跨链、安全风险等问题。

当普通人可以像使用支付宝、Visa一样自然地使用链上金融服务时，我才会认为这个行业进入了更成熟的阶段。

3. 行业不再高度依赖投机周期。
目前Crypto的交易量、融资活动、项目收入和市场情绪，仍然高度受到币价周期影响。

成熟行业当然也有周期，但其核心产品需求通常不会因为资产价格下跌而大面积消失。

这一点，Crypto还有很长的路要走。

所以我个人认为Crypto 依然还算朝阳行业，但的确过了普通人只要入行就能无脑吃到行业红利的阶段。

24年之前，只要你不戴有色眼镜，不被主流媒体带偏以为加密是灰灰男行业，控制好风险管理，能沉下心钻研币圈一个赛道，无论是撸毛，做KOL，玩Defi，屯币，跟项目团队干活，甚至是做个Mod，一个小白年轻人都有机会快速翻身积累到同龄人难以企及的财富。

但现在，你需要会择时，择标的，要选好参与行业的角度，并做好忍耐周期低谷的心理准备。
author: BroLeon
author_name: 土澳大狮兄BroLeon | Crypto | AI | Stocks
quoted_text:
《2049跑会总结 - 行业发展篇》

这次去 TOKEN2049前，我给自己定了一个很重要的目标。

就是尽可能多地和行业内不同层级的参与者，尤其是那些经历过多个周期、有长期积累的资深玩家们，进行一些真正深入的交流。

我想搞清楚几个问题：

👉现在的行业究竟处于什么阶段？
👉币圈到底还能不能继续往前走，还是不是朝阳行业？
👉接下来未来的机会可能在哪里？
👉还值不值得年轻人进入从业？
👉散户还能不能普遍赚到钱？
👉以及，我们这些在行业里待了很多年的人，未来还能不能期待像过去一样大块掘金？

这次我分别和一些资深 VC 小伙伴、非常成功的项目 Founder、老KOL、KOL Agency，以及交易所的朋友进行了深度交流，每次交流基本都在一个小时以上。

时间和资源有限，我聊到的大概70%是华人，30%是欧美老外（以及一位欧美项目中的日本小伙伴）。

有意思的是，大家对于未来的判断存在着不小的分歧。我想先把这些不同的观点摆出来，再谈谈自己的感受。

毕竟，与其只寻找支持自己判断的声音，不如先看看大家究竟在争论什么。

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

悲观派, 这一派朋友的核心判断是：

币圈的暴利时代可能正在结束

1、合规
任何一个行业都不可能永远繁荣，都会经历艰辛的萌芽期->蹒跚的孩童期->锐意进取大刀阔斧的青年期->沉稳但略显无趣的成年期->暮色沉沉走向没落的老年期。

加密行业早已走过了早期黑暗森林野蛮生长的阶段，主旋律必然是合规化，合规的结果必然是因为规则不明，管控不严而带来的各种bug红利被补上，普通小白集体暴富窗口缩小。

今天的加密货币市场已经大到了不可能再被各国政府忽视的程度。随着时间推移，各国的监管、税务和法律部门对于加密货币的运作方式越来越了解。欧美各国对加密税收已经日趋成熟，对CEX牌照的管控也越来越像传统金融靠拢。

这会造成几个必然结果：
1、曾经CEX们通过互联网没有门槛可以不管不顾可以把各国散户吸入自己的场子里交易抽水，但现在大所们在发达国家都已经开始按部就班的遵循相关法规，Travel Rule，合约倍数，衍生品准入门槛等都在给曾经盲目冲入的资金降温。

2、敢于拉盘攒局的人和资金会减少。
说起暴富，我很难忘记曾经的LUNA和SBF时期的FTX，一个帮皇马造就了单人8亿美金纸面财富又竹篮打水一场空的奇迹，另一个通过左脚踏右脚，借助用户资金把早期的Solana生态拉上天。

为什么美股基本不会出现这样的案例，正是因为严格的合规管控。

曾经有大量黑灰资金进入币圈一定程度上促进了crypto的阶段性大繁荣，比如曾经的旺汇资金，比如俄罗斯的赌场资金，被制裁国家的资金。这些钱在合规收紧的当下将很很难再进入池子里成为推高币价的推手。

2、传统资金进入Web3的渠道中断
很多人只看到山寨币跌了、Meme 不好玩了、散户不再接盘。但如果往更深一层看，会发现过去几年支撑币圈繁荣的一套重要资金循环，正在逐渐失效。

上一轮流动性宽松之后，大量传统资金包括家办，基金都找到了一种相对合规的方式进入了加密行业：

那就是投资 Crypto VC。

这些传统资金并不需要自己去交易 Meme，也不需要直接参与各种链上投机，他们只需要把资金配置给加密基金。

VC 拿到钱以后，一部分可能配置 BTC、ETH 等主流资产，另一部分则投入一级市场。

项目方获得融资，招募团队、开发产品、进行市场推广、发放空投、对接交易所，最终项目上线，代币进入二级市场抛售，VC回笼资金。

这形成了一个相当完整的资金循环。

但是去年开始这套模式正在面临严重挑战。传统资金的出资人逐渐发现，投资 Crypto VC 的体验并不理想。

首先，投资周期很长，资金回收慢。其次，山寨币上市以后越来越难达到过去那种疯狂的估值，即便达到了，等他们能解锁的时候，也已经跌的没剩多少。更重要的是，散户已经不愿意继续为这些高估值项目买单。

当 VC 无法为出资人创造理想回报，新的募资自然会越来越困难。而当 VC 募不到钱，项目方也就很难再像过去那样获得源源不断的融资。

这是过去一年多时间，币圈大量VC关停离场(尤其是亚洲VC)的根本原因。

再加上 AI 浪潮，美股科技股的波动完全不输Crypto，吸引了大量资金和优秀创业者离开Web3去参与。 导致我们行业逐渐变成一个缺乏新增参与者、流动性稀缺的存量市场。

怎样重新让这些传统资金可以合法合规的回来，给行业重新输血，这可能才是当前市场最棘手的问题之一。

3、叙事缺乏创新
从短期看，币圈更大的问题在于，过去币圈最重要的造富环节之一 -- 山寨币叙事的共识已经瓦解，而继任者Meme也并没有好多少。

流动性匮乏后，DePIN、GameFi，以及许多曾经被寄予厚望的赛道也逐渐暴露出商业模式和真实收入上的问题。

最终导致散户不再相信山寨币，也不再相信那些听起来非常宏大的叙事，转而去支持“反华尔街”的Meme。

但Meme 曾经是反 VC 的武器，如今却也开始走向僵化，今天的 Meme，虽然摆脱了传统 VC 抱团发币、上所出货的模式，却又逐渐形成了另一套利益集团。

发币集团、喊单集团，以及各种相互绑定的小团体，开始主导越来越多的机会。普通散户想依靠早期参与或者个人认知，实现几倍甚至几十倍的收益，已经变得越来越困难。

前段时间Vtalik也说到，https://t.co/ealUYe7tVg 上的小团体通过持续发行 Meme，累计收割了超过一亿美元，玩Fomo的散户亏损比例超过90%。

无论具体案例如何，背后反映的问题是值得关注的：

曾经以公平、开放为卖点的 Meme 游戏，也在逐渐被新的利益结构所占据。

旧的游戏被打破，新的游戏又开始僵化，而我们还没能找到下一个能令人兴奋，让相对多散户们吃到红利，博弈没有那么激烈的新游戏模式。

~~~~~~~~~~

乐观派, 这一派朋友的核心判断是：

行业基本面好转肉眼可见，我们已经走出谷底。

虽然各自的表达方式有些不一样，但不少朋友赞同今天的币圈，可能很像 2019 年 ICO 泡沫破灭之后的状态。

当时，市场对于上一轮主流叙事（万物皆可ICO）的信任彻底崩塌。市面上没人任何新项目，老项目批量死亡，从业者不知道未来的方向在哪里，纷纷跳槽回金融行业和互联网。

整个行业看起来似乎没有一个能落地并持续产生收入的项目，也已经没有什么值得期待的东西。但结果是，接近一年的熊市里，孕育出了Defi这朵耀眼的花。

而现在，类似的事情正在重新发生。

其实这个感觉，我从去年就已经有了。当时市场开始下行，散户不再愿意为山寨币买单，反而 Meme 依然风行一时。

我那时候就觉得，行业可能需要经历一次比较彻底的出清。还专门写过一篇长推，谈 VC 抱团组局、项目上所砸盘已经让行业陷入了彻底的僵局，不知道谁能解开这个结，否则熊可能会来的很快。

后边Meme的崛起和币安Alpah的革新玩法把市场续命了大半年，一直到1011后市场流动性大幅萎缩，市场却经历了一个漫长的、逐步消亡的过程。

直到将近一年后的这次2049我才明显感觉到，市面上那些老项目已经被清理得差不多了。

能上所的早就上了，上不了所的很多也已经死掉了。

从这个角度来看，当前行业的萧条，未必是一件坏事。

它更像是一次漫长的排毒过程，而排毒是需要时间的。只有旧的东西逐渐退出市场，新的叙事和新的玩法才有机会真正成长起来。

所谓不破不立。

冬天来了以后，真正有生命力的东西，才有机会在下一个春天重新发芽。如果把时间维度拉长，我们或许可以更加理性地看待当前的市场环境，也更有耐心地等待下一次创新。

何况现在我们已经能看到有一些可以持续创造收益的，拥有稳定用户群体的项目存在了，别人很难再Diss加密货币就是个空中楼阁的大Ponzi。

关于悲观派提到的合规进程问题，乐观派的看法是，换个角度看 -- 

“加密货币被越来越多的国家接受，逐渐进入主流金融体系，这不正是我们这些早期参与者曾经梦寐以求的事情吗？”

回想很多年前，我们这些Crypto早期信仰者希望的是什么？

是加密货币能够真正被广泛使用。是越来越多的人了解区块链和数字资产。是加密货币不再只是一个小圈子里的游戏，而是能够进入真实世界的金融和商业体系。

现在，这些事情其实正在逐步发生，比如 @circle 和加密货币企业上市，不少交易所被主流金融机构投资，Hyperliquid被Trump提到，8200万台美国三星手机开始内嵌稳定币钱包，Robinhood和富途为用户提供加密货币交易入口。

这些看起来离我们每日赚钱Alpha有点远的虚头巴脑的利好在外部大环境改变，比如流动性重新宽松起来的时候，将很有可能成为更大量级用户涌入Crypto的基石。

正如同曾经我们不能仅仅因为风靡一时的ICO不再Work就认定行业完蛋了，我们也不能因为VC 发币模式不再 Work，Meme模式散户也难赚钱了就认定整个行业已经不行了。

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
其实还有不少内容，但我也不想过于长篇大佬，前面抛出的问题我回头再分开慢慢给出自己的思考答案。

只想说把时间维度拉长，以更加开放的心态去看待行业的发展，而不是用旧时代的游戏规则，去判断一个新时代是否还有未来。

这可能是我这次 TOKEN2049 和不同朋友交流之后，最值得继续思考的事情。

text:
贝莱德大调整：美股中性，超配短期美债
模型越便宜，卡越贵，买卡的借钱的利息也越来越高

Silicon Data token均价自5月高点跌了52%，同期B300租金涨了38%。10年期美债到5.2%以上，24年来最高。
三件事看起来毫无关系。但它们在同一条因果链上。

1｜模型层在杀价
Jefferies的Chris Wood在10月9日的GREED & fear里写：AI故事最可能的长期结局，是美国“大规模资本毁灭”，市场份额流向更便宜的中国开源模型。
他看到的数字：Silicon Data token均价自5月高点跌52%，到每百万token 0.98美元。OpenRouter 9月27日当周，中国顶级模型处理76.12万亿token，美国顶级模型14.2万亿。
Wood把这件事比作2008年次贷危机的前夜，只不过这次的“次贷”，是云厂给亏损AI公司提供的无担保信用。

2｜利润流向卡
同一条因果链上，@GavinSBaker在10月11日引用Silicon Data数据：token指数5月31日见顶之后，B300租金涨了38%，B200涨了10%。
为什么模型在降价，卡在涨价？
开源权重把模型层利润压扁了。但一个开源token和一个前沿token，吃的算力差不多。单价跌，总量涨得更快，总算力需求反而扩大。利润从模型层转移到了拥有GPU的基建层。
Wood的建议同向：从2023年起就说持有镐与铲，不是云厂本身。

3｜卡的钱来自信用
但买卡的钱，不是凭空来的。
微软、谷歌、亚马逊、甲骨文四家云厂的RPO到2.34万亿美元，约一半来自还在亏损的OpenAI和Anthropic。云厂在给亏损的租户垫资建数据中心。
Wood说，真正喊停这轮周期的，会是信用市场。

4｜信用的价格是利率
信用的价格，就是利率。
贝莱德投资研究院10月13日调仓，结束了从2020年10月开始的美债低配（当时10年期不到0.9%）：
美股：超配→中性
短期美债：→超配
长期美债：→中性
降美股一是给美债腾钱，二是对冲AI基建这条线的波动，原话是“短期风险管理”。
但对AI的信心没变，继续偏好AI相关公司和上市基础设施，入场点更好时会再加风险。

PIMCO的Rupert Harrison上周也说，PIMCO债券组合久期“差不多是很长一段时间以来最长的”。

5｜这周看CPI
贝莱德说，市场年初以来多计入了160个基点的加息，打得太满。按当前收益率，美债收益率未来12个月再涨75个基点，总回报才转负。

周三（10月14日）美国9月CPI，FactSet预期同比3.6%，核心2.4%。5.2%能不能守住，看这周。

| 模型越便宜，卡越贵。钱流向稀缺的卡，卡的钱来自信用，信用的价格是利率。

NEW: 🇳🇴 Chinese-owned rental cars used by the Norwegian Armed Forces reportedly recorded soldiers, their movements and security codes during a major military exercise in Oslo, raising serious questions about the security of vehicles used in sensitive military operations.

The incident occurred during Operation Hovedstad, held from September 14 to 18, when Norway’s Home Guard District 02 trained for security operations, including scenarios involving the defence of Oslo Airport during wartime.

The Armed Forces had rented the cars through Hertz Norway under a nationwide rental agreement signed in 2024, worth up to 350 million Norwegian kroner and running until May 2028. Hertz Norway’s ownership chain ultimately leads to China’s Zhejiang Geely Holding Group, which also owns Volvo Cars. The agreement provides rental vehicles for exercises, operational activities and everyday military use.

During the exercise, soldiers discovered that the cars had recorded and stored video footage. Lieutenant Fredrik Blanck told Norwegian newspaper Dagens Næringsliv (DN) that the recordings showed who entered and exited the vehicles, where they travelled, whom they picked up and how long they remained at different locations.

More concerningly, the footage reportedly captured security codes entered by soldiers when opening military gates. Some access points require both a key card and a code, meaning the recordings could expose sensitive access procedures.

The vehicles remained in use throughout the exercise because alternative transport was in limited supply.

text:
The Mysterious Case of the Missing Talarico

The objective facts on both sides

One side:

1. An inexplicable disappearance and campaign blackout -- could be incompetent team, could be real crisis

2. Phone recording of employee saying Talarico was at a mental hospital -- could be real, could be fake

3. A charter flight consistent with Talarico being there -- circumstantial

4. A changing story from a nervous Talarico -- he could have been trying to make himself not look fragile

Other side:

5. The phone call to the mental hospital gave the wrong discharge date -- could be invalidating, could be lagging paperwork on discharge that happened a day earlier

6. Hospital with a lawyerly (?) PR announcement saying he wasn't treated *by* the hospital -- "by" or "at"?

7. New York Times claiming they saw security camera footage -- could real, could be fake

8. Denials by Talarico's team -- not credible

My take:

The most damning two facts are facts 1 and 4.

Fact 1. Either Talarico had a real crisis that he is not telling us about, and his team kept it quiet, or they just messed up.

Fact 4. The most charitable interpretation is that Talarico misled the audience during his interview where he claimed "just a primary care physician", and left out the "urgent care in Dallas" part to minimize the severity of the illness, which may have been possibly much worse than he let on.

Fact 4 combined with Fact 1 presents the possibility that his staff was either worried or intentionally kept in the dark over an illness whose severity worried Talarico's inner circle.

This is the most charitable, least conspiratorial take, and it doesn't look good for Talarico. Is he going to die from the cold while in office? We know that this is not his first rodeo, either. He has been hospitalized with severe diabetic complications from ordinary illnesses before.

Was Talarico in a mental hospital? Is the Talarico campaign keeping something from us about the severity of his illness? Can we trust the NYT reporting saying they reviewed his security footage (of course they want Talarico to win)?

Many questions remain open about Talarico's mysterious disappearance.

Anthropic says it has reduced the data harvested from Claude in distillation attacks by around 90–99%. I congratulate them on this achievement.

It’s consistent with the point I made a few months ago (All-In Ep. 282): Anthropic, not the government, was in the best position to stop distillation of its own models. Once the horse is out of the barn, there’s limited value in after-the-fact government action.

At the time there was a major push in Washington to restrict open models on IP grounds. The threat looked serious enough that 50 companies — including Nvidia, Microsoft, Meta, IBM, Palantir, and Dell — published an open letter in defense of open-weight models. Jensen Huang promoted it in his first-ever X post. Nearly 200 startups sent a similar letter.

I argued that restricting open models risked removing the incentive for closed-model companies to solve the problem themselves — and could reward negligence by stifling competition while they continued collecting revenue from distillation. The administration did not impose those restrictions.

Now we see the result. Anthropic invested in defenses and they worked. Not every technical challenge is a reason to run to Washington for new regulation.

author: tengyanAI
quoted_text:
Dusting off this tweet from April because this gap in shared understanding of LLM capability is *widening*. It's now less "two groups of people speaking past each other" and more a sharp funnel.

- Napkin math somewhere around 6B people (~75% of the population) have barely come in contact with LLMs at all.
- Around 1-2B (~20%) are casual and infrequent users of free-tier ChatGPT-like products. This group sees derpy chatbots and treats them a bit like a better Google search, a writing aid, or etc. Maybe an agent tries to book you a flight. I have non-tech friends who (reasonably, imo) say they have not much use for it at all. Even many professionals outside of math&code are in this tier. For example, execs and many other functions spend a lot of their time talking to other people, so while they understand what is happening intellectually, it is still second-hand and a bit abstract.
- Now we get to professional use of frontier-grade LLMs in math&code. Somewhere around 20M people (0.2%) see first-hand that large, complex projects that used to take them weeks/months can now be completed by agents with a prompt. Building apps, copying apps, translating apps, decompiling apps from binaries... This has all happened very quickly and recently - less than 1 year ago, I was writing code manually by hand, typing memorized computer code commands into a code editor character by character, occasionally pressing Tab to autocomplete a little chunk of code.
- And finally we get to the ~5,000 people (~0.00006%) with access to frontier-grade systems internally. The external world has seen the preview. It looks like swarms of thousands of agents collaborating over weeks on software mega projects: minting zero days, running cyber attacks and defenses at machine speeds, discovering new science, advancing the frontier of mathematics. Things that would have taken top professionals in the industry years of work. Meanwhile, human review and comprehension are starting to fall behind. For example, people are still involved in the "archeology" of the OpenAI-HF incident from many months ago. Mathematicians may be poring over the 722 manuscripts on frontier mathematics for a while.

The funnel is driven by a combination of factors:
1. The impact scales with ambition, problem size, and horizon. A question with a paragraph answer barely stresses the system. You need a reservoir of big, difficult problems that you really care about. This aspect drives the consumer / professional dimension of the funnel.
2. The jaggedness of the system (which I have written about a lot separately). Capability peaks in domains that are digital, verifiable and economically valuable. This is because LLM capability emerges from reinforcement learning on verifiable rewards on a curated environment mixture driven by revenue potential. This aspect primarily drives the area (e.g. math&code) dimension of the funnel.
3. Access. Free-tier, paid-tier, internal.

So this is the weirdness of the moment. The general public has mostly not interacted with these systems. When they have, it looks like a derpy chatbot. The majority of professionals still see only a modest uplift. And a small sliver of professionals are experiencing the vertigo of the curve going vertical. And it is all happening at the same time.

text:
Let's take a closer look at $VRAX. I think it is quite different from many of the other memes on RH Chain that are simply riding the RH narrative.

0x94641b97010608c3827fb058074889f19868ff33 

Its biggest advantage is that Vrax itself is a character from Robinhood's official HOOD Summit storyline.

Specifically, at the HOOD Summit on September 29, Robinhood used the sci-fi world of Starship Robinhood to package its products, with Vlad Tenev playing the Captain and Vrax appearing as one of the antagonists. Shortly afterward, the official Robinhood account directly posted: “Update on Commander Vrax: he’s a cat now.”

This is important because it turned what was originally just a character from an event storyline into a meme character that could spread independently.

So the path became:Robinhood officially creates Vrax → Robinhood officially turns Vrax into a cat → the community launches VRAX → trading volume explodes

But what really started to change this time were two signals.

First, Vlad Tenev is already following Vraxrh.

Second, the Vraxrh account directly has the CA in its bio.

This means the account is no longer simply operating as a Vrax fan account. It is explicitly connecting the official character to an on-chain token.

So the Attention path now looks like:Robinhood officially creates Vrax → Robinhood officially turns Vrax into a cat → the community creates VRAX → Vraxrh creates the account and posts the CA → Vlad Tenev follows Vraxrh

In other words, Vlad very likely knows about the token.

Of course, we still need to make the boundaries clear:Vlad following the account ≠ Vlad buying VRAX

Vlad following the account ≠ Robinhood officially issuing VRAX

Vlad following the account ≠ Robinhood officially endorsing VRAX

But for the Meme market, Vlad's Follow itself is a very strong Attention Signal.

Because if Vlad had never followed the account, the market would only be trading:“The community turned Robinhood's Vrax character into a Meme.”

Now there is another layer:“The CEO of Robinhood himself has noticed the account.”

And because the account also directly has the CA in its bio, the market can easily connect the chain:Official Character → Community Account → Token

This is the biggest difference between VRAX and an ordinary RH Chain Meme.

A normal Meme usually looks like:Community → Meme → KOL / Official Attention

While VRAX looks more like:Official IP → Official Meme → Community → Tokenization → CEO Attention

In other words, the story was first created by Robinhood, and then the community turned it into a Meme and financialized it.

So what the market is betting on now is no longer simply:“Is Vrax an interesting Meme?”

It is:“Will Robinhood continue using the character it created?”

If Vrax only appeared once during the HOOD Summit, then fundamentally it is just an Event Meme.

But if Robinhood continues posting Vrax memes, Cat Vrax images, videos, new storylines, or even puts Vrax into future advertisements, product Easter eggs, Social content, or events, then the nature of Vrax changes.

It could gradually move from:HOOD Summit Event Character

to:Robinhood Native Meme IP

And that is the biggest upside potential for VRAX.

I also think the most important factor in whether Robinhood continues telling the Vrax story is not whether it “likes the Meme,” but whether Vrax continues generating Attention for Robinhood's brand and products.

If the community keeps producing Vrax derivatives, videos, memes, and other content while VRAX maintains strong trading activity, then it becomes very low-cost for Robinhood to keep using the character, because the community is already doing the content production for them.

Another important point is that the HOOD Summit itself already demonstrated that Robinhood is willing to use a complete world-building concept involving Starship, the Captain, alien civilizations, and other characters to package its products.

So Vrax is not a Meme that appeared out of nowhere. It is part of a Lore created by Robinhood itself.

If Robinhood continues holding large product events in the future, Vrax could potentially continue appearing as a recurring character within that universe.

Another direction worth watching is Robinhood Social.

If Vrax eventually enters Robinhood's Social content, product Easter eggs, or community interactions, then it would move from being a character from a single event into Robinhood's broader day-to-day content ecosystem.

So I would roughly think about the upcoming catalysts in terms of strength like this:Robinhood officially posts Vrax again → proves that Robinhood does not view Vrax as a one-time character.

Vlad interacts with the Vrax account again → stronger than simply following the account.

Vrax appears on Robinhood Social / in products / advertisements → shows that Vrax is entering Robinhood's longer-term content ecosystem.

Vrax appears again at a future Robinhood event → very strong validation, because it would mean Vrax has moved from an Event Character to a Recurring Character.

And the most important step is actually:CEO Attention → Official Re-engagement

The first step has already happened:Vlad follows Vraxrh

Now the thing to watch is whether Robinhood actively uses Vrax again.

So this is how I currently understand VRAX:

Before:Vrax = an antagonist character from the HOOD Summit.

Now:Vrax = Robinhood official character + officially turned into a cat + community Tokenization + community account with a CA + Vlad Follow.

This means its Narrative Validity and Attention are stronger than those of an ordinary RH Chain Meme.

But its traditional fundamentals have not changed because of this. VRAX still has no independent product revenue and is not an official Robinhood Token.

text:
现在看美银上周这份《FLOW Show》时机很好，Hartnett认为高利率已经开始影响市场内部结构，而中期选举可能进一步改变盈利、资本开支和监管预期。在这个窗口里，现金有收益，投资者也就有耐心等待。他给的建议是：
1）对继续追加拥挤敞口保持谨慎
2）科技内部相对偏好七巨头，胜过半导体；
3）开始压押注收益率见顶相关资产，少量尝试30年期美债、小盘股、REITs和香港地产。
4）更长期的方向，维持对黄金、商品和新兴市场的偏好。

个人角度：
1）赞同Hartnett提高防守权重的理由，尤其是把市场广度和信用变化放在一起观察。上周也有https://t.co/rYYQn4BuQL聊到：近期市场会走的很不稳当，CPI前的避险、中选、还有产业上的担心，都会导致稍有风吹躁动就引发调整。

2）但也不会把“不降息”直接作为不能加仓的条件。若盈利继续上修、信用风险稳定、能源压力缓和，即使政策利率暂时不动，股票也可以重新变得有吸引力。
author: qinbafrank
quoted_text:
花旗10月5日发布的《全球股票季度展望：韧性还是自满？》核心其实是在回答一个很重要的问题：为什么在油价高位、全球重新进入加息周期、长端利率大幅上行、美国—伊朗冲突没有彻底解决、市场广度又明显恶化的情况下，全球股票仍然接近历史高点？
这是基本面真的比想象中强，还是市场已经对风险麻木？
花旗给出的答案：目前仍站在 “Resilience（韧性）” 一边。它实际上把未来半年全球股票继续上涨的条件压缩成了两个变量：盈利必须继续兑现，地缘和利率冲击不能进一步升级。

当然长债收益率上涨绝不是没有影响：影响主要落在传统行业、中小盘、房地产、消费等利率敏感资产。而 AI / 半导体 / 大型科技由于盈利增长足够强，靠“分子”增长抵消了“分母”折现率上升。
花旗的逻辑跟我之前推文逻辑很一致，

花期这份报告对当下美股投资三个意义：
1）AI交易目前没有结束。
因为驱动 AI 股票的东西正在从估值扩张
逐渐切换成EPS兑现；
2）收益率上涨为什么科技不跌、传统行业跌这个现象仍然可能持续；
3）未来真正能够让美股牛市发生趋势性逆转的变量，很可能不是第一次或者第二次加息，而是盈利revision开始转负。

花旗认为目前的市场韧性大体是真的，因为盈利增长足够强，过去一年甚至在股价上涨的同时把全球股市估值从19倍消化到了16倍；但市场已经进入一个对EPS兑现高度依赖的阶段，未来再靠估值扩张赚钱越来越困难。

只要盈利没有开始下修，这种分化本身还不能当作牛市结束信号。真正需要警惕的是 高利率从“经济强的结果”逐步变成“财政/通胀/term premium失控的结果”，与此同时AI盈利revision开始见顶。 这两个条件如果同时出现，才会把花旗的“韧性”真正推向“自满”。

之前10月1号对9月份有一个回复和10月展望 跟花旗的这期报告逻辑很类似： https://t.co/kpblUc6mco

text:
一个 4B 模型，学会「怎么改 Agent」之后，在没见过的任务上，平均改得比 35B Teacher 还好。

这篇工作有意思的地方是把「如何改 Harness」本身训练成了一种可以迁移的能力。

系统里有两个角色：

Solver 负责做任务，Proposer 观察执行结果，再修改 Solver 的 Harness，包括模型调用、工具使用、信息流和控制逻辑。

训练阶段，Proposer 用 RL 学习哪些修改真的有效。

到了新任务上，两个模型的权重全部冻结，Proposer 只根据执行反馈继续改 Harness。

在 21 个训练时没见过的 Reasoning Gym 任务上，4B Proposer 的平均修改得分从 0.32 提升到 0.62，超过 35B Teacher 的 0.56。

还有就是它只训练过单次修改，却能在测试时连续迭代。

在未见过的 MuSiQue 上，独立修改平均只有 0.15，连续改 10 轮后达到 0.27；在两个未见 QA benchmark 上，连续修改甚至超过了从 80 个独立方案里挑出的最好结果。

所以 Harness 自进化再往前一步会变成训练出一个会持续改工作流的 Agent。

它学到的，是一种改进方法本身。

text:
Anthropic 这篇官方檄文可以说是彻底撕破脸了，
直接公开点名智谱和月之暗面，把大模型圈工业级偷思维链的黑产老底全掀了。

A社刚发了今年火药味最浓的一篇官方研究，
直接公开点名智谱和月之暗面，把大模型行业暗流涌动的工业级蒸馏偷家产业链掀到了台面上。

很多人一直在好奇，为什么海外大厂砸几十亿美金苦练的顶级推理能力，一些团队只要花几分之一的时间和成本就能迅速追平。

Anthropic 这次拿出的数据极其吓人，
他们发现有大量黑产和机构控制着几十万个虚假账号，
通过代理网络疯狂给 Claude 发送数百万次请求，
核心目标根本不是偷答案，而是偷 Claude 在输出前的完整思维链。

数据表明，拿完整的推理思考过程去训小模型，
代码评测能直接冲到 80.4%，而只拿精简答案去训只有 71.8%，这十个点的差距就是大模型最值钱的核心资产。

为了防住这种工业级抽血，Anthropic 这次直接上了三套极其绝情的硬手段：

一是锁死推理上下文，新 API 账号彻底禁止篡改对话历史，把思维链只留给本机构；
二是把防蒸馏的安全分类器直接拉到了防生物武器的同等级别，误伤率低于千分之一； 
三是把被拦截的恶意请求照样扣费，并在几小时内封掉了几万个洗白账号。

这一套组合拳打下来，官方统计直接把被偷走的数据量砍掉了 90% 到 99%，为此 Anthropic 宁可主动拒掉数万亿 Token 的真金白银收入。

说白了，以前大模型赛道表面拼的是参数和跑分，暗地里拼的是谁能更隐蔽地把前沿大模型当免费老师来抽血，

当思维链的输血管道被巨头彻底焊死，真正拼底层原生内功的淘汰赛也许才刚刚开始啊～～

text:
A lot of AI security research asks: “Can this model be fooled?”

@perturbaix turns that question into a competitive market.

On Bittensor SN 26, miners are effectively adversarial bounty hunters. They search for inputs that can flip a model's answer with the smallest possible change.

Validators don't just reward anyone who finds something. They verify that the model actually fails, check the size of the perturbation, and reject copied attacks.

That incentive structure is what I find interesting.

The network is continuously pushing miners toward stronger, more efficient attacks, while the useful output can become robustness scores, vulnerability maps and verified attack data for retraining.

It's a good example of what Bittensor can do beyond simply serving inference:

create a market around a difficult AI problem, define what “good work” looks like, verify it, and pay whoever does it best.

Fight AI with AI. @perturbaix

text:
I found a critical safety issue in one major new consensus protocol in the blockchain sector.

The protocol had been formally verified, HOWEVER the formally verified protocol is not the same as the pseudocode.

This appears to be the same scenario that OpenAI has run into with Navier-Stokes.

If this had gotten into production it could have triggered a catastrophic failure, since only a small portion of stake could have broken safety.

The protocol in question is Fast Tendermint. It lets a single Byzantine validator (out of 5f+1) make honest validators decide different values. With 2 validators, equivocation is not even required.

Paper with two fixes and proofs: https://t.co/vj5Qdtwebx

Disclaimer: The authors also specified they consider the formally verified protocol the source of truth.

text:
UPDATE: I can confirm that the Ledger supply chain is compromised in Europe as well. @Ledger should initiate an immediate product recall to protect users.

I just purchased a second device from a different Mediamarkt location today, recorded the unboxing process, and discovered spyware once again (video linked in the second tweet).

The device was compromised in the exact same manner, featuring identical modifications (such as additional cables and an LTE module). This indicates its a widespread issue rather than an isolated incident, potentially affecting Ledger inventory across MediaMarkt and Saturn stores throughout Europe (comprising over 1,000 stores across 11 countries).

My initial hypothesis was that these devices were returns that looked unopened to the employees and were just sold again as new however, a MediaMarkt employee confirmed that the device I purchased was not a return, and that returned Ledgers are sent directly back to the manufacturer rather than resold.

Store records show the inventory originated from Aqipa GmbH. While Ledger's CTO was unsure if Aqipa serves as the direct distributor between Ledger and MediaMarkt, it appears to be the case. Given that Aqipa distributes across Europe, any physical retail store receiving stock through them may be at risk.

I sent the first ledger to mark and the second one is going to ledger now, so that they can analyse it.
If you purchased a ledger from anyone other than the official ledger store, make sure to check your device!!
